description: Deliver pairs of stimulus pulses with systematically varied inter-pulse intervals and read out single-cell AP-1 target induction, fitting the decay of potentiation to obtain a memory time constant. Compute the mutual information between past stimulus history and current single-cell state to quantify how many bits of history AP-1 stores, and whether memory is graded or bistable.

title: Synthetic enhancer library screen for AP-1 motif architectures that support persistence
description: Build a reporter library systematically varying AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, and flanking partner motifs, integrate it at a fixed locus, and sort for reporters that remain active long after the stimulus ends. This tests sufficiency and identifies which cis-architectures are needed to convert a transient AP-1 input into a persistent state.

title: Degron depletion of AP-1 between priming and rechallenge
description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on endogenous FOS, JUN, JUNB and FOSL1 to eliminate AP-1 selectively during the interval between a priming stimulus and a rechallenge, leaving the induction and readout phases intact. If priming survives AP-1 loss during this interval, AP-1 establishes the memory in chromatin; if priming collapses, persistence of AP-1 protein is itself the memory. The two cases are distinguished by the timing of depletion.

title: Single-molecule footprinting of primed enhancers
description: Apply long-read methylation footprinting (Fiber-seq or SAMOSA) to naive, stimulated, and rested cells to determine whether primed AP-1 enhancers show a bimodal population, in which a subset of molecules remain fully open and bound, or a uniform intermediate state across all molecules. Population-average ATAC-seq cannot distinguish these, and they imply different memory mechanisms (a stable per-allele state versus graded relaxation).

title: Hysteresis mapping across stimulus doses
description: Measure AP-1 target output across an ascending and then descending series of stimulus doses with matched equilibration times, testing for a hysteresis loop in which cells approaching from high doses remain active at doses that cannot activate naive cells. An open loop is a direct, model-free signature of bistable memory, and the loop width quantifies memory depth; its absence argues for slow relaxation instead.

title: Tracking the primed state through mitosis and replication
description: Combine clonal barcoding with division counting (dye dilution or FUCCI-gated sorting) and single-cell multiome to measure how many cell divisions a primed AP-1 chromatin state survives, and whether sister cells inherit priming concordantly. Heritability across mitosis plus sister concordance is taken as the operational definition of cellular memory and separates it from a long-lived but non-heritable cytoplasmic state.

title: Reporter panel varying AP-1 site architecture
description: Integrate at a fixed safe-harbor locus a panel of reporters whose enhancers differ in AP-1 site number, affinity, spacing and neighboring cofactor motifs, then run identical prime–wait–rechallenge protocols on each. This identifies the minimal cis architecture sufficient to store a transient AP-1 input and shows which features set memory duration.

title: Phase-specific degron depletion of AP-1 during priming, interval, and restimulation
description: Tag endogenous c-Jun/c-Fos (and a second redundant family member) with dTAG or auxin degrons and deplete AP-1 acutely in non-overlapping windows: only during the priming stimulus, only during the memory interval with no stimulus present, and only at the moment of restimulation. If memory survives depletion during the interval but not during priming, AP-1 is required to establish but not to store the memory, which separates causality from maintenance and avoids the confounds of constitutive knockouts.

title: Sister-cell split assay with heritable barcodes
description: Lineage-barcode cells (ClonMapper/Watermelon) and prime the population. Physically split sister cells after one division, challenge one sister and profile the other, and repeat across increasing numbers of divisions. This distinguishes per-cell heritable memory from selection of a pre-existing responsive subpopulation, and quantifies memory as the probability of concordance between relatives rather than a bulk average.

title: Transfer-function mapping to detect latent memory
description: Instead of testing whether a resting AP-1 state persists, measure the full dose-response and kinetic transfer function to a second stimulus across a matrix of priming doses and rest intervals, using a live AP-1 (TRE) reporter and a target-gene reporter. Memory appears as a shift in threshold, amplitude, or latency even when baseline chromatin and transcriptome have returned to the naive state, capturing primed states that steady-state assays would miss.

title: Dimer composition of the AP-1 state
description: Use subunit-resolved CUT&RUN or CUT&Tag for Fos, FosB, Fra-1, Fra-2, JunB, JunD, c-Jun and ATF3 at matched timepoints, combined with split-reporter or proximity-ligation dimer sensors and rapid-exchange measurements (FRAP, SNAP-tag pulse-chase) at the same loci. The test is whether memory is encoded as a stable change in dimer identity and residence time at shared sites rather than as a change in total AP-1 output.

title: Cell-versus-matrix swap to localize where memory is stored
description: Prime cells on a deformable or decellularizable substrate, then cross-transplant: primed cells onto matrix derived from naive cells, and naive cells onto matrix derived from primed cells. Also do conditioned-medium swaps and serial replating onto fresh stiffness-matched surfaces. If recall follows the matrix rather than the cell, AP-1 is re-reading an extracellular trace and the intracellular memory is reconstructed each time rather than stored.

title: Hysteresis mapping with a live AP-1 reporter
description: Using a live AP-1 activity reporter, drive cells up and then back down a graded stimulus dose (e.g., serum, TGF-beta, stiffness, or an optogenetic FOS/JUN input). Test whether the up- and down-going dose-response curves separate into a hysteresis loop with a bistable region rather than retracing each other. This distinguishes a self-sustaining memory state from slow first-order relaxation, which a persistence-duration experiment cannot do.

title: Dimer-resolved pulse-chase of AP-1 subunits
description: Endogenously HaloTag every major AP-1 subunit, then use pulse-chase labeling, CUT&RUN, and sequential ChIP to measure, for each specific dimer, protein lifetime and residence at candidate memory enhancers across the memory window. If memory duration tracks one long-lived species (e.g., a FosB/deltaFosB- or JUND-containing dimer) and not aggregate motif accessibility, the storage element is a particular dimer rather than AP-1 in general.

title: Extracellular matrix transfer and autocrine blockade
description: Test whether memory is extrinsic by moving cells with memory onto decellularized naive ECM, and naive cells onto ECM deposited by cells with memory. Also replate cells at clonal density in fresh matrix with autocrine signaling blocked. If memory transfers with the matrix or disappears when self-deposited ECM and autocrine loops are removed, AP-1 is continuously re-driven by an environmental store rather than being the memory itself.

title: Locus-targeted writing and erasing of AP-1 occupancy to test sufficiency and necessity
description: Use dCas9-recruited synthetic AP-1 activation domains to transiently establish AP-1 occupancy at a few candidate memory enhancers without an upstream stimulus, remove the recruiter, and test whether the downstream state persists. Separately, apply an acute AP-1 degron only after the state is established to test whether AP-1 is required to maintain the state and not only to establish it. Combine this with inhibition of candidate chromatin writers to distinguish AP-1 as the cause from AP-1-associated accessibility as a readout.

title: Lineage-barcoded tracking across controlled division rates
description: Combine heritable barcoding (Rewind/ClonMapper-style) with longitudinal live imaging of an AP-1 reporter to measure sister-sister and mother-daughter correlation decay, giving a memory half-life in generations versus hours. Repeat with division rate manipulated (contact inhibition, serum starvation, CDK inhibition, or post-mitotic cells). If memory decays per unit time rather than per division, and barcodes show the persistent state is re-entered by naive cells rather than only inherited by a pre-existing clone, the mechanism is neither replication-coupled nor selection.

title: Memory decay curves from a two-stimulus interval and dose grid
description: Deliver stimulus 1, then stimulus 2 after a logarithmically spaced interval series (1 h to 6 weeks), and read out the full dose-response of the second response rather than a single dose. Fit the decay of the memory index to obtain a timescale, and compare it with measured FOS/JUN protein half-lives and chromatin mark turnover to distinguish a bistable stable state from a slowly decaying graded trace.

title: Sufficiency test: stimulus-free AP-1 pulse
description: Use an optogenetic or chemically dimerizable FOS-JUN, or a dCas9-fused AP-1 activation domain targeted to specific motif sets, to deliver an AP-1 pulse of defined amplitude and duration in otherwise unstimulated cells. Then test whether the later response to a real stimulus is shifted in the same way as in genuinely pre-stimulated cells. Pair this with an acute degron that removes AP-1 only during the quiescent interval to separate establishment from maintenance. This tests whether AP-1 necessity implies AP-1 is the memory mechanism.

title: Dimer-resolved analysis of AP-1 paralogs during induction and memory
description: Endogenously tag each FOS- and JUN-family paralog with distinct degrons and fluorophores. Track absolute per-cell protein abundance and dimer composition over the memory interval by live imaging plus proximity ligation or dimer-specific CUT&RUN, and degrade each paralog individually in narrow time windows. This identifies which dimer occupies memory loci during the interval, which is only transient during induction, and whether composition switching (e.g., FOS to FRA1) carries the memory.

title: Lineage-barcoded single-cell tracing of memory through division
description: Heritably barcode cells before stimulus 1, let them divide a controlled number of times, then apply stimulus 2 and read out scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq with barcodes so sibling cells can be compared. This distinguishes heritable per-cell memory (siblings concordant, memory present in all cells) from selection of a pre-existing responsive subpopulation (memory confined to specific clones), and quantifies how many divisions the trace survives.

title: Medium-transfer and nuclear-transplant tests of where the memory is stored
description: Cross-transfer conditioned medium, decellularized extracellular matrix, and cells between naive and pre-stimulated conditions. Separately, move nuclei or chromatin from pre-stimulated cells into naive cytoplasm (heterokaryon, nuclear transfer, or permeabilized-cell reconstitution). If memory travels with the medium or matrix rather than the nucleus, AP-1 reads out an extracellular loop. CRISPRi or scarless motif deletion at candidate memory enhancers then tests whether the AP-1 sites are causally required.

title: Degron removal of AP-1 after the first stimulus
description: Use a degron to remove the relevant AP-1 subunits (for example FOSL2 or JUN) only after the first stimulus has ended, then check whether the faster response to a second stimulus disappears. If AP-1 is needed only during the first exposure, it initiates the memory rather than maintaining it.

title: Separating open chromatin from ongoing AP-1 binding
description: In the interval between stimuli, measure open chromatin (ATAC-seq) and AP-1 binding (CUT&RUN) at the same sites over time. Then use dCas9-KRAB or dCas9-p300 to close or open individual AP-1 sites and test whether this removes or creates memory at nearby genes.

title: Single-cell barcode tracking of memory
description: Label cells with heritable barcodes and perform single-cell RNA and chromatin profiling before the first stimulus, after it, and after the second. This determines whether cells with a stronger second response derive from AP-1-high cells that responded to the first stimulus, or from cells that were already primed before any stimulus.

title: Persistence of memory across cell divisions by live-cell imaging
description: Use a live-cell AP-1 activity reporter with time-lapse imaging to compare related cells (sisters and cousins) across several divisions after the stimulus. Measure how quickly the reporter level and the faster second response decline per division, and compare normal cells with cells whose division has been stopped.

title: Mapping the roles of AP-1 dimer pairs
description: Use a CRISPRi screen across AP-1 family members, or tethered dimers that force specific pairs, to test which are needed to establish the memory and which are needed to maintain it. Support this with mass spectrometry of chromatin-bound AP-1 complexes during the period between stimuli.

title: Transfer of cells to naive matrix and medium with secretome blocking
description: After stimulation and washout, serially transfer barcoded cells into decellularized naive ECM, defined hydrogels, or fresh medium with blocking antibodies or receptor inhibitors against candidate autocrine ligands. Ask whether AP-1 activity and second-response priming travel with the cell or remain with the culture environment. Reciprocally, transfer naive cells onto conditioned matrix to test whether memory can be transmitted without any cell that experienced the stimulus.

title: Dimer-resolved identification of the AP-1 species carrying memory
description: Combine endogenous tagging of multiple Fos/Jun/ATF members with pulse-chase proteomics, per-member CUT&RUN, and dimer-specific readouts (BiFC or proximity ligation) to measure which dimer composition persists after washout and at which loci. Then use dimer-selective dominant negatives (A-Fos vs A-Jun) and member-specific degrons to determine which single species is required, testing the prediction that a long-half-life member such as Fra-1/JunB, rather than the canonical c-Fos pulse, carries memory.

title: Acute degron depletion to separate storage from maintenance
description: Establish memory, then acutely deplete AP-1 protein with a dTAG/auxin degron for a defined window and restore it. Measure whether accessibility, histone marks and the primed second response persist during the absence of the factor. Persistence indicates that chromatin stores the memory; collapse indicates that AP-1 occupancy itself is the store, so the epigenetic interpretation of the ATAC peak would be wrong.

title: Lineage-resolved live imaging of memory half-life across divisions
description: Use a live-cell AP-1 transcriptional reporter plus clonal barcoding and continuous tracking through several divisions to compute the decay of mother-daughter and sister-sister correlations, and to score whether memory is re-established after each mitosis or passively diluted. This distinguishes a uniform population half-life from a rare subpopulation of long-memory cells and yields a heritability coefficient.

title: Constant-AP-1 clamp and synthetic AP-1 sufficiency test
description: Use optogenetic or dox-tunable synthetic AP-1 to hold AP-1 activity at a fixed level in cells with different stimulus histories: if history still predicts future behavior at matched AP-1 activity, AP-1 is not the store but a relay. Separately, deliver a defined synthetic AP-1 pulse to naive cells and challenge them with a panel of orthogonal stimuli to test whether AP-1 alone is sufficient to establish a memory, and whether that memory is stimulus-specific or generic.

title: Clamping upstream signals rather than AP-1
description: After stimulus withdrawal, hold candidate upstream maintainers at defined levels during the memory window using optogenetic ERK/JNK clamps, MEK or FAK/ROCK inhibition, substrate-stiffness switching, and conditioned-medium swaps. Then assay whether primed AP-1 accessibility and the enhanced second response persist. If memory collapses only when the upstream input is removed, AP-1 reads out a sustained signal rather than storing the memory itself.

title: Subunit-specific degradation during encoding versus maintenance
description: Build a panel of subunit-specific degrons (cFos, FosB/ΔFosB, JunB, JunD, ATF3, JDP2) combined with per-subunit CUT&RUN and dimer-specific proximity ligation or split-fluorophore reporters. Degrade each subunit selectively during encoding versus during maintenance, and rescue with a different subunit during the maintenance window to test whether the dimer that establishes the state differs from the one that maintains it.

title: Sister-cell and barcoded-clone priming assay
description: Lineage-barcode cells and live-image an AP-1 transcriptional reporter through a prime-rest-restimulate cycle. Compare second-response concordance between sister cells, clonal relatives, and unrelated cells, with split-clone scATAC-seq at both time points. This tests whether bulk measurements reflect single-cell behavior: true per-cell memory predicts within-cell and sister concordance exceeding what clone-level selection of pre-existing responders can explain.

title: Acute degron depletion after encoding with footprint-resolution readout
description: Deplete all AP-1 activity only after encoding is complete, using an auxin or dTAG degron plus a dominant-negative A-Fos. Ask whether primed accessibility, nucleosome positioning, and accelerated second-response kinetics persist without the factor. Pair this with single-molecule footprinting, SLAM-seq, and histone-turnover measurement to identify what maintains the open state if AP-1 is dispensable for maintenance.

title: Per-division versus per-hour decay accounting
description: Measure the state's decay as a function of division number rather than elapsed time by varying proliferation rate (serum, CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, mitotic arrest), and simultaneously pulse-chase-label AP-1 protein with HaloTag or SNAP ligands to compare protein half-life to state half-life. Add live imaging of AP-1 during mitosis to test for bookmarking. Memory that decays per division but outlives the protein would implicate an actively re-established chromatin state rather than residual factor.

title: Removing persistent extracellular and signaling inputs from remembering cells
description: Take cells that remember a stimulus and systematically remove candidate continuous inputs: serial single-cell isolation into fresh microwells, decellularization and replating onto naive matrix, and acute inhibition of MAPK, integrin or autocrine receptor signaling. Then measure AP-1 occupancy and target expression. In a reciprocal arm, plate naive cells onto matrix deposited by remembering cells, which would show whether the memory is stored outside the cell.

title: Dimer-resolved AP-1 occupancy time course
description: Instead of bulk AP-1 motif accessibility, use subunit-specific CUT&RUN or sequential re-ChIP, plus split-fluorophore or proximity-ligation dimer reporters, to determine which FOS/JUN dimer occupies which enhancer at induction versus weeks later. Pair this with single-subunit degron panels to identify which dimer is dispensable for establishing the state but required for maintaining it.

title: Acute total AP-1 degradation followed by washout
description: Degrade all FOS/JUN family members with a multiplexed dTAG/auxin degron for a defined window in the primed state, then restore them and assess whether the enhancer landscape and phenotype return. Spontaneous recovery would mean AP-1 is a readout of an upstream memory store; failure to recover would mean AP-1 itself, or the chromatin it maintains, is the store.

title: Transient recruitment of FOS/JUN to defined loci to test sufficiency
description: Recruit a FOS/JUN activation domain to specific candidate memory enhancers with dCas9 or a chemically induced dimerizer for a controlled pulse, remove the recruiter, and track whether the locus and the associated phenotype self-sustain. Titrating pulse amplitude and duration maps the threshold and dose-dependence of memory installation, which a knockout cannot reveal.

title: Lineage-resolved decay constants and division counting
description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with heritable barcoding and long-term imaging to extract per-lineage autocorrelation times, sister-cell correlation decay across divisions, and the fraction of lineages that retain the state. Compare decay in cycling versus pharmacologically arrested or slowed cells to distinguish dilution per division from turnover per unit time, yielding a measured timescale and heritability value.

title: Dimer-resolved memory map
description: Endogenously tag each major Fos/Jun/ATF subunit and use sequential ChIP/CUT&RUN and dimerization-dependent split-fluorophore reporters to determine which dimer compositions occupy memory loci during induction, maintenance, and recall. Pair this with subunit-specific degrons to test whether the dimer that establishes a site is the same one that maintains it.

title: Acute degron removal and restoration of AP-1 with single-molecule tracking
description: Use an auxin/dTAG degron to fully remove AP-1 protein for a defined window during the maintenance phase, then restore it and test recall; simultaneously measure AP-1 residence times and turnover by live single-molecule tracking and SNAP-tag pulse-chase. If memory survives transient total loss of AP-1, the information is stored elsewhere and AP-1 is a reader or relay; if it does not, AP-1 occupancy is itself the store.

title: Synthetic sufficiency test by targeted AP-1 recruitment
description: Recruit a Fos/Jun bZIP effector to defined candidate memory enhancers with dCas9 without any stimulus, then withdraw recruitment and assay whether primed behavior appears days later. Complement this with base-edited destruction of individual endogenous AP-1 motifs to test necessity for maintenance separately from necessity for the acute response.

title: Transfer of the primed state across cells and matrix
description: Test whether the primed state is carried by the cell or by its environment by swapping decellularized ECM and conditioned medium between primed and naive cultures, co-culturing primed with naive cells, and transplanting primed cells into naive hosts (and vice versa). Measure AP-1 site accessibility and recall competence in the recipient population.

title: Optogenetic dose, duration, and order encoding with clonal lineage recall
description: Deliver quantitatively defined ERK or Fos input patterns with optogenetics while live-imaging an endogenous AP-1 activity reporter. Then barcode and track single lineages through division to a second, independent recall stimulus. This measures how much information (amplitude, duration, pulse order) the AP-1 state stores, its decay half-life, and how quickly sister-cell correlations are lost.

title: AP-1 motif and binding analysis of MemorySeq memory genes
description: Use published MemorySeq data (Shaffer et al. 2020, Cell) identifying genes whose expression stays on or off across several generations of a clone. Test whether these memory genes have more AP-1 motifs, and more AP-1 binding in public ENCODE ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq data, than non-memory genes matched for expression level, variability and baseline accessibility.

title: AP-1 activity similarity within barcoded clones
description: Reanalyze public lineage-barcoded single-cell RNA, ATAC, or multiome datasets (e.g., FateMap, Rewind, LARRY, ClonMapper, CellTag-multi). Score each cell's TF motif accessibility with chromVAR, then compare how much more similar sister cells are than unrelated cells for AP-1 versus other TF families. Also test whether a cell's AP-1 activity at an early time point predicts the later fate of its clone.

title: Duration of AP-1 site accessibility versus AP-1 presence after stimulus removal
description: Collect public time courses that include a withdrawal phase, such as inflammatory memory in epithelial stem cells (Larsen et al. 2021), trained immunity in macrophages, serum/TPA pulses, and BRAF-inhibitor drug holidays in melanoma. Estimate how fast FOS/JUN mRNA and protein disappear versus how fast chromatin at AP-1 motif sites closes. Use TOBIAS footprinting to determine whether AP-1 is still bound or has left open chromatin without the factor. If sites stay open long after the factor is gone, that suggests AP-1 establishes a lasting chromatin mark.

title: Meta-analysis of AP-1 motif enrichment at persistently open sites across systems
description: Gather public before/during/after chromatin datasets from multiple memory paradigms (inflammatory memory, trained immunity, wound healing, senescence, drug-tolerant persisters, T-cell exhaustion, activity-dependent neuronal enhancers). Classify induced chromatin sites as persistent or transient, then test whether AP-1 motifs are enriched at persistent sites compared with transient sites matched for GC content, induction strength, and baseline accessibility. The matching controls for AP-1 motifs being common at enhancers in general.

title: Reanalysis of AP-1 knockout/inhibition data and mitotic binding data
description: Reanalyze public datasets where AP-1 was knocked out or blocked with dominant-negative FOS or JUN, either before or after a priming stimulus (e.g., Vierbuchen et al. 2017; Fosl2/Jun knockouts in inflammatory-memory and T-cell studies). This tests whether AP-1 is needed only to set up lasting accessibility or also to keep it. Separately, check public mitotic ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq data to see whether AP-1 sites stay bound or open during mitosis, which would show whether AP-1 itself can carry the memory through cell division.

title: Decay kinetics of AP-1 binding versus chromatin accessibility after a pulse
description: Deliver a transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA or a brief MEK-inhibitor pulse), wash out, and collect a time course out to 2-3 weeks for low-input ATAC-seq plus CUT&RUN for FOSL1/JUN, asking whether accessibility at AP-1 sites persists after AP-1 protein has returned to baseline. Roughly 30-40 libraries with in-house Tn5 and a shared NovaSeq lane fits under $20k and distinguishes a transient signal from a durable chromatin mark.

title: Degron test of AP-1 requirement for maintaining vs. establishing a state
description: Knock a dTAG or auxin degron into an endogenous AP-1 subunit, then compare acute depletion during state establishment versus after the state has been stably held, reading out accessibility at a few hundred AP-1 loci by targeted ATAC or a small qPCR/amplicon panel. The informative result is whether an established state survives AP-1 removal and whether it re-establishes after degrader washout, which is the operational definition of a memory-maintaining factor.

title: Clonal barcoding to test heritability of AP-1 state across divisions
description: Combine a lentiviral barcode library with FACS sorting of an AP-1 activity reporter, split each sorted population, and sequence barcodes and re-measure reporter distributions over about 20 divisions. This tests whether high- and low-AP-1 clones regenerate the parental distribution or stay fixed. Barcode amplicon sequencing is inexpensive (a few thousand dollars), and the division number at which memory decays gives a quantitative half-life of the state.

title: Second-stimulus priming assay
description: Prime cells with a stimulus, allow AP-1 activity to return fully to baseline, then restimulate and compare induction kinetics and amplitude of AP-1 target genes with naive cells. Use a small qPCR or 3'-end RNA-seq panel; faster or larger secondary responses indicate transcriptional memory.

title: Live single-cell imaging of AP-1 reporter dynamics across lineages
description: Use a stable AP-1-responsive fluorescent reporter plus a nuclear marker, image dividing cells for several days on an existing widefield or confocal system, and build lineage trees to quantify mother-daughter and sister-sister correlations in reporter level. Mother-daughter correlation that decays slowly relative to sister correlation would show heritable, cell-intrinsic memory rather than shared microenvironment; the main cost is reporter construction plus imaging time.

title: Prime–rest–rechallenge single-cell imaging with lineage tracking
description: Using cells with endogenously tagged AP-1 subunits (e.g., c-Fos, c-Jun, FosL1) plus a short-lived AP-1-responsive transcriptional reporter, image continuously through a stimulus pulse, a long washout, and a second identical pulse, tracking each lineage. Memory is supported if a cell's second-response amplitude or latency is predicted by its first response beyond what current AP-1 levels explain.

title: Decay versus persistence kinetics after signal withdrawal
description: Measure, in single cells, the time constants of nuclear AP-1 protein, AP-1 reporter output, and a downstream phenotype after acute removal of the stimulus, including with inducible-degron removal of specific AP-1 subunits. A memory mechanism should show reporter and phenotype persistence that substantially outlasts the inducing signal, and this persistence should be lost when AP-1 is degraded during the rest period.

title: Mother–daughter and sister-cell correlation of AP-1 state across divisions
description: Track AP-1 reporter intensity through mitosis in long movies to quantify how strongly daughters inherit the mother's AP-1 level and how long sister-cell correlations decay relative to unrelated cells. Heritable, slowly decaying correlations that exceed the lifetime of the AP-1 proteins themselves argue for a self-propagating memory rather than passive protein dilution.

title: Optogenetic imposition of defined AP-1 histories to test sufficiency
description: Use a light-controlled AP-1 dimer (e.g., photo-dimerizable Fos/Jun or LOV-caged activation domain) to impose precisely timed amplitude, duration and pulse-number histories in single cells while imaging the reporter and a phenotypic marker. If AP-1 stores memory, the retained downstream state should depend on the integrated history (total dose, pulse number) rather than only on the instantaneous light level.

title: Live readout of AP-1 chromatin residence and target-locus accessibility over time
description: Combine single-molecule tracking or FRAP of tagged AP-1 (to measure bound fraction and residence time) with a live chromatin-accessibility or locus-visualization readout (e.g., ANCHOR/ParB-labeled enhancer or nucleosome-sensor reporter) at a key target enhancer before, during, and long after stimulation. A memory role predicts that AP-1-dependent increases in enhancer accessibility and rapid-rebinding behavior persist after signal removal and are lost upon acute AP-1 degradation.

title: Pulse-washout-rechallenge chromatin time course
description: Expose cells to a brief, defined stimulus pulse (e.g., TNF, serum, or a MEK inhibitor), wash it out, and then profile ATAC-seq plus CUT&RUN for Fos/Jun family members at a dense series of timepoints spanning hours to weeks after washout. Memory is supported if a subset of AP-1-bound accessible regions remains open long after AP-1 protein levels and upstream signaling have returned to baseline, and if rechallenge produces a faster or larger response specifically at those retained sites.

title: Live-cell AP-1 reporter lineage tracing through division
description: Use a non-integrating or pre-existing AP-1 activity reporter line and long-term live imaging to track individual cells and their progeny through many divisions. Quantify how reporter intensity correlates between mother and daughter and between sisters as a function of elapsed time. The decay constant of this correlation gives a model-free measurement of how long AP-1 state information persists and whether it survives mitosis, which distinguishes heritable memory from transient signaling.

title: Pharmacological inhibition during establishment versus maintenance
description: Use small-molecule AP-1 inhibitors (e.g. T-5224 or a JNK inhibitor) applied either only during the initial stimulus or only during the post-stimulus memory window, then assay the response to a later re-challenge. If blocking AP-1 during establishment abolishes memory but blocking it afterward does not, AP-1 establishes the memory; if blocking it during the window also erases memory, AP-1 is required continuously to maintain it, which distinguishes an establishing role from a self-sustaining state.

title: Single-cell multiome correlation of AP-1 motif accessibility with response history
description: Perform joint single-cell ATAC and RNA profiling on a population with heterogeneous stimulus histories (created by staggered pulse timing or by sorting cells on an early response reporter). Test whether per-cell AP-1 motif accessibility scores predict each cell's transcriptional response to a subsequent challenge. A strong single-cell predictive relationship, stronger than for other motif families, would indicate that AP-1 chromatin state carries the information about prior stimulation rather than merely correlating with it.

title: Mitotic bookmarking and post-mitotic reestablishment kinetics
description: Synchronize cells pharmacologically (e.g., thymidine block and release, or nocodazole arrest), then measure AP-1 factor retention on mitotic chromosomes by imaging and by CUT&RUN on sorted mitotic and early-G1 cells, tracking how quickly accessibility and transcription are restored at previously induced loci. Retention of a subset of AP-1 on condensed chromatin plus accelerated reactivation of those same loci in G1 would provide a molecular mechanism for how memory crosses cell division.

title: Serial fin amputation to test priming of AP-1 regeneration enhancers in zebrafish
description: Amputate caudal fins, allow complete regeneration and a long rest period, then re-amputate and ask whether previously injured tissue responds faster or more strongly, while profiling ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN (Fosl1a, Junba, H3K27ac, H3K4me1) at AP-1-bound tissue-regeneration enhancer elements at matched timepoints. A memory model predicts residual primed chromatin (retained accessibility or H3K4me1 without H3K27ac) at these enhancers long after the first regenerate is complete, and that fosl1a/junb mutants or enhancer motif deletions eliminate the accelerated second response.

title: Pulse-chase degron separation of AP-1 initiation from maintenance in Drosophila wing discs
description: Use auxin-inducible or GFP-nanobody degrons to deplete Jra/Kayak protein at defined times after genetic ablation of a wing disc, to test whether AP-1 is needed only to establish the damage-responsive state or continuously to maintain it. Use G-TRACE lineage labeling of AP-1-reporter-positive cells to track how long descendants retain the state. Measure the decay of target accessibility and expression after acute AP-1 removal to obtain a half-life for AP-1-independent memory versus AP-1-dependent persistence.

title: Mitotic inheritance of AP-1 occupancy and state in zebrafish melanoma cells
description: In ZMEL1 zebrafish melanoma cells, perform single-molecule tracking of HaloTag-Fosl1a/Junb to measure residence times and mitotic chromosome retention, combined with mitotic CUT&RUN to test for mitotic bookmarking of AP-1 target enhancers. Pair this with clonal barcoding and sister-cell split assays (scRNA-seq of separated daughters) to quantify how many divisions an AP-1-high transcriptional state persists and whether that heritability predicts drug-tolerant behavior.

title: Synthetic AP-1 pulses to map dose and duration requirements for memory formation
description: In Drosophila S2 cells (or zebrafish embryos), deliver calibrated optogenetic or dCas9-recruited AP-1 activation pulses at an endogenous or integrated reporter locus, varying amplitude and duration. Then withdraw the stimulus and measure how long accessibility, histone marks, and expression persist. This sufficiency test defines whether a threshold pulse converts a transient input into a self-sustaining state, and whether memory decays by dilution at division or by time-dependent chromatin reversion, distinguished using cell-cycle arrest.

title: AP-1 and positional memory in axolotl limb regeneration
description: Profile AP-1 motif accessibility and Fos/Jun binding in connective-tissue cells from proximal versus distal limb levels before injury, during the AP-1 injury pulse, and in blastemas, including proximal-to-distal grafts and retinoic-acid proximalization that rewrite positional identity. If AP-1 is a memory mechanism rather than a generic injury response, position-specific chromatin differences should be stored at AP-1-bound elements before injury and be reset by treatments that reprogram positional identity. AP-1 inhibition (dominant-negative A-Fos) should then disrupt memory recall without blocking wound healing.

title: Pulse–chase hysteresis assay of AP-1 activity after signal withdrawal
description: Deliver graded, defined-duration pulses of an AP-1-activating stimulus (TPA, serum/growth factor, or substrate stiffness) and then withdraw it. Sample RNA-seq and a TRE-driven destabilized-fluorophore reporter at 0, 6, 24, 48, 96 h and 1 week to measure the decay timescale of AP-1 target output relative to FOS/JUN protein half-life. Hysteresis is the key memory signature: cells approaching the same final stimulus level from above versus below should settle into different stable AP-1 output states. This is a 6–8 week experiment using a dose×history matrix read out by flow cytometry.

title: Degron separation of establishment versus maintenance
description: Knock dTAG or auxin-inducible degrons into endogenous FOSL1/JUN (or express a dominant-negative A-FOS under a Tet promoter) so AP-1 can be removed either during a priming stimulus or only after the primed state is established, then compare ATAC-seq and RNA-seq outcomes. If late depletion collapses the primed state, AP-1 is the memory carrier; if it leaves the state intact, AP-1 only establishes a state stored elsewhere, e.g., in chromatin or DNA methylation.

title: ATAC-seq and FOS/JUN CUT&RUN time course of latent enhancer priming and re-stimulation
description: Run matched ATAC-seq and FOS/JUN CUT&RUN time courses across stimulus, washout, and re-stimulation. Test whether AP-1 motif-containing peaks opened during the first exposure remain accessible days after AP-1 binding has decayed, and whether those loci show faster or larger induction on a second exposure. Quantify the fraction of primed peaks and the magnitude of the re-stimulation increase, with nascent transcription measured by SLAM-seq or EU-seq, to test a latent-enhancer model of AP-1 memory.

title: Clone-splitting heritability test with barcode lineage tracing
description: Sort cells on an AP-1 activity reporter into high and low bins, let each bin expand for 5–10 divisions, then re-measure the distribution and compute the memory half-life in generations. In parallel, use a lentiviral barcode library so sister cells from the same clone can be split across plates and compared. Strong within-clone concordance of AP-1 state relative to between-clone variance (an intraclass correlation estimate) distinguishes mitotically heritable memory from fast stochastic fluctuation, and can be run in about 10 weeks in a fast-cycling line.

title: Targeted AP-1 recruitment as a sufficiency test
description: Use dCas9 fused to a JUN or FOS activation domain (or a chemically induced dimerization recruitment system) to pulse AP-1 onto a handful of endogenous primed enhancers for 24–48 h, then release and track locus accessibility, target gene expression, and reporter output for two weeks. If a transient synthetic AP-1 pulse alone installs a self-sustaining accessible state at those loci without any upstream signal, that is causal evidence that AP-1 writes, rather than merely reports, cellular memory.

title: Split-clone assay for heritable AP-1 state
description: Lineage-barcode a population, let it expand, then split each clone's descendants into two dishes. Harvest one immediately for scATAC/scRNA (AP-1 motif accessibility, FOS/JUN/FRA-1 levels) and challenge the other with a stimulus and harvest once for recall magnitude. Clone-level correlation between baseline AP-1 state in one dish and recall response in the other would indicate a heritable, cell-intrinsic AP-1 state rather than transient signaling noise.

title: Timed degron cohorts to separate maintenance from readout
description: Use dTAG/auxin-degron FOS, JUN, and FRA-1 lines with a pulse stimulus, then degrade AP-1 in different cohorts during distinct windows (during the pulse, during the stimulus-free interval, or only at re-challenge), with each dish measured exactly once at a fixed endpoint. If degradation only during the stimulus-free interval erases enhanced recall, AP-1 protein is actively maintaining the memory, not merely reading it out.

title: Division-resolved memory via dye dilution at a single endpoint
description: Label cells with CellTrace/CFSE before a priming pulse and, at one harvest, use dye intensity to read out each cell's division history while simultaneously measuring AP-1 target transcripts and AP-1 motif accessibility by flow-sorted scATAC or single-cell imaging. This tests whether the AP-1-associated state survives a quantifiable number of mitoses.

title: Separating latent enhancer accessibility from AP-1 occupancy
description: In a cohort series of primed-and-rested versus naive cells, each profiled once, combine CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN/FRA-1, ATAC footprinting, H3K4me1/H3K27ac, and CpG methylation at the same loci. Memory encoded by persistent AP-1 occupancy predicts footprints without ongoing stimulus, whereas accessible but unoccupied AP-1 motifs would instead implicate transfer to chromatin marks, distinguishing AP-1 as the storage site from AP-1 as the factor that establishes marks.

title: Synthetic locus writing and release with dCas9-tethered JUN
description: Tether a dox-inducible dCas9-JUN (and a DNA-binding-dead AP-1 control) to a naive reporter locus, withdraw dox, and assay independent dishes at a single fixed endpoint for reporter accessibility, expression, and inducibility. Persistence of an acquired permissive state after the tether is gone is a sufficiency test of whether AP-1 binding alone can install a self-maintaining memory at a defined site.

title: Serial-biopsy persistence test across a drug holiday
description: In patients with planned intermittent dosing (e.g., BRAF/MEK or EGFR inhibitor holidays), collect matched pre-treatment, on-treatment, and off-drug biopsies and profile them by single-nucleus ATAC/RNA multiome to test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and AP-1 target expression induced on treatment persist after drug withdrawal. Persistence uncoupled from ongoing MAPK/JNK signaling (measured by phospho-ERK/JNK staining on the same specimens) would indicate memory rather than sustained signaling.

title: Recall kinetics in patient-derived organoids after washout and re-challenge
description: Expose patient-derived organoids to drug or cytokine, wash out and expand for a defined number of divisions, then re-challenge and compare the speed and amplitude of the AP-1-dependent transcriptional response to naive sibling cultures. A faster or larger second response that scales with retained AP-1-primed accessibility distinguishes memory from simple re-induction.

title: Clonal barcoding to test heritability of the AP-1 state through division
description: Lentivirally barcode low-passage patient-derived cells or PDX-derived lines, split each barcoded population into two parallel arms, and test whether AP-1-high clones in one arm predict AP-1-high or resistant fate in the matching arm. Concordance across sibling clones would demonstrate a heritable, clonally transmitted AP-1 state rather than stochastic fluctuation.

title: Relaxation dynamics after sorting on a live AP-1 reporter
description: Introduce a TRE-driven fluorescent reporter (or sort on a validated AP-1 surface-marker proxy) into patient-derived organoids or cell lines, isolate the top and bottom tails by FACS, and track how quickly each fraction re-establishes the parental distribution. Slow, multi-generation relaxation implies a long-lived memory state, whereas rapid re-equilibration implies fast stochastic switching.

title: Degron and CRISPRa tests of AP-1 necessity and sufficiency in patient-derived organoids
description: In patient-derived organoids carrying an auxin-inducible FOS/JUN degron or dCas9-based activation targeted to AP-1-bound enhancers, degrade AP-1 only during the maintenance window after stimulus removal to test whether the stored state is erased, and separately force AP-1 activity in naive cells to test whether it alone installs the primed state. ATAC and CUT&RUN readouts show whether the enhancer landscape is lost, retained, or newly created.

title: Memory decay per division versus per hour
description: Establish the AP-1-dependent state, then compare matched arms with identical elapsed time but different numbers of divisions (CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, serum titration, mitomycin-C arrest). Fit whether memory half-life is better expressed in generations or hours, to distinguish replication-coupled chromatin storage from a slowly decaying protein/RNA reservoir. Also use EdU-based nascent-chromatin capture to measure how quickly AP-1 sites regain accessibility and factor occupancy behind the replication fork.

title: Heterokaryon fusion with allele-resolved readout
description: Fuse a memory-bearing cell to a naive cell of a distinguishable genotype (F1 hybrid or SNP-divergent lines) and read out AP-1 target expression and accessibility allele-specifically in the shared nucleus. Conversion of the naive genome implies a diffusible trans carrier, whereas persistent discordance between the two genomes implies the state is stored in cis in chromatin, a distinction a washout time course cannot make.

title: Mitosis-restricted degron plus mitotic bookmarking measurement
description: Quantify whether AP-1 factors are retained on condensed mitotic chromosomes using single-molecule tracking/FRAP residence times and CUT&RUN on sorted mitotic cells. Then deplete AP-1 only during the mitotic window with a timed degron, so it is present in interphase both before and after division. Failure to transmit the state under this narrow perturbation would localize storage to mitotic bookmarking rather than to steady-state interphase occupancy.

title: Frequency-domain stimulation to estimate the memory time constant
description: Deliver stimulus as square waves across roughly two orders of magnitude of frequency at matched total dose using microfluidics or automated media exchange, and fit the amplitude and phase of AP-1 target output as a transfer function. A memory element would act as a low-pass integrator whose corner frequency sets the retention time, giving a dynamical memory estimate that can be cross-validated against the per-division estimate.

title: Conditional independence test of AP-1 state as a sufficient record of history
description: Using expressed clonal barcodes, measure stimulus history, intermediate AP-1 activity, and later fate within the same lineages. Test whether conditioning on AP-1 state makes past history and future outcome conditionally independent. Residual history-dependence quantifies the fraction of stored information that AP-1 does not carry, testing whether AP-1 state is sufficient to account for memory.

title: Allele-resolved analysis to distinguish cis from trans memory
description: In F1 hybrid or densely heterozygous cells, phase ATAC/CUT&RUN/nascent-RNA reads to the two alleles of the same AP-1 target enhancer after a transient pulse and ask whether the alleles retain or lose the state independently. Persistent trans-acting AP-1 protein predicts tightly correlated alleles within a nucleus, whereas cis-encoded chromatin memory predicts allelic independence and stable monoallelic memorized states.

title: Replication-coupled dilution and re-establishment kinetics
description: Pulse-label nascent chromatin (EdU/BrdU capture or nascent-chromatin ATAC) at defined times after a stimulus to measure how much AP-1 occupancy and accessibility survive passage of the replication fork, how fast they are restored on daughter strands, and whether sister chromatids inherit them symmetrically. Self-propagating memory should show rapid template-directed restoration rather than slow re-equilibration from bulk AP-1 levels.

title: Stimulus order dependence (non-commutativity)
description: Deliver matched pairs of pulses in opposite orders (A then B versus B then A) with identical total dose and spacing, then compare final AP-1 binding, accessibility, and transcriptome. Reproducibly different end states show the system stores more than a single decaying scalar, and counting distinguishable history-to-state mappings estimates memory capacity in bits.

title: Synthetic enhancer library and targeted AP-1 recruitment to test sufficiency of persistence
description: Integrate a barcoded library of synthetic enhancers at a single landing pad that systematically varies AP-1 motif affinity, copy number, spacing, and partner motifs (pioneer factor, NF-kB, TEAD). Separately, deliver a timed pulse of AP-1 recruitment by chemically induced dimerization of a bZIP domain to dCas9 at naive loci. Together these test which sequence configurations convert a transient AP-1 pulse into a persistent state, and whether an AP-1 pulse alone can install memory where none existed.

title: Dimer composition of chromatin-bound AP-1
description: Apply quantitative targeted mass spectrometry of the chromatin-bound AP-1 interactome, plus dimer-specific sequential CUT&RUN and proximity ligation, across the decay phase, and test whether forced expression of individual dimers reproduces the maintained state. The hypothesis is that memory depends not on the amount of bound AP-1 but on a shift to long-lived, slowly exchanging dimers such as FRA1-JUND, which pan-AP-1 occupancy measurements cannot detect.

title: Cis/trans variance decomposition with allele-resolved reporters
description: Place two spectrally distinct but otherwise identical AP-1-driven reporters at the two homologous alleles of one locus, and read endogenous memory loci allele-specifically in F1 hybrid cells using SNPs. Correlated allelic states implicate a diffusible trans carrier (the AP-1 protein pool), while independent allelic memory implicates a cis chromatin mark, a distinction bulk degron or washout experiments cannot make.

title: Replication-coupled restoration kinetics of AP-1 sites
description: Use nascent chromatin capture (ChOR-seq or EdU-pulldown ATAC) to time re-establishment of AP-1 occupancy, accessibility, and H3K27ac behind the replication fork at memory loci versus acutely induced loci. Compare memory decay in time-matched cycling versus replication-arrested (CDK4/6-inhibited or quiescent) cells; erasure that scales per division rather than per hour, with slow locus-selective restoration, would identify replication as the rate-limiting step for AP-1 rewriting.

title: Mitosis-restricted AP-1 degradation to test mitotic bookmarking
description: Fuse AP-1 subunits to a cell-cycle-gated degron (APC/C-dependent, or chemically timed in synchronized cells) so the protein is absent only during mitosis and early G1, then restored. Loss of heritable accessibility with this narrow depletion window, but not with an equal-duration interphase depletion, would show that AP-1 transmits memory by mitotic bookmarking rather than continuous interphase occupancy.

title: Open-loop clamp of AP-1 expression
description: Delete or mutate the AP-1 binding sites in the FOS/JUN promoters and re-supply the subunits from a tunable exogenous promoter titrated to match wild-type mean protein level. Loss of the heritable state despite identical average AP-1 activity would localize memory to the trans autoregulatory feedback loop rather than to the chromatin that AP-1 binds.

title: Single-molecule residence time and fiber co-occupancy at matched AP-1 levels
description: In primed versus naive cells with equal AP-1 protein concentration, measure FOS/JUN residence-time distributions and bound fraction by single-molecule tracking, and measure combinatorial multi-site co-occupancy on individual DNA molecules by methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA). Memory stored as kinetic stabilization or cooperative multi-motif occupancy predicts longer-lived binding and non-independent site occupancy, which bulk ChIP and ATAC averages cannot resolve.

title: Heterokaryon fusion to test cis- versus trans-encoded memory
description: Fuse stimulus-primed cells with naive cells (distinguished by nuclear-localized fluorophores or species-specific reads) and assay, nucleus by nucleus, whether primed AP-1 target expression and accessibility spread to the naive nucleus or stay confined to the primed one. Trans-dominant transfer would implicate a diffusible AP-1 protein/dimer pool as the store, whereas strictly nucleus-autonomous persistence would implicate chromatin-encoded memory at AP-1 sites, a distinction bulk time courses cannot make.

title: Allele-specific memory at heterozygous AP-1 motifs
description: In F1 hybrid cells, or CRISPR-generated heterozygotes in which the TRE/CRE motif is destroyed on one allele only, use allele-resolved ATAC, CUT&RUN, and nascent RNA to test whether primed accessibility and faster re-induction persist only on the motif-bearing allele within the same nucleus. Because both alleles share the same cytoplasm and trans environment, allele discordance would indicate that the memory is encoded in cis at AP-1 elements rather than inherited as a cellular signaling state.

title: Open-loop clamp of AP-1 autoregulation
description: Replace the endogenous AP-1 binding sites in the JUN/FOS/FOSL1 regulatory regions with an orthogonal doxycycline- or rapamycin-controlled input, titrating dose so that the mean and cell-to-cell variance of AP-1 protein match wild type under acute stimulation. If memory is lost in these open-loop cells despite matched acute responses, memory resides in transcriptional positive feedback; if it persists, feedback is dispensable and a chromatin or cofactor mechanism must carry it.

title: AP-1 binding kinetics and single-fiber co-occupancy in primed cells
description: Compare naive cells with cells long after stimulus (primed) by single-molecule tracking of HaloTagged JUN (residence times, bound fraction, search time, cluster/condensate formation) and by single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) that reports actual protein occupancy and combinatorial co-accessibility of linked enhancers on the same DNA fiber. This tests whether memory is stored as altered AP-1 binding kinetics or as coordinated multi-enhancer configurations, rather than as changes in AP-1 abundance or bulk accessibility.

title: Mutual-information analysis with designed stimulus histories
description: Expose single cells to a library of distinguishable stimulus histories (varying order, spacing, amplitude), then jointly measure AP-1 state and downstream phenotype in the same cells. Compute mutual information between history and AP-1 state, between history and phenotype, and the conditional information about history remaining once AP-1 state is known. If AP-1 is the memory channel, the data-processing inequality should hold with little history information bypassing it; substantial residual information identifies a parallel, non-AP-1 memory store and bounds how much of the memory AP-1 can explain.

title: Cis versus trans memory using two identical reporters
description: Integrate two spectrally distinct but sequence-identical AP-1-responsive reporters at different genomic loci in the same cell and track both after a stimulus pulse. Locus-autonomous chromatin memory predicts that the two reporters decorrelate and decay independently, while cell-wide protein/feedback memory predicts that they remain tightly correlated. This separates the two mechanistic classes with one measurement.

title: Decay per unit time versus per cell division
description: Compare decay of the stimulus-induced state in cell-cycle-arrested versus cycling cells (CDK4/6 inhibition, serum starvation, contact inhibition) over matched elapsed time, and use EdU- or sister-chromatid-resolved readouts to test whether loss occurs specifically at replication. Template-copied chromatin memory should decay per division, whereas protein-level or metabolic memory should decay with time.

title: Binding kinetics and dimer composition of the memory state
description: Use single-molecule tracking of HaloTagged JUN/FOS in live nuclei together with two-color single-molecule pull-down or FRET to compare post-stimulus and naive cells in residence time, bound fraction, and dimer identity (e.g., long-lived FRA1-JUND replacing transient FOS-JUN) at matched total activity. This tests whether memory is stored in binding kinetics and partner choice rather than in AP-1 abundance.

title: Surrogate bZIP domain swap
description: In an AP-1-null or degron-depleted background, re-express a chimera of the AP-1 bZIP DNA-binding domain fused to a minimal heterologous activation domain, so the same motifs are bound and activated by a protein lacking AP-1's native cofactor and pioneer interactions. If the surrogate restores acute induction but not persistence, memory depends on AP-1 protein surfaces rather than motif occupancy alone.

title: DNA-based molecular recorder of AP-1 activity history
description: Drive a prime-editing or recombinase-based recorder (e.g., ENGRAM or DNA Typewriter) from an AP-1-responsive promoter so each cell accumulates an ordered, cumulative record of its past AP-1 activity. Read the record and the current transcriptome from the same single cell. This separates integrated past AP-1 dose from present state without sorting or fixing cells at an arbitrarily chosen early timepoint.

title: Hysteresis mapping to distinguish bistability from slow relaxation
description: Titrate a tunable AP-1 input (e.g., degron-stabilized FOS/JUN or a graded cytokine dose) up and then back down the same concentration series, reading a single-cell AP-1 target reporter at steady state at each step and comparing the up and down branches. A true memory element should show a hysteresis loop with two stable states at the same input level, which a slowly decaying state cannot produce, and the loop should collapse if AP-1 self-reinforcement is broken with a TRE-motif decoy or a feedback-deficient promoter allele.

title: Separating elapsed time from cell-division number
description: Hold cells at matched post-stimulus times in cycling versus arrested conditions (CDK4/6 inhibitor, contact inhibition, reversible serum withdrawal) and compare decay of AP-1 target accessibility and expression per unit time versus per division, then release arrest to test whether decay resumes on the division schedule. Combine with EdU-pulse sorting and nascent-chromatin readout to measure how accessibility at AP-1 sites is re-established behind the replication fork, determining whether memory is diluted by replication, refreshed by replication, or independent of S phase, which constrains which class of mechanism is possible.

title: Dimer identity as the storage variable
description: Test whether memory is carried by which AP-1 family member occupies a site rather than by AP-1 occupancy itself. Use ChIP-reChIP or proximity ligation to track the shift from labile FOS/JUN to long-lived FRA1/FOSB/JUNB at the same motifs over time, and pulse-SILAC to measure half-lives of proteins resident at persistent sites. Then swap degrons between family members (chimeras with identical DNA-binding domains but exchanged stability determinants) to test whether protein lifetime alone, rather than chromatin, sets the duration of the state.

title: Synthetic AP-1 element library to define design rules for memory-competent sites
description: Integrate a combinatorial library of synthetic AP-1 elements at a single genomic landing pad, varying motif number, affinity, spacing/helical phasing, flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence, and co-occurring partner motifs, each linked to a reporter. Pulse the cells and sequence or sort to identify which configurations retain the on-state after the stimulus is gone. This yields a quantitative rule for which AP-1 site features support memory and predicts which endogenous sites should be memory-competent.

title: Information content of the AP-1 state about past stimuli
description: Stimulate cells with a panel of distinct AP-1-activating inputs at several doses and durations, then at later time points measure single-cell AP-1 target states and compute the mutual information between past stimulus identity/dose and present state. This tests whether AP-1 stores high-capacity information that preserves stimulus identity or only a single binary state, and tracking how capacity decays over time separates loss of amplitude from loss of specificity.

title: Heterokaryon cis/trans test of memory storage
description: Fuse a primed cell with a naive cell of distinguishable genotype (SNP- or species-distinct) and measure allele-specific transcription and accessibility in the shared cytoplasm. Retention of each genome's own state implicates storage in cis chromatin, whereas conversion of the naive genome implicates diffusible AP-1 protein or autoregulatory feedback.

title: Hysteresis and bistability mapping of the AP-1 input-output curve
description: Titrate an AP-1-activating input upward from zero and downward from saturation, measuring steady-state single-cell output at each dose with a quantitative reporter. A memory system should show a hysteresis loop, bimodal populations within the loop, and measurable spontaneous switching rates, which slow passive decay would not produce.

title: Single-molecule footprinting of primed enhancers
description: Apply dual-enzyme methyltransferase single-molecule footprinting with long reads at candidate memory enhancers to determine whether priming increases the fraction of cells with an open element or alters per-molecule occupancy. Correlations in co-occupancy among multiple AP-1 sites on the same molecule reveal cis-coordination not visible by population ATAC-seq.

title: AP-1 dimer composition as the stored variable
description: Track dimer identity at primed loci over the memory window using sequential/co-IP CUT&RUN and crosslinked-dimer mass spectrometry, testing whether short-lived FOS is replaced by long-lived FRA1/FRA2/JUND. Isoform-specific degrons applied only during the maintenance phase test whether the long-lived subunit, rather than chromatin, carries the memory.

title: Decoding stimulus history and measuring memory capacity
description: Deliver combinatorial stimulus histories that differ in identity, order, and spacing, then quantify how much of the history can be decoded from current chromatin and transcriptome, and whether decoding fails when AP-1 motifs are disrupted. Run matched arms in proliferating versus arrested cells to separate replication-driven dilution from time-dependent decay.

title: Fusion of primed and naive cells
description: Fuse differentially labeled primed and naive cells (PEG or virus-mediated heterokaryons scored by imaging, or cells with distinguishable SNP/barcode genomes read out by allele-specific ATAC/RNA) and ask whether each nucleus keeps its own AP-1 accessibility and response state in a shared cytoplasm. Nucleus-autonomous persistence indicates a chromatin-encoded record, whereas rapid equalization of both nuclei indicates a diffusible or autoregulatory AP-1 network state.

title: Division-based versus time-based memory decay
description: Hold primed cells in conditions that separate time from proliferation: cycling versus arrested (CDK4/6 inhibition, contact inhibition, or serum deprivation) and fast versus slow cycling (thymidine or low-dose aphidicolin). Fit the decay of AP-1 motif accessibility and restimulation advantage to a per-division model versus a per-hour model. Additionally, use nascent-chromatin ATAC (repli-ATAC or early/late BrdU-sorted fractions) to measure how quickly AP-1 footprints are rebuilt behind the replication fork. Replication-coupled dilution versus continuous turnover implies different molecular carriers and different predictions about heritability.

title: Hysteresis mapping of AP-1 dose versus enhancer state
description: Using a tunable AP-1 input (doxycycline-titratable JUN/FOS, or graded degron depletion), raise AP-1 dose stepwise and then lower it along the same steps, measuring accessibility and target output at each matched dose. Memory predicts hysteresis, where the same AP-1 concentration gives different chromatin/transcriptional states depending on history, and loop width quantifies memory strength. A perfectly retraced curve indicates AP-1 is a graded relay without memory.

title: Single-molecule fiber footprinting of AP-1 motif occupancy
description: Apply long-read single-molecule chromatin footprinting (Fiber-seq, SAMOSA or nanoNOMe) to primed and naive cells so that occupancy of many AP-1 motifs across an enhancer cluster is read on the same DNA molecule. This distinguishes an all-or-none heritable state (molecules fully primed or fully naive, with correlated multi-site occupancy) from a graded probabilistic shift, and reveals whether memory requires cooperative engagement of several motifs or a single site.

title: Measuring how much stimulus history the AP-1 state stores
description: Deliver a graded series of first-stimulus doses and distinct stimulus identities. At single-cell resolution, compute the mutual information between prior exposure and the later AP-1 reporter or response distribution, repeating at several delays to obtain a decay curve in bits. This measures memory capacity and tests whether cells record only that a stimulus occurred or also its amount and identity. AP-1 perturbation is expected to reduce capacity toward zero bits.

title: Lineage-barcoded decay curves for AP-1 chromatin states
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes plus joint single-cell ATAC and RNA profiling to measure how similar related cells remain at AP-1 motif-containing enhancers across 1 to 10+ divisions, yielding a memory half-life in generations. Compare that half-life against non-AP-1 enhancers and against cells where AP-1 factors are acutely degraded, to determine whether AP-1 sets the timescale or merely marks it.

title: Separating memory establishment from maintenance with timed degron depletion
description: Tag FOS, JUN, and FOSL1 with auxin or dTAG degrons and deplete them either during a stimulus (blocking establishment) or days afterward (testing maintenance), then re-challenge the cells and measure the magnitude of the primed response. If memory survives late depletion, AP-1 establishes memory that is maintained by another substrate; if memory is lost, AP-1 itself is the stored state.

title: Synthetic AP-1 tethering to endogenous enhancers
description: Use dCas9 or a chemically inducible recruitment system to deposit AP-1 family members at defined endogenous enhancers for a controlled duration, release them, and then test whether the locus reactivates faster and more strongly upon a later real stimulus. This tests sufficiency, and dose and duration titration maps the minimum AP-1 exposure needed to install a persistent state.

title: Replication-coupled tracking of AP-1 site reassembly
description: Combine nascent-chromatin capture (such as labeling newly replicated DNA and profiling the proteins and accessibility on it) with live imaging of tagged AP-1 factors to measure how quickly AP-1 reoccupies its sites behind the replication fork. Memory that survives mitosis should show rapid, site-specific reassembly with preserved relative occupancy, and the recovery kinetics distinguish bookmarking from de novo re-establishment driven by upstream signaling.

title: Predictive modeling of response from AP-1 state after prior exposure
description: Expose isogenic cells to combinations of stimuli separated by defined intervals and fit a model in which the AP-1 state measured after the first exposure predicts the quantitative response to the second, at single-cell resolution. A genuine memory mechanism should make AP-1 state a better predictor of future behavior than current signaling activity or overall cell state, and the model's failures identify additional components that memory requires.

title: Timed degron removal of AP-1 after priming
description: Tag endogenous FOS, FOSL1, and JUN family members with dTAG or auxin degrons and deplete them at defined intervals after a priming stimulus, then re-challenge the cells. Compare loss of the response when AP-1 is removed during priming versus long afterward to separate an establishment role from a continuous maintenance requirement.

title: Lineage-barcoded measurement of memory half-life
description: Combine clonal barcoding with sister-cell transcriptomics and ATAC profiling to quantify how many divisions AP-1 target programs and AP-1-bound accessible sites stay correlated within a clone. Repeat in AP-1-inhibited cells (A-FOS or compound inhibition) to obtain a measured decay timescale for the memory.

title: Hysteresis mapping with live AP-1 reporters
description: Image endogenous AP-1 activity together with upstream kinase reporters while slowly ramping a stimulus up and then back down over days. A memory mechanism should show a gap between the rising and falling dose-response curves, and the width of that gap gives a quantitative measure to compare across cell types and stimuli.

title: Synthetic AP-1 tethering as a sufficiency test
description: Use inducible dCas9 or optogenetic recruitment to place AP-1 subunits at defined loci for a brief window, then release them and track accessibility, histone marks, and re-inducibility for weeks. This tests whether AP-1 occupancy alone, without upstream signaling, is sufficient to write a persistent state.

title: Mitotic retention of AP-1 sites and daughter-cell inheritance
description: Profile AP-1 binding and chromatin accessibility in synchronized mitotic cells and in freshly divided daughter pairs to see whether AP-1-marked sites are retained through chromosome condensation. Pair this with live imaging of reporter reactivation timing in daughters to test whether physical inheritance, rather than re-establishment from signaling, carries the memory.

title: Pulse-chase AP-1 degron timing experiment
description: Fuse FOS/JUN family members to auxin- or dTAG-degrons, deliver a defined stimulus pulse, then degrade AP-1 at staggered delays and measure how long the degradation window must be to erase the altered response to a second stimulus days later. This separates AP-1 as a transient signal transducer from AP-1 as the physical carrier of the memory.

title: Lineage-resolved memory tracing with heritable barcodes
description: Combine expressed clonal barcodes with longitudinal single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC across a stimulus, rest, and restimulus protocol. Test whether sibling cells share AP-1 site accessibility and reactivation behavior more than expected by chance. Memory is quantified directly as the heritability of the AP-1 regulatory state through cell divisions.

title: Mitotic bookmarking of AP-1 target enhancers
description: Use live imaging of tagged FOS/JUN plus CUT&RUN at synchronized cell-cycle stages to ask whether AP-1 remains bound to its target enhancers on mitotic chromatin. Use separation-of-function mutants that lose mitotic retention but keep interphase binding to test whether bookmarking transmits memory across division.

title: Synthetic AP-1 circuits to test sufficiency
description: Build a minimal synthetic locus with tunable numbers and affinities of TRE/AP-1 motifs together with inducible synthetic AP-1 factors, and map the parameter regime in which a transient input produces a self-sustaining chromatin state. This tests sufficiency, rather than only necessity, for bistable cellular memory.

title: Joint single-molecule and single-cell measurement of the feedback loop
description: In the same cells, measure AP-1 protein abundance, chromatin residence time by single-molecule tracking, target enhancer accessibility, and transcriptional bursting before, during, and after stimulus. Fit dynamical models to these data to test whether AP-1 autoregulatory feedback is strong enough to sustain memory or whether a slower chromatin/DNA-methylation layer is required.

title: Lineage-resolved decay rates of AP-1 chromatin state versus transcription
description: Use clonal barcoding with paired single-cell ATAC and RNA readouts to track sister cells for many divisions after a transient stimulus, measuring separately how fast AP-1 motif accessibility and AP-1 target transcription return to baseline. Memory is demonstrated if accessibility half-lives substantially exceed those of both AP-1 protein levels and target mRNA.

title: Degron depletion of AP-1 to test whether it maintains its own chromatin footprint
description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN family members with inducible degrons and deplete them at defined times after stimulation. Assay whether previously opened AP-1 sites stay open and whether the cell still responds faster to a second stimulus, to distinguish a self-sustaining chromatin state from one requiring continuous AP-1 occupancy.

title: Re-stimulation dose-response mapping of the primed state
description: Quantify at single-cell resolution the stimulus dose and latency needed to re-trigger a response in previously stimulated versus naive cells across a long range of rest intervals. Memory predicts a lower response threshold and shorter latency that decay with a characteristic timescale, giving an operational, quantitative definition of memory rather than a correlative one.

title: Mitotic bookmarking and inheritance fidelity across the cell cycle
description: Combine live imaging of tagged AP-1 with cell-cycle sensors and post-mitotic chromatin profiling of daughter pairs to ask whether AP-1 sites are re-established after mitosis, and whether the two daughters inherit matched or divergent states. Measuring inheritance fidelity per division expresses memory as a per-generation transmission probability.

title: Synthetic AP-1 site insertion to test sufficiency at a naive locus
description: Insert defined arrays of AP-1 motifs, with varied spacing and partner motifs, at neutral genomic locations alongside a reporter. Then stimulate and measure whether the site autonomously acquires and retains accessibility and shows a faster second response. This is a sufficiency experiment with tunable sequence grammar.

title: Memory decay per cell division versus per unit time
description: Deliver a defined pulse of AP-1 activity (optogenetic FOS/JUN dimerization or a degron-stabilized bZIP), then measure the decay of primed enhancer accessibility and of the amplified secondary response while independently varying proliferation rate (contact inhibition, serum, CDK4/6 inhibitors, or cell-cycle-arrested cells). Memory that dilutes with cell divisions implicates a chromatin-based carrier, whereas decay that tracks elapsed time regardless of division implicates protein/RNA half-life; the two models should be quantitatively distinguishable from the decay curves alone.

title: Sister-cell splitting and clonal barcoding to measure heritability of AP-1 state
description: Combine a live AP-1 transcriptional reporter with lineage barcoding, then physically split sister cells or clonal subpopulations, challenging one half while profiling the other. Quantify how much of a cell's future stimulus response is predicted by its mother's prior AP-1 state versus the population average, as mother-daughter and sister-sister correlation across generations, and compare this with DNA methylation or H3K27me3 as alternative carriers.

title: Single-enhancer AP-1 tethering and release to test sufficiency
description: Recruit the FOS/JUN bZIP or transactivation domain to one chosen naive enhancer with dCas9, then wash out or degrade the tether and measure whether that element remains accessible, nucleosome-depleted, and hyper-responsive to later stimulation, relative to unmanipulated alleles in the same nucleus. Allele-specific readouts (targeting one haplotype) provide an internally controlled test of whether transient AP-1 occupancy is sufficient to establish a persistent local state.

title: Mitotic bookmarking and daughter-cell inheritance of AP-1 sites
description: Use live single-molecule imaging of FOS/JUN residence times through mitosis, plus mitotic CUT&RUN/ATAC and daughter-cell-resolved accessibility profiling, to determine whether AP-1 retains, rapidly re-occupies, or entirely loses its binding sites across division. The key measurement is the timing of re-establishment in early G1 relative to global chromatin reopening: bookmarking predicts that AP-1 sites reopen first and in a parent-matched, allele-correlated pattern.

title: Acute post-priming AP-1 degradation and restoration
description: Use an auxin/dTAG degron to remove AP-1 subunits only after a primed state is established, separating the encoding window from the maintenance window. Test whether the potentiated response survives the AP-1-free interval and returns when AP-1 is restored. Persistence without AP-1 would indicate the memory is stored elsewhere (nucleosome positioning, histone marks, or a cofactor) and AP-1 acts as writer and reader rather than the storage medium.

title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming to separate memory writing from maintenance
description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN family members with degron systems and deplete them only after a priming stimulus has ended, then re-stimulate. If primed accessibility and faster re-induction persist without AP-1 during the interval, AP-1 establishes the memory but does not store it.

title: Lineage-barcoded clonal tracking of AP-1 state heritability
description: Combine clonal barcoding with paired single-cell ATAC and RNA readouts to quantify how strongly AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression are shared among sibling cells across many divisions. The decay of within-clone similarity over generations gives a half-life for the putative memory.

title: Mitotic bookmarking imaging of AP-1 through division
description: Live-image endogenously tagged AP-1 subunits with single-molecule residence-time measurement through mitosis, paired with ATAC on mitotic chromosomes. Determine whether a subset of sites retains bound factor or open chromatin through chromosome condensation, which is the physical requirement for passing the state to daughter cells.

title: Motif-level editing at primed AP-1 sites
description: Use targeted editing or CRISPRi tiling to disrupt individual AP-1 motifs within primed enhancers without altering the factor itself, then measure the response to a second stimulus. This distinguishes site-specific memory elements from a global AP-1 dosage effect.
