description: Measure a continuous candidate marker (e.g., drug-efflux pump level, mitochondrial membrane potential, or a fluorescent stress reporter) in each cell before dosing and link it to fate by live imaging. Compare the marker distribution to the observed survival curve to test whether survival follows a threshold on this marker.

title: Barcoded replicate-population fluctuation analysis
description: Use a lineage-barcoded clonal library split into many small replicate cultures, then apply the drug and count surviving barcodes in each replicate. Variation in survivor counts across replicates, compared with Luria-Delbrück-type fluctuation models, distinguishes pre-existing survivors from those induced by drug exposure, and shows whether survivors come from a few clones with rare pre-existing tolerance.

title: Dominant-response baseline with analysis of deviant survivors
description: Using paired single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq before and after drug exposure, first define the dominant response shared by most dying cells. Then isolate the survivors whose profiles deviate from that response and reconstruct their pre-treatment state, testing whether the deviation was already present before drug exposure.

title: Frequency-stratified test of survival-linked genomic features
description: Measure whether survivors are enriched for high-expression, high-copy-number, or heterochromatin-locked loci, using expression- or frequency-matched gene sets as controls. A pooled CRISPR screen with guide abundance tracked across treatment can show whether these features predict survival beyond chance.

title: Barcoded lineage phylogenetics to separate heritable from stochastic tolerance
description: Label founder cells with heritable lentiviral barcodes, reconstruct clonal trees from the sequenced barcodes, and fit Bayesian phylogenetic models to ask whether drug survival is clustered within clades (heritable, cell-intrinsic) or scattered across the tree (stochastic).

title: Fitting persister emergence over repeated drug pulses
description: Track the fraction of surviving cells across repeated drug pulses and fit S-curve or spread models. Adding spatial imaging in 3D culture tests whether tolerant states propagate between neighboring cells or arise independently in each cell.

title: Cross-cell-line comparison of survival signatures
description: Compare survival gene programs across several cancer cell lines or patient-derived models. Phylogenetic-style analysis identifies conserved, lineage-independent survival mechanisms versus lineage-specific ones, which can be checked by reprogramming a candidate gene in a naive line.

title: Lineage-barcoded live-cell tracking with retrospective analysis of survivors
description: Track genetically identical cells by live time-lapse microscopy with lineage barcodes from before drug exposure through death or survival. Then trace each survivor's history backward to find the pre-treatment state, timing, or cell-cycle phase that distinguished it.

title: Systematic enumeration of perturbation orderings
description: Systematically enumerate combinations and orderings of sub-threshold perturbations (drug dose timing relative to cell-cycle phase, short pre-treatments with signaling or stress modulators, staged knockdowns) and measure survival for each schedule. This identifies which specific sequence of cell-state conditions produces the survival phenotype.

title: Perturbations of known magnitude and timing
description: Apply perturbations of known magnitude and timing, such as drug pulses, serum or heat shocks, or forced cell-cycle synchronization, and measure how the survival fraction changes with each. Plotting survival rate against perturbation intensity distinguishes a perturbation-sensitive, timing-dependent mechanism from a stochastic baseline that is insensitive to perturbation.

title: Replicate variance decomposition across clones
description: Derive many single-cell-founded clones from one parental line, treat each under identical conditions across many replicate wells, and measure the survival fraction per clone and per well. Comparing between-clone variance to the binomial variance expected from within-clone sampling tests whether heritable hidden state (epigenetic memory) exists, as opposed to purely intrinsic randomness.

title: Minimal feature-set identification of pre-treatment states predicting survival
description: Profile pre-treatment cells by single-cell multiomics or reporter levels (e.g., chromatin accessibility, signaling reporters, stress markers). Then sort and reconstitute subpopulations to test which minimal set of features reproduces survival, progressively narrowing the features. Confirming the minimal set by sorting and re-treating cells provides a causal test of the predictive state.

title: Time-to-death survival model on pre-treatment single-cell states
description: Track individual cells by live-cell imaging and fit a Cox proportional hazards survival model in which time-to-death under drug is the outcome and pre-treatment measurements (reporter levels for drug efflux, NRF2 or antioxidant state, cell-cycle phase, mitochondrial membrane potential) are the covariates. This tests which pre-treatment states predict survival, rather than only comparing endpoint survivors and non-survivors.

title: Pulsed or interrupted dosing schedules as timing-based exposure variation
description: Compare cell fates across drug schedules that create variation in exposure timing, such as drug holidays, pulses of different lengths, or staggered starts across otherwise identical wells. Because exposure differs only through timing, this tests whether survival depends on the state the cell was in when the drug was applied.

title: Null simulation of survival from stochastic heterogeneity alone
description: Build an agent-based model in which identical cells have random, transient fluctuations in drug target levels or uptake, and simulate the expected survival fraction. Compare the simulated fraction and its variance with the observed persister fraction to show whether chance alone explains the survivors or whether a specific heritable or regulated state is needed.

title: Lineage-linked survival and inheritance tests
description: Use lineage barcoding or lineage tracing to link surviving cells to their progenitors, then test whether survival clusters within lineages more than expected by chance. Heritable clustering would point to a stable cell state passed on at division, while no clustering would support transient, stochastic switching.

title: Re-challenge of sorted survivors after drug removal
description: Isolate survivors after drug removal, let them regrow, and re-challenge them with the same drug to compare their survival rate with that of the parental population. This distinguishes a stable adaptive state from a transient, reversible one and measures how long the survival advantage persists.

title: Per-subpopulation drug dose–response survival curves
description: Treat clonal populations across a graded series of drug doses and exposure times, and fit a survival-probability curve for each. Compare curve shapes and thresholds between subpopulations to determine whether survival reflects a shifted threshold or a fixed fraction of tolerant cells.

title: Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis over cell-intrinsic parameters
description: Build a stochastic model of the drug response with parameters for target expression, efflux pump activity, cell-cycle phase, and signalling noise, and sample these parameters across their variation. Use variance decomposition (e.g., Sobol indices) to find which parameter spread best reproduces the observed survivor fraction.

title: Pre-treatment profiling of survivors versus dead cells
description: Before treatment, record each cell's state with live reporters (e.g., FUCCI for cell cycle, fluorescent drug-efflux or stress reporters) and single-cell transcriptomics or chromatin accessibility. After treatment, sort survivors and dead cells and compare their pre-treatment profiles to find the features associated with survival.

title: Lineage-barcoded fate tracking
description: Label founder cells with heritable DNA barcodes and follow each clone through drug exposure and drug withdrawal to measure whether survival is pre-determined, stochastically acquired, or inherited. Correlation of survival outcomes within clones distinguishes heritable tolerance from random per-cell escape.

title: Survivor fraction across many environmental and treatment conditions
description: Expose the same clone to a battery of conditions such as seeding density, serum level, hypoxia, and drug combinations or sequences. Map how the survivor fraction shifts across conditions to identify the environmental and temporal factors that most strongly govern survival.

title: Per-cell persistence kinetics under continuous dosing
description: Track each cell's time to death or exit from drug tolerance under continuous dosing with live-cell reporters. Fit per-cell survival-time distributions to separate a component reflecting the typical time a cell persists before dying from a component reflecting cell-to-cell variability in response timing. This reveals whether survivors are in a stable resistant state or a transiently tolerant one.

title: Randomized drug-schedule benchmarking
description: Apply random sequences of drug pulses and holidays to clonal and mixed populations, then fit the per-cell survival decay as a function of sequence length to extract a per-exposure failure rate that is independent of dosing-timing artifacts. Comparing this rate across subclones distinguishes intrinsic per-cell tolerance from effects of when and how long the drug was given.

title: Calibrated single-cell drug concentration and target occupancy
description: Measure each cell's intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy (e.g., with a fluorescent or click-tagged drug analog plus spike-in controls), then reconstruct the per-cell response function. This separates survivors that received less effective drug (delivery or pharmacokinetic differences) from survivors that received the full dose but still tolerated it (intrinsic resistance).

title: Neighbour-perturbation mapping of survival dependence
description: Selectively ablate, stimulate, or pattern killing of defined neighbouring cells (for example with optogenetic or laser-based perturbation) and measure whether a cell's survival changes with its neighbours' state. Spatial transcriptomics of survivor versus dying neighbourhoods can then identify paracrine or contact-dependent protective signals.

title: Pre-treatment baseline features linked to post-treatment fate
description: Measure pre-treatment per-cell features (copy-number profile, chromatin accessibility, efflux-pump and mitochondrial levels, cell-cycle phase, lineage barcode). Link them to each cell's survival using photoconvertible or barcode-based retrospective sequencing of the same cells. Statistical models then test which baseline variables, or combinations, predict survival, including whether two features interact.

title: Four-point susceptibility analysis of drug survival events
description: Use time-lapse imaging of a live-cell death reporter (e.g., caspase or SYTOX sensor) under drug and compute a four-point susceptibility (χ4) fluctuation measure of survival to find the spatial extent and temporal lifetime of survivor clusters. A χ4 peak with a correlation length beyond nearest neighbors would show that tolerance is cooperative rather than independent in each cell.

title: Classifier prediction of survival from pre-treatment single-cell state
description: Before drug exposure, record each cell's morphology, cell-cycle reporter (e.g., FUCCI), signaling activity (e.g., ERK or AKT biosensors), and mitochondrial state. Then train a classifier to predict which cells survive and which die. High predictive accuracy would indicate a pre-existing state signature, while chance-level performance would indicate stochastic, non-heritable tolerance.

title: Null-model tests against spatial and lineage structure
description: Compare the observed survivor pattern to null models that shuffle cell positions, reassign fates randomly within lineages, or use independent Bernoulli survival, to determine whether survival follows local structure or chance. Agent-based simulations of the same model can then test which mechanism reproduces the measured clustering.

title: Barcode-based lineage tracing of tolerant-state inheritance
description: Label founder cells with heritable DNA barcodes and track them through drug exposure and recovery to determine whether the survival state is passed to daughter cells and how long it persists across generations. Fitting the decay of the survivor-lineage correlation over time gives a characteristic lifetime for the tolerant state.

title: Washout and re-challenge to measure tolerance relaxation time
description: Remove the drug after a defined exposure, then re-challenge at intervals and measure how quickly the surviving fraction reverts toward the naive baseline. Plotting the relaxation time against drug dose and cell density would reveal whether tolerance is a long-lived, self-sustaining state or a transient one.

title: Live-cell single-cell fate tracking with fluorescent activity reporters
description: Track thousands of individual cells under drug with a live reporter of caspase-3/7 activity, ERK-KTR signaling, or mitochondrial membrane potential, recording each cell's trajectory over days. Sort the cells that stay active or survive and compare their pre-treatment reporter levels to those of cells that die.

title: Same-cell multiplexed profiling before and during treatment
description: Use imaging mass cytometry, multiplexed immunofluorescence, or cyclic imaging to measure phospho-proteins, drug-target occupancy, and efflux-pump levels in the same cells at several time points during treatment. This shows whether survival is linked to a specific signaling state that changes over time, rather than to a fixed trait.

title: Pre-treatment feature mapping linked to later survival
description: Record baseline single-cell features (cell size, cell-cycle phase, organelle content, chromatin marks) by imaging, then follow the same cells through treatment and use correlative imaging to identify which pre-existing features predict survival. Survivors are then checked for the presence or absence of those features.

title: Comparing the population distribution of a baseline variable with that of survivors
description: Measure a candidate intrinsic variable (drug-target expression, efflux transporter levels, DNA content, or cell size) across the whole population by flow cytometry or single-cell RNA-seq, then compare its distribution with the distribution among survivors. Enrichment in a narrow tail points to a causal marker, while no enrichment points to a stochastic or state-based explanation.

title: Pulse-chase drug exposure with lineage barcoding
description: Pulse the drug for a short period and then withdraw it, combined with heritable DNA barcodes, to see whether surviving cells are a pre-existing subpopulation or a transiently induced state. Track whether survivors regrow sensitive progeny after drug removal and whether the barcode lineages of survivors are the same as those of the untreated population.

title: Single-cell intracellular drug-level mapping
description: Quantify effective intracellular drug concentration per cell using fluorescent drug analogs or imaging mass spectrometry, and sort cells by drug level. This tests whether survivors accumulate less drug through reduced uptake, increased efflux, or lysosomal sequestration. Live-imaging survival tracking would show whether drug-low cells are the ones that persist.

title: Sorting by mitochondrial state and heteroplasmy before treatment
description: Before drug exposure, sort cells by mitochondrial membrane potential and by mtDNA heteroplasmy (e.g., single-cell mtDNA sequencing of sorted subpopulations), then re-challenge each fraction with the drug. A significant survival difference would indicate that pre-existing mitochondrial variation determines tolerance independently of nuclear gene expression.

title: Per-cell protein turnover profiling
description: Use pulse-chase labeling (e.g., click-chemistry amino acid analogs) combined with flow sorting to measure the synthesis and degradation rates of the drug target and key survival proteins in individual cells. Comparing turnover between survivors and dying cells would test whether proteostasis or translational capacity, rather than target levels, underlies tolerance.

title: Density-dependent and secreted-factor dependence of survival
description: Plate the population across a range of seeding densities and measure the survival fraction under drug, then test survivors' dependence on neighbors using conditioned medium, transwell co-culture, and sparse-plating controls. A density-dependent survival fraction would indicate a community-level, paracrine protection mechanism rather than an intrinsic single-cell property.

title: Asymmetric partitioning of tolerance factors at mitosis
description: Use live imaging with fluorescently tagged drug target or efflux proteins to track how these proteins partition between daughter cells at division, and correlate the inherited amount with each daughter's fate under drug. If unequal inheritance predicts survival, tolerance may arise through stochastic division asymmetry rather than a fixed pre-existing state.

title: Pre-treatment apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
description: Measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming in each cell before drug exposure (BH3 profiling by flow cytometry, with cytochrome c release after BH3 peptides), then sort high- and low-priming subpopulations and compare their survival under the drug. If priming predicts survival, test whether BH3 mimetics that push low-priming cells toward death eliminate the survivors.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation linked to target occupancy
description: Use a fluorescent or clickable analog of the drug, or a target-engagement biosensor, to measure intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy in individual live cells by imaging. Correlating these values with each cell's later fate separates pharmacokinetic causes (less drug inside) from pharmacodynamic causes (target still active despite drug).

title: Death-hazard kinetics from single-cell fate tracking
description: Track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy with a caspase or apoptosis reporter and record each cell's time to death, arrest, or escape. Fitting survival models to these distributions distinguishes permanent arrest from slow, stochastic killing and shows whether survivors are a fixed subpopulation or reflect cell-to-cell differences in death rate.

title: Chromosomal instability reporter sorting with clonal re-derivation
description: Before treatment, sort cells by a reporter of chromosome missegregation or micronucleus formation. Expand the sorted groups and test drug survival and karyotype (copy-number profiling) in each derived clone. This tests whether pre-existing aneuploidy or chromosomal instability drives tolerance, which bulk and transcriptome-based approaches cannot answer directly.

title: Neighbor-density and local contact perturbation
description: Measure each cell's local density and number of contacts in live imaging before treatment, then experimentally remove neighbors (laser ablation or mixing with dead cells) or add conditioned medium to test whether survival depends on local crowding or cell-cell contact rather than cell-intrinsic state.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification and sorting
description: Measure how much drug each cell accumulates, using a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging, then sort low- and high-accumulating cells and test whether low uptake or lysosomal sequestration alone predicts survival. This separates pharmacokinetic heterogeneity from changes in cell state.

title: Lineage-tracked proteostasis inheritance
description: Use photoconvertible or tandem aggregation reporters with time-lapse mother-daughter tracking to test whether survivors inherit lower protein-aggregate or misfolded-protein burden through division. Asymmetric segregation of damaged proteins would produce survival without any stable genetic or transcriptional difference.

title: Paracrine rescue by survivor-secreted factors
description: Fractionate conditioned medium from survivor cultures, identify candidate secreted proteins or metabolites by mass spectrometry, and test whether they rescue drug-sensitive cells in co-culture. This tests whether a few survivors protect neighboring cells, which a per-cell readout would miss.

title: Pre-treatment ERK/AKT signaling dynamics with optogenetic causality test
description: Track ERK and AKT activity pulses in single living cells with FRET biosensors before drug addition, and test whether pulse frequency or amplitude predicts later survival. Then use optogenetic control of the pulses to test whether the dynamics cause the survival difference.

title: Nascent translation rate as a pre-treatment predictor of survival
description: Quantify per-cell nascent protein synthesis with puromycin or HPG labeling at the start of treatment, sort cells by translation rate, and test whether high-translation cells survive more and are more sensitive to translation inhibitors. This tests whether a protein-synthesis state, rather than transcription, sets tolerance.

title: Single-cell ecDNA copy-number tracking
description: Quantify extrachromosomal DNA copy number per cell (FISH on metaphase spreads or interphase, plus single-cell DNA sequencing) before drug exposure and in survivors. Test whether cells with high ecDNA burden of the drug target or resistance oncogene are enriched among survivors, since random ecDNA segregation creates large copy-number variation between genetically identical cells.

title: Pre-treatment target-engagement imaging linked to fate
description: Pre-load live cells with a clickable or fluorescent version of the inhibitor, or a target-occupancy reporter, and image per-cell effective drug occupancy before adding the drug. Sort cells by occupancy, re-plate them under treatment, and check whether low-engagement cells are the ones that survive.

title: Micropatterned control of density and cell contact
description: Grow cells on micropatterned islands that set local density, cell spreading, and cell-cell contact independently of clone size. Measure survival fraction under drug as a function of geometry, and test whether the effect operates through mechanotransduction by perturbing YAP/TAZ.

title: Inheritance of proteostatic capacity through cell division
description: Use timer or photoconvertible reporters of chaperone and proteasome activity, tracked by time-lapse imaging through cell division, to determine whether daughter cells inherit different proteostatic capacity. Then test whether daughters that inherit high proteostatic capacity are the ones that survive drug treatment.

title: Single-cell mitochondrial heteroplasmy and drug tolerance
description: Measure mtDNA copy number and variant allele fraction in single cells, comparing sorted survivors with sensitive cells. Then test causality by swapping mitochondrial variants or depleting mtDNA, to determine whether heteroplasmy level alone changes drug tolerance.

title: Pre-treatment mitochondrial membrane potential sorting with mtDNA heteroplasmy readout
description: Sort live cells by baseline TMRM or MitoTracker signal before drug exposure, challenge each sorted pool with the drug, and sequence mtDNA and measure OXPHOS capacity in survivors. This tests whether baseline mitochondrial state and mtDNA heteroplasmy predict survival, independent of nuclear-genome or transcriptional explanations.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug accumulation versus survival
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration in individual cells using a clickable or intrinsically detectable drug analog, or by single-cell mass spectrometry imaging, and correlate it with later survival in live-cell tracking. If survivors accumulate less drug at the time of exposure, the cause is cellular pharmacokinetics rather than target biology.

title: Live ERK/AKT activity pulse dynamics before treatment, linked to fate
description: Express kinase translocation reporters (e.g., ERK-KTR) in a clonal population and record pulse frequency and amplitude for many hours before adding drug. Then photoconvert or trace the cells that survive and compare their pre-drug signaling dynamics with those of cells that die, to test whether temporal signaling dynamics rather than mean activity set the survival fate.

title: Nascent protein synthesis rate per cell as a survival predictor
description: Label newly made proteins with puromycin or OPP click chemistry in single cells before treatment, sort by translation rate, and challenge each sorted fraction with the drug. This tests whether low or high translational throughput determines the chance of survival, which would implicate proteostasis and ribosome biogenesis as the controlling variable.

title: Spatial mapping of survivors in micropatterned or density-controlled colonies
description: Seed cells on micropatterned adhesive islands or at defined densities, treat with the drug, and use multiplexed spatial transcriptomics or imaging to map where survivors sit relative to neighbors, edges, and matrix contacts. If survivors cluster at specific positions, the survival state is a niche-dependent property rather than an intrinsic cell-level one.

title: Sorting pre-treatment cells by mitochondrial membrane potential, then drug challenge
description: Stain untreated cells with TMRM or a similar potential-sensitive dye, sort high- and low-potential fractions, and expose each to the drug. If survival tracks the pre-existing mitochondrial state, this would show a functional, heritable OXPHOS trait that predicts survival before any drug exposure.

title: Single-cell intracellular drug quantification by imaging mass cytometry
description: Use a mass-tagged or fluorescent analog of the drug, or mass spectrometry imaging, to measure intracellular drug concentration in each cell shortly after dosing. Correlating per-cell drug load with later survival tests whether survivors accumulate less drug, a pharmacokinetic explanation distinct from altered target signaling.

title: Time-to-death distributions from a live caspase biosensor
description: Express a caspase-3 FRET or translocation reporter in the cell line and track each cell's time to apoptotic commitment for several days after drug addition. Comparing survivors that never commit with cells that commit late would separate a fixed resistant subpopulation from a population that simply delays death.

title: Nuclear deformability and chromatin compaction by microfluidic constriction
description: Pass untreated cells through a constriction channel to measure nuclear deformability, then sort by deformability and test drug sensitivity. A link between nuclear stiffness and survival would indicate a mechanical, nucleus-level determinant of drug tolerance that gene expression assays would miss.

title: smFISH and live-cell MS2 imaging of transcriptional bursting in efflux and target genes
description: Measure burst frequency and size of the drug target and efflux transporter mRNAs in individual cells before treatment, either by smFISH on fixed cells or MS2 reporters in live cells. Testing whether survival is predicted by bursting kinetics would show whether persistence arises from stochastic transcriptional noise rather than a stable cell state.

title: Pre-treatment ERK/AKT pulse dynamics linked to fate
description: Use live fluorescent kinase translocation or FRET reporters to record signaling pulse frequency and amplitude in each cell before drug addition, then score each cell's fate after treatment. If pulse dynamics, rather than average activity, predict survival, this identifies a temporal signaling signature that determines tolerance.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug and target-engagement quantification
description: Combine fluorescent or isotope-labeled drug analogs with imaging or flow-based readouts to measure how much drug each cell accumulates and how much target is occupied (e.g., with a NanoBRET or CETSA-style readout). This tests a pharmacological explanation, variability in uptake or efflux, separately from any genetic or cell-state explanation.

title: Spatial niche and neighbor-density effects on survival
description: Plate cells at controlled densities and in mixed co-cultures. Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to map survivors relative to their neighbors and local secreted-factor gradients. Then run conditioned-medium and paracrine-blocking experiments to test whether a local microenvironment protects a subset of cells.

title: Pre-treatment mechanical phenotype sorting
description: Sort cells by nuclear and whole-cell deformability using microfluidic deformability cytometry or AFM before drug exposure, then test the sorted fractions for drug tolerance and compare their cytoskeletal and nuclear-lamina profiles. This asks whether physical cell state, rather than molecular state, predetermines survival.

title: Per-cell nascent translation rate as a predictor of tolerance
description: Measure nascent protein synthesis in individual cells before treatment using puromycin incorporation or a SunTag-based translation reporter, sort high- and low-translation fractions, and compare their drug responses. Ribosome profiling of the sorted fractions would show whether translational capacity sets the threshold for surviving drug-induced stress.

title: Live-cell kinase reporter measurement of pathway rebound kinetics
description: Expose cells to a titrated dose of a targeted inhibitor while imaging a live ERK or AKT kinase translocation reporter (KTR) in each cell. Compare the speed and extent of pathway reactivation between cells that later survive and those that die, to test whether survival depends on how quickly individual cells recover from inhibition rather than on their baseline state.

title: Asymmetric drug partitioning at mitosis
description: Use the intrinsic autofluorescence of the drug, or a fluorescent analog, with time-lapse imaging and daughter-cell tracking across division. Quantify whether unequal drug segregation at mitosis leaves some daughters below the lethal threshold, which would make survival a chance outcome of division rather than a heritable trait.

title: Single-cell mtDNA heteroplasmy and membrane potential
description: Sort cells by mitochondrial membrane potential (e.g., TMRM) before drug exposure, then perform single-cell or clonal mtDNA sequencing to measure heteroplasmy in each sorted fraction. Test whether mitochondrial genotype or variant load predicts survival after treatment, which would point to a non-nuclear source of heritable variation.

title: Drug-induced mutagenesis fluctuation assay
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation tests with a reporter for mutation under sublethal drug, and compare the mutation rate and spectrum in survivor clones with those from drug-naive lineages. This distinguishes resistance that arises from drug-induced mutagenesis after exposure from resistance that was already present before treatment.

title: Lysosomal sequestration of basic-amine inhibitors
description: For kinase inhibitors with basic amines, co-stain for lysosomal volume and acidity (LysoTracker, LAMP1) and measure per-cell drug fluorescence by imaging or flow cytometry. Test whether cells with expanded or more acidic lysosomes sequester more drug away from the target and therefore survive, and whether lysosome inhibition resensitizes them.

title: Barcode lineage tracing to distinguish pre-existing from drug-induced survivors
description: Label each founder cell with a heritable DNA barcode, expand the population, treat with drug, and use scRNA-seq to determine whether surviving barcoded clones were already transcriptionally distinct before treatment. Clonal overlap between pre-treatment and survivor states distinguishes selection of rare pre-existing cells from induction of a new state in naive cells.

title: Live-cell signaling and cell-cycle reporters with retrospective fate tracking
description: Express a KTR-type ERK or AKT activity reporter together with a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter, image cells by time-lapse before and during drug exposure, and compute each cell's signaling pulse frequency and cell-cycle phase history. Comparing these dynamics between cells that die and cells that survive tests whether temporal signaling behavior, not average activity, predicts survival.

title: Sorting on pre-treatment mitochondrial state and testing survival and metabolism
description: Sort the untreated population by TMRM or mitochondrial membrane potential and by NADH autofluorescence, then challenge each fraction with drug and measure survival. Also perform 13C tracing on sorted survivors to determine whether an OXPHOS-high or glycolysis-high metabolic state is a causal, pre-existing determinant of persistence.

title: Single-cell measurement of drug uptake and efflux heterogeneity
description: Use fluorescent drug analogs or intracellular LC-MS on sorted subpopulations to quantify how much drug each cell accumulates and how quickly it is pumped out. If survivors show low intracellular drug at the time of exposure, reduced uptake or increased efflux would be a sufficient non-genetic explanation for survival that does not require any target-level change.

title: Drug-holiday and re-challenge assays for reversibility and epigenetic memory
description: Expose cells to drug until a persister pool forms, withdraw drug for several passages, then re-challenge and track the survivor fraction and CUT&Tag or ATAC profiles over time. Whether survivors revert to baseline sensitivity, and how quickly, indicates whether persistence is a transient adaptive state, a heritable epigenetic memory, or a stable genetic change.

title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter tracking linked to fate
description: Track signaling and cell-cycle reporters (e.g., FUCCI, ERK-KTR, p53 pulses) in individual cells before drug exposure, then map each cell's pre-treatment state to its post-treatment fate. This tests whether survival is predictable from a cell's state at the time of treatment.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from induced tolerance
description: Introduce heritable barcodes into the population, treat, and use scRNA-seq to see whether survivors share barcodes with pre-marked clones or arise from many lineages that switch state after drug exposure. This distinguishes selection of rare pre-adapted cells from drug-induced reprogramming.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement
description: Quantify intracellular drug concentration in each cell using fluorescent drug analogs or imaging mass spectrometry, and correlate it with survival. Differences in uptake or efflux could explain survival even when target and genotype are identical.

title: Chromatin accessibility priming with epigenetic perturbation
description: Use scATAC-seq on untreated cells to find regions that are already open near survival-associated genes in the rare cells that later persist. Then perturb the implicated chromatin regulators to test whether they are causal for tolerance.

title: Metabolic state sorting by NAD(P)H FLIM
description: Measure each cell's NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime as a label-free readout of its metabolic state, sort cells by that readout, and test whether the metabolically distinct subsets differ in drug survival. Follow up with metabolic tracing on the sorted groups to identify the specific pathways involved.

title: Live-cell reporter tracking linked to retrospective single-cell profiling
description: Use live-cell fluorescent reporters (e.g., CDK2 activity, cell-cycle or stress-pathway sensors) to follow individual cells through drug exposure and record their fate. Then profile the tracked cells retrospectively (e.g., by fixing and sequencing or by photo-labelled recovery) to identify which pre-treatment states predict survival.

title: Lineage barcoding to distinguish pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance
description: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable DNA barcode before treatment and track barcode frequencies through drug exposure and recovery. If survivors come from a small set of pre-marked clones, tolerance was pre-existing; if barcodes are randomly represented, tolerance is induced by the drug.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification
description: Measure how much drug each cell accumulates, using fluorescent drug analogs or LC-MS on flow-sorted cells. Test whether survivors have lower intracellular drug levels due to differences in uptake or efflux rather than altered target biology.

title: Chromatin accessibility priming and causal perturbation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility by scATAC-seq in drug-naive cells and identify regions that are open in cells that later survive. Then perturb the implicated chromatin regulators to test whether they causally change the survival fraction.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen with single-cell transcriptomic readout
description: Run a genome-wide knockout screen under drug treatment with single-cell RNA readout so each perturbation's effect on both survival and cell state is measured together. This separates genes that drive survival from those that merely mark a tolerant state.

title: Lineage barcoding plus scRNA-seq to trace survivor origin
description: Label each cell with a heritable barcode before treatment, then compare barcode frequencies and transcriptomes of survivors to pre-treatment clones. This shows whether survivors were pre-existing lineages with a stable state or arose from induced switching in cells that were not previously distinguished.

title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter tracking linked to fate
description: Track individual cells with a cell-cycle or stress reporter before drug addition, then add the drug and follow each cell to death or survival. Matching pre-treatment reporter state to eventual fate tests whether slow cycling or another specific pre-drug state predicts survival.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement
description: Quantify intracellular drug levels in individual cells with a fluorescent analog, or in sorted subpopulations by LC-MS, and relate them to survival. This tests whether differences in uptake, efflux, or sequestration, rather than target biology, explain why some cells escape.

title: Sort-and-replate assay of memory and heritability
description: Sort cells defined by a survival-linked reporter before treatment, re-expose them to drug, and measure how well the survival phenotype is inherited across divisions and after drug withdrawal. Heritable survival indicates a stable epigenetic or regulatory memory, while loss of the phenotype on replating indicates transient tolerance.

title: Endogenous target-abundance and noise profiling
description: Tag the drug target at its endogenous locus and quantify per-cell target protein levels and their variability before treatment. Test whether cells with low target abundance or high expression noise are preferentially spared, which would identify a dose-target stoichiometry mechanism that could be therapeutically exploited.

title: Pre-treatment lineage barcoding with fate mapping
description: Label individual progenitor cells with heritable DNA barcodes before drug exposure, then sequence barcodes in survivors after treatment. If surviving clones share barcodes with specific pre-treatment clones, survival reflects pre-existing cell identity rather than stochastic or induced changes.

title: Pre-treatment live-cell imaging linked to fate
description: Track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy with cell-cycle and stress reporters (e.g., FUCCI, pathway-activity biosensors) before drug addition, then record each cell's fate. Machine-learning models on pre-treatment features can test whether survival is predictable from measurable single-cell states.

title: Chromatin accessibility profiling in early-treated cells
description: Profile ATAC-seq and histone marks in cells sorted by early drug response (e.g., reporter activation at 24 h) versus bulk. Differential accessibility at lineage or stress genes would indicate epigenetic priming that precedes survival.

title: Genome-wide CRISPRa and CRISPRi screens for persister modifiers
description: Run pooled CRISPR activation and interference screens at sublethal-to-lethal drug doses and sequence surviving cells to identify genes that raise or lower persister frequency. Hits that act only when the drug is present indicate tolerance mechanisms distinct from baseline essentiality.

title: Re-challenge and reversibility test of heritable tolerance
description: Sort surviving cells, expand them without drug, and re-challenge them alongside parental cells, measuring survival fraction and tracking reversion over multiple cycles. Persistent tolerance after drug withdrawal indicates heritable epigenetic memory, whereas rapid reversion indicates a transient, reversible state.

title: Baseline signaling and cell-cycle dynamics with fate tracking
description: Express live-cell reporters (e.g., ERK-KTR and FUCCI) in cells before adding the drug, then track each cell's history and fate. This tests whether survivors already show distinct ERK signaling pulse patterns or cell-cycle states that predict survival before any treatment.

title: Lineage barcoding with single-cell transcriptomics
description: Label founder cells with heritable barcodes, treat with drug, and sequence both barcode and transcriptome in single cells. This distinguishes survivors descending from a few pre-existing clones from survivors that reach a shared state through induced switching.

title: Sorting by drug accumulation and mitochondrial state
description: Sort live cells by efflux-pump activity, intracellular drug level, or mitochondrial membrane potential, then challenge each fraction with the drug. Pair this with mtDNA heteroplasmy sequencing to test whether intracellular drug handling or OXPHOS state primes survival.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen with time-resolved persister sampling
description: Run a genome-wide knockout or CRISPRi screen and sample at several times during drug exposure and during drug holidays. Comparing enrichment dynamics separates genes that set persister frequency from genes that maintain the tolerant state.

title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility priming before treatment
description: Profile chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) and transcription jointly on untreated cells, then identify loci accessible in future survivors. Validate candidate regulators by sorting cells for accessibility and testing survival in the sorted cells.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification linked to fate
description: Use fluorescent drug analogs or imaging mass spectrometry to measure how much drug each cell accumulates, then compare survivors with dying cells. If survivors hold lower drug levels, the cause is uptake or efflux heterogeneity rather than a change in the target pathway.

title: Live-cell cell-cycle reporter tracking at drug addition
description: Use FUCCI or a similar reporter with time-lapse imaging to record each cell's cycle phase when the drug is added and follow it to death or division. This tests whether quiescent or slow-cycling cells are the ones that persist, and whether they re-enter the cycle later.

title: Lineage barcoding combined with pre-treatment scRNA-seq
description: Barcode cells before treatment and profile their transcriptomes. Then determine which barcoded lineages and states survive. This separates survivors that were already in a distinct state from survivors whose state was induced by the drug, and shows whether a few clones dominate.

title: Reversibility and memory test of sorted survivors
description: Sort survivor cells by a reporter, withdraw the drug, and re-challenge them over several generations. Comparing re-challenged cells with naive controls shows whether tolerance is heritable epigenetic memory or a reversible state that resets.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen with single-cell readout
description: Run a pooled CRISPR perturbation screen read out by single-cell RNA-seq under drug. Check which knockouts shift cells out of the survivor state or change their survival. This tests whether candidate survival programs are causal rather than just correlated with survival.

title: Lineage barcoding with drug challenge and transcriptomic readout
description: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable barcode, expose the population to the drug, and sequence barcodes and transcriptomes of survivors. This tests whether survivors arise from a few pre-existing clones or from stochastic, independent cell-level switches, and whether survivor states are inherited.

title: Pre-treatment apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
description: Measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming of each subpopulation by BH3 profiling before drug exposure, then sort high- and low-priming cells and treat each with the drug. If survival tracks priming, tolerance is set by a pre-existing mitochondrial apoptotic threshold rather than by drug-specific pathways.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement
description: Quantify intracellular drug concentration in single cells using a fluorescent analog or mass-spec imaging, paired with efflux-transporter reporters. Test whether low drug accumulation, rather than differences in target levels, explains which cells survive.

title: Single-cell multiome of chromatin state before and during treatment
description: Profile paired ATAC and RNA in drug-naive cells and at early drug timepoints to find accessible-chromatin states and transcription factor motifs that predict survival. Validate top factors by perturbing them and measuring survival.

title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and OXPHOS heterogeneity in survivors
description: Sequence mtDNA and image membrane potential and respiration in sorted survivor and dying populations. Test whether naturally varying mitochondrial genotype or function among cells with identical nuclear genomes sets drug tolerance.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment clone tracking
description: Label a population with a heritable DNA barcode library (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcodes), then compare barcode clone frequencies before and after drug exposure and after drug withdrawal and re-challenge. Clones already enriched among survivors indicate pre-existing heritable states, while survivors spread across many clones indicate induced, non-heritable switching. This tests whether survival arises from a single mechanism and whether the survivor state is stable and inherited.

title: Live-cell reporter tracking of pre-treatment predictors and reversibility
description: Use fluorescent reporters for cell-cycle phase (FUCCI), signaling activity (e.g., ERK-KTR), or stress state, and follow individual cells through drug exposure with time-lapse imaging. Link each cell's pre-treatment reporter state to its fate, and test whether the survivor state is transient by washing out the drug and checking whether sensitivity returns. This tests whether survival is a stable, binary trait and whether a single endpoint captures it.

title: Single-cell multiomics of the untreated population with survival classifier
description: Profile transcriptome and chromatin accessibility (scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq) of the untreated population, then train a classifier that predicts which cells survive and check it with sorted cells in a validation experiment. A continuum of predicted survival probabilities would argue against a discrete persister subpopulation. This tests the assumption that survivors form a distinct, stable subpopulation and that the starting state is a representative snapshot.

title: Error-corrected single-cell genomics of pre-existing variants
description: Use single-cell DNA sequencing or duplex-consensus, deep-coverage sequencing of the pre-treatment population to detect rare subclonal SNVs and CNVs. Then test whether those variants are enriched in survivors and whether they are causal using CRISPR knock-in. This checks whether the cells are truly genetically identical, which bulk sequencing cannot show.

title: Spatially resolved drug exposure and co-culture perturbations
description: Run the treatment in a microfluidic gradient, a 3D spheroid, or an in vivo xenograft, and measure local drug concentration (for example with a fluorescent drug analog or a drug-response biosensor) alongside spatial transcriptomics of survivors. Then test whether conditioned medium from survivors or neighboring cells, or a co-culture with stromal cells, changes survival of sensitive cells. This tests the assumptions of uniform drug exposure and cell autonomy.

title: Duplex sequencing and barcoded lineage tracing of pre-existing subclones
description: Use duplex or error-corrected deep sequencing, plus heritable DNA barcodes, to detect rare pre-existing variants and clonal lineages before treatment and compare them with survivors. This tests whether the apparently genetically identical population contains low-frequency clones that account for survival.

title: Live-cell reporter tracking to predict survival from pre-treatment state
description: Track single cells over time with fluorescent reporters (e.g., FUCCI for cell cycle, or a pathway activity sensor) before and during drug exposure, then test whether pre-treatment reporter state predicts which cells die. If survival is not predictable, it is stochastic, which tests whether fate is fixed and whether bulk averaging is adequate.

title: Drug washout and re-challenge with time-resolved single-cell multiomics
description: Expose cells to drug, withdraw it at defined times, and re-challenge, profiling scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq at each step. If survivors revert to drug sensitivity after washout, the persister state is reversible rather than a stable heritable resistance.

title: Spatial mapping of survivors against measured local drug exposure
description: Treat organoids or xenografts and combine spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging with a per-cell readout of drug exposure, such as a fluorescent drug analogue or a sensor of target engagement. This tests whether survivors cluster in low-exposure or protective niches (hypoxic, perivascular, contact-dependent) rather than being intrinsically resistant.

title: Sublethal-dose pooled CRISPR screen with survivor sorting and perturbation validation
description: Run a genome-wide or CRISPRi screen at a sublethal dose, sort or compare surviving populations, and validate top hits by individual knockouts, including bypass and efflux genes, in cells with and without the transporter blocked. Enriched hits that rescue survival after validation test whether the drug target is the only relevant pathway and whether the survivor correlates are causal.

title: Drug-holiday re-challenge with lineage barcodes
description: Barcode a clonal population, apply a drug pulse, sort survivors, and grow them drug-free for several passages before re-challenging with the same dose. If survival is heritable, survivor lineages will keep their tolerance across drug-free passages; if it is a reversible state, tolerance will reset and the surviving fraction will return to baseline.

title: Deep single-cell genomic profiling of pre-existing variants
description: Perform ultra-deep amplicon or duplex sequencing of the drug target, and single-cell whole-genome or copy-number profiling, on drug-naive cells to detect rare pre-existing variants, amplifications, or ecDNA. Then check whether these variants are enriched in survivor-derived clones after treatment.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation and target occupancy imaging
description: Use a fluorescent or clickable analogue of the drug, or mass cytometry with a drug-bound-target readout, to measure intracellular drug levels and target engagement in each cell over time. Pair these with efflux transporter expression (e.g., ABCB1) and sort by accumulation to test whether survivors are simply those with the lowest effective exposure.

title: Spatial profiling of residual tumor in organoids or xenografts
description: Treat tumor organoids or xenografts and use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to map where survivors sit relative to hypoxic zones, cell-cell contacts, vasculature, and stroma. Survivor enrichment that tracks a niche rather than a fixed intrinsic profile would show that the environment, not the cell alone, drives survival.

title: Perturb-seq on drug-naive versus treated cells
description: Run a pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screen with single-cell RNA readout under low-dose drug, and compare it with drug-naive controls. Genes whose knockdown changes survival, and that are themselves part of the survivor signature in the pre-treatment state, are candidate causal regulators, while signature genes that only appear after treatment are likely consequences.

title: Lineage barcoding plus single-cell DNA sequencing of survivors
description: Transduce cells with a high-complexity genetic barcode library before treatment, then compare barcode frequencies in survivors versus the pre-treatment pool to see whether survivors derive from a few pre-existing clones. Pair this with single-cell DNA sequencing or duplex sequencing of survivors to detect rare pre-existing or newly acquired mutations.

title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter tracking with fate mapping
description: Before adding drug, image cells carrying fluorescent reporters for candidate states (e.g., FUCCI cell cycle, NRF2, or an EMT or stemness reporter) and record each cell's state. Then track each cell's fate under drug and test whether pre-treatment reporter state predicts survival, showing whether survival is pre-determined or drug-induced.

title: Sort-and-rechallenge with drug-free persistence assay
description: Sort surviving cells from a treatment window, then grow them drug-free for several passages before re-challenging them with the same dose. Compare survival fractions across cycles, and use FUCCI or EdU pulse-chase to see whether persisters are slow-cycling and whether their tolerance is heritable or reverts to the parental level.

title: Per-cell drug quantification with efflux reporter imaging
description: Measure per-cell intracellular drug concentration with a fluorescent drug analog or imaging mass spectrometry, alongside an ABC-transporter or drug-efflux reporter. Compare survivors with non-survivors at matched target-inhibition readouts (e.g., phospho-marker levels) to separate lower drug exposure from target-independent tolerance.

title: Spatial and microenvironment perturbation in 3D or in vivo models
description: Grow the same cell line as spheroids, organoids, or in co-culture with stromal or immune cells, and use spatial transcriptomics or imaging to map where survivors sit relative to gradients of oxygen, drug, and cell density. Add conditioned medium or stromal-derived factors to test whether a paracrine signal rescues survival, and confirm key findings in an in vivo xenograft.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with drug washout and rechallenge
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, treat with the drug, then remove the drug and re-challenge the survivors. Whether the survivor phenotype is inherited by barcoded descendants, reversed after washout, or re-derived by new cells distinguishes stable clonal resistance from reversible drug-tolerant states.

title: Single-cell live reporters of drug exposure and target engagement
description: Combine fluorescent drug analogs or biosensors of target activity (e.g., ERK or AKT kinase reporters) with time-lapse imaging to measure each cell's effective drug dose and pathway inhibition. Test whether survivors show lower intracellular drug or sustained pathway reactivation, which would indicate pharmacokinetic heterogeneity rather than intrinsic resistance.

title: Microenvironment perturbation, co-culture, and spatial profiling
description: Compare survival rates across conditioned media, neighbor-density gradients, co-culture with stromal or immune cells, and in vivo xenografts. Spatial transcriptomics of surviving cells in tumors can show whether niche position or paracrine signaling, rather than cell-intrinsic state, drives survival.

title: Deep single-cell DNA sequencing of pre-treatment and surviving cells
description: Use high-depth single-cell or duplex sequencing to detect rare pre-existing variants, copy-number states, and target-site mutations in pre-treatment cells and in the surviving fraction. Enrichment of specific subclones among survivors would show a genetic contribution that bulk analysis misses.

title: Time-lapse fate tracking with causal perturbation of candidate survival markers
description: Track single cells by live imaging through drug exposure to separate true resistance from delayed death or quiescence, and record the pre-treatment state of each cell. Then sort or fate-map survivors and use CRISPRi or degron knockdown of candidate markers to test whether they are necessary for survival.

title: Barcode lineage tracing before and after drug
description: Label cells with a high-complexity heritable DNA barcode library (e.g., CellTag or LARRY) before treatment, then compare barcode frequencies in pre-treatment and survivor pools. Barcodes already enriched among survivors indicate pre-existing tolerant clones, while survivors with barcodes absent from the pre-treatment pool indicate de novo induction.

title: Reversibility and drug-holiday test
description: Sort survivors, grow them drug-free for several passages, then re-challenge with the drug alongside untreated parental cells. If sensitivity returns, survival is a reversible state; if it persists, it is a stable heritable trait. Pair with scRNA-seq/ATAC at each step to identify the state that is lost or retained.

title: Single-cell genome and clonal-variant profiling
description: Perform single-cell DNA sequencing (or deep targeted sequencing of pooled cells) on pre-treatment populations and matched survivors to detect rare subclonal SNVs, copy-number states, and structural variants. Test whether survivors share a variant or copy-number change absent from the bulk population, which would show that the nominally identical population contains a pre-existing genetic subclone.

title: Spatial mapping and co-culture niche perturbation
description: Map survivors in situ using spatial transcriptomics or imaging on tumor organoids or xenografts, and test whether their location (e.g., edge versus core, contact with stroma) predicts survival. Then perturb the niche by transferring conditioned media, adding fibroblasts, or using micropatterned colonies to test whether survival depends on extrinsic signals rather than the cell's own state.

title: Live-cell reporter tracking of pre-treatment state through drug addition
description: Use fluorescent reporters (e.g., FUCCI for cell-cycle phase and an ERK or AKT kinase translocation reporter) to track individual cells through drug addition over days. Measure whether reporter state or cell-cycle phase at the time of treatment predicts which cells survive, and whether survivors show a distinct dynamic trajectory rather than only an endpoint difference.

title: Live-cell fate tracking linked to pre-treatment state
description: Use time-lapse imaging with fluorescent reporters (e.g., cell-cycle, stress, or lineage markers) to follow individual cells before, during, and after drug exposure, then test whether pre-treatment features predict fate or whether survival is decided during treatment. Pair this with a heritable lineage barcode to see whether survival clusters within clonal families.

title: Reversibility test by drug withdrawal and re-challenge
description: Sort survivors (or use a reporter to isolate persister-like cells), culture them drug-free for several passages, then re-challenge with the drug and compare survival with that of the original population. If the survivor fraction resets and re-emerges from the naive population, the trait is a reversible state rather than a fixed genetic or epigenetic subpopulation.

title: Single-cell DNA sequencing of survivors versus pre-treatment population
description: Perform single-cell whole-genome or targeted DNA sequencing on the untreated population and on survivors to detect pre-existing rare subclones, copy-number changes, or mutations that expand under treatment. Compare allele and CNV profiles to determine whether survival is genetic or non-genetic.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation and target-engagement biosensor
description: Quantify intracellular drug levels in single cells (using a fluorescent drug analog or LC-MS on sorted cells) alongside a live-cell biosensor of target pathway activity, such as a kinase translocation reporter. This tests whether survivors have lower drug uptake, higher efflux pump expression, or maintained pathway signaling despite equal extracellular dosing.

title: In vivo barcoded xenograft or organoid comparison with spatial profiling
description: Treat barcoded tumors in mice or patient-derived organoids and use spatial transcriptomics on residual tumor tissue to map where survivors sit relative to vasculature, hypoxia, and stromal niches. Compare these spatial niches with in vitro survivor signatures to test whether the mechanism depends on the microenvironment and whether the culture model is representative.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with pre-treatment sorting
description: Label cells with a heritable DNA barcode library, sort pre-treatment subpopulations by a candidate reporter, apply the drug, and quantify which barcode lineages and sorted fractions survive. If survival is inherited from a pre-existing state, survivors should trace back to specific pre-treatment fractions, and a drug holiday followed by re-challenge can test whether that state is stable or reversible.

title: Deep single-cell and duplex DNA sequencing of survivors
description: Compare high-depth single-cell whole-genome sequencing and duplex error-corrected sequencing of the pre-treatment population with those of survivors to detect rare pre-existing mutations, CNVs, or subclones enriched after treatment. Enrichment of a specific variant among survivors would show the cells are not truly genetically identical.

title: Per-cell target-signaling dynamics with live reporters
description: Use a live kinase-activity reporter, such as an ERK translocation sensor, with time-lapse imaging across a drug dose range to track each cell's signaling before and after treatment and its eventual fate. Testing whether survival follows a threshold in pre-treatment signaling or a graded dose-response shows whether survivors are a discrete subpopulation or part of a continuum.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux with sorting and gradients
description: Quantify single-cell drug levels using a fluorescent or tagged drug analog combined with efflux-transporter reporters, and sort cells by accumulation before measuring survival. Adding a microfluidic drug gradient would also show whether low-accumulation cells survive because they receive less drug rather than because of intrinsic tolerance.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen under drug with causal validation
description: Run a genome-wide or focused CRISPR knockout or interference screen under sub-lethal and lethal drug doses, comparing guide abundance before and after treatment to identify genes whose loss sensitizes or protects cells. Then validate the top hits by individually perturbing them and confirming that survival changes, which tests whether the markers enriched in survivors cause survival.

title: Re-analysis of public time-course scRNA-seq of drug-treated cell lines
description: Pool published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from genetically uniform cell lines (e.g., EGFR-mutant lung lines treated with TKIs) sampled before and during drug exposure. Test whether survivors are already transcriptionally distinct at baseline (pre-existing persister state) or diverge only after treatment, and identify the genes that separate them.

title: Linking baseline transcriptomes to drug survival in CCLE/GDSC data
description: Use the CCLE baseline expression profiles and GDSC/PRISM dose-response curves across hundreds of cell lines to ask whether lines with a high-tolerance residual fraction share an expression or pathway signature. Focus on the shape of the dose-response curve (plateau or residual viability) rather than only IC50, since the plateau reflects the surviving fraction.

title: Clonal origin of survivors from public lineage-barcoding data
description: Reanalyze published DNA-barcode lineage-tracing experiments in drug-treated cancer cell populations to measure how many surviving clones trace back to a shared pre-treatment barcode versus de novo emergence. The ratio indicates whether survival is driven by rare pre-existing variants or by stochastic or induced switching.

title: Chromatin and epigenetic comparison of persisters with parental cells
description: Collect public ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq (H3K27me3, H3K4me3, H3K27ac), and DNA methylation data from drug-tolerant persister studies and compare them with matched untreated cells. Look for chromatin regions that are opened or closed in survivors and whether those regions are already accessible at baseline, which would suggest an epigenetic memory or priming mechanism.

title: Integrating CRISPR knockout screens with drug-response and signaling data
description: Cross-reference DepMap genome-wide CRISPR screens for the same cell lines with drug-response data to identify genes whose loss selectively sensitizes cells to the drug without reducing growth. Combine these with public phosphoproteomic data from drug-treated cells (e.g., PRIDE or CPTAC) to map the signaling rewiring that survivors depend on.

title: Lineage-barcoded scRNA-seq before and during drug pulse
description: Label a clonal line with a lentiviral lineage barcode library (~10,000 barcodes), profile untreated cells with single-cell RNA-seq, then profile cells at early and late timepoints of drug exposure. Comparing barcoded clones shows whether survivors come from a pre-existing transcriptional state or are induced by the drug. Estimated cost is about $12,000 to $16,000 (barcode library, 10x Genomics lanes, sequencing).

title: Live-cell reporter tracking with sort-and-recover
description: Use a fluorescent reporter for a candidate persister state (e.g., a cell-cycle or stress-pathway reporter) and track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy through drug treatment. Sort the cells that survive and the cells that die based on their pre-treatment reporter level, then test whether that level predicts survival. Estimated cost: about $8,000 to $12,000 (reporter construct, imaging time, sorting, reagents).

title: Chromatin accessibility and epigenetic memory test
description: Run ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag (H3K27me3, H3K4me3) on sorted pre-treatment cells and on drug-tolerant survivors, then wash out the drug and re-challenge to see whether any tolerance-linked chromatin state persists. Persistence after washout would indicate epigenetic memory rather than a transient response. Estimated cost is about $10,000 to $15,000 (library prep, sequencing, cell culture).

title: Time-resolved pooled CRISPR screen for survival genes
description: Transduce a genome-wide or focused CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi library, treat with the drug, and sample the population at several early timepoints instead of only at the end. Genes whose guides are depleted or enriched at early timepoints reveal the mechanisms that allow initial survival, separate from those that matter for long-term regrowth. Estimated cost: about $10,000 to $15,000 (library, sequencing, screen cell culture).

title: Single-cell metabolic and proteomic profiling of survivors
description: Measure autofluorescence-based NAD(P)H and FAD redox imaging, mitochondrial membrane potential, and ROS levels in individual cells before and during treatment, and combine this with mass cytometry (CyTOF) for signaling and drug-target proteins. Compare survivors with non-survivors to identify whether a metabolic or signaling state predicts tolerance, then test the top candidate with a metabolic inhibitor combined with the drug. Estimated cost: about $8,000 to $14,000 (CyTOF antibody panel, sorter and imaging time, metabolic assays).

title: Pre-treatment fate prediction with lineage-tracked cell-cycle and death reporters
description: Co-express a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter and a caspase-3/7 biosensor, then image the same cells for 24-48 h before and after drug addition. Trace each cell's lineage backward from its eventual fate to test whether cell-cycle phase, division history, or time since last mitosis before treatment predicts survival.

title: Live kinase translocation reporters to find pre-existing signaling states
description: Use ERK and AKT kinase translocation reporters (KTRs) to measure pathway activity in each cell before the inhibitor is added and then track it through treatment. Test whether survivors had a distinct baseline signaling level or pulse dynamics, and whether that difference is stable across generations.

title: Metabolic and organelle reporters of pre-existing survival states
description: Image mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM or similar dye), an ATP or NADH/NAD+ biosensor such as Peredox, and mitochondrial mass in single cells over time. Compare baseline and early-treatment metabolic profiles of eventual survivors and dying cells to identify a metabolic signature that precedes survival.

title: Pulse-washout and reseeding kinetics to separate reversible tolerance from heritable resistance
description: Apply the drug as a timed pulse, wash it out, and track survivors for several generations in drug-free medium using time-lapse imaging. Measure whether they regain normal proliferation and whether their progeny keep the tolerant phenotype, which separates reversible drug-tolerant states from stable, heritable resistance.

title: Label-free morphology and motility classifier for predicting survival
description: Record phase-contrast or brightfield time-lapse of the untreated population and extract single-cell features such as shape, texture, speed, and persistence. Train a classifier on the fates observed after treatment, then validate it on held-out cells and by live-sorting predicted survivors for follow-up.

title: Live-cell tracking of single cells through drug pulse and washout
description: Use label-free imaging (phase-contrast or quantitative phase microscopy) and a non-genetic dye such as CellTrace to record division history, and follow single cells from before treatment through drug exposure and washout. Correlate each cell's pre-treatment division history, morphology, and location with survival, and test whether survivors were already slow-cycling or arose through transient induction. Retrospective immunostaining of the same tracked cells links fate to protein state.

title: Single-cell multi-omics time course of early drug response
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or multiome) on cells sampled at baseline and at several early timepoints during drug exposure, such as hours to days, to capture the transition into the tolerant state. Use trajectory and RNA velocity analyses to identify the pre-existing or emerging persister program, and check whether baseline chromatin accessibility predicts which cells later survive.

title: Sorting pre-existing subpopulations by endogenous markers and testing drug tolerance
description: Before treatment, sort cells by endogenous surface markers and by functional dyes that report mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM), ROS (CellROX), lysosomal load, or drug-efflux activity (Hoechst or rhodamine efflux). Then challenge each fraction with the drug and measure survival and regrowth. This tests whether a pre-existing phenotypic state, rather than random chance, determines persistence.

title: Intracellular drug accumulation and metabolic profiling of survivors
description: Quantify intracellular drug levels in single cells or sorted fractions using LC-MS or a fluorescent drug analog, and measure efflux transporter activity to test whether survivors take up less drug. In parallel, run Seahorse respirometry and 13C-glucose or 13C-glutamine isotope tracing on sorted persisters versus bulk cells to identify metabolic dependencies.

title: Chromatin state profiling with drug washout and rechallenge
description: Profile histone modifications (CUT&Tag for H3K27me3, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and chromatin accessibility in sorted or bulk persisters over a drug holiday and after rechallenge. Testing whether the chromatin state persists after drug removal distinguishes a heritable epigenetic memory from a reversible, transient adaptive state.

title: Zebrafish BRAF-melanoma lineage barcoding with time-resolved single-cell profiling
description: In a zebrafish line with inducible BRAF(V600E) melanocyte tumors, apply a MAPK inhibitor and use heritable lineage barcodes (e.g., CRISPR scars or Brainbow-style color marks) to determine whether the surviving melanocytes were already present, and clonally related, before treatment. Pair this with scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq of residual tumor at multiple time points to identify chromatin and transcriptional states that distinguish survivors from cells that died.

title: Barcoded yeast Tn-seq and fluctuation analysis of drug tolerance
description: Grow a DNA-barcoded yeast library, or a transposon-mutagenized pool, under a sublethal and then lethal dose of a conserved-kinase or TOR-pathway inhibitor. Use barcode lineage tracking and Luria-Delbrück fluctuation assays to separate pre-existing from drug-induced survivors, and use Tn-seq enrichment to identify genes whose disruption changes the survivor fraction.

title: Drosophila oncogenic clone tracking with live ERK reporters
description: In Drosophila imaginal discs carrying RasV12 scrib-null tumor clones, feed a MEK inhibitor and track individual clones over time with a live ERK-translocation reporter and G-TRACE or MARCM lineage labels. This tests whether surviving clones had lower pre-treatment ERK output or a distinct growth-rate or cell-cycle state, and whether the survivors then expand.

title: Live imaging of pre-treatment signaling and cell-cycle state in a transformed rat cell line
description: Use a rat cell line transformed with oncogenic BRAF or KRAS and expressing a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter and an ERK-KTR biosensor. Record single cells for days under drug, then retrospectively link each survivor's pre-treatment ERK activity, cell-cycle phase, and drug-efflux reporter level, and confirm the link by sorting those subpopulations and testing their regrowth in drug.

title: Pulse versus continuous-exposure genome-wide CRISPR screen in a hamster cell line
description: Perform a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in a hamster (CHO) or rat cell line transformed with a targeted oncogene, comparing survivor populations after a short pulse of high-dose drug with those after continuous low-dose exposure. Knockouts that change the survivor fraction without changing drug-induced death, or that are enriched only after a drug holiday, would point to tolerance and reversible persistence mechanisms rather than stable resistance.

title: Clonal barcode lineage tracing before and during treatment
description: Transduce a cell line with a high-complexity lentiviral barcode library, sample the population before drug exposure, and sequence barcodes in survivors after treatment. Barcodes enriched among survivors that were already present at baseline indicate pre-existing persisters, while survivors with barcodes that were rare or absent at baseline indicate drug-induced adaptation.

title: Single-cell multiome of pre-treatment cells and early persisters
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on the untreated population and on cells sampled at days 0, 3, 7, and 14 of drug exposure. Comparing the survivor state with the pre-treatment state shows whether persisters were already enriched for particular transcriptional or chromatin programs, such as interferon, EMT, or slow-cycling signatures, and which regulators drive the shift.

title: Live-cell dual-reporter tracking linking baseline state to fate
description: Track single cells by time-lapse microscopy through drug exposure using a dual reporter line, for example FUCCI combined with an ERK kinase translocation reporter. Retrospectively compare each cell's pre-treatment reporter state with whether it divided or died, to show which baseline states predict survival.

title: Pooled CRISPR knockout screen for persister-determining genes
description: Transduce a genome-wide or focused sgRNA library, split the population into drug-treated and vehicle arms, and sequence guides in survivors versus input after 2 to 3 weeks. Genes whose knockout enriches or depletes persisters point to pathways required for, or that restrict, drug tolerance, and hits can be validated individually with single-guide competition assays.

title: Metabolic and mitochondrial profiling of sorted persisters
description: Sort drug-tolerant cells using a reporter or by surviving a short high-dose pulse, then expand them and measure oxygen consumption, glycolytic rate, mitochondrial DNA copy number, NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime, and sensitivity to OXPHOS and glycolysis inhibitors. Comparing these with matched parental cells tests whether persisters depend on a metabolic state that can be targeted as a co-treatment.

title: Paired pre-treatment and survivor single-cell multiome
description: Profile scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) of untreated cells and of cells surviving at a single post-treatment endpoint, then test whether survivors were already enriched for particular transcriptional or chromatin states before drug exposure. This separates pre-existing persister programs from states induced by the drug.

title: Endpoint lineage-barcode bottleneck analysis
description: Label cells with a heritable DNA barcode library before treatment, then sequence barcodes in the pre-treatment pool and the surviving pool at one endpoint. Few dominant barcodes would indicate that survival is pre-determined in a small clone, while a broad, even distribution would indicate stochastic survival.

title: Fixed-cell imaging of quiescence and pathway-activity reporters
description: Use a single fixed snapshot of FUCCI or Ki-67/EdU-based cell-cycle state together with a kinase translocation reporter (e.g., ERK-KTR) or phospho-ERK immunofluorescence in the same cells. Each cell then has its own quiescence and residual target-pathway activity measurement, which can be used to test whether survivors are non-cycling and have reactivated the pathway.

title: Spatial multiplexed imaging of drug-treated tumor or organoid niches
description: Run cyclic immunofluorescence or imaging mass cytometry on a treated tumor section or organoid, co-staining the drug target, hypoxia markers, and stromal and vascular markers.
