Map survivors relative to their neighbors and distance to vasculature or stroma to determine whether niche position, rather than cell-intrinsic state, governs persistence.

title: Mass cytometry of efflux, chromatin, and drug-retention states
description: Use CyTOF to measure drug efflux transporters (e.g., ABCB1), chromatin-regulator and histone-mark levels, and survival-pathway proteins in single cells, combined with a fluorescent or isotope-labeled drug-retention readout. This links each cell's drug accumulation and epigenetic state to its survival, identifying which protein-level features are associated with persistence.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing in patient-derived models
description: Label patient-derived organoids or PDX-derived cells with high-complexity DNA barcodes, treat with the targeted drug, and track which clones survive and when. Pair this with single-cell RNA-seq on the barcoded cells to separate survivors that were already transcriptionally primed from those that became tolerant only after drug exposure.

title: Time-resolved single-cell multiome on patient-derived organoids
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and gene expression together (scATAC + scRNA) across a dense time course, such as 0, 6, 24, 72 hours and later, after drug exposure. This shows whether persisters carry a pre-existing accessible chromatin state (transcription-factor motifs such as AP-1 or NFI) that is then amplified, and which regulators drive the transition.

title: Functional characterization of sorted persisters with reversibility tests
description: Sort surviving cells from patient-derived organoids using a slow-cycling or label-retention reporter (e.g., H2B-GFP pulse-chase) or a fluorescent cell-cycle reporter, then expand them in drug-free medium. Re-challenge them with the drug and run drug-holiday experiments to test whether tolerance is reversible and how stable it is across generations.

title: Pooled CRISPR knockout screen comparing persisters with bulk cells
description: Transduce patient-derived organoids with a genome-wide or druggable-genome CRISPR library, treat at a near-lethal drug dose, and compare guide representation in surviving cells against untreated bulk cells. Genes whose loss enriches or depletes survivors identify regulators of persister tolerance and dependencies that could serve as combination targets.

title: Spatial multiplexed profiling of persister niches in matched patient biopsies
description: Collect matched pre-treatment and on-treatment biopsies (or on-treatment PDX tumors). Map surviving tumor cells with multiplexed imaging (CODEX or IMC) or spatial transcriptomics. Relate their positions to hypoxia, vasculature, stromal and immune neighborhoods, and cell-cell contacts to identify microenvironmental signals that protect the rare survivors.

title: Asymmetric inheritance of drug-damaged protein aggregates
description: Express a fluorescent aggregate-prone reporter (e.g., a misfolding-prone GFP fusion or a PROTEOSTAT dye) in a clonal line, then track mother-daughter pairs by time-lapse through drug exposure. Test whether survival tracks with which daughter receives the larger share of damaged protein at division, which would make tolerance a result of unequal segregation rather than a fixed cell state.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug accumulation by label-free imaging
description: Quantify each cell's intracellular drug concentration with label-free methods such as stimulated Raman imaging or intrinsic fluorescence of the compound, then sort or image-correlate with later fate. If survivors hold systematically lower free drug despite identical efflux transporter levels, uptake or partitioning into lipid and organelles becomes the candidate mechanism, testable with uptake-transporter knockdowns.

title: Single-cell mtDNA heteroplasmy as a natural lineage marker
description: Use naturally occurring, maternally inherited mtDNA variants as endogenous lineage markers by applying single-cell mtDNA-calling methods (e.g., mgatk analysis of scATAC or scRNA reads) to pre-treatment and survivor populations. Shared heteroplasmic haplotypes across timepoints reveal the clonal origin of survivors without any engineered barcode, and may expose mitochondrial genotype as a survival determinant.

title: Micronucleus rupture and cGAS-STING history as a survival predictor
description: Use live imaging of a nuclear-localization reporter and a cGAS sensor to score which cells form micronuclei, rupture them, or activate innate immune signaling during the first drug cycle. Then test whether cells with prior micronuclear damage are enriched among survivors, and whether blocking cGAS or STING before treatment changes persister frequency.

title: Neighbor-cell rescue assays with dying-cell secretomes
description: Co-culture a labeled reporter population with drug-killed neighbors in transwell and direct-contact configurations, and separately collect conditioned medium from dying versus surviving cultures for mass spectrometry of secreted factors. Adding back candidate factors or depleting them from the medium will show whether survival depends on signals from neighboring cells rather than on intrinsic cell properties alone.

title: Dynamic BH3 profiling of baseline apoptotic priming
description: Before drug exposure, measure each population's mitochondrial apoptotic priming by dynamic BH3 profiling with peptides such as BIM and BAD, then sort on priming level and treat. If survivors are at the low-priming end, survival reflects distance from the mitochondrial death threshold rather than a specific drug-resistance pathway.

title: Intracellular drug accumulation and target engagement in survivors
description: Use a fluorescent or clickable analog of the drug, or LC-MS on FACS-sorted cells, to measure intracellular drug levels, and use NanoBRET or CETSA to measure target occupancy in survivors versus dying cells. This tests whether persisters retain less effective drug (through efflux, lysosomal sequestration, or uptake differences) before any signaling rewiring occurs.

title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy as an endogenous lineage marker
description: Use single-cell mtDNA sequencing (for example mtscATAC-seq or long-read mtDNA profiling) to read endogenous mtDNA variants as heritable clone markers in a population that is treated and allowed to regrow. Comparing heteroplasmy frequencies in survivors with baseline reveals whether specific mitochondrial genotypes, which alter oxidative metabolism, are enriched without engineered barcodes.

title: Paracrine rescue via conditioned media and extracellular vesicles
description: Collect conditioned medium and extracellular vesicles from sorted persisters, fractionate them, and add each fraction to drug-naive cells under treatment to see whether survival can be transferred to neighboring cells. Then use transwell co-cultures with sorted survivors to test whether the protection is secreted and dose-dependent.

title: Collateral-sensitivity profiling of survivors across a drug panel
description: Expose drug-tolerant survivors and naive control cells to a panel of 100 or more mechanistically diverse compounds and build a drug-response profile for each. Compounds that kill survivors but spare the parental population reveal collateral vulnerabilities, and the pattern shows whether tolerance is a broad state or a narrow, drug-specific adaptation.

title: Sorting cells by intracellular drug content
description: Measure each cell's drug load with a clickable or fluorescent drug analog, or by LC-MS on FACS-sorted fractions. Then compare survival of low- and high-accumulation cells at matched target engagement. This separates pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (efflux, uptake, sequestration) from true target-based tolerance.

title: Mitochondrial genome swap via cybrids
description: Fuse enucleated cytoplasts from survivor-enriched clones into a rho0 nuclear background carrying sensitive-clone nuclei, and reciprocally. If drug survival follows the mtDNA rather than the nuclear genotype, mitochondrial genome variation is causal; this test is rarely run in persister studies.

title: Spatial niche mapping in drug-treated spheroids
description: Use multiplexed imaging (e.g., CODEX or MERFISH) on spheroids at 24–72 h of treatment, registering each surviving cell to local hypoxia, nutrient, and necrotic-core gradients. Then reproduce the spatially enriched niche in controlled hypoxia or nutrient gradient devices to test whether it causes survival.

title: Pulse-duration by dose matrix with a mechanistic transition model
description: Expose cultures to a grid of drug concentrations and pulse durations, and measure survivor fractions over time. Fit an ODE model with explicit rates for death, dormancy entry, and reawakening. Model-selected rates then predict the outcome of untested schedules, inferring the switching mechanism without lineage labels.

title: Asymmetric inheritance of proteostasis damage at first mitosis
description: Label a drug-induced aggregate or chaperone reporter with HaloTag and pulse-chase it through the first post-treatment division, then track which daughter cell inherits the damaged load. If daughters receiving less damage are the ones that persist, segregation of proteotoxic burden at mitosis is a candidate determinant of survival.

title: Natural mtDNA heteroplasmy as a lineage marker
description: Use naturally occurring mitochondrial DNA variants, which need no transduction, as heritable clonal markers. Profile heteroplasmy by mtscATAC-seq or mtDNA long-read sequencing before and after drug, and test whether survivors come from clones with a particular mtDNA haplotype or from heteroplasmy shifts.

title: Sorting by intracellular drug accumulation
description: Use a fluorescent or intrinsically fluorescent analog of the drug, or mass-spectrometry imaging, to measure each cell's drug uptake and efflux pump activity. Sort cells into low, mid, and high accumulation bins, treat each bin, and test whether survival tracks pharmacokinetic heterogeneity rather than a molecular state.

title: Micropatterned adhesion area as a survival variable
description: Plate cells on fibronectin micropatterns of defined sizes to control spreading area and cytoskeletal tension, apply the drug, and quantify survival against area. Test whether YAP/TAZ nuclear localization and nuclear size explain which cells survive, which would indicate that mechanics determines persistence.

title: Paracrine protection from dying neighbors
description: Test whether dying cells release factors that protect neighboring cells. Use transwell co-cultures, conditioned medium from drug-killed cells with extracellular vesicles removed by ultracentrifugation, and proteomic or metabolite profiling of that medium. Then apply the candidate protective factor to naive cells to see whether it rescues them from drug.

title: Ferroptosis threshold and membrane lipid composition
description: Sort or image cells for lipid peroxidation with C11-BODIPY and profile membrane phospholipid acyl chains by lipidomics, comparing survivors and non-survivors. Then add a GPX4 or ferroptosis inhibitor and a polyunsaturated fatty acid challenge to test whether survivors are less susceptible to lipid peroxidation.

title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy as a natural lineage barcode
description: Sequence mtDNA variants and copy number in single cells (e.g., mtscATAC or single-cell mtDNA sequencing) before treatment and after drug selection, using naturally occurring heteroplasmy as a heritable lineage marker. If survivors are enriched for particular mtDNA haplotypes or respiratory-capacity states, that points to oxidative-phosphorylation fitness as a pre-existing determinant of tolerance, testable by swapping mitochondria with cybrids.

title: Asymmetric partitioning of drug at mitosis
description: Use a click-tagged or intrinsically fluorescent drug analog to track by live imaging how intracellular drug is divided between daughter cells during division. If one daughter systematically inherits less drug or more efflux-pump protein, survival of that lineage would reflect stochastic segregation rather than a stable cell state.

title: Per-cell target protein turnover measured by HaloTag pulse-chase
description: Endogenously tag the drug target with a HaloTag, pulse-label with a cell-permeant dye, and measure the per-cell synthesis and degradation rate of the existing protein pool by time-lapse imaging under treatment. Survivors may have slower target turnover or a higher replacement rate that buffers drug occupancy, which can be tested by modulating proteasomal or lysosomal degradation.

title: Pre-treatment optical redox imaging to sort by metabolic state
description: Image NAD(P)H and FAD autofluorescence in living cells to compute an optical redox ratio for each cell before drug exposure, then sort the extremes and test drug response in each fraction. This label-free readout captures mitochondrial and glycolytic balance without genetic perturbation, and can reveal whether tolerance follows a continuous metabolic gradient rather than a discrete subpopulation.

title: Spatial neighborhood mapping of survivors in dense versus sparse colonies
description: After treatment, map surviving cells in situ (multiplexed imaging or spatial transcriptomics) and quantify survival as a function of local neighbor density and contact with dying cells. If survival depends on local neighborhood rather than intrinsic cell identity, the mechanism involves community or contact-dependent protection, which can be tested by co-culture and conditioned-medium experiments.

title: Single-cell BH3 profiling for apoptotic priming
description: Before drug exposure, measure each cell's mitochondrial apoptotic priming by exposing permeabilized cells to BH3 peptides and quantifying cytochrome c release. Sort cells by priming level and test whether the least-primed fraction is enriched for survivors, which would show that persistence reflects a sub-lethal apoptotic threshold rather than a specific signaling state.

title: Mitotic partitioning of drug target and efflux capacity
description: Tag the drug target and an efflux or drug-metabolizing protein with photoconvertible or split fluorescent reporters, then follow individual divisions by time-lapse. Test whether one daughter cell inherits a low target or high efflux load, and whether persisters preferentially descend from the asymmetrically endowed sister.

title: Natural mtDNA heteroplasmy as a lineage marker
description: Deep-sequence the mitochondrial genome of the parental population and of survivors to find pre-existing mtDNA variants that serve as native lineage tags. Enrichment of specific mtDNA haplotypes among survivors would indicate that heritable mitochondrial background underlies persistence, and an ethidium-bromide-depleted arm would test whether this depends on oxidative phosphorylation.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification with lysosomal probes
description: Measure the free intracellular concentration of the drug in individual cells, using intrinsic fluorescence or a clickable analog, together with LysoTracker-based acidic compartment volume. Survivors with low cytosolic drug despite equal extracellular dosing would indicate that sequestration of the drug is a cause of persistence, separate from target biology.

title: Density-dependent autocrine rescue and conditioned-medium swap
description: Titrate seeding density and swap conditioned medium between high- and low-density cultures before drug addition to test whether the persister fraction depends on secreted factors accumulated by neighboring cells. If the effect is medium-borne, fractionate the conditioned medium (e.g., by size exclusion) to isolate the protective factor.

title: Single-cell intracellular drug-load mapping
description: Quantify how much drug each cell accumulates, using intrinsic fluorescence of the drug, an isotope-labeled analog, or imaging mass spectrometry, and link each cell's drug load to its survival over time. If survivors take up or retain less drug, the mechanism is pharmacokinetic rather than signaling-based, which would call for dosing or transporter interventions rather than pathway inhibitors.

title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy profiling of survivors
description: Call mtDNA variants and estimate heteroplasmy in single cells using reads from existing scATAC or scRNA-seq data (for example with mgatk), then compare survivors to non-survivors. This tests the assumption that the population is genetically identical, since mtDNA is not controlled by nuclear clonality, and can reveal inherited mitochondrial genotypes that shape drug tolerance.

title: Membrane potential sorting with ion-channel perturbation
description: Stain live cells with voltage-sensitive dyes to measure resting membrane potential, sort the hyperpolarized and depolarized fractions, and re-challenge each with the drug. Then test whether pharmacological or genetic changes to specific K+ or Cl- channels shift the survival fraction, which would indicate a bioelectric state that predisposes cells to tolerance.

title: Test of survival signaling from dead neighbors
description: Encapsulate single cells or defined small numbers of cells in droplets with and without supernatant or lysate from drug-killed cells, then score survival by droplet. Fractionate the active material and identify it by mass spectrometry, to test whether dying neighbors release factors that rescue survivors.

title: Nuclear deformability and envelope-rupture phenotyping
description: Use real-time deformability cytometry to measure nuclear stiffness in untreated cells, sort by deformability, and track drug-induced nuclear envelope rupture with a fluorescent NLS reporter. Correlate lamin A/C levels with survival to test whether nuclear mechanics, rather than signaling, gates early drug-induced damage.

title: Mother-daughter inheritance of protein aggregates
description: Express an aggregation-prone fluorescent reporter or an HSP70 chaperone sensor, then track mother-daughter pairs through mitosis during drug exposure. Test whether daughters that inherit a low aggregate or damaged-protein burden are the ones that survive, which would indicate that persistence reflects asymmetric inheritance of proteostatic burden rather than a fixed transcriptional state.

title: Micropatterned mapping of survival by density and position
description: Plate cells on micropatterned islands of defined size and shape so that local density and edge position are controlled, then measure where survivors arise within each island. If survival clusters at specific positions regardless of genotype, the trait is a community or geometry effect rather than a cell-intrinsic one.

title: Single-cell intracellular drug quantification linked to fate
description: Measure the intracellular concentration of the drug in individual cells by imaging mass spectrometry or by a fluorescent or isotopically labeled analog, then sort or back-gate cells by drug content and test their survival. This separates pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (differences in uptake, efflux, or metabolism) from genuine target-state differences.

title: Baseline nascent translation rate as a survival predictor
description: Quantify per-cell nascent protein synthesis before treatment using puromycin or OPP click labeling, sort high and low translators, and compare their drug response and survival. This tests whether translational capacity, rather than transcription, determines how much stress response a cell can mount.

title: Secretome-mediated rescue of naive cells
description: Collect conditioned medium or extracellular vesicles from drug-treated cultures enriched for survivors and apply them to naive cells under drug, then identify the active factors by proteomics and a neutralizing-antibody or vesicle-depletion screen. A positive rescue would indicate that survival can be extrinsically conferred between cells, not only inherited.

title: Barcode-based lineage tracing through a drug pulse
description: Label each progenitor cell with a heritable CRISPR or lentiviral barcode (e.g., CellTag or LARRY), treat the population, and sequence survivors to test whether they come from a pre-existing clone or arise de novo. This tests whether survival tracks a specific pre-marked lineage rather than stochastic induction.

title: Live-cell ERK/AKT pulse tracking linked to fate
description: Use fluorescent kinase translocation reporters and time-lapse microscopy to record signaling dynamics in individual cells during the first hours of drug exposure, then score each cell's eventual fate. Test whether the amplitude or timing of early signaling pulses predicts survival better than baseline pathway activity measured before treatment.

title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility to identify epigenetic priming
description: Profile untreated cells with joint scATAC-seq and RNA (multiome) and map which enhancers are already open in the cells that later survive, linking them to bypass or stress-response programs. This tests whether persisters are epigenetically primed before any drug exposure.

title: Dependency screens restricted to the drug-tolerant state
description: Sort or enrich drug-tolerant cells, then run a pooled CRISPR knockout screen (in vitro or in vivo) only in that state to find genes essential for survival under drug but dispensable in bulk cells. The expected result is a small set of survival dependencies, unrelated to the drug target, that could be co-targeted to eliminate persisters.

title: Asymmetric organelle inheritance during division
description: Label mitochondria, lysosomes, and drug efflux machinery with distinct fluorescent tags and track how they partition at mitosis. Then test whether daughter cells that inherit a larger share of efflux or mitochondrial capacity are the ones that survive, which would indicate that survival depends on how damaged or protective organelles are divided between daughters rather than on gene expression differences between parent cells.

title: Pre-treatment lineage barcoding to identify pre-existing survivor states
description: Label individual cells with heritable barcodes (e.g., CellTag lineage tags), expose the population to a targeted drug, and trace which clones persist. If survivors already carried a distinct barcode-linked state before treatment, random switching does not explain survival and the pre-existing state becomes the target.

title: Baseline multi-omic classifier with prospective sort-and-treat validation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and transcription in drug-naive cells at single-cell resolution and train a classifier that predicts which cells will survive. Then sort the predicted survivors and treat them with drug to check the prediction. Success or failure of this prospective test shows whether a survival signature exists before any drug exposure.

title: Live reporters of drug engagement and cell-cycle state at the time of dosing
description: Combine a kinase or target-occupancy biosensor with a cell-cycle reporter (e.g., FUCCI) and time-lapse imaging to record each cell's drug binding and cycling status at the moment of treatment. Retrospectively tracking which cells remain unbound, quiescent, or efflux-high would show whether survival is determined by drug pharmacology rather than by intrinsic cell biology.

title: Pulsed-dose CRISPR screens for persister-specific dependencies
description: Run genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens at multiple timepoints during intermittent (pulsed) drug exposure rather than a single high dose, and compare guide dropout in persisters versus bulk cells. Genes essential only in the persister state would reveal therapeutic vulnerabilities that bulk-cell screens miss.

title: Epigenetic inheritance of survival across drug holidays, tested with epigenetic editing
description: Track chromatin marks (ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag for histone modifications) across drug holidays and regrowth to see whether the survival state is inherited epigenetically. Then use targeted epigenetic editors to erase or install the marks and test whether survival is lost or gained without any genetic change.

title: Barcode lineage tracing before and after drug exposure
description: Label thousands of genetically identical cells with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., CellTag or LARRY), treat with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes plus transcriptomes at intervals. Determining whether survivor clones were already present before treatment or arose de novo from drug-exposed cells shows whether survival is pre-selected or induced.

title: Live ERK/AKT reporter tracking of survivor cells
description: Use fluorescent kinase-activity biosensors (ERK-KTR, AKT-KTR) and time-lapse microscopy to follow individual cells through drug exposure, then recover and sort the survivors. Pre-treatment signaling dynamics, such as pulse frequency or basal activity, may predict which cells persist.

title: Single-cell multiome of pre-treatment cells to find a chromatin priming signature
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and gene expression together (scATAC plus scRNA) in drug-naive cells, then sort and compare cells that later survive versus those that die, using a reporter or live-cell marker. A chromatin-state signature present before any drug exposure would indicate epigenetic priming.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen in persister-enriched populations
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens under sustained drug pressure with a sub-lethal dose, and compare guide representation in the rare surviving population against controls. Genes whose loss or gain changes survival, especially those that act only in the tolerant state, would point to the mechanism.

title: Single-cell metabolic and mitochondrial imaging of survivors
description: Combine live metabolic readouts (NAD(P)H autofluorescence, TMRM for membrane potential, or Seahorse measurements on sorted cells) with single-cell RNA-seq to test whether slow-cycling, oxidative-phosphorylation-high cells are the drug-tolerant fraction. Then perturb mitochondrial function in those cells to test whether the metabolic state is causal.

title: Lineage barcoding with live-cell fate tracking
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., CellTag-style) and track each lineage by time-lapse imaging through drug exposure and washout. This reveals whether survivors come from a pre-existing clone or arise stochastically within lineages that were initially sensitive.

title: Pre-treatment multi-omic profiling linked to later fate
description: Profile individual cells before treatment with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, or index-sort them, then follow the same cells' fates with a live reporter of drug response. Searching for baseline chromatin or expression signatures that predict survival tests whether survival is encoded before the drug is added.

title: Reversibility kinetics after drug withdrawal
description: Use a fluorescent chromatin-state reporter (for example, an H3K27me3 or H3K4me3 sensor) and measure at single-cell resolution over days how survivors revert to sensitivity after drug removal. Whether the survival state decays on a predictable timescale distinguishes a heritable epigenetic memory from a reversible, non-genetic switch.

title: Pulsed-drug Perturb-seq screen
description: Run a pooled CRISPR perturbation screen with single-cell RNA readout while cells receive short drug pulses rather than constant exposure. Genes whose knockdown changes the probability of survival, rather than just the average response, reveal the regulators that control entry into the tolerant state.

title: Spatial mapping of survivors within tumor niches
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on treated tumors or organoids to locate surviving cells relative to hypoxic zones, stromal contact, and vasculature. If survival clusters in specific niches, then niche-dependent signals, not intrinsic cell heterogeneity alone, drive persistence, making the niche a therapeutic target.

title: Distinguishing heritable from induced survival by lineage barcoding
description: Label a founder population with a dense, heritable barcode library (e.g., CellTag), apply a targeted drug pulse, and track barcode frequencies over time. If survivors share barcodes with pre-treatment clones, survival is pre-existing and selected; if they do not, it reflects drug-induced state switching.

title: Pre-treatment single-cell multiome to predict survivors
description: Profile the untreated population with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, then sort or sequence the cells that persist after treatment and project them back onto the baseline map. Identifying a pre-existing chromatin and expression state that marks the eventual survivors would make persistence a predictable, measurable trait.

title: Live reporters of epigenetic memory with drug washout
description: Use fluorescent reporters for histone marks or chromatin-state readouts, combined with time-lapse imaging and drug washout, to follow individual cells through treatment and regrowth. Measuring whether the survival state is inherited across divisions or reset after drug removal distinguishes stable epigenetic memory from reversible, stochastic tolerance.

title: Single-cell intracellular drug accumulation mapping
description: Quantify intracellular concentration of the drug in individual cells, for example with a fluorescent analog or mass-spectrometry imaging, alongside efflux transporter expression. If rare cells keep sub-lethal drug levels because of low uptake or high efflux, survival is explained by single-cell drug pharmacokinetics rather than by cell-state biology.

title: Time-resolved CRISPR screen under sub-lethal dosing
description: Run a pooled CRISPR knockout library at a sub-lethal drug dose and sort cells at multiple time points, rather than only at endpoint. Genes whose loss kills cells early but not late, or that enrich only in the persister fraction, reveal the sequence of adaptive steps that build tolerance and suggest which dependencies to target.

title: Lineage barcoding plus single-cell transcriptomics before and during drug exposure
description: Tag each founder cell with a heritable barcode, treat the population, and profile surviving clones by scRNA-seq at baseline and early timepoints. This tests whether survivors were already transcriptionally distinct before treatment (pre-existing tolerance) or switched state after exposure (induced tolerance).

title: Chromatin accessibility time course to find a primed epigenetic state
description: Run single-cell ATAC-seq across a drug time course and align the profiles with later survival, so the chromatin landscape of cells that will persist can be compared with that of cells that will die. Accessibility at lineage or stress-response enhancers that is already open before treatment would indicate epigenetic priming.

title: Live-cell fate tracking with reporters, then sort and re-challenge
description: Use fluorescent reporters for cell-cycle phase, stress signalling (e.g., NRF2 or p53 activity), and mitochondrial state to follow individual cells under drug, then recover the cells that survive and re-challenge them. Reporter states that predict eventual survival identify the decisive variable.

title: Time-resolved pooled CRISPR knockout screen of persistence entry and exit
description: Perform a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen with samples taken at multiple points during drug exposure and during drug withdrawal, not only at the endpoint. Genes whose loss changes the rate of entering the tolerant state, or the chance of regrowing from it, would separate mechanisms that initiate persistence from those that sustain it.

title: Pre-treatment metabolic imaging to predict survival
description: Measure single-cell metabolic readouts such as NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime imaging and mitochondrial membrane potential in untreated cultures, then score each cell's metabolic state against its later survival under drug. A predictive metabolic signature before treatment would show whether survival is set by a baseline metabolic state.

title: Lineage-barcoded live imaging of pre-treatment cells
description: Tag each cell with a heritable DNA barcode, image live cells under drug, and sequence barcodes at endpoints to test whether survivors descend from a pre-existing rare clone or arise de novo after exposure. Comparing barcode frequencies before and after treatment separates pre-existing from induced tolerance.

title: Paired single-cell multiomics to find pre-treatment predictors
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and transcription together (paired scATAC and scRNA) in untreated cells, then sort the rarest predicted-tolerant states and test whether they alone survive drug exposure. This checks whether a pre-existing epigenetic state is sufficient for survival, not just correlated with it.

title: Dose-timed pooled CRISPR screens on sorted survivors
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens with the drug added at defined times, then compare guide representation in sorted early survivors versus the bulk population. Genes whose perturbation changes survival probability reveal the mechanisms that control tolerance rather than just marking it.

title: Label retention and metabolic imaging of persisters
description: Use dye dilution (e.g., CFSE) to isolate slow-cycling cells and, in parallel, FLIM of NAD(P)H or mitochondrial reporters to measure each cell's metabolic state before and during drug exposure. Correlate these live readouts with later survival to test whether quiescence or oxidative metabolism predicts which cells persist.

title: Drug-holiday reversion kinetics with fate-model fitting
description: Expose cells to drug, withdraw it at intervals, and track how quickly survivors revert to drug-sensitive behavior. Fit stochastic switching and heritable memory models to the lineage-resolved fate data; reversion timescales distinguish reversible non-genetic switching from stable epigenetic memory, which predict different clinical dosing strategies.

title: Heritable lineage barcoding with pre-treatment tracking
description: Introduce a CRISPR-based lineage recorder into a clonal cancer line, then follow single-cell lineages by time-lapse imaging through a drug pulse and sequence barcodes in survivors. If survivors cluster in lineages already distinguishable before treatment, persistence is pre-specified rather than drug-induced.

title: Sorting on a pre-treatment reporter and re-challenging
description: Build a live reporter for a candidate persister-associated transcription factor or chromatin state, sort reporter-high and reporter-low cells before any drug exposure, and measure each sorted population's survival under drug. A large survival difference between sorted pools would show that a pre-existing state, not random chance, determines which cells survive.

title: Temporally staged pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell readout
description: Run a pooled CRISPR perturbation screen with drug added at several time points. Read out each perturbation by single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing. This shows which regulators are required to enter, maintain, or exit the tolerant state, and when each one acts.

title: Label-free metabolic imaging of single cells before treatment
description: Use fluorescence lifetime imaging of NAD(P)H or Raman spectroscopy to classify individual living cells by metabolic state before drug exposure, then track which metabolic profiles survive. Sort cells by that profile and test metabolic inhibitors to determine whether survivors depend on a specific energy pathway.

title: Spatial mapping of persisters within intact tumors
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to patient-derived xenograft tumors taken during and after treatment, and map where persister cells sit relative to vasculature, hypoxia, and stromal neighbors. If survivors are concentrated in particular niches, niche signals rather than intrinsic cell properties would be the main driver of survival.

title: Barcoded scRNA-seq to test for pre-existing survivor states
description: Label an isogenic population with a lineage barcode library, profile single-cell transcriptomes before drug exposure, and then at several time points during treatment. Compare barcoded clones to see whether survivors already carried a distinct expression program before treatment, or whether they acquired it only under drug, with no genetic change in either case.

title: Live-cell lineage tracking with cell-cycle and stress reporters, plus washout
description: Use time-lapse imaging of FUCCI or p21/ERK biosensor reporter cells under drug to follow each cell's fate, cycling history and switching rate over days. Remove the drug at defined points to test whether the tolerant state reverses (non-genetic, reversible persistence) or stays heritable.

title: Sorting cells by pre-treatment metabolic state
description: Measure single-cell metabolic state with NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime imaging or SCENITH, then sort cells by their pre-treatment metabolic profile and track which sorted fractions survive. Test with targeted inhibitors whether survivors depend on oxidative phosphorylation or fatty-acid oxidation.

title: Paracrine protection assay using survivor secretomes
description: Co-culture sorted survivors with drug-sensitive cells under treatment, and profile the survivor secretome by mass spectrometry and cytokine arrays. Test candidate factors by conditioned-media experiments and by knocking them down in survivors, to see whether survivors keep neighboring cells alive.

title: Sublethal-dose CRISPR screen and chromatin profiling of the tolerant state
description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen at a sublethal dose to find genes whose loss prevents the tolerant state, and pair it with scATAC-seq and CUT&Tag on sorted persisters to map the accompanying chromatin changes. Dosing across a graded range of drug strengths maps the threshold at which survivors emerge, and checking whether the chromatin state persists after a drug holiday tests for epigenetic memory.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with drug-pulse timing
description: Label each founder cell with a heritable DNA barcode, expose the population to the drug, and track which clones persist. If survivors are already present before treatment, their barcodes will appear in the pre-treatment sample, and their lineage history will show whether they are stable pre-existing persisters or cells that switched state under drug.

title: Time-resolved single-cell multiomics across the drug response
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on the same cells at several times during the first days of treatment, and cluster the cells to find a transcriptional or chromatin state enriched before the drug takes effect or during the early tolerant window. Comparing the state of cells that survive with that of cells that die shows whether the survivors were already different before treatment.

title: Epigenetic memory test using drug holidays and sorted survivors
description: Sort drug-tolerant survivors and profile their chromatin (ATAC-seq, H3K27ac/H3K4me3 CUT&Tag, and DNA methylation) against drug-naive controls. Then release the survivors from drug for several weeks and repeat the profiling. Chromatin marks that persist after release indicate heritable epigenetic memory, while marks that reset indicate reversible adaptation.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen comparing survivors to controls
description: Perform a pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screen under sustained drug exposure and compare guide abundance in surviving cells against an untreated reference at several time points. Genes whose loss consistently changes survival identify pathways the survivors depend on, such as stress signalling, drug efflux, or mitochondrial or NAD metabolism. Follow up with knockouts of the top hits in both survivor-enriched and non-enriched lines to test whether these pathways are necessary for persistence.

title: Spatial and live metabolic mapping of survivor niches
description: Use multiplexed spatial imaging or spatial transcriptomics on tumour sections or 3D organoids during treatment to locate surviving cells relative to hypoxic, stromal, or immune niches. In parallel, use fluorescence lifetime imaging of NAD(P)H and FAD to measure the metabolic state of individual living cells, and sort survivors by that state to test whether it predicts persistence.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with live fate tracking
description: Label genetically identical cells with unique heritable DNA barcodes, then apply a drug pulse and track each lineage by time-lapse imaging and barcode sequencing. This separates cells that were already tolerant from cells that switched into a tolerant state after treatment, and shows whether survival is a stable inherited trait or a reversible, stochastic state that changes over time.

title: Pre-treatment single-cell multi-omics to predict survival
description: Profile untreated cells with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq), then sort or computationally match cells by their eventual fate after treatment. Train a classifier on pre-treatment transcriptional and chromatin states to identify rare pre-existing programs (for example, a slow-cycling or stress-response state) that predict survival before any drug is given.

title: Live single-cell kinetic reporters of drug-target signaling
description: Express FRET biosensors for the drug target's downstream pathway (e.g., ERK or AKT activity) and a cell-cycle reporter, then record signaling dynamics in each cell during drug exposure. Comparing the timing, amplitude, and recovery of pathway suppression between survivors and dying cells tests whether rapid rebound or slow, incomplete pathway shutdown explains persistence.

title: Spatial mapping of survivor niches before, during, and after treatment
description: Use multiplexed spatial imaging (e.g., MERFISH, CODEX, or imaging mass cytometry) on tumor sections or organoids collected before treatment, during treatment, and at relapse. Analyze the local neighborhood, oxygenation, extracellular matrix, and proximity to stromal or immune cells to determine whether survivors occupy a distinct protective microenvironment.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen with reversibility and re-challenge tests
description: Run a pooled CRISPR knockout screen under sustained drug treatment, comparing guide enrichment in survivors versus the starting population, then validate hits in sorted survivors that are released from drug and re-challenged. Measuring whether tolerance is reversible and whether knockouts shift the survival fraction distinguishes genetic resistance from transient, epigenetically maintained persistence.

title: Lineage-barcode tracing of persister origins
description: Label drug-naive cells with a heritable lentiviral or CRISPR barcode library (e.g., LARRY or CellTag), apply the drug, and sequence barcodes in surviving clones. Compare barcode frequencies before and after treatment and across independent replicates to show whether persisters descend from a pre-marked subpopulation or arise de novo from unmarked cells.

title: Pre-treatment single-cell multiomics to find predictive states
description: Profile drug-naive populations with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, then use machine learning to find chromatin and expression signatures that predict which cells later survive. Validate by sorting live cells on the top predictive markers (for example AXL, NGFR, or a slow-cycling reporter) and testing their drug survival in vitro and in xenografts.

title: Live-cell reporter tracking with washout and re-challenge
description: Use fluorescent reporters of candidate persister states together with time-lapse imaging to follow individual cells through drug exposure, drug holiday, and re-challenge. Measuring switching rates, lag times, and whether state memory persists after withdrawal distinguishes stochastic non-genetic switching from instructive, drug-induced reprogramming, and fitting these data with stochastic models quantifies the rates.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens for genes that gate survival
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRa screens under sustained drug pressure and compare sgRNA dropout between early persisters and established resistant populations. Hits that block or enable entry into the persister state, especially genes whose loss changes chromatin accessibility, identify the link between transient tolerance and stable resistance.

title: Spatial mapping of persisters within their niche
description: Apply multiplexed spatial transcriptomics or imaging to residual tumor sections from treated patients or organoids, and measure how persister cells' distance and contact with vasculature, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and extracellular matrix relate to their state. Co-culture experiments with and without the niche components then test whether surrounding cells supply signals that allow a few cells to survive.

title: Pre-treatment state sorting to test whether survivors were distinct before the drug
description: Profile untreated cells with single-cell multiome (RNA plus ATAC) or live-cell fluorescent reporters of stress and chromatin states, then sort or computationally link pre-existing states to later survival after drug exposure. If persisters were already distinct before treatment, the rare state is a pre-existing cell state rather than a drug-induced change.

title: Lineage-barcoded clone tracking through drug holidays and re-challenge
description: Label cells with heritable lentiviral DNA barcodes, then track clone frequencies through repeated drug pulses, drug-free holidays, and re-challenge. Stable clonal resistance should persist across cycles, whereas transient tolerance should reset, which separates genetic or epigenetic memory from a transient state.

title: Washout kinetics: how long does the survivor state last?
description: After removing the drug, measure how quickly persisters regain drug sensitivity and resume proliferation, using time-lapse imaging and reversion rates at single-cell resolution. Pair this with CUT&Tag for repressive and active histone marks (H3K27me3, H3K4me3) to test whether the reversible state depends on chromatin memory that fades over time.

title: Longitudinal multiomic trajectory from sensitive cell to persister
description: Collect scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq at closely spaced timepoints from hours to weeks after drug addition, then reconstruct the ordered path of state transitions with RNA velocity and chromatin trajectory inference. This identifies the transcription factors that drive the transition and shows whether there is a single route or several distinct routes to survival.

title: Genetic versus nongenetic dissection with deep sequencing and CRISPR screens
description: Deep-sequence survivors against their pre-treatment population to detect rare pre-existing mutations or copy-number subclones, and run genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens in persisters versus bulk cells under drug. Together these show whether survival is selected from a genetic subpopulation or is nongenetic, and reveal dependencies of persisters that could be targeted to eliminate them.

title: Lineage barcoding with drug-pulse single-cell profiling
description: Label genetically identical cells with heritable lineage barcodes (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcodes), expose them to the drug, and run scRNA-seq at several time points. This determines whether survivors come from a pre-existing barcoded subclone or arise de novo from drug-induced state switching.

title: Pre-treatment profiling linked to later fate
description: Use live-cell imaging of reporters (e.g., FUCCI for cell cycle, or a chromatin-accessibility or lineage reporter) before drug exposure, then fix or sort cells and profile them with scRNA-seq or ATAC-seq to see whether survivors were already distinguishable before treatment. Predictive baseline markers would support a pre-existing-state model.

title: Live-cell kinase biosensor tracking of signaling dynamics
description: Express FRET-based ERK and AKT activity biosensors and track single cells through drug treatment by time-lapse microscopy, comparing the signaling pulse patterns of cells that die with those that persist. This tests whether the intensity and timing of pathway activity during treatment predict survival.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens of survivors versus bulk
description: Run genome-wide or focused CRISPR knockout and CRISPRi screens, comparing guide representation in surviving cells against untreated controls under drug, to identify genes whose loss enriches or depletes persisters. Hits that are essential only in the persister state would point to targetable vulnerabilities that the drug alone does not reveal.

title: Washout, re-challenge, and epigenetic memory assays
description: Remove the drug after the surviving population has formed, then re-challenge and profile chromatin (ATAC-seq, H3K27ac or H3K4me3 CUT&Tag) and metabolic state (e.g., OXPHOS dependence) to test whether the persister phenotype is reversible and heritable. Stable epigenetic memory would suggest a regulated state transition rather than a fixed genetic one.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from induced persisters
description: Label a clonal population with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcode libraries), treat with the drug, and sequence the survivors to determine whether they come from a few barcoded clones present before treatment or arise de novo. Each barcode marks a defined lineage that can be tracked, and drug-washout and re-challenge cycles show whether the survival state is reversible.

title: Pre-treatment reporter sorting with time-resolved single-cell RNA-seq
description: Use live fluorescent reporters (e.g., FUCCI for cell-cycle phase or stress-pathway reporters) to sort cells before drug exposure and then profile them by scRNA-seq at multiple time points, looking for a transcriptional state that predicts survival. This tests whether persisters are already present in the population before treatment.

title: Chromatin accessibility profiling of persisters versus naive cells
description: Run single-cell ATAC-seq on cells at baseline, during early drug exposure, and in the surviving fraction to find chromatin regions that open or close in persisters. Then withdraw the drug and check whether the accessibility profile returns to baseline, to test whether the changes are stable epigenetic memory or reversible plasticity.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen on sorted or re-challenged persisters
description: Introduce a genome-wide or focused CRISPR knockout library, apply the drug, and compare guide representation in survivors against the untreated population to find genes whose loss blocks or enhances survival. Hits that act in both the early and late phases of treatment would point to a common survival program, and a minimal set of such hits could be validated individually.

title: Spatial profiling of persister niches in vivo or in organoids
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging (e.g., MERFISH or CODEX) on treated tumors or organoids to check whether surviving cells cluster in particular microenvironments, such as hypoxic zones, vascular niches, or contact with stromal cells. If survival depends on location, the explanation lies partly in the cell's surroundings rather than in its intrinsic state alone.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing to test pre-existing versus induced survival
description: Label each cell with a heritable DNA barcode before treatment, then compare barcode frequencies in survivors with pre-treatment frequencies to see whether survivors descend from a few pre-existing clones or arise de novo from many lineages. Pair this with single-cell RNA-seq of barcoded cells to link each survivor's clone to its baseline state.

title: Time-lapse reporter imaging of fluctuating drug-tolerant states
description: Use live-cell fluorescent reporters for candidate survival pathways (such as cell-cycle or stress-response transcription factors) and track individual cells over days of drug exposure, scoring whether tolerance is a transient fluctuation that reverses or a stable heritable state. Measure whether tolerance is inherited across divisions and whether it depends on pre-treatment reporter levels.

title: Pre-treatment profiling of cells that later survive
description: Use a dye-based or reporter-based sort to isolate cells from the untreated population that are most likely to survive, then profile their chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq), transcriptome, and proteome before any drug exposure. Compare these profiles with those of cells that die to identify baseline predictors of survival that could be targeted or used as biomarkers.

title: Spatial mapping of survivors within the tumour niche
description: Apply multiplexed spatial transcriptomics or imaging mass cytometry to treated tumour sections or organoids to locate surviving cells relative to hypoxic zones, vasculature, stromal cells, and cell-cell contacts. Test whether survival clusters in particular microenvironments and whether ligand-receptor signals from those niches protect cells from the drug.

title: CRISPR screening combined with drug-holiday and re-challenge assays
description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout or activation screen during drug exposure and compare guide enrichment in survivors versus controls to find genes required for survival. Then apply drug holidays and re-challenges to test whether survival is reversible and whether the identified genes are needed for regrowth, separating persistent cell states from permanent genetic resistance.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with live cell-cycle reporters
description: Label each founder cell with a heritable DNA barcode and a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter, then image the population through drug exposure to see whether survivors were already slow-cycling or in a distinct state before treatment. Comparing survivor clones with their pre-treatment lineage shows whether persistence is pre-existing and inherited or arises de novo.

title: Single-cell multiomics on early persister cells
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on cells sorted at multiple early time points after drug exposure, and compare the chromatin accessibility and transcriptional states of survivors with those of cells that die. This tests whether a pre-existing or rapidly induced tolerant state, marked by chromatin regions that may act as insulators gating gene programs, predicts survival.

title: Drug-holiday and re-challenge test of heritable epigenetic memory
description: Expose cells to the drug, withdraw it until survivors regrow, then re-challenge them, while profiling histone marks (CUT&RUN for H3K27ac and H3K4me3) at each step. If the survivors' tolerance and chromatin state persist through several cell divisions without drug, the memory is stable; if both reset, the tolerance is reversible and non-genetic.

title: Per-cell drug accumulation biosensing linked to survival
description: Use a FRET-based intracellular drug biosensor or a fluorescent drug analogue with live imaging to measure how much drug each cell takes up and how fast it is effluxed, then track each cell's fate. Cells with low intracellular drug, from efflux-pump activity or reduced uptake, may be the survivors, so comparing uptake with the target-engagement readout (for example a phospho-reporter) tests whether the drug never reaches a lethal dose in those cells.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen comparing sublethal and lethal drug doses
description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screen in the cell line under both sublethal and lethal drug doses, then sequence the surviving pool to find guides that enrich or deplete. Hits that appear only at the lethal dose point to genes whose loss sensitizes or protects cells, and validating them one by one in single-clone experiments separates genetic causes from stochastic tolerance.

title: Heritable DNA barcode lineage tracing
description: Label a clonal population with a pooled lentiviral DNA barcode library, expand it, sample before treatment, and sequence barcodes in the survivors. If survivors carry barcodes already enriched before treatment, the tolerance was pre-existing in a rare lineage; if the barcode distribution is unchanged, survivors arose from non-heritable switching, which can be tested with single-cell RNA-seq of the same barcoded cells.

title: Drug-withdrawal and re-challenge assay
description: Treat cells until the surviving fraction plateaus, remove the drug, and track regrowth and drug sensitivity over several passages before re-challenging. Survivors that regain full sensitivity indicate a reversible, plastic persister state, while survivors that stay tolerant indicate a heritable genetic or epigenetic change.

title: Pre-treatment reporter tracking in live cells
description: Use time-lapse microscopy of cells carrying fluorescent reporters for cell-cycle phase (e.g., FUCCI) and pathway activity (e.g., an ERK kinase translocation reporter) to record each cell's state before adding the drug and its fate afterward. Comparing the pre-treatment reporter states of cells that die with those that survive shows whether a measurable pre-existing state predicts survival.

title: Pooled genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen of survivors
description: Transduce cells with a genome-wide sgRNA library, apply a lethal dose of the drug, and compare guide abundance in survivors to the untreated population. Genes whose knockout enriches or depletes survivors reveal the mechanisms that protect cells, and the hits can be validated individually and tested for synthetic interactions with the drug.

title: Dye-dilution division history combined with single-cell multi-omics
description: Label cells with a dye that halves with every division, such as CFSE, before treatment, then sort the survivors by dye intensity to find out whether they divided less often than the bulk population. Profile the sorted slow-cycling survivors with single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq to test whether the survivors occupy a distinct quiescent, chromatin-accessible state that could be targeted.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing across a drug pulse
description: Label each starting cell with a unique heritable barcode (e.g., lentiviral or CRISPR-based), treat with the drug, and sequence barcodes in survivors versus the pre-treatment pool. This distinguishes survivors that were already present (pre-existing persisters, where one barcode's clone expands from a single founder) from cells that transiently switched state after treatment.

title: Pre-treatment single-cell profiling linked to outcome
description: Run scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on the untreated population, then use live-cell or FACS-based sorting to isolate candidate cells (e.g., slow-cycling, high-AXL, or specific chromatin-accessibility states) before drug exposure. Test whether these sorted subpopulations are enriched for survival, which would show the tolerant state is predictable from baseline.

title: Live-cell fate tracking with signaling and cell-cycle reporters
description: Use FUCCI cell-cycle reporters and ERK or AKT activity biosensors in time-lapse microscopy during drug exposure, then correlate each cell's pre-treatment reporter state with whether it dies or divides. This links the survival decision to the signaling dynamics of individual cells rather than population averages.

title: Washout and re-challenge to test reversibility
description: Expose cultures to the drug, remove it for varying periods, and re-challenge, while tracking survivors' chromatin state (ATAC/CUT&Tag for H3K27me3 or H3K4me3) and transcriptome. If survivors revert to the drug-sensitive state, the tolerance is nongenetic and epigenetically reversible; if not, it indicates stable adaptation.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen comparing sublethal and lethal dosing
description: Perform a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen at a sublethal drug dose that allows a small fraction to survive, and compare guide enrichment in survivors against the untreated library. Validate top hits by knocking them out individually and measuring the survival fraction, which identifies the genes that let a minority of cells escape the drug.

title: Lineage barcoding to test whether survival is bimodal and inherited
description: Label each cell with a heritable DNA barcode, expose the population to the drug, and check whether surviving clones were already present and sized before treatment. If survival is a bimodal, pre-existing trait, survivors will share barcodes with pre-treatment clones; if it is a stochastic, reversible switch, survivors will be spread across many barcodes with no pre-treatment enrichment.

title: Pre-treatment single-cell profiling of the untreated population
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on the untreated parental population, then score each cell's pre-existing expression and chromatin signature against its later survival, using barcodes or sorted reporter cells to link the two. This finds any pre-existing state (for example slow cycling or a particular chromatin configuration) that predisposes cells to persist under drug treatment.

title: Live-cell reporters of signaling and cell-cycle dynamics during drug exposure
description: Use time-lapse imaging with a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter and a kinase translocation reporter (for example ERK or AKT activity) to follow individual cells through the drug pulse. Test whether cells that eventually survive show distinct pathway rebound, a delayed cell cycle entry, or a transient signaling dip before the drug takes effect.

title: Re-challenge and metabolic profiling of sorted survivors
description: Sort the surviving cells, release them from drug for several passages, then re-challenge them to measure whether tolerance is heritable or reverts. In parallel, run Seahorse respirometry and metabolomics on survivors versus sensitive cells to test whether survivors maintain a stable internal metabolic state that buffers the drug's effects.

title: Pooled CRISPR knockout screen with single-cell readout
description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen under drug, comparing sequenced guide representation in survivors versus treated bulk. Pair this with single-cell readouts to see which knockouts change the probability of survival rather than just its magnitude. Hits such as chromatin regulators or stress-response genes would point to mechanisms that make some cells persist.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with drug pulses
description: Label each founder cell with a heritable DNA barcode, then apply the drug and sequence barcodes in survivors and in cells that re-expand after drug withdrawal. Shared barcodes between pre-treatment and surviving clones show whether survival is a pre-existing, inherited state or a stochastic, drug-induced switch.

title: Pre-treatment single-cell multiomics to find predictive states
description: Profile the same population by scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq before any drug exposure, then sort or computationally match cells that later survive using a live reporter. This reveals whether chromatin accessibility or compaction states predict persistence before the drug acts.

title: Live imaging of signaling dynamics and mechanical tension
description: Use a kinase translocation reporter (for example, an ERK biosensor) and a FRET-based tension sensor in time-lapse microscopy, and measure pathway activity and cytoskeletal stress in each cell after drug addition. Correlating these readouts with later fate tests whether the early signaling pulse or tension predicts survival.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen comparing survivors with bulk cells
description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screen under the drug and compare guide representation in surviving cells with the untreated population, using sgRNA sequencing at several time points. Hits enriched in survivors point to genes causing tolerance, and insertional or saturation mutagenesis can confirm them.

title: Metabolic and redox sorting followed by drug-holiday re-challenge
description: Sort cells by autofluorescence (NAD(P)H/FAD imaging) or mitochondrial membrane potential before treatment, then compare the metabolic profiles of later survivors with those of cells that die. Re-challenge the survivors after a drug holiday, or combine the drug with a metabolic inhibitor, to test whether the tolerant state is reversible.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing through drug exposure
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes before treatment, then sequence barcodes in survivors versus the pre-treatment pool. If survivors share barcodes with pre-existing clones, persistence is selection on pre-existing variation; if barcodes are diverse and survivors arise from many lineages, the program is more likely drug-induced.

title: Pre-treatment single-cell multi-omics linked to fate
description: Profile the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility (scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq) of untreated cells, then expose them to drug and track which cells survive. Train a classifier on the baseline profiles to predict survival, and validate by sorting cells on candidate markers (for example, slow-cycling or stress-tolerant states) and testing their drug tolerance in isolation.

title: Live-cell biosensor tracking of signaling dynamics
description: Use fluorescent reporters for pathway activity (such as ERK translocation reporters) and cell-cycle state (FUCCI) in time-lapse microscopy, recording each cell's history before and after drug addition. Compare the pre-treatment signaling dynamics and cell-cycle phase of cells that die with those that survive, to find dynamic features, not just average levels, that predict persistence.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens for persistence modifiers
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi/a screens under drug and vehicle conditions, using the persister fraction as the readout after treatment. Hits that enrich in survivors identify genes whose loss or gain changes tolerance, and combining them with chromatin profiling tests whether the effect runs through epigenetic memory.

title: Fluctuation analysis with washout and re-challenge
description: Measure persister frequency across drug doses, timepoints, and drug-withdrawal and re-challenge schedules, then fit stochastic models (for example, Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation tests) to separate pre-existing random switching from induced adaptation. Reversible tolerance that resets after withdrawal suggests a non-genetic state, while stable tolerance after reintroduction suggests heritable change; the dose-escalation schedule helps distinguish these.

title: Barcode lineage tracing with single-cell profiling before and after drug
description: Label each founder cell with a heritable DNA barcode (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcodes), then combine barcode tracking with scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq at baseline. Compare pre-treatment states of the clones that later survive to those that die, to test whether survival is predicted by a pre-existing dormant or slow-cycling state rather than new induction.

title: Live-cell reporters with sort-and-re-challenge reversibility assays
description: Use fluorescent cell-cycle reporters (e.g., FUCCI) and a fluorescent transcriptional marker of the candidate state in time-lapse imaging under drug to follow individual cells from treatment to regrowth. Sort the surviving fraction, release it from drug, and re-challenge, to test whether the tolerant state is reversible and heritable or a stochastic, transient switch.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen for survival and survivor-enriched gene loss
description: Run a pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screen under sub-lethal and lethal drug doses, and sequence guides in surviving cells versus untreated controls. Genes whose loss sensitizes or enriches survivors point to the causal pathways and separate true genetic resistance from non-genetic tolerance.

title: Chromatin and epigenetic profiling of sorted survivors
description: Isolate drug-tolerant cells early in treatment and profile chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), histone marks (H3K27me3, H3K4me3), and DNA methylation, comparing them with bulk and drug-naive populations. Chromatin regions that open or close consistently in survivors would suggest an epigenetic program that enables the tolerant state and could be targeted to block it.

title: Single-cell drug uptake, efflux, and metabolic flux measurements
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration and efflux-pump activity per cell using fluorescent drug analogues or LC-MS on sorted fractions, and pair this with 13C-glucose or glutamine isotope tracing to map metabolism in survivors. Differences in drug accumulation or a shift toward oxidative phosphorylation would show whether survival comes from pharmacokinetic variation or a metabolic adaptation that can be combined with the drug.

title: Lineage-barcoded live imaging to test whether survivors were pre-marked
description: Label a clonal population with heritable lineage barcodes and a fluorescent cell-cycle or stress reporter, then track single cells through drug exposure by time-lapse microscopy. Comparing pre-treatment reporter states of cells that survive with those that die tests whether survival is predicted by a transient, heritable, fluctuating expression state rather than by genetics.

title: Paired single-cell multiome of pre-treatment versus persister cells
description: Profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility (scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq) in the untreated population and in cells that persist after drug exposure, then identify which regulatory programs are already active before treatment. Enrichment of specific transcription-factor motifs or chromatin states in the survivors would indicate an epigenetic mechanism that can be validated experimentally.

title: Drug washout and re-challenge of reporter-sorted subpopulations
description: Sort cells by a fluorescent reporter of candidate persister genes, then remove the drug and re-challenge each sorted fraction with a dose-response curve and measure regrowth rate. This shows whether the pre-treatment state itself confers tolerance and whether it reverts over time or is stably inherited across divisions.

title: Adhesion and matrix-attachment perturbation screen in survivors
description: Compare focal-adhesion and integrin signaling in survivors versus killed cells, then run a targeted CRISPR knockout or small-molecule screen of adhesion genes (which anchor the cell to its substrate) during drug treatment. If loss of adhesion sensitizes persisters, adhesion-linked survival signaling becomes a testable mechanism and a potential combination-therapy target.

title: Duplex sequencing for ultra-low-frequency pre-existing resistant variants
description: Use error-corrected duplex sequencing or deep amplicon sequencing on untreated cell populations and on cells persisting after drug exposure, to detect rare pre-existing variants at frequencies below 0.1%. This distinguishes genetic pre-existence from non-genetic tolerance: if no survivors carry a shared variant, survival must be non-genetic, which argues for single-cell state assays.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment sibling tracking
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and treat one arm while profiling the sibling arm by scRNA-seq. This tests whether survivors are pre-existing, heritable states, and allows the pre-treatment transcriptional state of clones that later survive to be read out.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging with retrospective single-cell profiling
description: Track thousands of individual cells by time-lapse microscopy before and during drug exposure, using reporters for signaling activity (e.g., ERK), cell cycle, and apoptosis. Fix and profile survivors afterward, for example by multiplexed FISH or imaging-based proteomics, to link pre-drug dynamics and fluctuations to survival fate.

title: Single-cell multiomics across a drug time course
description: Profile the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility (scRNA and scATAC) of untreated, early-treated, persister, and regrown populations. This identifies epigenetic and transcriptional programs, such as a drug-tolerant or dedifferentiated state, and shows whether they are present before treatment or induced by it.

title: Functional perturbation screens of candidate persistence regulators
description: Run CRISPRi/CRISPRa or epigenetic-modifier-focused screens under drug pressure, with single-cell readouts such as Perturb-seq. This tests whether candidate genes, such as chromatin regulators, stress-response pathways, or drug efflux and metabolic genes, are causally required for persister survival.

title: Metabolic and stress-state measurements of persisters
description: Use single-cell assays such as FLIM of NADH, mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, lipid peroxidation, and drug-uptake fluorescence, combined with FACS sorting and metabolomics, to compare survivors and non-survivors. Pair these with pharmacologic tests (e.g., GPX4 inhibition) to determine whether metabolic or redox states predict and enable survival.

title: Barcode lineage tracing with pre-treatment sampling
description: Label cells with heritable expressed DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and profile one arm by scRNA-seq while treating the other arm. Linking surviving clones to their pre-treatment transcriptional states shows whether survival is predetermined, how heritable it is, and which states predict it.

title: Single-cell multi-omic profiling of persisters over time
description: Run scRNA-seq combined with scATAC-seq or CITE-seq on cells before treatment, during drug exposure, and after regrowth. This can identify persister-specific transcriptional programs, such as drug-efflux, stress-response, or dedifferentiated states, along with their regulatory chromatin changes.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging with lineage tracking
description: Use time-lapse microscopy with fluorescent reporters for signaling (ERK or AKT), cell cycle, and apoptosis. Follow single cells and their relatives through drug addition to determine whether dynamics, such as pulsatile signaling, slow cycling, or mitochondrial priming, predict survival, and to separate pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance.

title: Functional CRISPR screens in the persister state
description: Run genome-wide or focused CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens, with and without drug, that read out persister survival or re-entry into proliferation. Hits reveal genes and pathways required for tolerance, such as epigenetic regulators, antioxidant or lipid-peroxidation defenses, and anti-apoptotic factors, and point to combination therapies.

title: Single-cell metabolic and apoptotic-priming measurements with sorting
description: Measure mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, NADH/FAD autofluorescence (FLIM), and BH3 profiling in individual cells, and sort cells by these readouts before drug exposure. Testing the survival of the sorted subpopulations shows whether metabolic state or apoptotic threshold drives the stochastic survival.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre- and post-treatment transcriptomics
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, profile one arm by scRNA-seq, and treat the other to identify survivors. Matching survivor clones to their pre-treatment sister cells shows whether a pre-existing, heritable state predicts survival or whether survival arises stochastically after drug exposure.

title: Live-cell imaging with single-cell tracking and retrospective fate mapping
description: Image reporter-labeled cells (e.g., signaling activity, cell cycle, apoptosis, mitochondrial state) for days before and during treatment, then trace survivors back to their earlier histories. This links dynamic features such as pulsatile ERK or p53 activity, cell-cycle phase, or cell size to survival, and shows how long a predictive state persists.

title: Multi-omic profiling of persisters (chromatin accessibility, epigenome, proteome)
description: Isolate surviving cells at multiple time points and run single-cell ATAC-seq, histone-mark profiling (CUT&Tag), and proteomics or phospho-proteomics, alongside untreated controls. This tests whether persisters occupy a distinct chromatin or signaling state, such as a drug-tolerant program driven by KDM5 or AP-1, rather than carrying new genetic mutations.

title: Single-cell DNA sequencing and copy-number analysis to test for genetic causes
description: Sequence survivors at single-cell resolution to check for rare pre-existing mutations, copy-number changes, or extrachromosomal DNA that the bulk population lacks. Comparing survivors with their reversible, drug-free regrown descendants separates genetic from non-genetic (reversible) tolerance.

title: Functional perturbation screens and drug-combination tests on the tolerant state
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or inhibition screens with drug treatment to find genes and pathways, such as antioxidant defense, ferroptosis suppression, or anti-apoptotic factors, that change the fraction of survivors. Validate hits by combining the targeted drug with inhibitors of those pathways and measuring the persister fraction and time to regrowth.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment population splitting
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., ClonTracer or Perturb-seq-style), split the population before drug exposure, and compare which barcodes survive across replicates. Shared surviving barcodes indicate pre-existing, heritable states, while randomly distributed survivors indicate stochastic or induced tolerance.

title: Single-cell multi-omic profiling of pre-treatment and persister cells
description: Run scRNA-seq paired with scATAC-seq or CITE-seq on untreated cells and on cells at multiple time points after drug exposure. Look for rare transcriptional or chromatin states, such as drug-efflux, stress-response, or EMT programs, that exist before treatment and are enriched among survivors.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging followed by retrospective omics
description: Time-lapse image cells carrying reporters for signaling activity (ERK, p53, apoptosis), cell cycle, and mitochondrial state before and during drug exposure, tracking each cell to its fate. After imaging, fix or isolate the survivors and the cells that died, then profile them (e.g., by spatial or single-cell sequencing) to link dynamic pre-treatment features to survival.

title: Epigenetic and chromatin state perturbation screens
description: Use CRISPRi/a screens or small-molecule inhibitors of chromatin regulators (e.g., KDM5, HDACs, EZH2) to test whether altering epigenetic plasticity changes the persister fraction. Pair this with ChIP-seq or CUT&Tag on sorted survivors to identify the marks that maintain the tolerant state.

title: Metabolic and stress-state measurements of survivors
description: Measure ROS, mitochondrial membrane potential, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid peroxidation or ferroptosis sensitivity, and drug uptake or efflux at the single-cell level using flow cytometry or imaging.
