Sort cells by these properties before treatment, then test whether they predict survival and whether targeting the pathway (e.g., GPX4 inhibition) eliminates persisters.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment sampling
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and profile sister clones by scRNA-seq or bulk sequencing after treatment. Barcodes shared between pre-treatment sister populations and post-treatment survivors show whether survival is a pre-existing, heritable state, and comparing sister transcriptomes identifies predictive features.

title: Live-cell imaging with reporters and retrospective single-cell profiling
description: Track thousands of individual cells by time-lapse microscopy before and during drug treatment. Use reporters for signaling (such as ERK or AKT activity), cell cycle, and apoptosis, then fix and profile the survivors by multiplexed imaging or spatial transcriptomics. This links pre-drug dynamics, such as slow cycling or pulsatile signaling, to later survival.

title: Single-cell multi-omics of transcriptome, chromatin, and proteome
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, or CITE-seq, on untreated, early-treated, and persister populations. Look for rare cell states, such as stress-response, drug-efflux, or dedifferentiation programs, and for the chromatin accessibility and transcription factor activity that maintain them. Trajectory and RNA-velocity analysis can show whether persisters arise by selection or by induced switching.

title: Quantifying state-switching kinetics with fluctuation assays and modeling
description: Use Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation assays and time-resolved sorting of high- and low-expressing subpopulations to measure how fast cells switch into and out of the tolerant state. Fit stochastic models to the data to distinguish random mutation, stochastic non-genetic switching, and drug-induced adaptation, and to predict the best dosing schedules.

title: Functional perturbation screens in persisters
description: Run CRISPR knockout, CRISPRi, or CRISPRa screens, or small-molecule screens, during drug exposure. Use survival and persister outgrowth as readouts to find genes and pathways needed to enter or maintain tolerance, such as epigenetic regulators, metabolic and oxidative-stress pathways, or anti-apoptotic genes. Validate hits by testing whether co-treatment depletes persisters in vitro and in xenografts.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment split into replicate arms
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and compare which barcodes survive in replicate arms. Recurrence of the same clones across replicates indicates pre-existing, heritable states, while random survivors indicate stochastic or non-heritable states.

title: Single-cell multi-omics of persisters over time
description: Run scRNA-seq paired with scATAC-seq on cells before treatment, during drug exposure, and after regrowth, to identify transcriptional and chromatin states enriched in survivors. Trajectory and RNA-velocity analysis can show whether persisters arise from a rare pre-existing state or are induced by the drug.

title: Live-cell imaging with reporters and retrospective fate mapping
description: Image single cells for days before and after drug addition using fluorescent reporters of signaling (such as ERK or AKT activity), cell cycle, and stress. Then link each cell's pre-treatment history, such as signaling dynamics, cell-cycle phase, or mitochondrial content, to its survival outcome, and isolate survivors for sequencing.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens plus pharmacologic perturbation of candidate states
description: Run genome-wide or epigenetic-focused CRISPR knockout or interference screens under drug treatment to find genes that raise or lower persister frequency. Then validate causal mechanisms, such as drug efflux, anti-apoptotic buffering, or oxidative stress (e.g., GPX4/ferroptosis), with targeted inhibitors.

title: Quantitative modeling of switching rates with fluctuation assays
description: Use Luria-Delbrück fluctuation assays and sorted subpopulations to measure the rates at which cells switch into and out of the drug-tolerant state, and its memory duration. Fit stochastic models to the data to distinguish genetic mutation, epigenetic switching, and drug-induced adaptation, and predict dosing schedules that minimize persisters.

title: Lineage barcoding with split populations before treatment
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes (e.g., ClonTracer or Perturb-seq-style), split the population before drug exposure, and determine which barcodes survive in parallel replicates. Shared survivors across replicates would indicate a pre-existing, heritable state. Random survivors would indicate stochastic or induced tolerance.

title: Single-cell multi-omics of survivors versus matched pre-treatment states
description: Run scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, or CITE-seq, on untreated cells and on cells at several time points after drug exposure. Use barcodes to link survivors back to their pre-treatment transcriptional and chromatin states, to identify programs that predict survival, such as a drug-tolerant persister signature, EMT-like states, or stress-response states.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging with retrospective fate mapping
description: Time-lapse image cells carrying reporters for signaling (ERK or AKT activity), the cell cycle, apoptosis, and mitochondrial or ROS state. Track each cell's history before and after drug addition, then test which dynamic features, such as pulsatile signaling, a slow-cycling state, or a particular cell-cycle phase, predict survival. Follow-up fixed-cell sequencing or imaging of the same cells could add molecular detail.

title: Genetic and epigenetic perturbation screens in the persister state
description: Run CRISPR knockout, CRISPRi, or CRISPRa screens and epigenetic-modifier inhibitor screens (HDAC, KDM5, EZH2, and others) under drug pressure, measuring persister survival rather than only proliferation. Hits would show which pathways and chromatin regulators are necessary for tolerance, such as anti-apoptotic buffering, oxidative stress handling, or lipid metabolism.

title: Quantifying drug-target engagement and cell-intrinsic heterogeneity at the single-cell level
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration, target occupancy, and downstream pathway inhibition in individual cells, for example with fluorescent drug analogs, mass cytometry, or phospho-flow. Add measurements of apoptotic priming state (BH3 profiling) and metabolic state (e.g., FLIM of NAD(P)H). These would show whether survivors escape because of less drug exposure, rewiring after inhibition, or a higher threshold for death.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment sampling
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and compare which barcodes survive in replicate arms. Shared surviving barcodes across replicates indicate a pre-existing, heritable state. Sibling-cell sharing also allows estimating how long the resistant state persists.

title: Paired single-cell transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling over time
description: Run scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or multiome) on cells before treatment, during drug exposure, and after regrowth. Identify pre-treatment signatures of cells that later survive, such as drug-tolerant persister programs, EMT-like states, or stress-response pathways, and test them as predictors. Chromatin accessibility and histone marks can show whether the state is epigenetically encoded.

title: Live-cell imaging with reporters and single-cell tracking
description: Image cells for days before and after drug addition, using fluorescent reporters for signaling activity (e.g., ERK, p53, apoptosis, cell cycle). Track each cell's history to link fluctuations in signaling dynamics, cell-cycle length or mitochondrial state to eventual survival. Retrospective analysis of survivors' lineages shows whether survival can be predicted before the drug is added.

title: Isolation and functional perturbation of survivors
description: Sort cells by candidate markers or a live reporter of the survivor state, then compare their drug response to unsorted cells and measure how fast they interconvert with the bulk population. Test candidate drivers with CRISPR knockout or inhibition screens in the persister state. Combine this with sequencing to rule out rare pre-existing genetic mutations.

title: Fluctuation analysis and stochastic modeling of state switching
description: Apply Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation tests and stochastic models to the distribution of survivor counts across many small replicate cultures. This distinguishes pre-existing rare states, drug-induced adaptation and random switching, and it estimates the rates of switching in and out of the tolerant state. Predictions from the fitted model can be tested by varying drug dose, timing and pre-treatment history.

title: Fluctuation-test lineage barcoding
description: Split a barcoded clonal population into many parallel replicate cultures before drug exposure and compare the variance in survivor counts and barcode identities across replicates. Very high variance with unshared barcodes indicates pre-existing or spontaneously arising resistant states, while low variance with the same barcodes recurring indicates heritable states. Sequencing barcode-matched sister cells before treatment allows profiling of the pre-drug state of cells that later survive.

title: Estimating the half-life of the persister state from survival versus delay after sorting
description: Sort cells by a candidate state marker, treat them at varied delays after sorting, and fit survival versus delay to estimate the state's decay (switching) rate and its heritability across divisions. Combine this with single-cell ATAC-seq or CUT&Tag to identify which chromatin marks track the measured half-life.

title: Intrinsic/extrinsic noise decomposition of gene expression
description: Use dual-reporter live imaging and single-cell RNA-seq to separate cell-intrinsic stochastic bursting from extrinsic factors such as cell size, cell-cycle phase and mitochondrial content for survival-linked genes. Then test causality by tuning noise without changing the mean, for example by altering promoter burst kinetics with CRISPRi/a, and measure the effect on survival fraction.

title: Lineage-tree heritability analysis of survival fate
description: Use long-term live-cell imaging with fluorescent reporters of signaling (such as ERK or AKT activity), cell cycle and apoptosis to build full lineage trees before and during drug exposure. Then apply heritability analysis: do survival fates cluster in sister cells and cousins more than chance predicts, and how many generations does the correlation persist? This separates inherited states from random, non-heritable chance and shows which pre-treatment dynamics, such as ERK pulse frequency, predict survival.

title: Spatial mapping of survivors relative to the microenvironment
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on 3D spheroids or xenografts before and after treatment to map survivors against local gradients in oxygen, drug penetration, neighbor identity, and cell density. Use spatial statistics, such as neighborhood enrichment tests, to test whether survival depends on the microenvironment or on intrinsic state. Follow up by manipulating the microenvironment, for example with controlled drug gradients in microfluidic devices.

title: Fluctuation-test lineage barcoding
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into parallel replicate pools, and apply the drug. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, resistance is pre-existing and heritable. If survivors differ randomly between replicates, it arises stochastically from transient states. Comparing the variance in survivor number with Luria–Delbrück expectations estimates the switching rates.

title: Pre-treatment state tracing with sister-cell pairing
description: Split recently divided sister cell pairs, profile one sister by scRNA-seq before drug exposure, and expose the other to the drug. Survival of the treated sister is then used to infer the pre-treatment transcriptional state of the profiled sister. This identifies predictive pre-existing states without post-hoc survivor profiling, which is confounded by drug-induced changes.

title: Live-cell reporter time-lapse with hidden Markov and dynamical-systems modeling
description: Track single cells for days in microfluidic or imaging platforms using fluorescent reporters of ERK/AKT signaling, cell cycle, and apoptosis. Fit hidden Markov or dynamical-systems models to find signaling states and transition rates before and after the drug, and determine whether survivors occupy rare stable states or follow specific trajectories.

title: Information-theoretic analysis of signaling noise
description: Measure single-cell pathway activity (e.g., phospho-flow or kinase translocation reporters) across drug doses. Compute the mutual information between drug input and apoptotic decision, and test how much survival is due to intrinsic noise versus cell-specific upstream differences. Perturbing noise sources, such as the expression variability of key nodes, tests whether noise itself enables survival.

title: Measuring the half-life of the tolerant state's epigenetic memory
description: Sort cells by a candidate resistance-state marker, then follow how quickly the sorted population relaxes back to the original distribution of the marker. Pair this with single-cell ATAC-seq or CUT&Tag for chromatin marks such as H3K27me3 and H3K9me3. The decay half-life shows how stable the tolerant state is, and epigenetic drugs (EZH2 or HDAC inhibitors) can test whether the state is causally maintained.

title: Fluctuation-test lineage barcoding
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicate cultures, and apply drug. If resistant survivors cluster in a few replicates (jackpot distribution), resistance arises from rare pre-existing or heritable states. If survivors are spread evenly across replicates, it arises from stochastic induction. Comparing barcode overlap across replicates and before versus after drug quantifies how heritable the state is and how quickly it switches.

title: Pre-treatment state memory via sister-cell pairing
description: Split dividing sister cells: profile one by single-cell RNA-seq, and let the other expand and be drug-challenged, linking each pre-treatment transcriptional state to the sister's later fate. Clonal barcoding or live-cell lineage tracking can pair the sisters. This tests whether survival is predicted by a pre-existing state and how many generations that state persists.

title: Information-theoretic analysis of cell-to-cell variability and survival
description: Measure cell-to-cell variability in target pathway proteins, using live reporters for the drug target's pathway, drug efflux and stress-response activity. Then estimate the mutual information between pre-drug reporter levels and survival, and use time-lapse microscopy with autocorrelation to determine the persistence time of the state. This shows whether survivors are a heritable stochastic subpopulation with a fitness cost in drug-free conditions.

title: Attractor-landscape modeling and early-warning dynamics
description: Treat cell states as basins in an attractor landscape and perform time-resolved single-cell multiome profiling (RNA plus ATAC) at fine intervals after drug exposure. Infer trajectories and transition rates (RNA velocity, optimal transport) to see whether survivors reach a drug-tolerant state via a distinct path, and look for critical-slowing-down signatures, such as rising variance and autocorrelation, before the transition. Perturbing the identified barriers, for example with chromatin modifiers, tests whether tolerance can be prevented.

title: Spatial and microenvironment mapping of survivors
description: Map survivors in 3D culture or xenograft sections with spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging, using cluster-detection methods. Test whether survivors cluster near hypoxic, nutrient-rich or paracrine-signalling niches beyond what chance predicts. Spatial statistics, such as Ripley's K and neighbourhood enrichment, separate cell-intrinsic from niche-driven survival. Disrupting the implicated niche factor then tests causality.

title: Fluctuation-test lineage barcoding
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into parallel replicate cultures, and treat with the drug. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, resistance is a pre-existing, heritable state. If different barcodes survive in each replicate, it is a stochastic, transient state. The variance in survivor numbers across replicates distinguishes the two models and gives switching rates.

title: Sister-cell pairing to link pre-treatment state to survival
description: Split recently divided sister cells, or use clonally expanded barcoded sublines, so that each pair has two matched halves. Profile one half by single-cell RNA-seq before drug and expose the other half to drug. The survival outcome of the matched half links the pre-treatment transcriptional state to survival, which allows a predictive signature to be trained and tested.

title: Live-cell reporter time-lapse with dynamical systems analysis
description: Image cells carrying fluorescent reporters for signaling (e.g., ERK or AKT activity), cell cycle and apoptosis through drug exposure. Apply dynamical-systems tools such as autocorrelation, variance and attractor reconstruction to determine whether survivors occupy a distinct stable state or cross a threshold. Retrospectively track each survivor back to its pre-drug trajectory to show when and how the divergence arose.

title: Metabolic and mitochondrial priming profiling with BH3 profiling
description: Use BH3 profiling and single-cell measurements of mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP, and ROS to quantify apoptotic priming, meaning how close each cell is to its apoptotic threshold, before and after drug exposure. Compare the distributions to determine whether survivors are less primed or have rewired metabolism, such as a shift toward oxidative phosphorylation.

title: Epigenetic memory mapping with single-cell multiome profiling
description: Apply single-cell ATAC plus RNA profiling to untreated, drug-treated, and drug-withdrawn populations. Test whether survivors keep a chromatin state after drug removal and whether it fades with a measurable half-life. Perturb candidate chromatin regulators with CRISPRi or inhibitors to test whether erasing the state removes the survivors' advantage.

title: Fluctuation-test lineage barcoding
description: Split barcoded clonal populations into many parallel replicates before drug exposure, as in a Luria-Delbrück fluctuation test. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, the survival state is heritable and pre-existing. If different barcodes survive in each replicate, survival is stochastic or induced. Fitting the variance-to-mean ratio of surviving clones to a mathematical model gives the rate of switching into the resistant state.

title: Cell-state transition rates via Markov modeling
description: Sort cells by a candidate marker, such as a drug-tolerant-state reporter, and track how fast the sorted subpopulations re-equilibrate to the original mixture. Fit a Markov transition matrix to the time-lapse data to estimate switching rates and energy barrier heights between states. This shows whether tolerant cells are a stable state, a transient fluctuation, or a drug-induced adaptation.

title: Sister-cell concordance in survival with live signaling reporters
description: Use time-lapse live imaging with fluorescent signaling reporters, such as ERK and p53 activity, and follow sister cells and cousins through division. Then treat them with the drug. Sister-cell concordance in survival, compared with unrelated cells, estimates how much survival is heritable versus due to non-heritable noise. Pre-treatment reporter dynamics can then be tested as predictors of which lineages survive.

title: Spatial neighborhood mapping of survivors
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to map survivors against local features such as cell density, oxygen, nutrient gradients, and contact with neighboring cells or stroma. Compare survivors with matched non-survivors in the same neighborhoods. Then test the hits by manipulating cell density or by micropatterning cells.

title: Single-cell variability profiling of metabolic and stress-response variables
description: In untreated cells, measure cell-to-cell variability in mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, drug efflux, and apoptotic-priming proteins (for example by BH3 profiling), using high-dimensional single-cell mass cytometry. Determine which variable carries the most information about later survival, for example by mutual information, then perturb the top variable to test whether it shifts the surviving fraction, which would indicate causality.

title: Barcode-based fluctuation test across replicate pools
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into replicate pools, and treat each with drug. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, resistance is pre-existing and heritable; if different barcodes survive in each replicate, it reflects stochastic state switching. Comparing the variance in survivor counts across replicates to a Poisson expectation gives a quantitative switching rate.

title: Pre-treatment state tracing with split-clone sister-cell sampling
description: Use lineage barcoding with split-clone sampling. Profile one sister arm by single-cell RNA-seq before the drug, and treat the other sister arm. Survivors' barcodes then link each pre-drug transcriptional state to its fate, identifying predictive pre-existing signatures. Comparing how concordant sister cells are against unrelated cells indicates how heritable the state is.

title: Live-cell reporter time-lapse with hidden Markov model state inference
description: Image thousands of single cells over days with reporters for stress-response, drug-target activity, and cell cycle. Fit hidden Markov models to the single-cell trajectories to infer discrete latent states and transition rates between them. Then test which states and transitions precede survival, and whether drug exposure induces the persister state or merely selects for it.

title: Noise-propagation analysis of signaling networks
description: Quantify cell-to-cell variability in pathway nodes (e.g., phospho-flow or CyCIF imaging of the target and its bypass pathways). Use information-theoretic or covariance-based measures to find nodes where noise is amplified or buffered. Perturb feedback loops with CRISPRi and check whether altering the noise gain changes the surviving fraction without changing mean expression, which would point to feedback-driven bistability.

title: Spatial mapping of survivors with spatial statistics
description: In 3D culture or tumor sections, map survivors with multiplexed imaging or spatial transcriptomics. Use point-process and spatial-autocorrelation statistics to test whether survivors cluster in microenvironmental zones, such as hypoxic, low-drug-penetration, or cell-contact zones, rather than being randomly scattered. Combine this with drug-penetration measurements and local-density manipulations to separate extrinsic microenvironment effects from intrinsic cell state.

title: Barcode lineage tracing with fluctuation tests
description: Barcode cells and split clonal populations into many parallel replicates before drug exposure, as in Luria–Delbrück fluctuation tests. The variance in surviving-barcode counts across replicates shows whether persistence is pre-existing and heritable (clone-specific) or induced stochastically. Sister-cell pairs and multigenerational pedigrees can then be used to measure how many divisions the persister state is retained.

title: Energy-landscape modeling of cell-state transitions
description: Using an energy-landscape (attractor) model of cell states, perform single-cell RNA/ATAC profiling of untreated, early-drug and late-drug cells. Infer a quasi-potential and transition rates between states, and test whether the survivors occupy a rare shallow basin that was already populated before treatment. Perturbing predicted barrier-controlling regulators would test whether the model correctly forecasts survival fractions.

title: Signal-processing analysis of live-cell reporter time series
description: Image single cells over days using fluorescent reporters of ERK, p53, or apoptosis signaling, and compute autocorrelation, variance, and pulse-frequency spectra in the hours before drug addition to test whether future survivors have distinct signaling dynamics. Retrospective tracking followed by classifier training would identify which dynamic features predict survival.

title: Spatial statistics of survivor clustering in microenvironments
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging of 3D cultures or tumors and apply spatial statistics such as Ripley's K and neighborhood enrichment. This tests whether survivors cluster in regions with particular oxygen, density, or paracrine signals, and whether they sit at the edges or core of colonies. Local microenvironments can then be manipulated, for example by changing density or conditioned media, to separate non-genetic cell-intrinsic causes from positional ones.

title: Graded-stress profiling of single-cell metabolic and physiological capacity
description: Apply graded drug doses and stresses and measure each single cell's capacity to cope, using mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, ATP/NADH FLIM, cell-cycle slowing, and drug efflux as readouts. Index sorting links these readouts to later colony outgrowth, revealing whether survivors have a distinct tolerance threshold such as slow cycling, higher efflux, or altered metabolism. Sorted subpopulations can also be profiled by proteomics to identify causal mechanisms.

title: Fluctuation-test lineage barcoding
description: Split a barcoded clonal population into many parallel replicates, apply drug, and compare the variance in survivor barcodes across replicates. Pre-existing heritable states should give large, shared barcode overrepresentation across replicates, while drug-induced switching should give Poisson-like variation. Sequencing barcodes before and after treatment, and after regrowth, also shows how stable the resistant state is.

title: Live-cell tracking with lineage reconstruction and sister-cell concordance
description: Use long-term time-lapse microscopy with fluorescent reporters (e.g., ERK activity, cell cycle, p53) to track single cells and their lineages before and after drug. Retrospectively test which pre-treatment features predict survival. Concordance of survival between sister cells would separate inherited from stochastic causes.

title: Energy-landscape and attractor inference from single-cell trajectories
description: Perform time-resolved scRNA-seq with metabolic labeling or RNA velocity before, during, and after drug exposure, then infer stable states and transition rates between sensitive and tolerant states, modeling cell states as positions on a potential landscape. Perturb candidate regulators and check whether the barriers between states shift, to test whether the tolerant state is a rare stable state or a transient excursion.

title: Noise-propagation analysis of the drug target, pathway and apoptosis machinery
description: Quantify expression noise (Fano factor, correlated fluctuations) in the drug target, its pathway, and the apoptosis machinery using single-cell protein imaging or CyTOF. Fit a circuit-style noise-propagation model to identify which node amplifies noise into a survive-or-die decision. Test the causal role of fluctuations by perturbing noise without changing mean levels, for example with promoter variants.

title: Case-control comparison of survivors and matched non-survivors with multi-omic profiling
description: Sort or image cells before drug treatment and track them, then define survivors as cases and matched non-survivors as controls. Profile the same cells with spatial or single-cell transcriptomics, ATAC-seq, and mitochondrial/metabolic readouts, and use conditional-logistic regression to identify which pre-existing molecular features best predict survival. Test causality of the top hits with CRISPR screens.

title: Paired survivor-versus-casualty multi-omic mapping at the single-cell level
description: Use live imaging to identify which cells later survive drug, then fix them in place and profile them with spatial transcriptomics/proteomics or single-cell sequencing. Compare each survivor with its nearest dying neighbors to find pre-existing or induced states (e.g., drug efflux, anti-apoptotic, stress-response, chromatin features) that mark survival.

title: Lineage barcoding with replicate-population statistics
description: Barcode cells, split the population into many identical replicate dishes, treat all with the drug, and count which barcodes survive in each replicate. Barcodes recurring across replicates indicate pre-existing heritable survivors, whereas random barcodes indicate stochastic or induced survival.

title: Survival-time distribution analysis with Weibull and mixture hazard models
description: Measure time to death after drug exposure in large numbers of single cells or small wells, and fit Weibull or mixture hazard models to the death-time distribution across doses. A distinct tail or separate subpopulation in the fitted shape and scale parameters would show whether survivors are a discrete tolerant class or the extreme end of a continuum, and would quantify how treatments shift the tail.

title: Live-cell tracking of damage initiation and recovery
description: Use time-lapse microscopy with reporters for drug-target activity, DNA damage, apoptosis caspases, ROS, and cell-cycle state to follow each cell from before treatment through death or survival. Tracking where and when damage starts (e.g., signaling rebound, mitochondrial priming, slow cycling) shows what survivors do differently.

title: Pre-treatment state sorting and causal perturbation of candidate features
description: Before drug exposure, sort cells by candidate features such as reporter-defined transcriptional state, cell-cycle phase, mitochondrial content or epigenetic marks. Then challenge each sorted fraction with the drug to test whether the feature predicts survival, and use CRISPR or small-molecule perturbations to add or remove it, which would show whether it causes survival or only correlates with it.

title: Lineage-barcoded matched-pair comparison of survivors and non-survivors
description: Use heritable DNA barcodes to split a clonal population into replicate arms, then test whether the same lineages survive drug in independent replicates (pre-existing, heritable state) or whether survivors are random (stochastic). Sister-cell pairs or barcode-matched lineages sampled before treatment can be profiled by scRNA-seq to compare the pre-treatment states of future survivors with those of matched non-survivors.

title: Hazard-model analysis of single-cell live imaging with pre-treatment covariates
description: Track thousands of individual cells by time-lapse microscopy with reporters (e.g., apoptosis, cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, mitochondrial state) before and after drug, and fit Cox/competing-risk survival models for death versus arrest versus division. Covariates measured before drug (cell cycle phase, signaling pulse history, size, lineage relatedness) quantify which hidden state variables predict survival.

title: Perturbing candidate state regulators and comparing survivor fraction to controls
description: Perturb candidate survival-state factors (e.g., drug efflux, anti-apoptotic BCL2-family proteins, stress-response or chromatin regulators) with CRISPRi or inhibitors, and compare the change in survivor fraction before and after drug versus matched untreated and non-targeting controls. This separates a causal effect on drug tolerance from general effects on proliferation or baseline fitness.

title: Titration of dose, drug combination, and environmental stress
description: Systematically vary drug dose, exposure duration, pathway co-inhibition, and nutrient and oxygen stress, and measure the survivor fraction and survivor transcriptional states in each condition. The resulting dose-response curves for survivors show whether tolerance is a single robust state or condition-dependent, and which stresses reduce the survivor fraction.

title: State-transition modeling from multi-omic single-cell data with neighbor covariates
description: Combine paired single-cell RNA, ATAC and protein or metabolic readouts of untreated cells and fit a dynamical model (e.g., Markov state-transition or RNA velocity-based) estimating switching rates between sensitive and tolerant states with and without drug. Include spatial or neighbor-cell covariates (contact, paracrine signaling), then validate by sorting predicted high-tolerance-state cells and testing their survival prospectively.

title: Single-cell lineage tracking with fate mapping
description: Barcode individual cells (e.g., lineage barcodes or live-imaging tracking) and follow their fates before, during and after drug exposure, then retrospectively compare pre-treatment states of survivor lineages versus killed lineages. This tests whether survival is predicted by a heritable or transient pre-existing state.

title: Spatial microenvironment mapping around survivors
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging in 3D cultures or xenografts to measure local density, oxygen, drug penetration, nutrient gradients and neighbor identity around survivors versus dead cells. Fit spatial models (e.g., point-process or occupancy-style) to test whether survivors occupy drug-protected microniches rather than being intrinsically different.

title: Reciprocal transplant of survivors into common and different environments
description: Isolate survivors and non-survivors (or their pre-treatment sorted siblings), grow them in identical drug-free conditions for varying durations, then re-challenge them with drug. Also move them into different microenvironments (density, matrix, co-culture). Persistence of resistance in a common environment indicates intrinsic epigenetic or state differences, while loss of resistance indicates environmental or plastic causes.

title: Manipulation of candidate microenvironmental variables
description: Experimentally alter local density, oxygen, drug concentration gradients, or stromal contact in a controlled way (microfluidics or patterned co-culture) and measure survival fraction response. The dose-response of survivor frequency to each manipulated variable separates causal environmental protective niches from stochastic or intrinsic causes.

title: Long-term time series of state dynamics with stochastic state-transition modeling
description: Image or sequence the same cell populations repeatedly across drug exposure and recovery, measuring state markers (e.g., drug-tolerant persister signatures, cell-cycle state, drug efflux, mitochondrial activity). Fit state-transition models that estimate switching rates and compare them with the observed survivor fraction, to test whether stochastic switching between states explains persistence.

title: Back-tracing survivors' pre-treatment state with lineage barcodes
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicate pools, and treat. Profile sister cells from untreated replicates by scRNA-seq to find the pre-existing state of cells whose barcodes later survive. This compares the pre-treatment state of survivors with that of non-survivors and separates pre-existing states from drug-induced adaptation.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with retrospective survivor tracking
description: Image single cells with fluorescent reporters (e.g. cell cycle, p53/ERK dynamics, mitochondrial potential, drug autofluorescence) for days before and during drug exposure. After treatment, trace the survivors back through their history and compare their trajectories with those of cells that died, to show which dynamic or state features predicted survival.

title: Controlled perturbation screen of candidate state variables
description: Systematically perturb suspected hidden variables such as cell-cycle phase, drug efflux, mitochondrial priming, chromatin state or stress-pathway activity, using CRISPRi/a, small-molecule modulators or synchronization. Measure how each shifts the survivor fraction, to test which state differences cause survival rather than merely correlate with it.

title: Multi-omic comparison of sorted survivors and non-survivors
description: Use FACS or microfluidics to isolate cells based on pre-treatment markers (e.g., drug uptake, apoptotic priming via BH3 profiling, or an efflux reporter). Run matched ATAC-seq, proteomics, and single-cell RNA-seq on the sorted groups to find the minimal set of state differences that separates the two.

title: Rare-event statistics and heritability of survival
description: Run Luria–Delbrück fluctuation-test experiments, plus sister-cell and clonal-relative comparisons, to estimate how often cells switch into and out of the survivor state and how long that state is inherited. Fit stochastic state-switching models to survivor-fraction data across doses and times to distinguish random switching, epigenetic memory, and rare genetic or mutational causes. Complement this with deep sequencing to rule out hidden mutations.

title: Matched survivor-versus-dying-neighbor profiling of pre-treatment state
description: Before drug exposure, barcode and live-image cells, then treat and identify survivors. Retrospectively compare the pre-treatment state of each survivor lineage (transcriptome via lineage-barcoded scRNA-seq, signaling reporters, cell cycle, mitochondrial content) with its matched dying neighbors, to test which pre-existing state predicts survival rather than which state appears afterward.

title: Microenvironment mapping of survivor locations
description: Record local conditions for every cell in culture or in tumor sections, including density, neighbor identity, oxygen, nutrient and pH gradients, drug penetration (using fluorescent drug analogs), and position within colonies. Then use spatial statistics to test whether survivors cluster in protective niches, and compare with spatial transcriptomics from treated tumors.

title: Stochastic mechanistic modeling of drug response with sensitivity analysis
description: Build mechanistic or stochastic models of the drug target pathway, apoptosis threshold, and drug efflux, drawing protein abundances and rate constants from measured single-cell distributions. Run sensitivity analysis to identify which variable's variation (such as BCL-2 family ratios or target expression noise) best reproduces the observed survivor fraction, then validate the top candidates experimentally.

title: Graded drug perturbation of sorted isogenic subpopulations
description: Apply graded, standardized drug doses, pulses, and combinations to sorted subpopulations, for example high versus low expression of a candidate state marker. Quantify dose-response curves, time to death, and survivor fraction. Then perturb the candidate variability source directly, such as by tuning expression with CRISPRi/a or inhibiting a stress pathway, to test whether it causally shifts the survivor fraction.

title: Heritability and state-transition kinetics of survival
description: Measure whether survival is transient or heritable by tracking sister cells and clonal lineages across drug-free and drug cycles. Use fluctuation-test (Luria-Delbrück) designs and Markov state-switching models to separate pre-existing epigenetic states from newly acquired mutations. Add whole-genome sequencing and chromatin accessibility of survivors to confirm they are genetically identical and to find the epigenetic basis of survival.

title: Lineage-barcoded longitudinal tracking of persister fates
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicate pools before drug, and sequence barcodes at several timepoints. This tests whether survival is pre-existing and heritable (the same barcodes surviving across replicates) or stochastic.

title: Single-cell profiling of pre-treatment cells that later survive
description: Use barcode-matched sister cells, or live-cell reporters with sorting, to profile the pre-drug transcriptome, chromatin state and signaling of cells that later prove to be survivors. Compare them with matched non-survivors from the same culture to identify factors, such as a drug-efflux or stress-response state, that predate treatment.

title: Time-lapse single-cell tracking with retrospective outcome linkage
description: Image fluorescent reporters of cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, and mitochondrial or redox state continuously before and after drug, then link each cell's history to its fate. The dynamic traces are used to generate hypotheses about behaviors, such as slow cycling or pulsatile signaling, that distinguish survivors.

title: Matched-control causal perturbation of candidate survival factors
description: Perturb candidate factors from the profiling, such as a state marker or regulator, by CRISPRi/a or drug in a randomized, matched design. Compare survivor fractions with propensity-matched or randomized controls, adjusting for cell cycle, size and density, to test whether each factor causes survival rather than merely correlating with it.

title: Spatial comparison of survivors and non-survivors in matched local neighborhoods
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging to compare survivors with non-survivors in matched local neighborhoods, controlling for cell density, nutrient gradients, and paracrine signals. This separates cell-intrinsic state from local context, and a co-culture or conditioned-medium experiment can then test the contextual factors.

title: Single-cell live tracking with lineage-resolved drug response
description: Use time-lapse microscopy to track thousands of individual cells and their lineages through drug exposure, with reporters for signaling (e.g., ERK, p53) and cell-cycle state. This gives the full distribution of single-cell trajectories and shows whether survivors differ in dynamics before the drug is added, and when divergence begins.

title: First-passage-time analysis of death and escape
description: Record each cell's time to apoptosis or to resumed division after drug addition, and fit the full distribution rather than the mean. A heavy tail or multimodal shape would indicate either a single stochastic rate process or a distinct slow-cycling subpopulation. Dose-dependence of the tail would constrain mechanistic models.

title: Retrospective and prospective tracing of survivor state trajectories
description: Follow cells continuously, then trace the survivors' ancestors backward to identify the states they passed through before the drug. Compare these trajectories with those of cells that died, and where possible use barcoded or live-reporter sorting to isolate cells in candidate pre-resistant states and test whether they are enriched for survival.

title: Autocorrelation and heritability of cell state to distinguish noise from slow hidden variables
description: Measure how long expression of candidate markers (e.g., drug-efflux or anti-apoptotic genes) stays correlated within a cell and between sister cells and cousins. Compare this timescale with the drug-exposure window: persistence over several generations implies a slow epigenetic or metabolic variable, while rapid decay implies fast noise. Test the inference by sorting cells by marker level and measuring how survival changes with the delay between sorting and treatment.

title: Barcoded clonal replicates with sister-cell comparisons
description: Label cells with heritable lineage barcodes, split a population into parallel replicates, and treat them. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, the survival state is pre-existing and heritable. If different barcodes survive, the cause is stochastic. Single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq on matched pre-treatment sister cells then identifies the molecular features that predict survival.

title: High-replicate dose-response curves to resolve the survival tail
description: Run drug titrations across many replicate wells and extended dose ranges, using live-cell imaging or barcoded counting to fit the plateau of the survival curve. This gives the persister fraction and a dose-response shape that separates a stable tolerant subpopulation (a plateau) from continuous sensitivity. Also compare how the fraction changes with time and dose.

title: Matched survivor and pretreatment-sister profiling with lineage barcoding
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes and split the population before treatment. Sequence the barcodes in the survivors and in the untreated sister populations to test whether survivors come from pre-existing clones. Then perform single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq on the matched pretreatment sisters to show which transcriptional or chromatin states predicted survival, as opposed to states induced by the drug.

title: Live-cell tracking of pre-treatment state, size, and cell-cycle stage
description: Image reporter cells for cell-cycle phase, cell size, and signaling activity (e.g., ERK or p53 reporters) over time before the drug is added. Track each cell through treatment and record its fate. Then regress survival on the pre-exposure measurements to test whether survivors were slower-cycling, larger, or in a particular cell-cycle phase.

title: Re-challenge and drug-holiday experiments for inheritance of tolerance
description: Expand the survivors in drug-free medium for varying numbers of generations. Re-challenge them at different time points and compare the surviving fraction with that of naive cells. A fraction that reverts over time indicates a reversible epigenetic or metabolic state. A fraction that stays high suggests a genetic change, which exome sequencing can then test for. Add single-cell-derived clones to measure how quickly the survival fraction returns to baseline.

title: Metabolic and epigenetic profiling with pathway perturbation
description: Compare sorted survivors and untreated cells using metabolomics (for example NADH/NAD+ and ROS levels, mitochondrial activity), drug-efflux and detoxification activity, and histone-modification or DNA-methylation profiles. Then test causality by blocking candidate pathways with epigenetic inhibitors or metabolic modulators and measuring whether the survival fraction changes.

title: Sister-cell pair tracking with post-hoc molecular readout
description: Image dividing cells live to identify sister pairs, treat with drug, and record which sister survives, then compare pre-treatment features between sisters. The decay of sister concordance in survival over generations quantifies the memory timescale of the survival-permissive state, separating heritable from stochastic fluctuations.

title: Predicting survival from pre-treatment live reporter dynamics
description: Image cells carrying multiplexed live reporters (e.g., p53, ERK, and NF-κB dynamics, mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis-priming dye) before drug addition. Track each cell's eventual fate and train a model to predict survival from the pre-drug dynamics, so the predictive features show which pathway states precede survival.

title: BH3 profiling and single-cell apoptotic priming and caspase kinetics
description: Measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming and the timing of drug-induced caspase activation in individual cells, sorted by survival outcome. This tests whether survivors have a lower apoptosis threshold (e.g., due to BCL-2 family levels) rather than escaping inhibition of the drug target.

title: Imaging intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy
description: Use fluorescent or label-free readouts (mass spec imaging, intrinsically fluorescent drugs, or a target-engagement biosensor) to quantify drug accumulation, efflux, lysosomal sequestration, and target inhibition per cell. This tests whether survivors experience less effective drug exposure rather than having altered downstream biology.

title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors
description: In 3D cultures or tissue sections, use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to relate survivor locations to local density, hypoxia, neighbor identity, and secreted-factor gradients, then perturb the implicated neighbor cues. This tests whether survival arises from transient local niche effects on genetically identical cells.

title: Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy and mitochondrial priming
description: Sequence mtDNA and perform BH3 profiling or live mitochondrial membrane potential and apoptotic-threshold measurements on sorted single cells before treatment. Test whether differences in mitochondrial state predict which cells survive.

title: Inheritance of survival state across cell divisions via sister-cell pair analysis
description: Use time-lapse imaging of sister pairs and pedigrees, then apply the drug at different generations, to quantify how many divisions the persister-prone state is remembered and whether it is inherited stably or reset stochastically.

title: Asymmetric partitioning of organelles and proteins at division
description: Label aggregated proteins, lysosomes, old mitochondria, or stress-granule components with photoconvertible or tandem timer tags, and track whether cells that inherit larger or smaller loads at mitosis preferentially survive.

title: Single-cell metabolic flux and redox imaging
description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, genetically encoded ATP, glutathione and ROS sensors, and lipid peroxidation probes in live cells that are later followed to survival. This tests whether ferroptosis sensitivity and metabolic state determine persistence.

title: Manipulation of stochastic gene-expression noise
description: Engineer cells with promoter variants or feedback circuits that tune expression noise of a candidate survival gene at constant mean expression, then measure persister frequency. This tests whether expression noise itself, rather than the mean level, causally drives survival.

title: Cell-cycle-history and inheritance tracking via sister-cell pairs
description: Use time-lapse imaging of FUCCI or similar reporters plus sister-cell tracking to test whether survival correlates with pre-drug cell-cycle duration and how strongly sisters share fate. Compare sister-pair concordance with unrelated cells and apply the drug at varied times after division to estimate the heritability and decay time of the survival state.

title: Mitochondrial content and mtDNA heteroplasmy sorting
description: Sort untreated cells by mitochondrial mass, membrane potential, or mtDNA heteroplasmy, then drug-challenge each bin to see whether mitochondrial state predicts survival. Single-cell mtDNA variants can also serve as natural lineage markers to test clonal inheritance.

title: Pre-treatment live-cell signaling dynamics as a predictor
description: Record dynamic reporters (ERK, AKT, p53, NF-κB kinase translocation) in single cells for days before drug addition. Then train a model on those dynamics to predict which cells survive, which would show whether signaling history rather than a static state determines the outcome.

title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors in 3D and tumor models
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging to spheroids or xenografts after treatment to test whether survivors cluster by hypoxia, nutrient gradients, drug penetration, or neighbor contact. Pair this with local drug-concentration measurements, such as mass spectrometry imaging, to separate intrinsic from positional causes.

title: Apoptotic priming measurement with BH3 profiling and live caspase reporters
description: Measure each cell's mitochondrial apoptotic priming with single-cell BH3 profiling or live caspase and MOMP reporters. Then test how priming, rather than drug target inhibition, sets survival after drug exposure. Compare the variance in priming with that in target-inhibition readouts to see which drives the surviving fraction.

title: Time-lapse lineage-linked pre-treatment history
description: Track single cells by live imaging with reporters (cell cycle, stress, apoptosis signaling) for several generations before drug addition, then retrospectively identify features of the cells that later survive. Sister-cell and cousin-cell survival concordance would quantify the heritability and timescale of the protective state.

title: Spatial-transcriptomic neighborhood mapping of survivors
description: Apply multiplexed in situ imaging (MERFISH or similar) to 3D cultures or xenografts during treatment to test whether survivors cluster by local microenvironment such as oxygen, density, or contact with stromal cells. Compare with matched non-survivors to separate cell-intrinsic from position-dependent protection.

title: Mitochondrial priming and apoptotic threshold profiling
description: Use BH3 profiling, single-cell quantification of BCL-2 family proteins, and caspase activation kinetics to measure how close each cell is to the apoptotic threshold. This tests whether survival comes from variable cell-death machinery rather than from the drug target pathway.

title: Drug uptake, efflux and intracellular concentration at single-cell resolution
description: Use fluorescent drug analogs or mass-spec imaging (e.g., CyTOF or nanoSIMS) to measure intracellular drug levels and target occupancy in individual cells, then link these to survival. Differences in transporter activity or lysosomal drug sequestration could explain survival without altering signaling.

title: Manipulation of stochastic gene expression noise
description: Use synthetic circuits or promoter and noise-modulating perturbations to raise or lower expression variability of candidate survival genes while keeping their mean level constant. Measuring the persister fraction as a function of noise tests causally whether cell-to-cell variation itself, rather than the average, sets the surviving fraction.

title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and mtDNA lineage tracing
description: Use naturally occurring mtDNA variants (for example, via mtscATAC-seq) as endogenous clonal barcodes, and relate heteroplasmy levels and mitochondrial content and membrane potential in pre-treatment cells to later survival. This tests whether inherited mitochondrial state, rather than nuclear genome or transcriptome, predisposes cells to tolerance.

title: Sister-cell pair tracking with fate prediction
description: Image dividing cells, then split or track sister pairs before drug exposure and test whether sister survival concordance exceeds that of random pairs. The decay of concordance over generations gives the memory time of the tolerant state. Combine with post hoc multiplexed profiling of the same cells to identify inherited features such as organelle load or cell size.

title: Pre-treatment measurement of apoptotic priming
description: Measure single-cell BH3 profiling or live fluorescent reporters of caspase/MOMP threshold and BCL-2 family stoichiometry before drug exposure, then follow cell fate. This tests whether survivors are cells stochastically positioned further from the apoptosis threshold rather than cells with a distinct drug-resistance program.

title: Stress-granule, translation, and ISR dynamics
description: Use ribosome profiling or puromycin/OPP incorporation at single-cell resolution plus integrated stress response (ISR) reporters (ATF4, eIF2α phosphorylation) during the first hours of drug exposure, with pharmacological ISR perturbation. This tests whether rapid translational reprogramming allows survival during the acute window before any transcriptional state change matters.

title: Single-cell metabolic and redox imaging with causal perturbation
description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, genetically encoded ROS/ATP/lipid peroxidation sensors, and lipidomics on sorted cells to detect metabolic states, such as altered ferroptosis susceptibility or lipid composition, that precede or accompany tolerance. Follow with perturbations (GPX4 inhibition, lipid supplementation) to test causality.

title: Pedigree-resolved sister-cell tracking with post-hoc transcriptomics
description: Time-lapse image cells for several generations before drug, then drug-treat and track survival, and finally lyse and sequence or FISH-profile identified survivors and their pre-drug sisters or cousins. This tests whether survival is heritable across divisions and which pre-existing state markers correlate with it, beyond static snapshots.

title: Single-cell mitochondrial and metabolic state mapping before drug
description: Measure NAD(P)H lifetime (FLIM), mitochondrial membrane potential, mtDNA copy number and ROS in individual live cells, sort or track them, and then challenge with drug to see if metabolic/redox state predicts survival. Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and apoptotic priming can differ between genetically identical cells.

title: BH3 profiling and live apoptosis reporters
description: Quantify per-cell mitochondrial apoptotic priming (BH3 profiling of sorted subpopulations, MCL1/BCL-xL/BIM levels) and use live caspase and cytochrome-c reporters. This tests whether survivors fail to commit to apoptosis after drug rather than escaping inhibition of the drug's target.

title: Extrachromosomal DNA and copy-number heterogeneity by single-cell sequencing and ecDNA imaging
description: Use single-cell DNA sequencing and ecDNA FISH/CRISPR-imaging to test whether uneven ecDNA segregation and copy-number variation of target or bypass genes produce rare high-copy survivors in nominally identical cells. Longitudinal sampling shows whether copy number changes reversibly under drug.

title: Live reporters of cell-cycle and stress dynamics with forced perturbation of fluctuations
description: Combine endogenously tagged reporters (p53 pulses, ERK/AKT activity, FUCCI, heat-shock/UPR) in single cells and use their dynamics to predict survival. Then test causality by forcing the dynamics optogenetically or chemically. This distinguishes whether transient signaling fluctuations or cell-cycle position causally determines which cells survive.

title: Pre-treatment state tracking with lineage-linked sister-cell sampling
description: Split clonally related sister cells (identified via barcodes) so that one sibling is profiled by scRNA-seq before drug while the other is treated, then use barcode matching to identify which pre-drug transcriptional states predicted survival. This directly tests whether survivors are predetermined, rather than inferring it after treatment.

title: Decay of survival heritability over generations
description: Isolate survivors and non-survivors, expand them without drug for varied numbers of divisions, then re-challenge them to measure how fast the survival phenotype is lost. Fitting the decay kinetics gives the switching rates and memory timescale, which indicate whether the mechanism is stochastic, epigenetic, or genetic.

title: Mitochondrial and organelle inheritance asymmetry at division
description: Use live imaging of mitochondrial content, membrane potential, ROS, and lysosomal drug sequestration in mother cells and daughters, then test whether unequal partitioning before treatment predicts survival. Use photoactivatable or tagged organelles to test whether the inherited organelle state causes survival.

title: Single-cell measurement of apoptotic threshold dynamics
description: Use live reporters for caspase activation and mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization, together with BH3 profiling of single cells. This quantifies cell-to-cell variation in how close each cell is to the death threshold and in the timing of commitment to death after drug exposure, separately from drug target inhibition.

title: Intracellular drug and target-engagement heterogeneity
description: Use a fluorescent drug analog, a biosensor, or mass-spec imaging to measure per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy or pathway-reporter suppression (e.g., ERK kinase translocation reporter) over time. Linking these to survival tests whether survivors escape because the drug never fully engages the target or because they tolerate full inhibition.

title: Pre-treatment state analysis via sister-cell pairing
description: Track lineages by time-lapse imaging, then split sister cells so that one is drugged and the other is profiled by scRNA-seq or proteomics. This links the pre-drug state of one sister to the survival fate of its pair, testing causes directly and avoiding after-the-fact correlation.

title: Cell-cycle and mitotic timing history as a predictor of survival
description: Use FUCCI or similar live reporters with long-term tracking to test whether the cell-cycle phase at drug exposure, G1 length, or a recent mitotic error predicts survival. Combine this with synchronization and perturbation of the cell cycle to test causality.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming and stress-response heterogeneity
description: Measure per-cell BH3 profiling or live mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization reporters, along with caspase kinetics and BCL-2 family protein levels. This tests whether survivors are cells with high apoptotic thresholds or slow accumulation of death signals.

title: Stochastic gene-expression noise and fluctuation timescale modeling
description: Perform time-resolved single-cell measurements of key drug-target pathway reporters in untreated cells. Fit stochastic state-switching models (Luria-Delbrück-type fluctuation analysis) to estimate how fast cells enter and leave the tolerant state and to predict how survival changes with drug-holiday schedules.

title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping with varied density
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on 3D cultures or xenografts, and vary local density, cell-contact and secreted-factor conditions. This tests whether persister fate depends on microenvironmental position, such as hypoxia or paracrine rescue, rather than on intrinsic cell state.

title: High-complexity lineage barcoding with fluctuation analysis
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into replicate arms, and treat; if the same barcodes survive across replicates, survival is a heritable pre-existing state, whereas random barcodes imply induced stochastic entry. Fitting state-switching rates to the barcode distributions quantifies how long the surviving state persists.

title: Sister-cell pairing with pre-treatment profiling
description: Separate the daughters of a cell division, profile one by scRNA-seq (destructively) and treat the other, then link the profile to survival using clonal lineage similarity. This could identify the pre-treatment transcriptional state that predicts survival, rather than inferring it after the fact.

title: Live-cell imaging with retrospective lineage tracking
description: Image thousands of single cells for days before drug addition with reporters for cell cycle, ERK/p53 or stress signaling, and mitochondrial state, then follow fates after treatment. Mapping survivors back to their pre-drug dynamics (e.g., pulses, cycle length) reveals which dynamic features predict survival.

title: Single-cell multiome of epigenetic priming
description: Perform joint ATAC and RNA profiling on untreated, early-treated, and persister populations to find chromatin accessibility present before drug exposure that foreshadows the persister program. Validate by perturbing the identified regulators or chromatin modifiers (e.g., KDM5, HDAC inhibitors) to see if the surviving fraction shifts.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens plus BH3 profiling
description: Run CRISPR knockout/activation screens under drug to identify genes that set the persister fraction, and pair them with single-cell BH3 profiling to test whether survivors are in a lower apoptotic-priming state. This separates causal drivers from correlates and shows whether survival works through apoptosis evasion, metabolism, or stress response.

title: Sister-cell splitting with lineage barcodes
description: Barcode a population, split it into replicate pools after a few divisions, and treat one pool while profiling the other by scRNA-seq. Matching barcodes between survivors and untreated sisters reveals the pre-treatment state of cells that would have survived, and shows how heritable it is.

title: Retrospective live-cell tracking of future survivors
description: Time-lapse image cells with reporters for signaling (ERK/AKT), cell cycle (FUCCI), and mitochondria before and during drug treatment. Trace survivors backward to find pre-treatment features that predict fate. Fixing the same cells afterward and performing multiplexed staining adds molecular information.

title: Fluctuation assays across subclones to estimate switching rates
description: Run fluctuation assays (Luria-Delbrück type) with many single-cell-derived subclones, measuring variance in survivor numbers and how quickly the survivor propensity is lost or regained after drug-free expansion. This distinguishes fixed rare mutations from reversible, epigenetic state switching and estimates the transition rates.

title: BH3 profiling and apoptotic priming in untreated cells
description: Measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming and BCL-2 family dependencies at single-cell resolution in drug-naive cells, and relate them to survival after treatment. This tests whether survivors simply sit lower in the apoptotic threshold distribution rather than having a distinct resistance program.

title: Persister-specific CRISPR dependency screens
description: Perform genome-wide or targeted CRISPR knockout/inhibition screens under drug, and compare guide depletion in persisters against untreated growth. This identifies genes needed only for survival (e.g., chromatin regulators, ferroptosis defense), which can then be tested in combination with the drug.

title: Barcoding with sister-cell split and pre-treatment profiling
description: Barcode a cell population, split it before treatment, and profile one half by scRNA-seq while treating the other. Matching barcodes of survivors to their untreated sister cells reveals pre-existing, predictive transcriptional states and shows whether survival is heritable.

title: Live imaging of signaling dynamics linked to survival
description: Track single cells with live reporters (ERK/AKT activity, FUCCI cell cycle, apoptosis markers) before and during drug exposure. Retrospectively analyze survivor trajectories to determine which dynamic features, such as pulses, rebound, or cell-cycle arrest, predict survival.

title: Fluctuation test with state-switching modeling
description: Run Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation assays across many parallel clonal cultures and compare survivor-count variance with stochastic models. This separates rare pre-existing genetic mutations from reversible non-genetic switching and estimates the switching rates.

title: Single-cell multiome of persisters across a drug time course
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and RNA jointly in the same cells at baseline, during drug exposure, and after drug withdrawal. This identifies enhancer and transcription factor programs that define the persister state and tests whether they are reversible epigenetic memory.

title: Pooled CRISPRi/a screen with persister-specific readout
description: Run genome-wide or targeted CRISPRi/a screens and score survival early under drug, before regrowth, and compare with late resistance outgrowth. Hits specific to persistence, such as chromatin regulators, stress pathways and apoptotic priming, identify causal drivers and combination targets.

title: Barcoded sister-cell lineage tracing with transcriptome readout
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split each clone into two halves, and profile one by scRNA-seq before treatment while treating the other. Surviving barcodes reveal the pre-treatment transcriptional state that predicted survival, and show whether persistence is pre-existing or induced.

title: Live-cell imaging with retrospective fate mapping
description: Time-lapse image cells carrying reporters (pathway activity, cell cycle, mitochondrial state) for days before drug addition. Then track each cell and its descendants through treatment. Correlate pre-drug dynamics and heritability across sister cells with survival to find predictive features.

title: Fluctuation test to separate phenotypic switching from mutation
description: Perform Luria-Delbruck assays with many parallel small clonal populations, plus drug-holiday re-challenge, and fit models to estimate phenotypic switching rates and memory duration. Combine this with sequencing of survivors to distinguish genetic, epigenetic, and stochastic origins of survival.

title: Sorting on pre-treatment physiology, then drug challenge
description: Use FACS to isolate untreated cells by mitochondrial membrane potential, drug uptake or efflux (fluorescent analogs), size or slow-cycling dye retention, and measure survival of each fraction. This directly tests which physiological axes causally enrich persisters.

title: Single-cell multiome with epigenetic perturbation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and expression jointly (scATAC plus RNA) in pre-persister and persister cells, and identify candidate regulators. Validate by CRISPRi/a or chromatin inhibitors targeting those regulators to see whether persister frequency shifts.

title: Lineage barcoding with split-sample single-cell RNA-seq
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it before drug, profile one arm by scRNA-seq and treat the other, then identify which barcodes survive. This allows the pre-treatment transcriptional state of cells destined to become persisters to be read out and tested for heritability.

title: Luria-Delbrück fluctuation analysis of persister frequency
description: Expand many small independent clones, treat each, and compare the variance in persister counts to that expected under pre-existing versus drug-induced tolerance. Fitting a state-switching model to the data yields switching rates and distinguishes stochastic state fluctuations from stable epigenetic or genetic inheritance.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging with retrospective pedigree tracing
description: Image cells for days before and after drug with reporters for signaling (ERK, p53), cell cycle (FUCCI) and stress, then trace surviving cells back through their lineage. This shows whether dynamics, cycle history or sister-cell correlations predict survival, which fixed snapshots cannot show.

title: Sorting on pre-treatment physiological state followed by drug challenge
description: Use FACS to sort untreated cells by mitochondrial potential, ROS, drug efflux activity, or fluorescent drug uptake, then treat each sorted fraction and measure persister yield. This tests whether candidate states cause persistence, and how long they last, by delaying the drug challenge after sorting.

title: Persister-fraction-focused CRISPR and epigenetic perturbation screens
description: Run pooled CRISPRi/a or epigenetic-inhibitor screens that read out the fraction of surviving cells at a fixed high dose, not bulk sensitivity. Hits that change only the persister fraction point to regulators of cell-state plasticity, and comparing them with scATAC/multiome data in persisters links them to chromatin mechanisms.

title: Barcode-linked pre-treatment transcriptomes
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split the population before drug, profile one half by scRNA-seq, and sequence barcodes in survivors from the other half. This reveals the pre-existing state of cells that go on to survive, and whether that state is shared among sister clones.

title: Fluctuation tests with heritability timing
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style assays on many small parallel clonal expansions, varying the time between subcloning and drug exposure. The variance in survivor numbers and its decay over generations quantify switching rates and memory duration, separating stable, transient, and drug-induced tolerance.

title: Live single-cell multi-reporter imaging with retrospective fate mapping
description: Image cells for days before drug addition with reporters for cell cycle, p53/stress signaling, and ERK activity, then add drug and record which cells survive. Tracing survivors' pre-drug dynamics back in time identifies predictive features such as slow cycling or pulsatile signaling.

title: Metabolic state sorting followed by drug challenge
description: Use NAD(P)H FLIM or mitochondrial membrane potential dyes to sort live cells by metabolic state before treatment, then expose each fraction to drug. This tests whether metabolic heterogeneity, such as oxidative phosphorylation reliance or redox buffering, causally predicts survival.

title: Single-cell multiome of persisters with chromatin perturbation
description: Profile persisters and matched untreated cells by joint scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq to find chromatin accessibility states and transcription factors that define tolerance. Then test causality by perturbing the candidates with CRISPRi or epigenetic inhibitors and measuring changes in persister frequency.

title: Lineage barcoding with sister-cell split before drug
description: Barcode a population, split it into replicate arms, and treat one arm while profiling the other by scRNA-seq. Matching barcodes between survivors and untreated sister clones reveals the pre-existing transcriptional state that predicts survival and shows whether it is heritable.

title: Live reporter imaging with retrospective survivor tracing
description: Image cells with fluorescent reporters of target pathway activity, cell cycle, and stress for days before drug, then follow them through treatment. Tracing survivors back identifies which pre-drug dynamics, such as pathway pulses or long G1 dwell, predict survival.

title: Fluctuation test with state-switching models
description: Perform Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation experiments on many small independent clonal cultures and measure the variance in survivor counts. Fit stochastic models to distinguish rare mutations from reversible non-genetic switching and to estimate switching rates and persister-state memory.

title: Single-cell multiome with FACS-based state enrichment
description: Use paired scRNA and ATAC profiling to define a persister-like signature and its regulatory elements. Sort cells by a surface marker or reporter for that state, challenge them with drug, and test causality by perturbing the identified chromatin regulators or transcription factors.

title: Single-cell drug exposure and apoptotic priming
description: Measure per-cell intracellular drug levels using fluorescent analogs or imaging mass spectrometry, and measure mitochondrial apoptotic priming with BH3 profiling. This tests whether survival comes from lower effective drug exposure or from a higher apoptotic threshold, which expression data alone cannot separate.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with sister-clone splitting
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes and split each population before drug treatment. Compare survival and transcriptomes of sister clones to quantify heritability of persistence, and recover pre-treatment states of future survivors by scRNA-seq of the untreated sibling arm.

title: Fluctuation test with switching-rate modeling
description: Run Luria-Delbrück fluctuation assays on many small clonal expansions, then fit stochastic models to separate pre-existing, rapidly switching states from drug-induced adaptation and estimate state switching rates and memory duration.

title: Live-cell imaging with retrospective fate mapping
description: Time-lapse image cells carrying reporters (cell cycle, stress response, mitochondrial potential) for days before and during drug treatment. Trace survivors back in time to identify which pre-drug features predicted survival.

title: Single-cell multiome of persisters with epigenetic perturbation
description: Profile chromatin accessibility and RNA jointly in untreated cells and persisters to identify reversible regulatory states. Then test causality with CRISPRi/CRISPRa or epigenetic inhibitors of the top candidate regulators.

title: Pre-sorting by metabolic and mitochondrial state
description: Use FACS or FLIM to isolate cells by mitochondrial potential, NADH state, or lipid peroxidation susceptibility before drug exposure, then compare their survival to test whether metabolic heterogeneity causally drives tolerance.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with sibling split and pre-treatment profiling
description: Label clonal cells with expressed lineage barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/FateMap-style), split sister cells before drug, profile one half by scRNA-seq and expose the other to drug, then test whether pre-treatment transcriptional state of a lineage predicts survival. This separates pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance and reveals the pre-treatment state of cells that are killed by the drug.

title: Epigenomic and extrachromosomal DNA profiling of isogenic single cells
description: Run single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA), histone-mark profiling (e.g., CUT&Tag), and ecDNA/copy-number sequencing on untreated and surviving cells to test whether chromatin states or ecDNA dosage heterogeneity, rather than sequence mutations, distinguish survivors. Perturb candidate regulators (e.g., with KDM5 or EZH2 inhibitors) to test causality.

title: Long-term live-cell imaging with single-cell tracking and fate mapping
description: Image thousands of individual cells for days before, during, and after drug treatment using fluorescent reporters (FUCCI cell cycle, ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, apoptosis caspase reporters, mitochondrial potential), then retrospectively link dynamics to cell fate. This captures fluctuating, non-binary states and the time course of persister entry, exit, and regrowth, rather than endpoint averages.

title: Spatial and single-cell multi-omics of survivors in 3D and in vivo models
description: Treat organoids, co-cultures, or xenografts with the drug and perform spatial transcriptomics/proteomics (e.g., MERFISH, imaging mass cytometry) to map where survivors sit relative to drug gradients, hypoxia, stroma, and immune cells. Compare to 2D culture to determine which survival states depend on the microenvironment and which contribute to survival independently of it.

title: CRISPR perturbation screens with single-cell readout across drug schedules
description: Run CRISPRi/a and Perturb-seq screens under different doses and schedules (continuous, pulsed, combination) to find regulators of the persister state beyond the target pathway, covering metabolism, stress response, and chromatin. Compare hits across persistence, tolerance, and resistance phenotypes (time-kill curves) to determine which layer of regulation drives survival.

title: Lineage barcoding with split-population fate tracing
