description: Label cells with heritable, expressed DNA barcodes, split the population into replicates before treatment, and compare which barcodes survive across replicates and how they relate to RNA profiles of sister cells taken before treatment. Shared survivors across replicates indicate a pre-existing heritable state, whereas random survivors indicate stochastic or induced entry into the surviving state.

title: Long-term live-cell imaging with lineage reconstruction
description: Track thousands of single cells and their families by time-lapse microscopy with reporters for cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, and apoptosis, before, during, and after drug. Test whether pre-drug history (cycle length, signaling pulses, sister-cell correlation) predicts survival, providing dynamic cell-by-cell data in place of endpoint snapshots.

title: Whole-genome and ecDNA/mtDNA profiling of clonally derived survivors
description: Sequence single-cell-derived clones, or single-cell DNA from pre-treatment and survivor cells, for rare mutations, copy-number changes, ecDNA amplification, and mtDNA heterogeneity, and test whether those variants are enriched in survivors. This tests the assumption that the cells are genetically identical, including variation below the resolution of standard exome or bulk sequencing.

title: Single-cell multi-omics with protein, chromatin, and metabolic readouts
description: Combine scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, CITE-seq or mass cytometry for signaling proteins, and metabolic imaging such as NAD(P)H FLIM or mitochondrial membrane potential, then sort and profile cells that survive. This tests whether transcript levels capture the relevant state and can identify epigenetic, proteomic, or metabolic determinants such as high mitochondrial priming or a drug-tolerant chromatin state.

title: Spatial and microenvironment perturbation of survival in co-culture, 3D, or in vivo models
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging in 3D spheroids, co-cultures, or xenografts to map survivors relative to neighbors, oxygen and drug gradients, and stromal secretion. Then perturb the niche, for example with conditioned medium, a drug-penetration reporter, or fluorescent drug analogs, to test whether survival depends on local drug exposure or paracrine support rather than intrinsic state, including whether drug exposure is uniform and whether monolayer culture is sufficient.

title: Lineage barcoding with sister-cell split-and-treat
description: Tag cells with expressed heritable barcodes and split clonal families before drug treatment. Sequence the untreated sibling cells to determine the baseline state of cells whose relatives survive. This tests whether survival is a pre-existing, heritable state versus a post-drug stochastic adaptation, and recovers the pre-drug transcriptome of future survivors.

title: Single-cell whole-genome and clonal deep sequencing for hidden genetics
description: Run single-cell DNA-seq (CNV, SNV) or deep clonal sequencing on pre-treatment populations and on survivors to test for rare subclonal variants, extrachromosomal DNA, or mtDNA heteroplasmy. A matched comparison of survivors against the clonal parental population shows whether apparent non-genetic persistence has a cryptic genetic basis.

title: Spatial and co-culture perturbation of microenvironment effects
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging with defined neighbor-density gradients, conditioned media, and sparse versus dense plating or microfluidic isolation of single cells to test whether survival depends on neighbors, paracrine signals, or local drug and oxygen gradients. Comparing isolated cells to colonies separates cell-intrinsic from community-driven survival.

title: Live-cell time-lapse tracking with retrospective fate mapping
description: Image reporter lines (cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, apoptosis, stress response) in single cells for days before and during drug treatment, then link dynamic histories (cycle length, signaling pulses) to fate by machine learning. This avoids post-hoc identification of survivors and shows whether survival is predicted by dynamics or history rather than by a static snapshot state.

title: Multi-omic profiling across dose, 2D, organoid, and xenograft contexts
description: Apply paired single-cell ATAC/RNA plus proteomics or metabolic imaging (NADH FLIM, mitochondrial membrane potential) across a dose range, in 2D culture, organoids, and xenografts, to determine whether survivors use multiple dose- and context-dependent mechanisms. Perturb candidate factors by CRISPRi in a pooled screen to test which molecular layers causally contribute, beyond mRNA-only single-cause models.

title: Lineage barcoding with sibling-pair and split-clone tracking
description: Barcode cells, split the expanded population into replicate arms before drug, and compare which barcodes survive across arms and between sister cells. This shows whether survival is heritable and pre-existing, or stochastic and drug-induced. It also gives the memory timescale of the state.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging with retrospective fate mapping
description: Image cells for days before and after drug using reporters for ERK or p53 dynamics, cell cycle, and apoptosis, then trace survivors back to their pre-drug history. Dynamic features such as pulsing or cell cycle phase can be tested as predictors of survival. Fixed-cell profiling of the same cells can be added afterward.

title: Single-cell multiomics of one clone, including genetic and non-nuclear variation
description: Run joint scRNA/scATAC with single-cell DNA sequencing, which gives copy number, ecDNA and mtDNA variants, on cells before drug, during drug and after it. This tests whether small genetic or mitochondrial differences exist within the apparently identical clone. It also tests whether survivors share any such difference or any state.

title: Pre-drug state capture linked to fate with Live-seq or photoactivatable isolation
description: Take a non-destructive RNA biopsy, or image-guided photo-marking and sorting, of individual cells before drug. Follow each cell to its fate, then train a model to predict survival from its prior state. This directly tests whether a pre-existing state exists, instead of inferring it from survivors only.

title: Mapping microenvironment and drug-exposure heterogeneity in 3D and in vivo models
description: Use spheroids, organoids or xenografts with spatial transcriptomics, hypoxia and nutrient sensors, and mass-spectrometry imaging of drug levels. Compare survivors' positions and local drug concentration with their intrinsic state. This separates truly resistant cells from cells that were under-dosed or protected by neighbors or stroma.

title: Lineage barcoding with split-clone fate tracing
description: Label cells with expressed heritable barcodes, split the population before drug, treat one arm and profile the other by scRNA-seq, so each survivor's sister cells reveal its pre-treatment state. Clone-level concordance of survival across replicates distinguishes pre-existing heritable states from stochastic switching, which tests whether survivors are a pre-existing, stable subpopulation.

title: Time-lapse single-cell imaging with live reporters and retrospective tracking
description: Image cells for days before, during and after drug using reporters for cell-cycle state, ERK/AKT activity, p53 dynamics, and mitochondrial or ROS state, then trace survivors back to their pre-drug histories. Dynamic features such as pulsing, cell-cycle duration and recent mitosis may predict survival where static snapshots fail, which tests the assumption that survival depends on fixed, single-time-point properties.

title: Genetic and epigenetic comparison of survivors with matched untreated sisters
description: Perform single-cell whole-genome or exome sequencing for copy-number changes and subclonal variants, along with scATAC or CUT&Tag for chromatin state, on sorted survivors and barcode-matched untreated sister cells. This tests whether the cells are in fact genetically identical and whether heritable chromatin states, rather than transcript levels, carry the difference.

title: Spatial and microenvironment-resolved survival mapping in 3D or in vivo
description: Treat spheroids, organoids with stromal cells, or xenografts, then use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging with drug-penetration measurements to map survivors against position, oxygen, neighbor identity and local drug concentration. This tests whether survival comes from cell-intrinsic state or from niche and pharmacokinetic heterogeneity.

title: Multi-omic single-cell profiling of proteins, metabolism and signaling
description: Use CyTOF or CITE-seq for proteins and phospho-signaling, along with single-cell metabolic readouts such as NAD(P)H FLIM or SCENITH, on cells sampled at several times after drug. Pair this with CRISPR perturbation of candidate non-target-pathway programs, such as oxidative phosphorylation, drug efflux or stress-response genes, to show causality. This tests whether transcripts are sufficient and whether the drug's target pathway explains survival.

title: Barcode lineage tracing with sibling-matched pre-treatment profiling
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split the clonal sibling cells before drug, and profile one half by scRNA-seq while treating the other half, so that barcodes identify which pre-treatment states gave rise to survivors. This tests whether survival is pre-existing and heritable and avoids reading survivors only after the fact. Comparing barcode enrichment across replicate splits separates pre-existing from drug-induced states.

title: Whole-genome and mtDNA deep sequencing of isolated survivors
description: Sort or isolate survivors and matched untreated clonal siblings, then run deep whole-genome, copy-number, ecDNA and mtDNA heteroplasmy sequencing to look for rare subclonal variants. This tests whether the cells are in fact genetically identical, and finds low-frequency genetic contributors if they are not. Re-treating clones expanded from survivors indicates whether the resistance is stably inherited.

title: Live-cell single-cell time-lapse with reporters and retrospective fate assignment
description: Image cells for days before and after drug with reporters for cell cycle (FUCCI), ERK or AKT signaling, apoptosis, and drug-target activity, and track each cell's lineage to its eventual fate. Dynamic features such as pre-drug cell-cycle phase, pulsatile signaling, and time of arrest can be tested as predictors of survival, replacing a single live/dead endpoint with trajectories. Fixing and staining the same cells afterward connects the dynamics to molecular state.

title: Spatial and co-culture manipulation of neighbor effects
description: Plate cells at controlled densities and in micropatterns, use conditioned-medium swaps and mixed cultures with fluorescent labels, and run spatial transcriptomics, to test whether survival depends on local neighbors, paracrine signals, or position. Compare the survival of an isolated single cell to that of the same cell type in a cluster. A neighborhood-dependent effect would show survival is not purely cell-autonomous.

title: Single-cell drug uptake, efflux and metabolic imaging
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration in individual cells, using fluorescent drug analogs or label-free mass spectrometry imaging, together with efflux activity, NAD(P)H/FLIM metabolic state, mitochondrial membrane potential and ROS, and then follow those cells' survival. This tests whether survivors differ in drug exposure or metabolism rather than in transcript levels. Pharmacological perturbation of the identified efflux or metabolic pathways can then provide a causal test.

title: Single-cell DNA and mtDNA lineage sequencing of survivors vs. matched sister lineages
description: Use barcoded lineage tracing plus single-cell DNA-seq (CNV, ecDNA, mtDNA heteroplasmy) on survivors and untreated sister lineages. This tests whether apparently identical cells carry rare heritable genetic or mtDNA differences that predispose them to survival.

title: Lineage-barcoded split-clone experiments with pre-treatment profiling
description: Barcode cells and split each expanding clone into two sister arms: one profiled by scRNA-seq/ATAC before drug, and one treated with drug. The barcodes link pre-existing states to survival. Sister-clone concordance and fluctuation-test statistics show whether tolerance is pre-existing and heritable or induced.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with lineage tracking, followed by in situ endpoint omics
description: Image thousands of single cells and their ancestry for days before, during, and after drug exposure using biosensors (ERK/AKT activity, cell cycle, apoptosis, mitochondrial state). Then fix the cells and perform multiplexed imaging or spatial transcriptomics on the same cells, to resolve dynamic trajectories and the timing of fate decisions that snapshot measurements miss.

title: Spatial and co-culture perturbation of microenvironment and neighbor effects
description: Compare survival in 3D spheroids, organoids or tumor sections using spatial transcriptomics, and in dense vs sparse cultures and conditioned-medium or neighbor-ablation set-ups, to test whether survivors depend on position, drug penetration, or paracrine signaling from neighbors rather than intrinsic state.

title: Multi-dose, multi-timepoint pharmacology with target engagement and CRISPR perturbation of candidate programs
description: Measure single-cell drug concentration (fluorescent or mass-spec imaging analogs), efflux activity, target occupancy and phospho-pathway rebound across doses and times, and run pooled CRISPR screens plus epigenetic profiling (histone marks, chromatin accessibility) of persisters. This tests which states causally govern survival and whether epigenetic or metabolic memory is required.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with pre-drug split-clone sampling
description: Label cells with heritable expression barcodes, split the population before treatment, and sequence one half while treating the other. This tests whether survivors are pre-determined by a heritable (non-genetic or hidden genetic) state by matching surviving lineages to their pre-drug transcriptomes, and measuring how much of survival is shared among sister clones versus random.

title: Single-cell multi-omic and long-read genomic profiling of survivors
description: Perform single-cell WGS or DNA+RNA co-profiling (plus ecDNA and copy-number analysis) on survivors and matched untreated cells, with ultra-deep duplex sequencing of the parental line. This tests the 'genetically identical' premise by detecting rare subclonal SNVs, CNVs, or ecDNA enriched in survivors.

title: Long-term live-cell imaging with reporters and retrospective fate mapping
description: Image thousands of single cells for days before and during drug exposure using reporters for signaling (ERK/AKT), cell cycle (FUCCI), and apoptosis, then identify survivors and trace their histories backward. This tests the assumption that survival is static, binary, and measurable at an endpoint, by revealing whether pre-drug dynamics such as pulsatile signaling, slow cycling, or division-time history predict survival, and whether cells enter and exit tolerance.

title: Spatial and co-culture perturbation of microenvironment and drug exposure
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging in 3D spheroids or xenografts, together with microfluidic or conditioned-medium manipulations, to map where survivors are located relative to drug gradients, hypoxia, stroma, and neighboring dying cells. This tests whether local niche, paracrine signals (e.g., from dying neighbors), or reduced effective drug dose, rather than a cell-intrinsic state, cause survival.

title: Sorting live pre-drug cells by non-transcriptional state and testing causality
description: Use live-cell reporters or dyes (mitochondrial membrane potential, NADH/FLIM, ROS, lysosomal content) and single-cell ATAC or histone-mark profiling to sort rare states, then challenge sorted fractions with drug. Pair this with CRISPR perturbation or inhibitors of the candidate states (e.g., GPX4, histone demethylases) to test whether the tolerance state is encoded outside mRNA levels and whether it is causal rather than correlative.

title: Pre-existing versus induced tolerance from lineage-barcoding datasets
description: Reanalyze public clonal barcoding scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., studies of BRAF-inhibitor-treated melanoma and EGFR-inhibitor-treated lung cancer, including Shaffer, Hata, Oren and Goyal data in GEO). Test whether sister cells' pre-treatment transcriptomes predict survival, and quantify how much of survival is heritable versus stochastic, to separate pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance.

title: Pre-treatment expression signature of persisters
description: Use public paired pre- and post-treatment single-cell expression data to build a classifier of the rare pre-treatment cell state, such as NGFR-high, AXL-high or dedifferentiated melanoma states, and EMT-like or drug-tolerant states. Validate it on held-out cell lines and on public drug-response data (GDSC, CTRP, DepMap PRISM) by testing whether the signature predicts tolerance across lines.

title: Meta-analysis of chromatin accessibility and epigenetic memory
description: Integrate public scATAC-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq and histone-mark data (H3K27me3, KDM5 targets, SWI/SNF) from persisters and parental cells. Find the transcription factor motifs and enhancers that open or close in persisters, and check whether those accessibility changes are already present in a subset of untreated cells, to identify the regulators that carry the memory.

title: Modeling transcriptional noise, cell-cycle state, and metabolic state
description: Using public time-course scRNA-seq and live-cell imaging datasets, calculate gene-expression variability, cell-cycle phase (slow-cycling or G0/G1 arrest) and metabolic signatures (oxidative phosphorylation, ferroptosis defense via GPX4). Fit stochastic state-switching models to estimate the switching rates and ask whether survival is better explained by noise, quiescence or metabolic state.

title: Genetic exclusion and clinical concordance analysis
description: Reanalyze public whole-exome and whole-genome data and copy-number profiles from persister cells, resistant clones and matched patient biopsies (such as minimal residual disease samples). Rule out pre-existing mutations and copy-number changes as the cause, and check whether the persister transcriptional programs also appear in patient on-treatment samples and associate with relapse in TCGA and clinical trial cohorts.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing before and after drug
description: Label a clonal line with a high-complexity expression barcode library, split into replicate pools, treat with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes pre- and post-treatment. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, the cause is a pre-existing heritable state. If different barcodes survive, the cause is stochastic or induced. Cost is roughly $5–10k, covering the library, cell culture and amplicon sequencing.

title: scRNA-seq of matched lineages: pre-drug sister cells versus survivors
description: Split barcoded cells so that sister cells are profiled by scRNA-seq before drug and survivors are profiled after. This links the pre-treatment transcriptional state (for example drug-efflux, EMT-like, or stress-response programs) to later survival. Sequencing about 10–20k cells across timepoints fits within about $10–15k.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with fluorescent reporters and lineage tracking
description: Image cells for days before and during drug exposure, using reporters for ERK or AKT signaling, cell cycle (FUCCI), and apoptosis, and track single-cell lineages. This shows whether survival is predicted by pre-existing signaling dynamics, slow cycling, or inherited fluctuations, and whether it correlates between sister cells. It uses an existing microscope and open-source tracking software, with reagents costing about $3–8k.

title: Sort rare states by candidate markers, then profile and re-challenge with drug
description: Sort cells by candidate markers such as a surface marker, a fluorescent reporter of a resistance-associated gene, or a mitochondrial or ROS dye. Then test drug sensitivity and chromatin accessibility and expression (bulk ATAC/RNA-seq) in each fraction. Compare how fast sorted populations return to the original distribution to measure state-switching rates and epigenetic memory. Reagents and sequencing cost about $8–12k.

title: Perturbation screen of candidate persistence mechanisms
description: Run a focused CRISPRi/CRISPRa screen, or a small-molecule screen, targeting chromatin regulators, stress-response genes, drug transporters, and metabolic enzymes. Treat with the drug and score enrichment or depletion of survivors. This tests which pathways are causally needed for survival, as opposed to merely correlated with it. Use a few hundred genes with 5–10 guides each, which costs about $10–15k.

title: Lineage-tracked pre-treatment history of survivors
description: Perform long-term time-lapse of cells before drug addition, tracking lineages with nuclear and cell-cycle reporters (e.g., H2B-mCherry, FUCCI), then add drug and retrospectively trace survivors back to their ancestors. This tests whether survival is predicted by pre-existing states such as cell-cycle length, quiescence or division history, and whether sister and cousin cells share fates, which would indicate heritable rather than stochastic states.

title: Live biosensors of signaling and stress dynamics
description: Image single cells carrying fluorescent reporters for the drug's target pathway (e.g., ERK KTR for MAPK inhibitors), p53, NF-κB, and the integrated stress response through drug exposure. Quantify whether survivors show faster pathway reactivation, pulsatile or adaptive dynamics, or lower stress amplitude than cells that die, linking dynamic signaling signatures to fate.

title: Real-time apoptosis and caspase-threshold imaging
description: Use live caspase-3/7 or FRET-based caspase reporters, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes and BH3-sensitivity reporters to measure each cell's distance from the apoptotic threshold. Compare the timing, rate and reversibility (anastasis) of caspase activation in survivors and dying cells to show whether survivors resist initiation of death, show sublethal caspase activity, or recover after partial activation.

title: Post-treatment fate mapping of persister state transitions
description: Continuously image survivors for weeks under drug with proliferation and cell-cycle reporters, plus size and morphology readouts. Classify fates such as arrest, slow cycling, polyploidization, or drug-tolerant re-entry, and measure regrowth kinetics after drug withdrawal. This shows whether persisters are a stable subpopulation or a transient, reversible state, and how rare re-entry events arise.

title: Live imaging of drug exposure and metabolic or organelle state
description: Image intrinsically fluorescent or fluorescently labeled drug to measure per-cell uptake and efflux, alongside live readouts of NAD(P)H/FAD autofluorescence (FLIM), mitochondrial content, ROS and lysosomal dye. Single-cell correlations with eventual fate test whether survival reflects lower intracellular drug dose, efflux activity, or distinct metabolic and organelle states.

title: Lineage barcoding with sister-cell split analysis
description: Label cells with heritable, non-perturbing expressed DNA barcodes (viral barcode library, no gene perturbation), split the population before treatment, and compare barcode abundance and pre-treatment transcriptomes of sister clones to test whether survival is pre-existing and heritable (clonal) versus stochastic. Pairing scRNA-seq of untreated sisters with the barcodes of survivors identifies the pre-treatment state that predicts persistence.

title: Live-cell time-lapse tracking with retrospective lineage analysis
description: Image thousands of single cells and their lineages for days before, during, and after drug using non-perturbing live reporters (e.g., FUCCI, ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes). Retrospectively link pre-drug cell-cycle length, signaling dynamics, and mother-daughter correlations to survival and then to regrowth, to identify which dynamic states predict survival and how heritable they are.

title: Time-resolved single-cell multi-omics of drug response
description: Perform scRNA-seq combined with scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) at multiple time points (untreated, hours, days, weeks of drug) to map the trajectory from baseline cell states to persister states. Inferring state transitions with RNA velocity or trajectory methods distinguishes selection of rare pre-existing states from drug-induced adaptive reprogramming, and chromatin accessibility reveals candidate regulatory programs.

title: Fluctuation test and state-sorting experiments
description: Compare variance in surviving colony numbers across many parallel small cultures versus bulk replicates, and sort cells by candidate markers or reporters (e.g., high/low of a drug-tolerance-associated surface marker, ROS, or lipid content) before drug exposure. Measure survival of each sorted fraction and how quickly sorted subpopulations re-equilibrate, to quantify switching rates and test whether tolerance is a reversible non-genetic state.

title: Orthogonal genomic, epigenomic and metabolic profiling of persisters versus matched controls
description: Run single-cell or low-input whole-genome/exome sequencing on survivors to rule out or identify genetic or copy-number changes. Combine this with epigenomic profiling (histone marks, DNA methylation) and single-cell metabolic readouts (mass cytometry, NAD(P)H FLIM, mitochondrial/lipid dyes, drug efflux assays, and measurements of intracellular drug concentration). Then use pharmacologic perturbations (e.g., small-molecule epigenetic or metabolic inhibitors, not genetic) to test which differences are functionally linked to persistence.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing in a canine or zebrafish-derived cancer line
description: Use a clonal lentiviral/CRISPR barcode library in a genetically identical non-human, non-mouse cancer line (e.g., canine osteosarcoma or zebrafish melanoma ZMEL1 cells). Split the barcoded population into replicate arms, treat each with a targeted inhibitor (e.g., BRAF/MEK inhibitor in ZMEL1), and sequence barcodes in survivors. Barcodes that recur across independent replicates indicate a pre-existing, heritable survivor state. Barcodes that are random across replicates indicate stochastic, drug-induced adaptation.

title: Single-cell multiome profiling of survivors in zebrafish melanoma before and after drug
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on ZMEL1 cells (or on tumors in transparent casper zebrafish) at baseline, at early drug exposure, and at the drug-tolerant persister stage. Match surviving cells to their pre-treatment states using barcodes or transcriptional trajectories. This shows whether survivors come from a rare chromatin or transcriptional state (e.g., neural crest-like or slow-cycling) and which regulators maintain that state.

title: Live-cell imaging of cell fate with zebrafish xenograft or transgenic reporters
description: Image fluorescent reporters of cell cycle (FUCCI), ERK/kinase activity (FRET biosensor), mitochondrial state, and apoptosis in individual cells in transparent zebrafish tumors or cultured fish cancer cells. Record cells for days before and during drug exposure, and retrospectively classify the cells that survive. Because cells are tracked over time, this links pre-treatment dynamics (pulsatile signaling, quiescence, cell-cycle phase, mitochondrial priming) to survival at single-cell resolution, which snapshot omics cannot do.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens in a Drosophila cell line or tumor model
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens in Drosophila S2R+ cells, or RNAi screens in a Ras/Scrib fly tumor model, under a targeted inhibitor (e.g., a MEK or PI3K inhibitor). Look for genes that change the fraction of survivors without changing the average drug IC50. These genes, such as chromatin regulators, stress-response genes and drug-efflux genes, would identify the machinery of tolerance as distinct from classical resistance, and the screens are cheaper and more tractable than in mammalian cells.

title: Genetic, epigenetic and reversibility tests on survivor clones in yeast models
description: Use drug-tolerant subpopulations of budding yeast (e.g., engineered with oncogenic RAS or TOR pathway activation under a TOR/kinase inhibitor). Sort survivors by growth rate, expand clones, and whole-genome sequence them. Test heritability by regrowing without drug and re-challenging at timed intervals. Combine this with ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq and single-cell growth-rate measurements in microfluidics to separate mutation from reversible epigenetic or noise-driven states and to measure state-switching rates directly.

title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment and post-treatment transcriptomics
description: Tag a clonal cell line with a heritable expression barcode library, split the population before drug exposure, profile one half by scRNA-seq, and treat the other half. Match surviving barcodes back to the pre-treatment sister cells to find the transcriptional states that predicted survival and test whether those states are heritable or transient. This takes about 2–3 months with an established barcoding system.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters followed by fate-linked fixed profiling
description: Image cells carrying reporters (such as FUCCI for cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, and apoptosis markers) for several days before and during drug treatment, and track single-cell fates. After imaging, fix the cells in place and run multiplexed immunofluorescence or in situ RNA staining on the same cells. This links dynamic signaling history and cell-cycle state to survival or death.

title: Single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA) of drug-tolerant persisters over a time course
description: Collect untreated cells and cells at days 3, 7, and 14 of treatment, and profile chromatin accessibility and gene expression jointly in the same cells. This tests whether persisters carry a distinct epigenetic state, such as an altered enhancer landscape or a stress/dedifferentiation program, and identifies the transcription factors that drive it.

title: Pooled CRISPRi/CRISPRa screen of candidate persister regulators
description: Run a targeted CRISPRi/CRISPRa library covering chromatin regulators, stress-response genes, anti-apoptotic factors, and metabolic genes, with drug and vehicle arms and sgRNA counts read out at several time points. Genes whose loss reduces the persister fraction, or whose activation raises it, identify pathways that are causally required for survival rather than only correlated with it.

title: Single-cell metabolic and apoptotic-priming measurements
description: Before treatment, sort cells by readouts such as mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, lipid content, or BH3 profiling for apoptotic priming. Then treat the sorted subpopulations and measure survival to test whether pre-existing differences in metabolism or mitochondrial apoptotic threshold set the likelihood of surviving. Follow with drug combinations that target the identified vulnerability, such as BCL-2 family inhibitors or ferroptosis inducers.

title: Single-cell multiome of drug-naive cells with lineage barcodes
description: Profile untreated cells at one time point with scRNA-seq plus chromatin accessibility, and use clonal barcodes in parallel sister samples (Rosetta/Watermelon-style) to link pre-existing transcriptional and epigenetic states to later survival. This identifies the cell-state signatures and regulatory programs that predispose to persistence, and tests whether states are heritable.

title: Single-cell profiling of survivors at one late time point with matched untreated control
description: Harvest cells after a fixed drug exposure and run scRNA-seq or CITE-seq, comparing against untreated cells to define the persister state (e.g., drug-tolerant, EMT-like, stress response, dormancy). Cell-surface markers from CITE-seq can then be used to isolate and test persisters.

title: Spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging of treated tumors
description: Take a single fixed snapshot of treated spheroids or xenograft sections and map surviving cells with spatial transcriptomics or CODEX/IMC. This tests whether survival depends on microenvironment, such as hypoxia, proximity to stroma, or drug-penetration gradients, rather than on cell-intrinsic state alone.

title: Pooled CRISPR screen read out at a single endpoint
description: Transduce a genome-wide or focused (epigenetic, stress-response, apoptosis, drug-efflux) CRISPR library, treat, and sequence guide abundance once at endpoint relative to the untreated control. Enriched or depleted guides identify genes that causally enable or prevent persistence, which goes beyond correlative profiling.

title: Fixed-cell single-cell measurement of drug, signaling and apoptotic priming
description: At one time point after treatment, use mass cytometry or high-content multiplexed immunofluorescence to measure target inhibition (phospho-signaling), intracellular drug levels (for fluorescent drugs), efflux pump expression, cell-cycle status, and BH3 profiling or cleaved caspase levels in each cell. This distinguishes persisters that avoid drug exposure, bypass target inhibition, or resist apoptosis, and captures multiple mechanisms simultaneously per cell.

title: Paired single-cell multi-omics of patient biopsies before and during targeted therapy
description: Perform scRNA-seq plus scATAC-seq (or multiome) on serial biopsies from the same patients at baseline, on-treatment (residual disease), and at progression to identify transcriptional and chromatin states enriched in surviving cells. Then test whether those states were already present at low frequency before treatment, which would indicate pre-existing rather than drug-induced tolerance.

title: Barcode lineage tracing with transcriptomics in patient-derived cultures
description: Introduce expressed DNA barcodes into patient-derived tumor cells, split the population into replicates, treat with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes and transcriptomes of survivors versus untreated sister cells. Barcodes shared across independent replicates indicate heritable, pre-existing persister states, while barcodes appearing in only one replicate indicate stochastic or induced survival.

title: Live-cell imaging and tracking of patient-derived cells with reporter-based fate readouts
description: Time-lapse image patient tumor cells expressing signaling reporters (e.g., ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, cell-cycle and apoptosis sensors) before and through drug exposure, tracking each cell's lineage to the end. Retrospective analysis tests whether pre-treatment signaling dynamics, cell-cycle position, or lineage history predict survival, and fixed-cell multiplex profiling of the same cells can then link the phenotypes to molecular states.

title: Single-cell genomic and epigenomic profiling of pre-treatment tumors and persisters
description: Run single-cell DNA sequencing (copy number and mutations) and single-cell DNA methylation or histone-mark profiling (e.g., CUT&Tag) on patient tumor samples before treatment and on persisters. This distinguishes rare pre-existing subclones or copy-number changes from non-genetic, epigenetically maintained states, and identifies which regulators, such as KDM5 or other chromatin modifiers, sustain the tolerant state.

title: Spatial profiling of patient tumor sections around residual cells
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed protein imaging to matched pre-treatment and residual-disease patient specimens to determine whether surviving cells cluster near specific stromal, immune, hypoxic, or nutrient-limited niches. Then use ligand–receptor analysis and co-culture of patient-derived cells with autologous stromal or immune cells to test whether these niche signals cause tolerance.

title: Fluctuation-test analysis of survivor-count variance
description: Seed many small replicate cultures from single cells or a few cells, expand them for varied times, treat with drug, and compare the variance and mean of survivor counts across replicates and expansion times. Fit stochastic state-switching models to estimate switching rates into and out of the tolerant state, distinguishing pre-existing heritable states, rapid reversible switching, and drug-induced adaptation, and to estimate state memory duration.

title: Survival concordance of related cells as a function of lineage distance
description: Plate cells at clonal density, track individual cell divisions, and treat sister pairs, cousins, and more distant relatives at defined times after division. Measure how survival concordance decays with lineage distance to quantify how long the tolerant state is inherited and whether the determinant is cytoplasmic (e.g., mitochondria, protein levels) or epigenetic.

title: Mitotic history and cell-cycle timing dependence of survival
description: Combine live imaging with fluorescent cell-cycle reporters and a short drug pulse to test whether survival depends on cell-cycle phase at exposure, time since last division, or mitotic duration, including slow-cycling or G0-like states. Use pulsed or synchronized drug application and asymmetric partitioning markers (e.g. label-retention dyes) to separate the effects of cycle state from stable cell identity.

title: Single-cell DNA copy number and ecDNA heterogeneity profiling
description: Use single-cell DNA sequencing, or ecDNA FISH combined with drug-target gene imaging, on untreated and surviving cells to test whether apparently identical cells differ in target or bypass-gene copy number, ecDNA content, or low-frequency mutations. Compare the rate at which copy number diverges in sub-clones with survivor frequency to see whether copy number variation or ecDNA drives survival.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug and target-engagement quantification
description: Measure per-cell intracellular drug concentration (using intrinsically fluorescent drugs, a fluorescent drug analog, or mass-spec imaging/CyTOF for metal-labeled compounds) together with target occupancy or downstream phosphorylation shortly after exposure. Sort cells on drug content and re-challenge them to test whether survivors experience lower effective target inhibition (via efflux, lysosomal sequestration, or target abundance) or tolerate equal inhibition.

title: Sister-cell concordance in microfluidic traps
description: Track pairs of daughter cells (or micro-colonies) in microfluidic traps and compare their drug fate with that of random unrelated pairs. Use the decay of concordance over generations to estimate the memory timescale of tolerance. Fitting the data to stochastic-switching models distinguishes fast fluctuation, epigenetic memory, and mutation without requiring molecular markers.

title: Single-cell DNA replication stress and mitotic history readout
description: Using scEdU, 53BP1 staining and fixed-cell cell-cycle profiling, quantify inherited DNA damage, under-replicated DNA, and 53BP1 nuclear bodies in mother-daughter pairs before drug, then relate them to survival. This tests whether persisters arise from a prior stress or mitotic-error history rather than from a stable transcriptional state.

title: Single-cell signaling-network profiling by mass cytometry or phospho-flow
description: Measure dozens of phospho-proteins and cleaved-caspase markers at several time points after drug in the same cells to infer rewiring of the target's pathway and feedback loops. Information-theoretic analysis (e.g., mutual information between input and output, or bypass-pathway reactivation) would show whether survivors reactivate signaling early, an event that transcriptomics often misses.

title: Mitochondrial DNA variants as lineage markers for heritable tolerance
description: Use natural mtDNA variants (via mitochondrial scATAC or MAESTER) as endogenous lineage barcodes in clonal lines. Test whether heteroplasmy level or mtDNA copy number in sister cells predicts survival. This tests whether non-genetic, non-nuclear heritable variation explains drug tolerance in a genetically identical population.

title: Intracellular drug quantification at single-cell resolution
description: Use intrinsically fluorescent drugs, a fluorescent drug analog, or a target-engagement biosensor (such as a cellular thermal shift or an imaging-based probe competition assay) to measure how much drug reaches and binds the target in each cell. Comparing this with cell fate shows whether survivors receive lower effective doses through uptake, efflux, or lysosomal sequestration, rather than being intrinsically resistant.

title: Sibling-pair death-timing correlation under drug
description: Film isolated daughter-cell pairs (and later cousins) from a recent division through drug exposure and record each cell's time of death or arrest. Compare sister-sister concordance with random pairing, and its decay over generations, to quantify the heritability and half-life of the tolerance state without molecular assumptions.

title: Single-cell metabolic and redox state measurement, then drug challenge
description: Measure NAD(P)H lifetime (FLIM), ATP/NADH biosensors, mitochondrial membrane potential, and ROS in individual drug-naive cells, then gently sort or track them and challenge with drug. This tests whether pre-existing metabolic or redox heterogeneity, rather than transcript level, predicts survival.

title: Heterogeneity in drug-target engagement and intracellular drug concentration
description: Use a fluorescent drug analog, a target-engagement reporter (such as a CETSA-like or phospho-substrate readout), or single-cell mass spectrometry/mass cytometry to measure how much drug reaches the target in each cell. Compare survivors with dying cells to determine whether efflux, lysosomal sequestration, or incomplete pathway inhibition explains survival rather than downstream adaptation.

title: Time-resolved nascent transcription and translation in early drug response
description: Apply scSLAM-seq or scNT-seq with 4sU labeling, plus puromycin-based translation readouts, during the first hours of drug exposure to separate newly induced stress programs from pre-existing mRNA. Comparing the labeled and unlabeled fractions shows whether survivors actively rewire, for example through ISR-driven selective translation, or simply start from a different baseline.

title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors in 3D culture or xenografts
description: Run spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging (such as CODEX) on drug-treated spheroids or tumors, and test whether survivors cluster by local oxygen, density, stromal contact, or neighbor-secreted signals. Complement this with conditioned-medium and density-titration experiments to determine whether tolerance is cell-intrinsic or induced by neighbors.

title: Division-history memory via dye dilution and H2B-FUCCI
description: Label cells with a retained dye or photoconvertible histone to record the number of divisions and time since last mitosis, then sort by division history before drug exposure. This tests whether survival is encoded by proliferative history (e.g., slow-cycling lineages, inherited from mother-cell age) rather than by a specific expression program.

title: Single-cell copy-number and mutation mapping of survivors
description: Run single-cell whole-genome sequencing (and scRNA-seq on the same cells via paired methods) on survivors versus matched pre-treatment clones to detect rare subclonal aneuploidy, extrachromosomal DNA amplification, or ongoing mutagenesis. This tests whether the cells are genetically identical at the sub-chromosomal level, and whether persisters transiently up-regulate error-prone repair.

title: Quantitative per-cell drug-target engagement
description: Use a fluorescent drug analog, a CETSA/NanoBRET target-engagement reporter, or a phospho-substrate biosensor to measure how much drug binds its target in each cell in the first hours after treatment. Then sort cells by engagement and follow their fates, to distinguish pharmacokinetic escape (low intracellular occupancy) from downstream signaling rewiring.

title: Manipulating gene expression noise
description: Use synthetic circuits or promoter/CRISPR edits that change the expression variability of a candidate gene while holding its mean constant, then measure the persister fraction. This tests causally whether non-genetic heterogeneity (noise itself) generates survivors, and whether bet-hedging is selectable.

title: Neighbor and microenvironment contribution via spatial co-culture and conditioned-medium swaps
description: Plate cells at controlled densities and micropatterns, or use mixed fluorescently labeled populations. Quantify survival as a function of neighbor identity, distance to dying cells, and secreted factors, using spatial transcriptomics or cell-cell proximity labeling (e.g., TurboID), to test whether persistence is a cell-intrinsic state or a collective property arising from paracrine rescue or local contact signaling.

title: Inheritance of drug tolerance across generations by sister and cousin concordance
description: Time-lapse image newly divided sister pairs and their daughters across several generations, then apply drug and score survival concordance in sister pairs versus cousin pairs. The decay of sister/cousin correlation with generation distance gives the memory time of the tolerant state. Asymmetric partitioning of mitochondria, p53, or protein aggregates can be tested as a causal inherited factor.

title: Single-cell metabolic and biophysical profiling of pre-drug cells
description: Before treatment, measure each cell's NAD(P)H/FAD lifetime (FLIM), mitochondrial membrane potential, cell mass (suspended microchannel resonator) and density, then track survival of those same cells. This tests whether physiological state, not just transcripts, predicts survival, and it avoids destructive profiling.

title: Replication-stress and DNA damage history mapping
description: Combine EdU/BrdU pulse-chase, 53BP1 nuclear body imaging, and γH2AX tracking in the generation before drug exposure, then follow outcomes. This tests whether inherited damage or replication-timing differences from the previous cell cycle set up drug tolerance, a mechanism expression profiling would miss.

title: Micropatterning and co-culture perturbation of cell-cell interactions and microenvironment
description: Culture identical cells at controlled densities, in micropatterned islands, or in co-culture with conditioned-medium swaps, and quantify persister frequency against local neighbor density, position, and secreted factors using spatial tracking. This separates intrinsic noise from local paracrine or contact-mediated protection that makes some cells survive.

title: Optogenetic or inducible forcing of candidate states
description: Use CRISPRa, degron, or optogenetic control to impose a candidate state, such as a pulse of a stress-response transcription factor or temporary slowing of the cell cycle, in cells before drug exposure, with a dose-response of the induced level. If the persister fraction rises or falls as predicted, the state is causal rather than merely correlated, and the dose-response gives the threshold for tolerance.

title: Single-cell mitochondrial mutation lineage tracing of persister ancestry
description: Use naturally occurring mtDNA variants (scATAC/mito-enriched or MAESTER-style) as endogenous barcodes to reconstruct clonal relationships among surviving cells without engineered labels. Test whether survivors are clonally clustered beyond chance and how deep in the lineage tree shared tolerance extends, giving a memory length in divisions.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming profiling (BH3 profiling)
description: Perform dynamic BH3 profiling or single-cell mitochondrial priming measurements on untreated cells, then sort by priming level and correlate priming with survival after treatment. This tests whether persistence is set by a pre-existing apoptotic threshold rather than by pathway reactivation.

title: Spatial and microenvironment-resolved persister mapping
description: Culture cells in 3D or spatially patterned conditions (micropatterns, spheroids) and use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging after drug exposure to test whether survivors localize to defined local density, hypoxia, or cell-contact niches. Perturbing density or contact (e.g., by cell-contact or secreted-factor manipulation) shows whether persistence is partly a neighborhood property rather than purely cell-intrinsic.

title: Single-cell drug-target engagement and intracellular drug concentration
description: Measure intracellular drug levels (using fluorescent drug analogs, label-free imaging, or mass cytometry of target occupancy/phospho-readouts) and downstream pathway inhibition in individual cells shortly after dosing. This reveals whether survivors escape by receiving less effective inhibition, through efflux, sequestration (e.g., lysosomal trapping), or target-level differences, versus tolerating full inhibition.

title: Cell-division asymmetry and partitioning of organelles and proteins
description: Track mother-daughter pairs by time-lapse imaging with labeled mitochondria, lysosomes, or aggregated proteins, and sort daughters by unequal inheritance to test whether asymmetric partitioning predicts survival. Pair this with sibling-pair concordance analysis to separate inherited cytoplasmic state from chromatin-based memory.

title: Inheritance timescale from sister and cousin survival correlations
description: Track lineage trees by time-lapse microscopy before drug and quantify survival concordance between sisters, cousins and more distant relatives as a function of relatedness. Fitting a decay curve gives the memory half-life of the tolerant state in generations, which discriminates fast stochastic switching, epigenetic memory and genetic mutation, and indicates the timescale on which to look for mechanisms.

title: Mutation, mtDNA, and copy-number profiling of survivors versus matched sibling clones
description: Isolate surviving clones and their pre-drug sibling clones (split-clone design) and perform deep whole-genome sequencing for low-frequency SNVs, extrachromosomal DNA amplifications, copy-number changes and mtDNA heteroplasmy. This tests whether supposedly identical cells carry rare, hidden genetic or ecDNA differences, and quantifies how much of survival these differences explain.

title: Transient mutator and DNA-damage-response state in persisters
description: Combine live reporters of DNA repair factors (53BP1 foci, mismatch-repair and error-prone polymerase expression) with single-cell mutation-accumulation readouts during drug exposure. Test whether persisters transiently down-regulate high-fidelity repair, which would link tolerance to later genetic resistance and identify a window for intervention.

title: Single-cell proteome and translation-rate profiling of persisters
description: Measure global and specific translation (puromycin/OPP incorporation, ribosome profiling or polysome-seq on sorted cells, plus single-cell proteomics) to find survivors that differ in protein synthesis, ISR/eIF2α state or proteostasis capacity despite similar mRNA. This exposes post-transcriptional tolerance mechanisms not detectable by scRNA-seq and ATAC.

title: Neighbor-effect analysis with density titration and conditioned-media swaps
description: Vary seeding density, local neighbor composition, and secreted-factor exposure, and use spatial transcriptomics or imaging to ask whether survivors cluster or depend on paracrine or contact signals, such as extruded metabolites, growth factors, or cell-cell junction signaling. Comparing survivor frequency against local cell density tests whether apparent cell-intrinsic heterogeneity is actually determined by position and neighbors.

title: Inheritance of organelle and protein content through asymmetric division
description: Use time-lapse imaging with labeled mitochondria, lysosomes, or drug-efflux pumps (or a fluorescent drug analog) to quantify how unequal partitioning at division creates drug-handling differences between sister cells. Then test whether sisters with more of the inherited cargo preferentially survive, and perturb partitioning (for example, with spindle or mitochondrial-dynamics inhibitors) to see whether survival changes.

title: Single-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy measurement
description: Measure drug accumulation per cell using intrinsically fluorescent inhibitors, mass cytometry or imaging mass spectrometry, or a target-engagement biosensor such as a NanoBRET or CETSA-style readout. This tests whether survivors experience lower effective target inhibition (through efflux, lysosomal sequestration or altered metabolism) rather than having rewired downstream signaling.

title: Transient pre-treatment cell-state perturbation followed by survival measurement
description: Before adding drug, briefly expose cells to a candidate stressor or state modulator (such as a metabolic stress, a differentiation cue, or a chromatin inhibitor), then wash it out. Compare survival fraction and the persistence of the effect over time to determine whether the tolerant state is causally inducible and heritable, and to estimate its memory length.

title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of survivors in 3D or in vivo
description: Use spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on spheroids or xenografts, together with a lineage or reporter label, to test whether survivors cluster by local oxygen, nutrient, density or contact-signaling niches. Randomize cell positions or density in matched cultures to separate cell-intrinsic from position-dependent tolerance.

title: Single-cell metabolic and proteostasis profiling of survivors
description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, a ROS or lipid-peroxidation sensor, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes, or a proteasome or autophagy flux reporter. Image the same cells before and after drug exposure to see whether a metabolic or stress-handling state predicts survival, and use FACS sorting by that readout to validate it by orthogonal drug-response assays.

title: Lineage-barcoded fate mapping before drug exposure
description: Tag each cell with an expressed DNA barcode, split the population into sister cultures, and profile one by scRNA-seq before treatment while the other receives drug. Matching barcodes between pre-treatment states and survivors shows whether survival is determined by a heritable pre-existing state or arises stochastically after drug exposure, and identifies the predictive signature.

title: Live-cell dynamic reporters with retrospective identification of survivors
description: Time-lapse image thousands of single cells for days before drug addition, using reporters for signaling (ERK, p53, NF-kB), cell cycle, and mitochondrial or stress state. After drug treatment, trace survivors back through their histories to find dynamic features, such as pulse frequency, cycle timing, or state-switching rates, that predict survival better than any static snapshot.

title: Multi-generational inheritance and decay-time measurement of the resistant state
description: Sort or isolate rare survivor-prone cells, then follow their lineages through divisions with imaging and single-cell multiomics to measure how long the state persists and how it fades. Fitting the data to stochastic state-switching models distinguishes epigenetic memory, transient noise, and slow-cycling states, and quantifies the transition rates between them.

title: Joint single-cell chromatin, transcriptome, and mutation profiling
description: Apply single-cell multiome assays with targeted DNA sequencing and copy-number calling to the same cells at baseline and at several times on drug, comparing survivors with matched sensitive cells. This rules in or out rare genetic variants, extrachromosomal DNA, and mitochondrial heteroplasmy, and shows which chromatin accessibility states and regulators precede survival.

title: Perturbation screens in the survivor state with in situ readouts of drug-target engagement
description: Run pooled CRISPR (knockout, interference, and base-editing) screens whose readout is survival fraction and single-cell state, combined with biosensors of drug-target occupancy and downstream pathway inhibition within individual cells. This tests causality, separating cells that never reach effective drug inhibition (uptake, efflux, metabolism) from those that inhibit the target yet rewire downstream, and it reveals which mechanisms can be targeted to eliminate survivors.

title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment sister-cell tracing
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into sister aliquots before drug, then profile one aliquot by scRNA-seq/ATAC and treat the other to identify which barcodes survive. This lets you read out the pre-existing state of future survivors and test whether the state is heritable, how long it lasts, and whether it predicts survival better than genotype.

title: Live-cell imaging of fate followed by in situ multi-omic readout
description: Time-lapse image thousands of single cells with reporters (e.g., stress, cell-cycle, mitochondrial, and signaling dynamics) through drug exposure, then fix the same cells in situ for spatial transcriptomics/proteomics. Linking pre-drug dynamics, such as ERK pulses or cycle phase, to survival or death for each cell identifies which dynamic features, rather than static expression, determine survival.

title: Deep single-cell DNA sequencing and mutation tracking to rule out hidden genetics
description: Perform single-cell whole-genome or exome sequencing and ultra-deep barcode-linked sequencing on the parental population and on survivors to measure rare pre-existing mutations, copy-number changes, and extrachromosomal DNA. Compare these to non-genetic signals to quantify how much survival is explained by rare genetic variants versus reversible states, and to determine whether the cells were truly genetically identical.

title: Perturbing candidate state regulators to test causality
description: Run a pooled CRISPRi/a screen with single-cell readout (Perturb-seq) in the drug-naïve population, then treat and read survival from guide enrichment and state shifts. Pushing cells into or out of the candidate survivor state and observing the change in survival would show which regulators, such as chromatin modifiers, stress-response factors, or metabolic programs, cause survival rather than merely mark it.

title: Quantitative modeling of molecular noise and microenvironment from in situ and in vivo data
description: Measure cell-to-cell variation in drug uptake or efflux, target occupancy, and apoptotic-threshold proteins (BCL2 family) in single cells, and map local microenvironment factors such as oxygen, neighbors, and cell density in 3D culture and xenografts. Fit a quantitative model to these data to test whether survival comes from intrinsic molecular noise, local niche differences, or their interaction, and to predict combination dosing that eliminates the surviving fraction.

title: Lineage-barcoded sister-population pre-treatment tracing
description: Barcode cancer cells, split each clone into two parallel populations before drug, profile one by single-cell RNA/ATAC and expose the other to drug, then use barcodes to retrospectively identify the pre-existing states of cells that later survive. This tests whether persistence is a heritable pre-existing state versus drug-induced adaptation, and quantifies how long the state is remembered across divisions.

title: Live-cell lineage tracking with multi-generational reporters
description: Time-lapse image thousands of single cells for many generations before, during, and after drug using reporters for cell cycle, stress signaling (p53, ERK, NF-κB), mitochondrial state, and growth rate. Then link each cell's dynamic history, including inherited fluctuations from mother and grandmother cells, to its survival fate, to test whether dynamics rather than static snapshots explain persistence.

title: Joint multi-omic profiling of drug-tolerant cells with same-cell survival readout
description: Combine single-cell RNA, chromatin accessibility, proteomics, and metabolomics with a survival marker, such as live-dead dye sorting or in situ barcoding, to determine which molecular layer first diverges in survivors. Perturbing the earliest-diverging layer, such as an epigenetic regulator or metabolic enzyme, tests whether it causally drives survival.

title: Pooled CRISPR perturbation of state switching with single-cell readout
description: Run genome-wide or epigenome-focused CRISPRi/a screens with Perturb-seq under drug, scoring not only survival but also the rate of switching into and out of the tolerant state and the shape of the state landscape. This separates genes that set the baseline probability of persistence from genes that maintain the tolerant state once it is entered.

title: In vivo and spatial mapping of persisters
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics and barcode lineage tracing to xenograft or patient tumor biopsies before treatment, during treatment, and at minimal residual disease. Map where survivors are located, such as near hypoxic or stromal niches, and what they share with matched cell-line persisters. Comparing in vivo and in vitro survivors shows which mechanisms are cell-intrinsic and which depend on the local environment.

title: Lineage-barcoded fate mapping before drug exposure
description: Tag a clonal population with expressed heritable DNA barcodes, split it into replicate pools, and treat some pools with drug. Sequence survivors and untreated sister pools to test whether persistence is pre-encoded in specific lineages, how many generations it is inherited, and which pre-treatment transcriptional states predict survival. Matching barcodes between sister pools tests whether survivors are pre-existing or drug-induced.

title: Live-cell lineage tracking with post-hoc multi-omic readout
description: Image thousands of single cells and their lineages for many generations before and during drug exposure, using reporters for signaling, cell cycle, and stress. Then fix the same cells in place and run spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, or chromatin profiling, linking each survivor's history to its molecular state. This shows which dynamic behaviors, such as pulsatile signaling, slow cycling, or mitochondrial state, precede survival and whether they are transient or inherited.

title: Single-cell kinetics of drug target engagement and intracellular drug levels
description: Use fluorescent or mass-spec-compatible drug analogs, target-engagement biosensors, and single-cell proteomics to measure how much drug reaches its target in each cell and how fast downstream signaling is shut off. Compare survivors and non-survivors within the same genotype to separate drug efflux, target-expression variation, and pathway rewiring from true downstream adaptation. This would show whether survival comes from a failure to inhibit the target or from tolerance despite inhibition.

title: Causal perturbation of candidate persister states with single-cell CRISPR and epigenome editing
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout, interference, and activation screens that read out single-cell transcriptomes under drug, along with targeted epigenome editing of loci that distinguish pre-persister cells. Test whether forcing or blocking a particular state, such as a chromatin configuration, stress-response program, or metabolic state, changes survival probability. This would turn correlative markers from observational studies into causal determinants and rank which are necessary, sufficient, or only passengers.

title: Stochastic state-switching models fit to fluctuation tests
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation analysis and time-resolved fate-mapping on survivor counts across many replicate clonal cultures, then fit stochastic models of state switching, drug-induced switching, and selection. The variance and time-dependence of survivor numbers across replicates would distinguish rare pre-existing states, induced adaptation, and mixtures of the two. This gives quantitative switching rates that predict how combination or scheduled dosing can reduce or exploit survivors.

title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment sister-cell splitting
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into matched sister aliquots before drug, profile one aliquot by single-cell RNA/ATAC and treat the other, then link each surviving barcode to its sister aliquot's pre-drug state. This tests whether survivors were predetermined and identifies the predictive molecular signature before any drug exposure.

title: Live-cell tracking with retrospective multi-omic readout
description: Time-lapse image thousands of single cells for weeks to record lineage history (cell cycle length, signaling reporters, mitochondrial state, division asymmetry), apply drug, then fix the cells and run in situ spatial transcriptomics or proteomics on the same tracked survivors. This tests whether fluctuating dynamics, inherited memory, or stress history, rather than static state, determines survival.

title: Heritability timescale mapping via fate-lineage correlation
description: Quantify how survival and the resistant-like state correlate across sister, cousin, and more distant relatives in lineage trees. Measure how that correlation decays across generations and after drug pulses at varying delays. The decay constant distinguishes stable genetic or epigenetic inheritance from fast stochastic transcriptional noise and from drug-induced adaptation.

title: Single-cell multiome with CRISPR perturbation of candidate state regulators
description: Use Perturb-seq or CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens targeting chromatin regulators and transcription factors found enriched in the pre-survivor state, with barcoded survivor readout under drug. Causally shifting the surviving fraction up or down shows which regulators set survival probability rather than merely marking it.

title: Single-cell DNA, copy number, and ecDNA sequencing of survivors versus matched ancestors
description: Perform paired single-cell whole-genome and mutation sequencing of barcode-matched survivors and untreated siblings to detect or exclude cryptic genetic changes such as ecDNA amplification, copy number shifts, or mutations in rare subclones. This separates truly non-genetic persistence from low-frequency genetic variation within apparently identical populations.

title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment sister-cell tracing
description: Label clonal cells with expressed DNA barcodes, split them into sister populations before drug exposure, and profile one by scRNA-seq while treating the other. Matching barcodes in survivors to the untreated sisters' pre-existing states shows whether survival was predetermined and which transcriptional or epigenetic state predicted it, without inference from post-drug cells.

title: Live-cell imaging of single-cell histories linked to fate
description: Follow thousands of individual cells for generations using multi-reporter live imaging (cell cycle, stress, signaling, mitochondrial state, and others). Then apply the drug, record which cells survive, and fix and profile the same cells by in situ spatial transcriptomics. This links each cell's past dynamics, such as fluctuation timing, division history, and inherited state, to its fate.

title: Multi-omic single-cell profiling of chromatin, RNA and protein before and after drug
description: Run paired single-cell ATAC, RNA, and proteomics, plus histone-modification profiling, on untreated populations and across a drug time course. Use computational lineage inference to separate selection of rare pre-existing states from drug-induced adaptation. This tests whether the persister state is a heritable epigenetic state and which regulators maintain it.

title: Pooled CRISPR perturbation screens with state readout
description: Combine genome-wide CRISPRi/a/knockout screens with Perturb-seq-style readouts, in drug-naive cells and during drug exposure. This shows which genes control how often the survivor state arises and which control survival once it exists, separating causal drivers from passenger markers.

title: Metabolic and physical single-cell phenotyping of survivors
description: Measure survivors and their untreated precursors for drug uptake and efflux, mitochondrial and redox state, translation rate, and target engagement. Use single-cell mass spectrometry, fluorescent drug analogs, and biophysical assays. This tests whether survival comes from cell-intrinsic physiology, such as less drug reaching its target or an altered apoptotic threshold, rather than from a specific gene program.

title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment sister-cell splitting
description: Barcode a clonal population, split sister cells before drug exposure, and expand one half while treating the other. Then use scRNA-seq/ATAC-seq on the untreated sisters of survivors to show which pre-existing states predicted survival and how much of the fate was heritable versus stochastic.

title: Live-cell tracking of lineages through drug onset with retrospective multi-omic readout
description: Time-lapse image thousands of single cells and their pedigrees for generations before and after drug addition, with reporters for signaling (ERK/AKT), cell cycle, and stress. Fix and spatially profile the same cells afterward, linking dynamic history (e.g., pulses, cycle timing, mitochondrial state) to survival at single-cell resolution.

title: Causal perturbation of candidate rare states with inducible single-cell-resolved CRISPR screens
description: Use Perturb-seq or CRISPRi/a screens with barcode tracking, forcing expression of a state-defining program in randomly chosen cells to test whether it is sufficient to confer survival. Pair this with knockdown in naturally high-state cells to test necessity, separating correlation from cause.

title: Early drug-response trajectories of survivors versus dying cells with metabolic and epigenetic profiling
description: Capture cells in the first hours to days of drug exposure with single-cell time-resolved sequencing, metabolic flux imaging (e.g., FLIM/NADH), and chromatin accessibility/histone mark profiling. Reconstruct how survivors diverge from dying cells, and test whether rewiring (e.g., lipid peroxidation defense, chromatin remodeling) is an induced adaptive response rather than a pre-existing state.

title: Mathematical modeling of fluctuation-assay dynamics to discriminate stochastic switching, selection, and mutation
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation assays with thousands of parallel clonal sub-populations at varied drug doses and timings, and fit models of state-switching rates, memory duration, and mutation. Validate the inferred rates by sequencing for mutations and re-measuring state transitions in sorted subpopulations, to show which mechanism dominates in each setting.

title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment sister-cell splitting
description: Barcode a clonal population, split sister cells before drug exposure, and profile one half by scRNA-seq/ATAC while treating the other half, then use shared barcodes to link each pre-existing state to its survival fate. This would show which baseline states predict persistence and quantify how much is predetermined versus stochastic.

title: Multigenerational live-cell tracking with reporters and retrospective fate mapping
description: Image thousands of single cells over many generations with reporters for stress, cell cycle, and signaling (e.g., ERK, p53, NF-kB) before and during drug treatment, then correlate pre-drug dynamics and mother-daughter inheritance with survival. This showed that transient, heritable dynamic states persisting over several cell divisions, rather than static expression levels, mark survivors.

title: Multi-omic single-cell profiling with CRISPR perturbation of the drug-tolerant transition
description: Combine Perturb-seq-style pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA, chromatin accessibility, and proteomic readouts at multiple timepoints after drug addition to map the causal regulators of entering and exiting the persister state. This identified epigenetic and metabolic nodes (such as chromatin remodelers or lipid-peroxidation defenses) whose perturbation changed persister frequency.

title: Spatial and microenvironmental mapping of persisters in vivo
description: Use spatial transcriptomics and intravital imaging in treated xenografts or patient-derived organoids with controlled gradients of oxygen, nutrients, and drug. This tests whether local niches or limited drug penetration create apparent survivors among identical cells, and it separates intrinsic cell-state effects from microenvironmental effects and their relative contributions.

title: Mathematical modeling of switching kinetics from fluctuation-test data
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation tests and time-resolved survival curves with many replicate clones, then fit stochastic models to infer rates of state switching, memory duration, and drug-induced versus pre-existing tolerance. This distinguishes mutation, random switching, and induced adaptation, and yields predictive rules for scheduling drugs to eliminate persisters.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing before and after drug
description: Label a clonal population with heritable expressed DNA barcodes, split it into replicates, and treat them with the drug. Sequence the surviving barcodes to test whether the same sister lineages survive across replicates (pre-existing, heritable state) or different ones each time (stochastic induction). Pair this with single-cell RNA-seq of sibling cells sampled before treatment, so that pre-treatment transcriptional states can be linked to each lineage's later fate.

title: Live-cell single-cell tracking with signaling and stress reporters
description: Use time-lapse microscopy with fluorescent reporters (e.g., ERK/AKT activity, apoptosis caspase sensor, FUCCI cell cycle) to follow thousands of cells for days before, during, and after drug exposure. Retrospectively align the dynamics of surviving and dying cells to find early features, such as pulsatile signaling, slow cycling, or mitochondrial priming, that predict survival. The predictors are dynamic patterns rather than static levels.

title: Multi-omic profiling of persisters over time, including chromatin accessibility
description: Run joint scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CUT&Tag for histone marks) on untreated cells, cells at early drug exposure, persisters, and cells after drug withdrawal. This tests whether survival depends on reversible epigenetic states, such as an open-chromatin stress-response or drug-tolerant program, and whether those states can be inherited. Perturbing the identified regulators (e.g., KDM5, HDAC) would then test causality.

title: Mother-daughter inheritance and state-switching rate measurements
description: Sort cells by a candidate marker of tolerance (e.g., a high-expressing subpopulation) and measure how quickly the population returns to the original marker distribution, using fluctuation-analysis or Luria-Delbrück-style experiments and mathematical modeling. Fit models to estimate switching rates and memory duration, and use time-lapse of cell pairs to measure how similar sister cells are in fate. This quantifies whether tolerance is a fast-fluctuating state or a stable, heritable one.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens with drug plus metabolic and survival-pathway readouts in persisters
description: Perform genome-wide or focused CRISPRi/a screens under drug treatment, selecting for cells that survive the first days rather than for stable resistance. Combine this with measurements of persister metabolism (oxidative phosphorylation, lipid peroxidation or GPX4 dependence, ATP/ROS) and drug-efflux activity. This identifies the genes and vulnerabilities that make survival possible and tests whether blocking them eliminates the surviving fraction.

title: Lineage barcoding to test pre-existing versus induced persisters
description: Tag a clonal population with heritable DNA barcodes, split into replicate dishes, and treat with the targeted drug. If the same barcodes recur among survivors across replicates, survivors were predetermined; if different barcodes survive, resistance is stochastic or induced. Sequencing barcodes together with scRNA-seq on sister cells links the pre-treatment state to cell fate.

title: Time-lapse single-cell tracking with reporters and post-hoc fate mapping
description: Image live cells carrying reporters for signaling (ERK, AKT), cell cycle and stress responses for several generations before and after drug addition. Then retrospectively align the traces of the survivors with those of the dead cells to find early dynamic features, such as slow cycling or pulsatile signaling, that predict survival.

title: Time-course single-cell multi-omics of surviving cells
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) on untreated cells and on survivors at several time points after treatment. This tests whether survivors occupy a distinct epigenetic or transcriptional state, such as a drug-tolerant persister program, and whether it is transient or stable. Trajectory and regulatory-network inference would then nominate the drivers and chromatin features that mark the state.

title: Isolation and perturbation of rare pre-treatment subpopulations
description: Use FACS on markers from multi-omics data, or a live reporter of the candidate state, to isolate the rare cells before treatment. Compare their drug survival with that of bulk cells, then CRISPR-perturb the candidate regulators. Sorted cells should be enriched for survival, and removing the regulator should eliminate it. Re-culturing the sorted cells shows how quickly the state regenerates from the clonal population, which measures state-switching rates.

title: Metabolic and drug-exposure heterogeneity measurements
description: Measure single-cell drug accumulation (fluorescent drug analogs or mass cytometry), efflux activity, mitochondrial state, ROS and lipid metabolism in survivors versus non-survivors. This tests whether survival comes from non-genetic physiological differences, such as lower effective dose or an altered redox state, rather than from target-pathway rewiring. Pairing the measurements with exome sequencing of survivors rules out hidden mutations.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicates, and treat them with the drug. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, tolerance was pre-existing and heritable; if different barcodes survive, the state is stochastic or induced.
