Sequencing barcodes together with single-cell RNA-seq of the same clones links each lineage's survival to its baseline transcriptional state.

title: Spatial map of survivors in situ
description: Use live-cell imaging or spatial transcriptomics to map where survivors sit relative to their neighbors, colony edges, local density, and oxygen or nutrient gradients. Spatial statistics such as clustering versus random dispersion of survivors would show whether tolerance depends on microenvironment or is cell-intrinsic. Neighbor-swap or conditioned-medium experiments can then test causality.

title: Time-lapse single-cell tracking with reporters before and after drug
description: Follow individual cells for days before drug addition using fluorescent reporters of signaling (such as ERK or AKT activity), cell cycle, and apoptosis. Then retrospectively ask which pre-treatment dynamics, such as slow cycling, pulsatile signaling, or high stress-response activity, predicted survival. This captures fluctuations that single snapshots miss, and it gives autocorrelation times that show how long the tolerant state lasts.

title: Multi-omic profiling of survivors versus matched untreated cells (RNA, chromatin, proteins)
description: Sort or isolate persisters and matched untreated cells, then compare single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and proteomics or metabolomics. Look for epigenetic states, drug-efflux, anti-apoptotic, or metabolic programs such as oxidative phosphorylation and lipid remodeling. Perturb the top candidates (with CRISPR or inhibitors of epigenetic regulators) to test whether they are necessary for survival.

title: Fluctuation assays and stochastic modeling of state-switching rates
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation assays with many small parallel clonal cultures and compare the variance in survivor numbers to the mean. Fit stochastic models to estimate rates of switching between sensitive and tolerant states and whether those states are inherited over several divisions. Re-sort survivors and regrow them to measure how quickly the mixture of tolerant and sensitive cells re-establishes itself. Use the inferred rates to determine which timescales to target with combination or sequenced therapy.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from drug-induced persisters
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicate arms, and treat each with the drug. Recurrence of the same barcodes across arms implies a pre-existing heritable state, while random barcodes imply stochastic induction. Sequencing untreated sister clones from before treatment reveals the pre-drug transcriptional state of lineages that later survive.

title: Single-cell multi-omic profiling over time before and after drug exposure
description: Run scRNA-seq combined with scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) at multiple time points: untreated, early drug exposure, and persister outgrowth. This identifies rare transcriptional or chromatin states, such as drug-efflux, stress-response or dedifferentiation programs, that are over-represented in survivors and traces how state transitions unfold from sensitive to tolerant.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging with lineage tracking and retrospective fate mapping
description: Image thousands of individual cells over days with fluorescent reporters for signaling activity (e.g. ERK, p53, apoptosis caspase activity, cell-cycle state). Track each cell's lineage through drug exposure, then relate pre-treatment dynamics, such as slow cycling, pulse frequency, or mitochondrial state, to which cells and their relatives survive. Fixing and sequencing the same cells afterward connects dynamics to molecular state.

title: Cell-cell communication and microenvironment effects on survival
description: Test whether survival depends on contact or secreted signals between neighbors. Use spatial transcriptomics or co-culture and conditioned-medium experiments, and compare isolated single cells with dense colonies. Survivors may be supported by paracrine factors or by gap junctions or ligand-receptor links between cells, so quantifying neighbor composition around survivors versus dying cells would show whether tolerance is a cell-intrinsic or a collective property.

title: Perturbation screens targeting the persister state with drug-treated versus untreated comparison
description: Perform a CRISPR knockout or interference screen with a drug-treated versus untreated comparison, plus pharmacological tests of candidate pathways identified in other analyses (e.g. epigenetic regulators, oxidative stress/GPX4, anti-apoptotic BCL2 family). Genes whose loss reduces the persister fraction without affecting bulk growth are causal mediators, and a combined drug plus inhibitor test shows whether the survivor fraction can be shrunk.

title: Lineage-barcoded pre-treatment vs. post-treatment tracing
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and sequence survivors in parallel replicates. If the same barcodes recur among survivors, survival is a pre-existing, heritable state; if survivors differ between replicates, it is stochastic. This also shows how long a cell keeps the state.

title: Live-cell time-lapse tracking with retrospective single-cell profiling
description: Image cells carrying reporters for signaling (ERK or p53 dynamics) and cell-cycle state through the drug pulse. Track each cell's fate, then fix the cells and run in situ RNA or protein profiling on the same cells. This links transient pre-treatment fluctuations to later survival and gives the timescale over which the state decays.

title: Single-cell multiome time course of the transition to the drug-tolerant state
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq at several times before, during, and after drug exposure. Infer trajectories to see whether survivors are a rare pre-existing subpopulation or cells that adaptively rewire chromatin and transcription after the drug is added. Look for transient early states, such as a stress or dedifferentiated program, that later settle into stable resistance or return to the baseline state.

title: Reversibility and memory test by drug holiday and re-challenge
description: Isolate survivors, grow them with and without drug for varied durations, and then re-challenge them while measuring how the surviving fraction changes with time off drug. Combine this with epigenetic perturbations, such as HDAC or KDM5 inhibitors, to test whether the tolerance is held by chromatin. The decay curve of tolerance shows whether the state is non-genetic and transient, and what maintains it.

title: Functional screen of survivor-state regulators with sorted-state CRISPR
description: Use a live reporter or surface marker for the high-tolerance state to sort cells. Run CRISPRi/a screens that read out either the frequency of the state or survival under drug, and compare the two. Genes that change survival through the state, rather than through general drug sensitivity, are candidate regulators of how the state is entered and exited, and are candidate targets for combination therapy.

title: Lineage barcoding to test pre-existing vs. induced persistence
description: Tag each cell with a heritable DNA barcode before drug exposure, split the population into replicates, and treat. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, survival is a pre-existing heritable state. If different barcodes survive in each replicate, this points to stochastic, induced adaptation. Sequencing barcodes together with single-cell RNA-seq on sister clones links lineage to transcriptional state.

title: Live imaging with a fluorescent reporter of cell fate before drug exposure
description: Use a fluorescent reporter for the suspected survival program, such as a stress-response or drug-efflux reporter. Track single cells by time-lapse microscopy for days before and after drug addition, then retrospectively correlate pre-treatment reporter brightness, cell-cycle length, and mitochondrial state with survival. This shows whether survivors were already distinct before treatment.

title: Paired single-cell multi-omics of survivors vs. bulk population
description: Run scRNA-seq combined with scATAC-seq on untreated cells and on cells at several time points after drug exposure. Identify rare pre-existing subpopulations, chromatin accessibility symmetry-breaking events, and the transcription factors that define the persister state. Trajectory analysis then shows whether survivors come from a rare primed state or converge on a common state after treatment.

title: Metabolic and redox profiling of single cells
description: Many drug-tolerant cells rely on altered oxidative metabolism, reactive oxygen species handling, or lipid peroxidation defenses. Use single-cell metabolic imaging (NAD(P)H FLIM, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes, ROS sensors) and sort by these readouts, then test drug sensitivity of each sorted fraction. Pharmacological or CRISPR perturbation of the identified pathway tests causality.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens plus state-switching mathematical modeling
description: Run genome-wide or epigenetic-focused CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens under drug to find genes that raise or lower the persister fraction, such as chromatin modifiers or stress regulators. Fit a stochastic switching model (as in Luria–Delbrück fluctuation tests) to survivor counts to estimate state-transition rates, then test whether each hit changes the switching rates or the fitness in each state.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from induced tolerance
description: Tag a clonal population with heritable DNA barcodes, split it into replicate pools, and apply the drug. If the same barcodes dominate the survivors across replicates, tolerance was pre-existing and heritable; if different barcodes survive, tolerance was stochastic or induced. Sequencing barcodes together with scRNA-seq on sister cells would link the pre-treatment state to the survival outcome.

title: Time-lapse single-cell tracking with live reporters
description: Image thousands of individual cells before, during and after drug exposure. Use fluorescent reporters for signaling activity (such as ERK), cell cycle and stress response, and follow lineages to see which pre-treatment dynamics predict survival. Retrospective analysis of the survivors' ancestors would show whether slow cycling, pulsatile signaling or a particular history marks the cells that survive, including whether survivors entered a quiescent state by chance.

title: Multiomic profiling of survivors over time
description: Collect scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq and proteomic or phospho-protein data at several time points: untreated, early after drug, and at persister expansion. Compare survivors with matched untreated cells to find transcriptional programs (such as drug efflux, EMT-like states, oxidative stress response or a slow-cycling program) and chromatin accessibility that distinguish them. Trajectory inference would show whether survivors are a distinct pre-existing state or a gradual adaptation.

title: State-marker sorting and CRISPR screens of rare-state cells
description: Sort cells on candidate markers of the tolerant state, such as high expression of a surface protein or a reporter, and compare their drug sensitivity with the rest of the population. Measure how quickly each sorted fraction returns to the population's mixed composition, as a measure of state stability. In parallel, run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout or interference screen under drug to find genes required for persistence, which tests causality and not just correlation.

title: Fluctuation tests and mathematical modeling of state switching
description: Run a Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation test, measuring the variance in survivor counts across many small parallel cultures. Fit stochastic models that distinguish random mutation, reversible phenotype switching and drug-induced adaptation, using the switching rates and the decay of tolerance after drug removal. The many replicate wells provide the statistics needed to estimate the rates. Model predictions about how fast the state changes could then be tested with drug holidays or altered dosing schedules.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from induced persisters
description: Label each cell with a heritable DNA barcode, split the population into replicates, and treat them. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, the resistance was pre-existing and heritable; if different barcodes survive in each replicate, the state is stochastic or drug-induced. Sequencing the surviving clones' transcriptomes (e.g., with CellTag-style methods) then links lineage to cell state.

title: Single-cell multiome profiling before and after drug
description: Run scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on untreated cells and on cells at several times after treatment. Look for a rare subpopulation with a distinct transcriptional or chromatin state, such as a drug-efflux, stress-response or dedifferentiated program, that exists before treatment and expands afterward. Compare it with the survivors to identify the regulators involved.

title: Live-cell time-lapse with fluorescent reporters and retrospective omics
description: Image thousands of individual cells for days with reporters for signaling activity (ERK or AKT), cell cycle, apoptosis, and mitochondrial state, recording each cell's dynamics, including fluctuations, before drug addition. Then follow which cells survive, and fix and profile the same cells afterward or isolate them by photoactivatable labeling. This tests whether pre-treatment signaling dynamics or slow-cycling behavior predict survival.

title: Stochastic modeling of state switching from fluctuation-test data
description: Perform a Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation test with sibling clones and measure the distribution of survivor counts and the persister fraction in clonal lineages over time. Fit stochastic models of phenotype switching between sensitive and tolerant states, including switching rates and memory duration, to estimate how heritable the tolerant state is and whether switching is random or induced, and to guide which timescales to profile.

title: Sorting on candidate state markers and functional perturbation
description: Use FACS to enrich subpopulations defined by candidate state markers, such as ALDH activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, drug efflux, cell-cycle dwell time or a reporter for the survival program, and test their drug survival. Then use CRISPRi/a screens or pharmacologic inhibitors targeting the implicated pathways, such as anti-apoptotic BCL-2 family members, oxidative phosphorylation, or chromatin modifiers like KDM5. These experiments test whether the pathways are causally required for survival, not just correlated with it.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with pre-treatment sister-cell splitting
description: Tag cells with heritable expressed barcodes, split the population into sister aliquots, and treat one while sequencing the other (scRNA-seq) before drug. Persister lineages can then be traced back to their pre-existing transcriptional states, which tests whether survival is predetermined or stochastic. The design relies on matching paired units across the two conditions.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporter fate tracking
description: Image cells with fluorescent reporters for cell cycle (FUCCI), apoptosis, and stress pathways (e.g., ERK, p53) for days before and after drug addition. Retrospectively link single-cell dynamics, such as cycle length, pulsatile signaling, or mitochondrial state, to survival or death. This adds the temporal dimension that fixed snapshots miss.

title: Single-cell multi-omic profiling of persisters (RNA + ATAC + protein)
description: Profile surviving cells and untreated controls at several timepoints with joint scRNA/scATAC and phospho-proteomics. This would identify chromatin accessibility and signaling states, such as an epigenetic drug-tolerant program or reactivated bypass pathways, that distinguish persisters. Comparing early and late timepoints separates selection of pre-existing states from drug-induced adaptation.

title: Functional perturbation screens within persisters (CRISPRi/a and epigenetic inhibitors)
description: Run pooled CRISPR screens, or treat with chromatin modifier inhibitors such as HDAC or KDM5 inhibitors, in combination with the targeted drug. Measure persister numbers to find causal regulators of survival rather than correlates. Hits from profiling experiments can then be validated by checking whether knockdown shrinks the persister fraction.

title: Metabolic and stress-state measurements at single-cell resolution
description: Measure ROS, mitochondrial membrane potential, lipid peroxidation (GPX4 dependence), and drug efflux or intracellular drug concentration in individual cells with flow cytometry or FLIM. Sort high and low cells, expose them to drug, and test whether these states predict survival. This tests non-genetic physiological explanations such as ferroptosis resistance or lower drug accumulation.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with sister-cell splitting
description: Use a high-complexity expressed barcode library, so each cell carries a unique tag, and split the expanded population before drug exposure. Compare barcode enrichment in survivors across replicate arms to test whether survival is a heritable pre-existing state or a stochastic, drug-induced one. Pair this with scRNA-seq of sister cells to find the predictive pre-treatment transcriptional state.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters and retrospective profiling
description: Image cells for days before and after drug treatment using reporters for the drug's target pathway activity, cell cycle, and apoptosis. Track each single-cell trajectory to see which pre-drug dynamics, such as pulsing, cycle phase or signaling noise, predict survival. Then fix the cells and run in situ sequencing or multiplexed immunofluorescence on the same survivors to link dynamics to molecular state.

title: Single-cell multi-omics of drug-tolerant persisters over time
description: Collect untreated, early-drug, and persister-stage cells for joint scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, or CITE-seq. Infer whether persisters come from a rare cell state or from an adaptive transition by testing for chromatin accessibility changes, with trajectory and RNA-velocity analysis. Look for epigenetic regulators or stress-response programs that are consistently enriched.

title: Metabolic and stress-state measurements on single cells
description: Measure mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, NAD(P)H lifetime by FLIM, and lipid peroxidation or ferroptosis sensitivity in individual cells. Sort cells by these properties before treatment and see if each fraction survives differently. This tests whether non-genetic variation in metabolism or redox buffering sets drug tolerance.

title: Perturbation screens to establish causality
description: Run a pooled CRISPRi/CRISPRa screen with a single-cell readout (Perturb-seq) or survival readout under drug treatment, focused on chromatin modifiers, transcription factors and stress pathways found in the profiling. Add pharmacologic tests, such as HDAC or KDM5 inhibitors given with the targeted drug. Genes whose perturbation changes the persister fraction without changing the genome show which mechanisms cause survival rather than merely correlating with it.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from induced tolerance
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicates, and apply drug. If the same barcodes recur among survivors across replicates, tolerance is pre-existing and heritable, whereas random barcodes imply drug-induced adaptation.

title: Paired pre-treatment single-cell profiling of sister cells
description: Split sister cells just after division, profile one sister by scRNA-seq/ATAC and treat the other, then link pre-drug transcriptional or chromatin state to survival. This identifies the baseline state predictive of persistence without needing to profile cells that have already been selected.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters and fate tracking
description: Image cells for days before and during drug exposure using reporters for signaling activity (e.g., ERK, apoptosis, cell cycle), then retrospectively trace survivors to see which dynamics, such as slow cycling, pulsatile signaling, or mitochondrial priming, predicted survival. This captures transient states that fixed snapshots miss.

title: Metabolic and stress-response measurements in survivors
description: Use single-cell mass spectrometry or fluorescent sensors, and flux assays on sorted cells, to measure ROS, mitochondrial membrane potential, lipid and glutathione metabolism, and drug efflux in persisters versus bulk cells. Follow with targeted inhibition of the identified pathway to test whether it is causal for survival.

title: Epigenetic perturbation screens on persister emergence
description: Run a CRISPRi/CRISPRa or small-molecule screen focused on chromatin regulators (e.g., KDM5, HDACs, EZH2) and measure change in the persister fraction and in the reversibility of tolerance after drug withdrawal. Hits would show whether non-genetic, reversible chromatin states drive survival and whether they can be blocked.

title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment sister-cell tracking
description: Label clonal cells with heritable expressed barcodes (e.g., ClonTracer/TREX-style), split the population before drug exposure, and compare sister-cell fates to see whether survival is heritable and which pre-existing transcriptional states predict it. This tests whether survivors form a distinct pre-existing subpopulation (bimodal distribution) versus the stochastic tail of a continuous distribution.

title: Live-cell reporter imaging followed by profiling of survivors
description: Image single cells for days before and after drug using fluorescent reporters for signaling (ERK, p53, apoptosis, cell cycle), then fix and profile the survivors by multiplexed imaging or in situ sequencing. Link dynamic history, such as pulsatile signaling or cell-cycle phase, to survival to identify the state variables that predict persistence.

title: Single-cell multi-omics of survivors across time
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq) on untreated cells, cells shortly after drug, and persisters weeks later. Trajectory analysis then shows whether persisters come from a rare pre-existing state, such as a drug-tolerant or dedifferentiated program, or from drug-induced adaptive rewiring.

title: Metabolic and stress-response profiling of persisters
description: Measure single-cell mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, lipid peroxidation, and NAD(P)H lifetime (FLIM) alongside drug-target activity, then sort high- and low-metabolism fractions to test survival. Follow with perturbations such as GPX4 or OXPHOS inhibition to establish which vulnerabilities are causal.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens plus epigenetic perturbation in sorted states
description: Run genome-wide or chromatin-focused CRISPRi/a screens with drug and read out survivor frequency, not just bulk fitness, to find regulators that tune the size of the tolerant fraction. Combine with histone-modifier inhibitors (KDM5, EZH2) and ChIP/CUT&Tag in persisters to separate epigenetic from genetic causes.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with split populations
description: Tag cells with heritable lentiviral barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and compare barcode enrichment among survivors across replicates. This tests whether persisters arise from pre-existing heritable states (the same barcodes recur) or from stochastic drug-induced switching (barcodes differ).

title: Single-cell multiome profiling before and after drug
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and ATAC-seq on untreated cells and on cells at several times after treatment. Identify rare pre-existing transcriptional or chromatin states, such as drug-efflux, stress-response or EMT-like programs, that predict survival, and confirm them by perturbing the key regulators.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters and retrospective omics
description: Image single cells for days with fluorescent reporters of signaling (ERK, p53), cell cycle and mitochondrial state, then follow which cells survive the drug. Fix and profile the survivors and their lineage relatives to link dynamic history, such as pulses or slow cycling, to survival.

title: Fluctuation-style kinetic analysis of state switching
description: Sort cells by a candidate marker, such as high or low expression, and measure how fast each subpopulation re-equilibrates and how its drug survival changes over time. Fit a Luria–Delbrück-type or Markov model to estimate switching rates, which distinguishes stable, slowly interconverting states from fast noise.

title: Metabolic and proteostasis phenotyping of persisters
description: Compare survivors and non-survivors for oxidative stress, mitochondrial activity, lipid peroxidation (ferroptosis sensitivity) and protein-homeostasis capacity. Use flow-based sensors, single-cell metabolomics and targeted inhibitors to test whether blocking the identified pathway selectively kills persisters.

title: Barcoded lineage tracing with pre-treatment sister-cell splitting
description: Track cells with a heritable lineage barcode. Split barcoded clonal populations into sister aliquots, profile one by scRNA-seq before drug and treat the other. Then test whether the surviving barcodes already carried a distinct pre-existing transcriptional state, which distinguishes heritable pre-existing tolerance from drug-induced tolerance.

title: Live-cell time-lapse with fate-mapping reporters
description: Track thousands of individual cells by long-term microscopy before and after drug using reporters for cell-cycle state, ERK/AKT signaling, apoptosis and stress. Retrospectively align pre-treatment dynamics, such as pulse frequency or cell-cycle length, with eventual survival to find earlier features that predict the outcome.

title: Multi-omic profiling of persisters over time (scRNA, scATAC, histone marks)
description: Collect cells at several timepoints (untreated, days after drug, regrowth) and measure chromatin accessibility, key histone modifications (e.g., H3K27me3, KDM5 targets) and transcripts in the same cells. This tests whether survival reflects reversible epigenetic states, in which the pattern of chromatin marks, rather than the underlying genome, differs.

title: Metabolic and stress-state measurements of survivors with pathway perturbation
description: Use FLIM of NAD(P)H, mitochondrial membrane potential dyes, ROS/lipid peroxidation sensors, and drug efflux/accumulation assays, with flow sorting, to compare surviving and dying cells. Then test causality by perturbing the identified pathway (e.g., GPX4, OXPHOS, ABC transporters) and measuring whether the persister fraction changes.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens plus mathematical modeling of switching rates
description: Run genome-wide or targeted CRISPRi/a screens under drug to find genes that raise or lower persister frequency, and use fluctuation-test (Luria–Delbrück-style) assays to estimate rates of switching into and out of the tolerant state. Fit stochastic models to determine whether the survival fraction is explained by pre-existing rare states, noisy induced adaptation, or both.

title: Lineage barcoding to separate pre-existing from induced tolerance
description: Tag a clonal population with heritable DNA barcodes, split it into replicate pools, and apply the drug. If the same barcodes survive across replicates, tolerance was pre-existing and heritable. If the survivors differ randomly across replicates, tolerance was stochastic or induced. Pair this with scRNA-seq of sister cells sampled before treatment to find the predictive state.

title: Live-cell time-lapse tracking with reporters and retrospective fate mapping
description: Image cells with fluorescent reporters of signaling (ERK, p53, NF-κB), cell cycle, and mitochondrial state for days before the drug, then follow each cell's fate after treatment. Machine-learning models trained on pre-treatment dynamics then show which single-cell features, such as pulse frequency or cycle phase, predict survival. They also show how long the state persists across divisions.

title: Single-cell multi-omics of survivors across time
description: Run paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, or CITE-seq, on untreated cells, cells at early drug exposure, and persisters at several weeks. Compare them to find a rare pre-existing transcriptional or chromatin state, such as a drug-tolerant, stress-response or EMT-like program. Then use RNA velocity and trajectory inference to test whether survivors arise from that state or switch into it after treatment.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens and perturbation of candidate state regulators
description: Run genome-wide or epigenetic-focused CRISPRi/a screens under drug to find genes that raise or lower the survivor fraction. Then validate hits by perturbing chromatin regulators (KDM5, HDACs) and anti-apoptotic or antioxidant pathways such as GPX4 or BCL-2. This shows which factors cause tolerance and which merely mark it.

title: Quantifying state-switching dynamics with fluctuation analysis and mathematical modeling
description: Sort cells by a marker of the tolerant state and measure how fast the sorted populations return to the original mix (Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation tests plus Markov state models). Fit the switching rates to the observed survival fractions to distinguish genetic mutation, stable epigenetic states, and rapid stochastic fluctuations. This also predicts dosing schedules that could shrink the survivor fraction.

title: Lineage-barcoded clonal tracking before and after drug
description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicates, and treat. Then sequence barcodes to see whether the same lineages survive across replicates (pre-existing heritable state) or different ones (stochastic switching). Each barcode marks one lineage, so persisting lineages can be counted. Pair this with scRNA-seq on sister cells collected before treatment to find the transcriptional state that predicts survival.

title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters and pedigree tracing
description: Image single cells for days before and during drug exposure, using fluorescent reporters for signaling (ERK/AKT), cell cycle, and apoptosis. Trace each survivor's ancestry to test whether pre-treatment dynamics (slow cycling, pulsatile signaling, or a lineage-shared state) predict survival, and compare sister cells to assess how heritable the state is.

title: Multi-omic profiling of survivors over time
description: Run single-cell RNA, ATAC and proteomic profiling at time points from untreated through early drug tolerance to regrowth. This separates persister states (such as epigenetic reprogramming, stress-response or drug-efflux programs) from mutations, by grouping apparently identical cells according to shared features in the data. Whole-genome sequencing of survivors would rule out rare genetic resistance.

title: Functional perturbation screens in the persister state
description: Run a CRISPR knockout or interference screen, or a small-molecule screen, during drug exposure. Measure which perturbations change the fraction of survivors, targeting chromatin regulators, metabolic and stress pathways, and anti-apoptotic genes. The results show which factors cause tolerance and which could be co-targeted.

title: Single-cell metabolic and drug-response phenotyping
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration, mitochondrial priming (BH3 profiling), ROS, and metabolic state (for example NADH fluorescence lifetime imaging) in single cells just after drug exposure. Then sort or image cells by these readouts and follow their fates. This shows whether survivors take up less drug, resist apoptosis more strongly, or have a different metabolism.

title: Twin-population lineage barcoding with retrospective state profiling
description: Label cells with heritable expressed barcodes, split the population into sister halves, and treat only one half so that surviving lineages can be identified by barcode. Then profile the matched untreated sisters by single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq to directly read out the pre-treatment molecular state that predicted survival.

title: Fluctuation analysis of pre-existing versus drug-induced resistance
description: Seed many small parallel cultures from single cells, expand them for varying numbers of generations, then treat each with drug and count survivors. Large between-culture variance in survivor number indicates heritable pre-existing states, and the dependence on expansion time estimates how many generations the state persists.

title: Highly multiplexed single-molecule RNA FISH of candidate resistance markers before treatment
description: Image thousands of untreated cells for simultaneous transcript counts of resistance-associated genes (receptor tyrosine kinases, stress and dedifferentiation markers) to measure how often rare high-expressing cells arise and whether the markers co-fluctuate as a coordinated program. Fixing and re-imaging the same field after treatment links the measured state to actual survival.

title: Long-term live-cell imaging with signaling and cell-cycle reporters through drug exposure
description: Track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy using reporters for pathway activity, cell-cycle phase, and division history, from before drug addition through the survival bottleneck. This reveals whether survival depends on dynamic properties such as quiescence, division timing, or transient signaling pulses rather than a static expression state.

title: Pooled CRISPRa/CRISPRi screens scored on the rare-survivor fraction
description: Run genome-scale or focused CRISPRa and CRISPRi screens and compare guide representation in drug survivors versus untreated controls, using barcode-level statistics suited to the extreme bottleneck. Hits identify which genes are sufficient or necessary to enter the survival-prone state, turning correlative markers into mechanism.

title: Time-lapse imaging to persistence with retrospective tracking
description: Continuously image a labeled population from before drug addition through the emergence of surviving colonies, tracking every lineage. Then work backward from the survivors to quantify what distinguished them beforehand: cell cycle phase at treatment onset, division history, size, motility, and local neighbor density.

title: Paired pre- and post-treatment profiling of the same clone by barcoding
description: Transduce cells with heritable expressed barcodes, split them into treated and untreated arms, and sequence both. Barcodes enriched among survivors identify which clones were pre-disposed to survive, and single-cell transcriptomes of the untreated cells carrying those barcodes reveal the pre-existing expression state responsible.

title: Clone-to-clone variance assay to separate heritable priming from stochastic events
description: Expand many independent small subpopulations from single cells, then treat each identically and count survivors. Large clone-to-clone variance in survivor number indicates a heritable, epigenetically transmitted predisposition, while Poisson-like variance points to a transient, cell-autonomous event at the time of treatment.

title: Chromatin accessibility and histone-mark mapping of survivors versus naive cells
description: Apply single-cell ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN for repressive and enhancer marks to drug-naive cells, early survivors, and cells after drug withdrawal. This tests whether survival depends on pre-opened enhancers at stress or lineage-plasticity genes and whether that state is reversible.

title: Live single-cell reporters of signaling, apoptotic priming, and metabolic state
description: Engineer fluorescent reporters for pathway reactivation (ERK or AKT kinase activity), mitochondrial apoptotic priming, and redox or lipid-peroxidation state, then image them in individual cells across treatment. Correlating reporter trajectories with each cell's fate shows whether survival reflects incomplete target inhibition, a high apoptotic threshold, or a distinct metabolic dependency.

title: Sister-cell split experiment to test whether survival is heritable
description: Expand a clone, then split sister cells into parallel wells and treat each separately, varying the time between split and treatment from hours to weeks. If survivor frequency is correlated between sisters at short delays and decorrelates at long delays, this quantifies how long the surviving state is retained and separates heritable priming from moment-to-moment randomness.

title: Expressed lineage barcodes with paired profiling of untreated relatives
description: Transduce cells with heritable, transcribed barcodes, then sequence both a drug-treated arm and an untreated arm sampled before treatment, so that relatives of future survivors can be identified retrospectively. Comparing the pre-treatment molecular profiles of clones that go on to survive versus those that die identifies the primed state directly, as opposed to post-treatment adaptation.

title: Live imaging of signaling and cell-cycle reporters through drug addition
description: Image cells carrying kinase-activity and cell-cycle reporters (for example ERK, AKT, CDK2 sensors) continuously from before dosing until survivors are visible, then trace each survivor backwards through the movie. This reveals whether survival is predicted by baseline pathway activity, by a quiescent or slow-cycling phase at the moment of exposure, or by how fast signaling rebounds after inhibition.

title: Chromatin and transcription factor state of rare pre-primed cells, with causal follow-up
description: Apply single-cell ATAC-seq or joint RNA/ATAC profiling to untreated populations and to survivors, looking for a rare subpopulation whose regulatory landscape already resembles the resistant end state. Candidate transcription factors identified this way are then tested with CRISPR activation or inhibition to see whether raising or lowering their frequency shifts the fraction of surviving cells.

title: Pooled genetic screens on the surviving fraction
description: Run CRISPR knockout, CRISPRi, or ORF overexpression screens in the presence of drug and score which perturbations change the number of survivors rather than bulk growth, including screens performed on survivors to find dependencies specific to that state. This distinguishes genes that set how often the surviving state arises from genes required to maintain it once entered, and nominates combination treatments that reduce the surviving fraction.

title: Lineage barcoding of paired populations to profile future survivors
description: Introduce expressed heritable barcodes into the cell line, split the population into treated and untreated halves, and identify barcodes enriched after drug treatment. Then profile the matched untreated sibling cells carrying those same barcodes to measure the pre-existing molecular state that predicted survival, rather than inferring it from survivors already altered by the drug.

title: Live-cell imaging of signaling and cell-cycle dynamics across the treatment window
description: Use fluorescent reporters for target-pathway activity, cell-cycle phase, apoptotic commitment, and stress responses, and track individual cells continuously from before dosing through survival or death. This yields each survivor's full dynamic history, distinguishing cells that never engaged the drug target from those that engaged it but failed to commit to death.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic time course of persistence and regrowth
description: Profile the population at closely spaced timepoints spanning naive, early drug exposure, deep persistence, and regrowth, and compare the trajectories. This tests whether survivors enter one convergent tolerant program or several distinct ones, and whether the surviving state reverts to the naive distribution after drug withdrawal.

title: Chromatin accessibility mapping plus epigenetic modifier perturbation
description: Perform single-cell ATAC-seq on naive, persister, and regrown cells to find regulatory regions that are already open in the rare subpopulation before treatment. Then test causality by knocking down or inhibiting the chromatin modifiers maintaining those regions and measuring whether the frequency of survivors drops.

title: Schedule and dose variation to distinguish reversible tolerance from fixed resistance
description: Systematically vary dose, treatment duration, and drug-holiday length, then re-challenge the expanded survivors and quantify how often they survive again. If survival frequency returns toward the parental rate after a holiday, the state is reversible and non-genetic; if it is retained, genetic or stably heritable mechanisms dominate, which can be confirmed by sequencing resistant clones.

title: Heritable barcodes to profile untreated relatives of survivors
description: Tag cells with expressed, heritable clonal barcodes, let them expand, then split the population so one arm is treated and the other is left untreated. Barcodes identify which untreated cells are close relatives of the eventual survivors. Single-cell RNA/ATAC profiling of those relatives reveals the pre-existing molecular state that predicted survival rather than the state the drug induced.

title: Long-term live imaging from before dosing through outgrowth
description: Image a sparse, fluorescently reporter-tagged population continuously from several divisions before treatment until resistant colonies appear, then trace each survivor's full lineage backward. This links measurable pre-drug properties (cell-cycle phase, size, reporter level, signaling dynamics, local density, time since last division) and post-drug behaviors (dormancy, division timing) to which cells survive.

title: Spatially resolved transcriptomics of rare survivors in situ
description: Apply in situ sequencing or multiplexed single-molecule FISH to the treated monolayer on fixed plates without dissociating cells, so that rare persisters are measured together with their immediate neighbors and their position in the colony. This tests whether survival is driven by cell-intrinsic state or by local microenvironment effects such as crowding, paracrine signaling, and nutrient gradients.

title: Prospective enrichment by sorting on a candidate marker
description: Use FISH- or antibody-based sorting on candidate high-expression markers (for example receptor tyrosine kinases or drug-efflux and stress genes) to isolate the rare marker-high subpopulation from an untreated culture. Treat sorted and unsorted cells in parallel. A reproducible shift in survival frequency turns a correlative signature into a causal, prospectively predictive one, and re-sorting after outgrowth measures how quickly the state reverts.

title: Perturbation screens with single-cell readouts of entry into and exit from the primed state
description: Run CRISPR activation/interference or epigenetic-modifier inhibitor screens with a single-cell or barcoded readout. Score not only total survivor number but also the frequency of cells in the primed transcriptional state before treatment. Separate factors that change how often cells enter the state from those that change whether primed cells stabilize resistance, to distinguish a fluctuation-driven model from a selection/epigenetic-lock-in model.

title: Sister-cell split assay to recover the pre-treatment state of survivors
description: Let single cells divide once or twice, physically separate the resulting sister subpopulations, expose one to the targeted drug and keep the other untreated, then use heritable lineage barcodes to trace which untreated sisters correspond to the rare survivors. Transcriptional or chromatin profiling of those retrospectively identified sisters reveals the pre-existing state present before any drug was applied.

title: Imaging-based rare-state quantification before and after treatment
description: Apply highly multiplexed single-molecule RNA imaging or protein immunofluorescence to tens of thousands of untreated cells to detect rare subpopulations expressing candidate tolerance programs, and quantify how often those marker combinations co-occur in the same cell. Repeating the measurement on survivors tests whether the same program is enriched, distinguishing pre-existing tolerance from drug-induced adaptation.

title: Longitudinal live imaging of individual cells through treatment
description: Track thousands of single cells with fluorescent reporters for pathway activity, cell-cycle position, and stress response from before drug addition through death or survival, and regress each cell's fate on its own prior dynamics. This tests whether features such as slow cycling, signaling pulse frequency, or reporter fluctuation amplitude predict which cells persist.

title: Clonal barcode tracking across repeated treatment and drug-holiday cycles
description: Barcode a population at high complexity, treat, allow outgrowth, remove drug, and re-treat, sequencing barcode abundances at each step. If the same clones dominate every round, tolerance is heritable and stable; if survivor identity changes between rounds, it is a transient, reversible state, and the rate of change estimates how fast cells switch in and out of it.

title: Paired genomic and epigenomic profiling of survivors versus bulk population
description: Perform single-cell joint chromatin-accessibility and transcriptome assays, plus whole-genome or targeted sequencing, on survivors and matched untreated controls. This separates genetic resistance mutations and copy-number changes from non-genetic chromatin reconfiguration, and identifies transcription factor motifs whose accessibility changes as cells enter or exit the tolerant state.

title: Prospective isolation by candidate-marker sorting
description: Use flow cytometry on untreated cells to purify the rare subpopulation expressing high levels of a suspected resistance-associated surface protein, then compare drug-survival frequency of sorted-high versus sorted-low fractions. A large enrichment implies the surviving fraction was specified before the drug was applied.

title: Clonal split-and-compare design
description: Expand single-cell-derived clones, split each into treated and untreated arms, and determine whether survival frequency is reproducible across clones or randomly distributed. Reproducible clone-specific rates indicate heritable causes, while scatter indicates transient fluctuations.

title: Longitudinal imaging of individual survivors
description: Track every cell in a field from before treatment through weeks of drug exposure to record division history, dormancy duration, and timing of outgrowth. Survivors can then be retrieved by micromanipulation or photoconversion for downstream molecular profiling.

title: Chromatin and epigenome profiling of the resistant state
description: Apply single-cell ATAC-seq and histone-modification mapping to survivors versus naive cells to find accessibility changes underlying tolerance. Test reversibility by withdrawing drug, reseeding, and re-profiling to see whether the state decays.

title: Genome-wide perturbation screens for state entry and exit
description: Run CRISPR activation and knockout screens scored on survivor frequency to identify regulators that change how often cells occupy the drug-tolerant state. Compare hits from perturbations made before treatment with those made after treatment begins to separate factors controlling state entry from those controlling survival during treatment.

title: Lineage barcoding with retrospective identification of pre-resistant cells
description: Label cells with expressed, heritable barcodes, split clonal populations into a drug arm and a reference arm, and use the barcodes of surviving clones to identify and profile their sister cells from before treatment by scRNA-seq or imaging. This reveals the transcriptional and epigenetic state that marked a cell as a future survivor before any drug was added.

title: Single-molecule RNA FISH of rare pre-treatment expression states
description: Use multiplexed smFISH (or iterative methods such as MERFISH or ClampFISH) on large numbers of untreated cells to measure the frequency and co-occurrence of rare cells that strongly express resistance-associated genes (e.g., AXL, EGFR, NGFR). Then test whether the fraction of these cells, and their spatial clustering, predicts how many colonies survive the drug.

title: Luria–Delbrück fluctuation analysis and memory measurements
description: Grow many small parallel clonal populations, then treat them and measure how much the number of surviving colonies varies between populations. Excess variance indicates that the pre-resistant state is heritable. Combine this with sister-cell and cousin-cell analysis of barcoded lineages to estimate how many generations the state lasts and how fast cells switch in and out of it.

title: Live-cell imaging of signaling dynamics and cell-cycle state during drug exposure
description: Use fluorescent reporters for the targeted pathway (e.g., an ERK kinase translocation reporter), plus cell-cycle (FUCCI) and stress reporters, to follow individual cells through treatment. This tests whether survivors differ beforehand in signaling reactivation, quiescence, or proliferation dynamics, or only adapt afterward.

title: Perturbation screens for regulators of the frequency of the pre-resistant state
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens with single-cell readout (Perturb-seq), or targeted perturbations of chromatin regulators and transcription factors, to identify genes that change how often the rare pre-resistant state appears and how many cells survive the drug. Follow up with single-cell ATAC-seq or multiome to identify chromatin features that maintain the state heritably.

title: Pre-treatment live-cell reporter time series to predict survival
description: Image thousands of cells for 48–72 h before treatment using fluorescent reporters for key pathways (e.g., ERK/AKT KTR sensors, an NF-κB or AP-1 reporter), then add the drug and track which cells survive. Train a classifier on the pre-drug traces to test whether survivors show distinct dynamic signatures beforehand, such as pulsing frequency or variance, rather than only steady-state levels.

title: Fluctuation analysis of the primed state
description: Run a Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation test: expand many single-cell-derived clones for different numbers of generations, treat them in parallel, and fit survivor-count distributions. This estimates how often cells switch into and out of the drug-tolerant state and how long that state is inherited, which separates stochastic switching from fixed heterogeneity.

title: Graded drug-pulse protocols with single-cell RNA-seq
description: Expose cells to systematically varied drug pulse lengths, doses and recovery intervals, then measure survivor fractions alongside single-cell RNA-seq at each step. Mapping the dose-history response surface shows whether survival comes from a pre-existing state, adaptation the drug induces, or both, and where the transition happens.

title: Spatial neighbor analysis of survivors
description: Use high-plex spatial imaging (e.g., multiplexed smFISH or CODEX) on treated cultures and organoids to check whether survivors are enriched near particular neighbors, local densities, or secreted-factor gradients. Then test the candidate niche signals with conditioned-media and co-culture perturbations.

title: Perturb-seq screen of regulators of transition to the tolerant state
description: Run pooled CRISPRi/a screens with a single-cell readout (Perturb-seq) to find regulators whose knockdown or activation changes how often cells reach the tolerant state. Then fit a gene-regulatory network model to these results to identify hub factors whose shared fluctuations push a cell over the threshold for survival.

title: CRISPR molecular recorder of the pre-treatment history of survivors
description: Engineer cells with a continuously writing CRISPR base-editing or prime-editing recorder coupled to promoters of candidate resistance pathways (e.g., AXL, NGFR, stress/ER programs), plus a static lineage barcode. After drug selection, sequence only the survivors and decode whether their recorders show pathway activity minutes to days before treatment, distinguishing pre-existing priming from post-treatment induction.

title: Split-sister transcriptomics with matched treated and untreated progeny
description: Split each cell's immediate progeny (by micromanipulation or by splitting an early-passage barcoded clone) so that one half is drug-treated while the matched half is profiled untreated by scRNA-seq or ATAC-seq. Correlating each sister pair's pre-treatment molecular state with its partner's survival measures how much of survival is predictable from the heritable state, and for how many divisions that memory persists.

title: Early-warning fluctuation statistics from live imaging
description: Use long-term live-cell imaging of endogenous reporters (MAPK/ERK, stress, cell cycle, mitochondrial potential) in thousands of cells before and during drug exposure. Compute per-cell fluctuation statistics (variance, autocorrelation time, dwell-time distributions) and test whether survivors are distinguished not by mean expression but by slow, large-amplitude excursions, which would indicate proximity to an alternative stable state, as rising variance and autocorrelation would precede a state transition.

title: Survivor-frequency scaling and fluctuation analysis to separate pre-existing heritable states from stochastic induction
description: Use Weibull weakest-link statistics to distinguish survival from pre-existing rare states versus random nucleation, by measuring survivor frequency as a function of population size, clone size, drug dose, and exposure duration, and fitting the resulting hazard functions. Pair this with a Luria–Delbrück-style fluctuation test across many parallel expansions of the same clone: large between-culture variance implies heritable, early-arising survivor states, while Poisson-like variance implies transient, independently arising survival events.

title: Mapping the physical and chemical microenvironment of survivors
description: Map each survivor's local context at the time of treatment: local cell density and neighbor identity from imaging, intracellular drug concentration via a fluorescent drug analog or MALDI mass-spectrometry imaging, and local oxygen, nutrient and matrix stiffness readouts. Mixed-effects modeling of survival against these niche covariates versus cell-intrinsic expression quantifies how much of the rare-survivor phenotype reflects a rare microenvironment, and this can be tested by transplanting survivors into uniform conditions and re-challenging them.

title: DNA-based molecular recording of pre-treatment history
description: Engineer cells with CRISPR molecular recorders (DNA Typewriter, base-editing tapes) driven by stress, cell-cycle, and bypass-pathway promoters so each cell permanently records its transcriptional history in DNA. Sequencing survivors then reads out the states they occupied before and during treatment, instead of inferring cause only from the surviving cells.

title: Early-warning signals of critical slowing down in pathway reporters
description: Apply dynamical-systems signatures of approaching state transitions — rising variance, rising lag-1 autocorrelation, and slowed recovery from perturbation — to long-term live-cell imaging of drug-target pathway reporters before treatment. Test whether cells that later survive show these precursor signatures, using optogenetic or drug-pulse perturbations to measure recovery rates directly.

title: Weibull reliability analysis of single-cell time-to-death
description: Fit single-cell time-to-death distributions across doses and clonal backgrounds using extreme-value and Weibull statistics, inferring how many independent protective lesions or pathway activations a cell needs to withstand treatment. The inferred count becomes a quantitative prediction testable against measured numbers of upregulated bypass pathways in survivors.

title: Sorting dormant versus active cells by metabolic labeling
description: Label cells before drug exposure by biosynthetic activity without destroying them (BONCAT or OP-Puro for translation, heavy-water stimulated Raman for metabolic turnover) and sort dormant from active cells. Comparing survival between sorted fractions directly tests whether generic quiescence, rather than any specific resistance program, is the causal determinant.

title: Sister-cell matched design across a barcoded lineage tree
description: Split sister cells at mitosis, profile one sister by single-cell multiome, and score the other sister's fate under drug. Extending the matching across generations of a barcoded lineage tree localizes how many divisions back the survival predisposition becomes heritable.

title: Barcoded sister-cell split profiling
description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes and let each clone divide into sister subpopulations. Destructively profile one sister population (scRNA-seq/ATAC) while treating the other with drug, and use the barcode to retroactively assign the pre-treatment molecular state of clones whose sisters survived. This directly tests whether survival is predictable from a pre-existing transcriptional/chromatin state rather than a post-hoc drug response.

title: Long-term live imaging for precursor signaling dynamics and lead time
description: Image cells for days before and during treatment with multiplexed live reporters (e.g., ERK/AKT kinase translocation sensors, NF-κB, stress and cell-cycle reporters), then align single-cell traces retrospectively to the survival outcome. Fitting the hazard of survival to the preceding signaling history identifies precursor signatures and the characteristic lead time over which the predisposed state exists.

title: Memory timescale of the surviving state by re-challenging subcultures
description: Isolate single cells, expand them for variable numbers of generations, and re-challenge replicate subcultures with drug at each time point. The decay of correlation in survival fraction between sibling subcultures as a function of elapsed divisions quantifies how many generations the resistant state is inherited. This separates transient fluctuation, epigenetic memory, and genetic mutation.

title: Per-cell drug dose and target engagement to rule out pharmacological escape
description: Measure the drug dose each individual cell actually receives and engages, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging of the unlabeled compound, efflux-pump reporters, and single-cell target-engagement readouts (phospho-target staining or in-cell thermal shift). This distinguishes survivors that are genuinely drug-tolerant from those that experienced a low effective dose because of differences in uptake, efflux, or target abundance.

title: DNA-based molecular recorders of signaling history
description: Use CRISPR base-editor or recombinase recording systems driven by pathway-responsive promoters so that each cell continuously writes a cumulative, time-resolved record of its signaling and stress history into its own genome. Sequence the recorder locus in rare survivors after treatment to recover their multi-day history without destructive sampling beforehand, revealing whether survivors came from cells with distinctive prior pathway activity.

title: CRISPR base-editor recorders of pre-treatment signaling
description: Use a CRISPR base-editor recorder that writes signaling and transcription-factor activity (AP-1, NF-kB, ERK, Wnt) into genomic barcodes during the days before drug exposure. Then sequence the recordings in survivors versus matched untreated cells to identify which pre-existing states predicted survival.

title: Heritability of fate across lineage trees
description: Perform time-lapse imaging of full lineage trees with drug added at varied times post-division, measuring fate concordance between sisters, cousins, and more distant relatives. The decay of concordance with genealogical distance estimates how long a survival-priming state is heritable versus randomly reset.

title: Survival modeling of single-cell death with dynamic live-cell reporters
description: Image cells carrying multiple live reporters (ERK kinase translocation, caspase sensor, FUCCI cell cycle, mitochondrial potential) through treatment. Fit survival models with time-varying covariates to find which dynamic features, rather than snapshot levels, change a cell's instantaneous risk of death.

title: Early-warning signals before entry into the drug-tolerant state
description: Test whether cells entering a drug-tolerant state show critical slowing down, meaning rising variance, rising autocorrelation, and flickering in reporter time series, before committing. This would allow prospective identification and sorting of pre-transition cells for molecular profiling.

title: Microenvironmental neighborhood effects on survival
description: Treat each cell's local context as an exposure: use spatial transcriptomics or imaging of dense cultures and organoids to test whether survival clusters spatially. Regress survival on local density, neighbor identity, and diffusible-factor gradients to separate cell-intrinsic priming from protection conferred by the local microenvironment.

title: Automated detection and isolation of rare dividing cells under drug
description: Continuously image millions of drug-treated cells and automatically flag the rare cells that are still dividing or re-entering the cell cycle. Photoconvert or photo-tag only those cells and isolate them immediately for scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and proteomics. This profiles the actual survivors as they diverge from the rest of the population, instead of using bulk measurements or post-hoc resistant lines.

title: Sinusoidal drug delivery to measure pathway signaling response
description: Use microfluidics to deliver the targeted inhibitor as sinusoidal concentration waveforms with periods from minutes to days, driving the system across many frequencies while recording pathway-activity reporters. Test whether pre-persister cells are defined by a distinct input-output (transfer) function, with a slower, more damped signaling response, rather than by a static difference in baseline expression.

title: Continuous versus pulsed dosing with survivor-distribution fitting
description: Deliver matched total drug exposure as one continuous dose versus many intermittent pulses across thousands of replicate wells. Fit the survivor-fraction distributions with Weibull/extreme-value models to ask whether survival follows a model of rare pre-existing states or a model of tolerance accumulated during treatment.

title: Sequential metabolic time-stamping of single survivors
description: Apply sequential labeling before and during treatment, using distinguishable 4sU and 5-EU RNA pulses plus SILAC heavy-amino-acid pulses, so each cell carries time-ordered markers of its transcription and translation rates. Read these out in single surviving cells to reconstruct whether they were already slow-cycling or translationally quiet before the drug was added.

title: Early-warning signals of fate commitment in single-cell reporter traces
description: Record long, high-frequency single-cell reporter traces through treatment and compute rolling variance, lag-1 autocorrelation, and relaxation time after small optogenetic or washout perturbations. Test whether cells that later become persisters show increased variance, autocorrelation, and recovery time (critical slowing down) hours before they visibly diverge from dying neighbors.

title: Twin-population lineage tracing with pre-drug profiling of untreated sisters
description: Give cells heritable barcodes and split each clone into twin populations before treatment: treat one half with drug, and profile the untreated twin with single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq to read out the pre-drug state of the lineages that went on to survive. This shows whether survivors were already distinct before the drug was added, and which genes and chromatin features marked them.

title: Live-cell signaling reporter history and survival-analysis modeling
description: Image live-cell reporters (for example ERK, AKT and p53 activity sensors, plus a cell-cycle reporter) for 48–72 hours before and during drug exposure. Then fit survival-analysis models to determine which features of each cell's signaling history, such as pulse frequency, baseline level, or cell-cycle phase, best predict whether it lives or dies.

title: Sister-cell correlation analysis to separate heritable from random effects
description: Track lineages by time-lapse microscopy and measure how often sister cells, cousins, and unrelated cells share the same outcome after drug treatment. Fitting these correlations to a branching model estimates how much of survival comes from a state passed down through divisions and how long that state lasts.

title: Sort-and-remix measurement of state-switching rates
description: Use FACS to sort cells that are high or low for a candidate persister marker (such as AXL, EGFR or NGFR), label each group with a different fluorescent dye or barcode, mix them back together, and sample at several time points to measure how fast cells switch between states. Drug-challenging the samples at each time point shows how survival potential changes as cells move between states.

title: Pooled CRISPR perturbation screens with single-cell readout at low drug dose
description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or activation screens with a single-cell readout (Perturb-seq) at low drug doses. Score each gene by how much it raises or lowers the fraction of surviving cells, not just whether cells grow. This separates genes that create the rare pre-resistant state from genes that only help survival after the drug is added.

title: Repeated drug pulses with varied washout to test reversibility of the resistant state
description: Expose cells to repeated pulses of drug with varying washout intervals and track single-clone phenotypes, measuring whether the surviving state relaxes back or becomes permanently fixed. Mapping how long drug exposure must last and how long memory persists after removal distinguishes transient transcriptional priming from heritable epigenetic or genetic fixation, and identifies the dosing interval that prevents the state from becoming fixed.

title: Distribution of dormancy depths and re-entry times as a bet-hedging trait
description: Use long-term live imaging and quiescence-depth reporters (CDK2 activity, p21, DNA-labeling dilution) to measure the full distribution of dormancy depths and cell-cycle re-entry times before and during treatment. Fitting bet-hedging models to the observed switching rates tests whether survival is an evolved stochastic dormancy strategy rather than a drug-induced response, and predicts the optimal drug-holiday timing to target cells re-entering the cell cycle.

title: Survival fraction across marker-expression bins for candidate priming markers
description: Build live reporters for candidate pre-resistance markers, FACS-sort untreated cells into narrow bins spanning the full expression range, and measure the fraction of each bin that survives drug. A marker whose survival fraction rises sharply and monotonically with expression is a likely causal determinant of survival, while markers that merely correlate with survivors show flat or noisy survival fractions, separating causal priming from bystander correlation.

title: Per-cell drug concentration and target occupancy in survivors versus dying cells
description: Use a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, intracellular mass-spectrometry imaging, and efflux-pump reporters to measure single-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy (e.g., by a target-engagement FRET or thermal-shift reporter) in survivors versus dying neighboring cells. This tests whether the surviving fraction results from heterogeneity in drug uptake, efflux, or sequestration rather than from a cell-state difference.

title: Survival modeling with time-varying covariates
description: From continuous imaging of thousands of cells during treatment, fit a Cox proportional-hazards model in which each cell's time to death is regressed on time-varying covariates (reporter intensities, cell size, cell-cycle phase, local density, mitotic history) measured hours earlier. The hazard ratios quantify how much each feature changes the instantaneous risk of death, and deviations from proportional hazards reveal whether survivors are a distinct subpopulation or the tail of a single continuous risk distribution.

title: Retrospective state mapping of survivors via lineage barcoding
description: Tag every cell with a heritable barcode, split the population so one half is profiled by single-cell RNA-seq or multiplexed imaging before drug exposure while the sister half is treated, then match survivor barcodes back to their untreated siblings' profiles. This identifies which pre-treatment molecular signatures the survivors carried in advance.

title: Live imaging of the drug-response trajectory with signaling reporters
description: Follow thousands of single cells by continuous time-lapse through treatment, using reporters for pathway reactivation (ERK/AKT kinase translocation), cell cycle (FUCCI), and apoptotic commitment. This records the exact frame at which a future survivor diverges from neighboring cells that die, rather than inferring it afterward.

title: Fluctuation and mixture-model analysis of survival variation across replicate clones
description: Expand many independent single-cell-derived clones and treat them identically. Analyze the variance in survivor counts and the shape of time-to-death distributions using Luria-Delbruck fluctuation statistics and Weibull or multi-component mixture fits. Inflated between-clone variance or a distinct long-lived component indicates a heritable pre-existing subpopulation rather than random chance within each cell.

title: Whole-cell imaging and sequencing for structural features enriched in survivors
description: Apply high-content 3D imaging, imaging flow cytometry, and DNA FISH alongside single-cell DNA sequencing to score every cell for extrachromosomal DNA copy number, micronuclei, ploidy, mitochondrial mass, and position within a colony. Then test whether each feature is enriched in survivors, to ask whether survivors lacked or possessed a particular feature.

title: Stepped dose titration to measure per-lineage tolerance threshold
description: Expose barcoded lineages to stepped drug concentrations and durations, estimating a survival threshold for each lineage. Then re-derive clones from survivors and repeat to see whether the threshold is heritable and how fast it relaxes. This converts a binary live/die readout into a distribution of per-lineage tolerance limits, and their stability over generations distinguishes stable resistance from transient tolerance.

title: Split-replicate barcode concordance assay to measure memory of the primed state
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into replicate flasks at defined numbers of generations before treatment, treat all replicates, and measure the overlap of surviving barcodes across splits. Concordance as a function of the interval between split and treatment gives a quantitative memory half-life of the primed state. This separates heritable priming present at the split from fluctuations arising afterward.

title: Tracing survivor barcodes back to pre-treatment cell state
description: Use expressed, sequenceable lineage barcodes so that the barcodes of drug survivors can be read out and matched to a sibling aliquot of the same population profiled (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, or barcode-targeted imaging) before any drug exposure. This retrospectively identifies the molecular state of the future survivors before drug exposure, rather than comparing survivors to the bulk population after selection has altered it.

title: Iterative drug selection cycles with re-expansion of early-passage aliquots
description: Run repeated cycles of drug kill, drug withdrawal, and re-expansion, tracking at each round whether the same barcodes survive (fixed survival potential) or a newly different set does (resampled survival). In parallel, re-expand frozen early-passage aliquots of the same clone to test whether survival potential was already fixed at that earlier point, comparing recurrence of the same barcodes against reset in the earlier-passage aliquots.

title: Factorial dissection of sources of cell-to-cell variability
description: Perturb, separately and in combination, each candidate source of cell-to-cell variability: chromatin-encoded memory (EZH2, DNMT, or HDAC inhibition), cell-cycle phase at exposure (synchronization or live reporters), division history and local density, and drug-exposure variability (uptake of a fluorescent drug analog). Score how each changes both the survivor fraction and the barcode concordance between split sister cells, to determine which source of variability determines survival.

title: Prospective sorting test of the pre-treatment state
description: Train a classifier on data linking pre-treatment single-cell state to survival, convert the top features into a live-cell readout (knock-in reporter, surface marker, or live RNA stain), then sort untreated cells on that readout and measure the fold-enrichment in survivor frequency after treatment. A large prospective enrichment establishes that the survival-determining state is present before treatment, while a null result localizes fate determination to events during drug exposure.

title: Sibling-split clones with lineage barcoding to profile pre-treatment state
description: Because profiling a cell destroys it, use lineage barcoding plus a sibling-split design (e.g., Rewind/FateMap-style): expand single-cell-derived clones, then split each clone so one half is profiled untreated by scRNA-seq/ATAC-seq while the matched half receives drug. This retrospectively assigns the pre-treatment molecular state of lineages that survived versus those that died.

title: Multiplexed live-cell reporters with time-varying survival regression
description: Image cells for days before and during drug exposure while recording a multiplexed panel of fluorescent reporters (ERK/AKT activity, CDK2 cell-cycle sensor, mitochondrial membrane potential, ATF4/stress response, autophagy flux). Fit a time-varying Cox proportional-hazards model to the single-cell traces to identify which transient states, and in which time window relative to dosing, predict survival.

title: Comparing survivors across drug classes, intensities, and schedules
description: Systematically vary the insult on barcoded replicate populations: drug class (kinase inhibitor, chemotherapy, nutrient withdrawal), intensity, and schedule (step, ramp, pulse, repeated short bursts). Use barcode overlap to test whether the same lineages survive every insult (a general robust state) or different lineages survive different insults (mechanism-specific states).

title: Cell-intrinsic resource state and local context at the time of dosing
description: Quantify intracellular drug concentration at dosing (using a fluorescent drug analog or MALDI mass-spec imaging), plus efflux-pump activity, lysosomal sequestration, NADPH/GSH redox buffer, ATP, and ribosome/translation capacity. Measure local cell density, neighbor identity, and mechanical confinement by spatial imaging, to separate survivors that never received the dose from survivors that absorbed it.

title: Forcing the candidate state to test causality
description: Take the top candidate state inferred from the earlier lineage-tracing and related experiments and induce it deliberately, using CRISPRa, optogenetic or small-molecule induction of the marker gene program in a tunable fraction of cells, or FACS pre-sorting on a live reporter of that state. Then test whether the surviving fraction rises proportionally and whether blocking the state sharply reduces survival, to turn a correlation into a causal test.

title: Sister-cell split design with pre-treatment profiling
description: After a cell division, profile one daughter destructively (scRNA-seq, proteomics, or a reporter snapshot) while its sister is exposed to the targeted drug and followed to a survival or death outcome. This measures pre-treatment covariates on a cell with the same genetic and epigenetic state as the one whose fate is observed, separating predetermined survival advantage from post-treatment adaptation.

title: Time-aligned single-cell trajectories with pre-treatment difference testing
description: Use long-term live imaging with multiplexed signaling and stress reporters to build per-cell time series from days before drug addition through weeks after. Align all cells on the treatment time and estimate the survivor-versus-dying-cell difference at each time point before and after treatment. Significant differences before treatment indicate preexisting heterogeneity, whereas a flat pre-treatment period with divergence only after exposure indicates that survivorship arises from the drug exposure itself.

title: Matched comparison of survivors and dying cells with residual analysis
description: Using barcoded clonal families profiled before treatment, construct nearest-neighbor or propensity-score matched pairs of future survivors and future dying cells, balanced on cell-cycle phase, size, target-pathway activity, mitochondrial content, and local density. Test how much of the survival probability remains unexplained after balancing. The size and structure of this residual bounds how much of persistence is attributable to measured states versus unobserved or purely stochastic factors.

title: Regression discontinuity around a tunable target-dosage cutoff
description: Use a degron- or inducible-promoter-titrated level of the drug target (or of a candidate resistance mediator) as a continuous running variable, with a sharp kill threshold, and compare cells falling just above versus just below the cutoff, where assignment is effectively random. This isolates the causal contribution of that one variable to survival, separating it from the many correlated states that confound a simple association between high expression and persistence.

title: Drug holiday and rechallenge with within-clone comparison
description: Split each barcoded clone into treated and vehicle arms, release survivors into drug-free medium, re-split, and rechallenge. Estimate within-clone changes in survival relative to the never-treated arm of the same clone. A persistent within-clone shift indicates an inherited or epigenetically stabilized advantage, while reversion to baseline indicates a transient adaptive response to drug.

title: Constant-dose kill-kinetics analysis
