description: Hold cell populations at a fixed drug concentration and measure the death rate over time using live-cell imaging. A single-exponential decay indicates a uniform stochastic death hazard, while a biphasic curve with a plateau indicates a pre-existing subpopulation with a lower hazard.

title: Luria–Delbrück fluctuation test across many small subclones
description: Expand many independent subclones, each started from a few cells, for different numbers of generations, then treat them in parallel and compare how much the survivor counts vary from clone to clone. Variance near Poisson suggests drug-induced or random survival. Very high variance suggests pre-existing survivor states, and how it changes with expansion time gives the rate at which cells switch into and out of that state.

title: Dose-ramp survival spectrum
description: Measure the fraction of surviving cells across a fine range of drug concentrations and convert it into a cumulative density of resistance-conferring states per cell. Compare these spectra between cell lines and growth conditions to test whether a fixed, quantifiable cellular feature sets the tail of the survival curve.

title: Retrospective lineage barcoding to identify pre-treatment features of survivors
description: Label cells with expressed lineage barcodes, split the population, treat one half, and use single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing on the untreated half to profile the pre-treatment state of the lineages that later survived. This identifies the specific molecular feature linked to survival.

title: Depleting or knocking down a candidate marker before treatment
description: Use FACS to deplete, or CRISPR to knock down, a candidate marker (for example, high expression of a drug-efflux or stress-response gene) before treatment, then check whether the low-survival tail disappears or returns. This tests whether the feature causes survival.

title: Pre-treatment state profiling to predict survival
description: Image barcoded clonal cancer cells with live reporters (signaling kinase translocation reporters, FUCCI cell cycle, mitochondrial membrane potential, cell size) for 24-48 hours before drug addition, then track each cell's fate. Train an interpretable model to test which pre-treatment features, especially their variance and temporal dynamics rather than their means, predict which rare cells survive.

title: Cell-to-cell variance of response-curve differences across re-challenge cycles
description: Expose cells to repeated drug pulse and washout cycles and record single-cell response curves (viability, apoptotic reporter, growth rate) in each cycle. Compute the cell-to-cell variance of the difference between early- and later-cycle curves, and test whether this variance predicts the surviving fraction better than any population-average metric.

title: Live imaging followed by in situ molecular profiling of the same cells
description: Perform live imaging through treatment to identify survivors, then fix the same plate and run single-molecule FISH or in situ transcriptomics at the imaged coordinates. This links each survivor's measured pre-drug behavior to its molecular state.

title: Clonal barcode replicate testing for reproducible versus stochastic survival
description: Split a highly barcoded population into parallel replicate cultures before treatment and test whether the same barcodes survive in all replicates. Reproducible barcodes indicate heritable, stable pre-existing states, while replicate-specific survivors indicate transient fluctuations, partitioning the variance that any predictive model must explain.

title: Non-destructive sub-lethal perturbation-response profiling
description: Apply brief sub-lethal probes such as low-dose drug pulses, nutrient or oxidative stress, or optogenetic pathway stimulation at several frequencies, and read out the single-cell response amplitude and recovery kinetics. Test whether this response spectrum, measured before full treatment, is a non-destructive signature of the drug-tolerant state.

title: Barcoded replicate-flask drug selection
description: Label an isogenic cell line with a high-complexity lentiviral barcode library, split the barcoded population into many independent replicate flasks that each receive the same targeted drug, and deep-sequence the surviving barcodes in each. Quantify the cross-replicate reproducibility of which barcodes dominate, as an intraclass correlation or rank overlap against a neutral-drift null. This partitions survival into heritable intrinsic priming versus path-dependent chance.

title: Sister-cell split design to measure fate predictability from pre-drug state
description: Use live imaging or microraft arrays to track single cells through a division, then send one daughter into drug treatment and the other into single-cell RNA/ATAC-seq or clonal expansion. Concordance between one sister's molecular state and the other sister's survival outcome gives a lineage-matched estimate of how much survival is determined by the prior cell state rather than generated during treatment.

title: Retrospective capture of rare surviving founders before treatment
description: Use RNA FISH or barcode-guided sorting to isolate the specific cells destined to survive, identified by barcodes recovered from a replicate population already treated with drug. Profile those exact founder cells in the untreated state to determine what, if anything, distinguished them.

title: Continuous time-lapse from before drug to colony outgrowth
description: Image the whole population continuously with signaling and stress-state reporters from several days before dosing through the emergence of resistant colonies, reconstructing full time-stamped pedigrees. This identifies which early events, such as a transient expression spike, an unusually long cell-cycle arrest, or a particular cellular neighborhood, preceded later dominance, versus which were common and inconsequential.

title: Manipulating cell–cell feedback with matched replicate cultures
description: Run matched replicate cultures that differ only in whether cell–cell feedback can operate: dense monolayers, single cells isolated in nanowells, or conditioned-media transfer, all at identical drug exposure. Compare the inequality of clone success (Gini coefficient) and reproducibility across replicates in these conditions to test whether paracrine and spatial feedback amplify small initial differences into large survival differences.

title: Longitudinal single-cell live imaging of the pre-resistant state
description: Use long-term live-cell imaging with lineage tracking and signaling or drug-target reporters (e.g., kinase activity, receptor tyrosine kinase, or stress-pathway reporters) for days before treatment. Then add drug and test whether survivors occupied a distinguishable reporter state and for how long. Autocorrelation and state-dwell-time analysis of each lineage shows whether tolerance is a stable per-cell property or a transient fluctuation that cells move in and out of.

title: Sister-cell split-and-retreat assay for heritability and reset
description: Barcode cells and split each expanded clone into parallel arms: treat one arm immediately and culture the other drug-free for varying numbers of generations before treating. If survival frequency stays clone-specific, the trait is heritable; if it decays with a characteristic relaxation time, it is a fluctuating state, and the decay constant quantifies its memory.

title: Graded drug dose and pathway perturbation to find the variable setting tolerance
description: Sweep drug concentration, target-pathway modulators, and microenvironmental variables (growth factors, density, nutrient levels) while scoring survivor frequency. A survivor fraction that shifts smoothly with these variables identifies which continuous cell-state variable sets the tolerance threshold, rather than only cataloguing survivor markers.

title: Retrospective molecular profiling of cells that later survive
description: Use methods that allow identification of the specific pre-treatment cells that later survived (e.g., Rewind-style barcode or FISH-based tagging of rare high-expressors, followed by isolation and RNA/ATAC/protein profiling of those exact cells). This separates the causal priming state from the downstream transcriptional program induced by the drug.

title: Replicate overlap and expression fluctuation spectra to separate genetic from stochastic origins
description: Apply high-depth clonal barcoding plus whole-genome or targeted sequencing of survivors to test whether survivors are a reproducible set of clones (genetic, fixed) or a different, non-overlapping set in each independent replicate of the same population (stochastic, fluctuating). Quantify barcode overlap across replicates and the power spectrum of expression fluctuations in implicated genes to assign each candidate mechanism to a stable or transient origin.

title: Sister-cell concordance decay curve
description: Use microfluidic traps to capture mitotic sister pairs, separate them, and add drug at a range of delays after division (0 to more than 10 generations), then measure how often both sisters survive or both die. The rate at which concordance falls gives the memory time of the survival-competent state, and shows whether the state is inherited at birth or determined stochastically after division.

title: Single-cell drug uptake and target-occupancy imaging
description: Use isotope-labeled drug with NanoSIMS or MALDI imaging mass spectrometry, or a FRET/fluorescent probe of target occupancy, to measure intracellular drug concentration and the fraction of target inhibited in each cell. Then relate these measurements to whether that cell survives. This tests whether survivors are simply under-dosed or have incomplete target engagement, rather than being in a different signaling or transcriptional state.

title: Altering gene-expression noise at fixed mean and measuring survival
description: For candidate genes, build promoter or 5'UTR variants (e.g., changes to TATA-box or burst size) that keep average expression fixed but raise or lower cell-to-cell variability. Then test whether the surviving fraction changes. This is a causal test of whether variability itself, rather than average expression level, produces the rare surviving cells.

title: Biophysical fate prediction with buoyant mass and growth rate
description: Measure single-cell buoyant mass, density and mass-accumulation rate with suspended microchannel resonators before adding drug, then follow each cell through treatment in the same device. This tests whether physical traits not captured by sequencing-based methods, such as cell size, density or biosynthetic rate, predict which cells survive.

title: Asymmetric organelle partitioning at the last mitosis before drug
description: Image photoactivatable or age-tagged (e.g., MitoTimer, SNAP-tag pulse-chase) mitochondria, lysosomes and protein aggregates through the last cell division before drug addition. Measure how unevenly each daughter cell inherits them and whether this predicts which daughter survives. This tests whether random, non-transcriptional inheritance of cellular contents gives rise to the rare surviving cells.

title: Single-cell drug exposure and target-engagement mapping
description: Measure how much drug each cell takes in and how strongly the target is inhibited, using fluorescent or isotope-labeled drug analogs (with NanoSIMS or stimulated Raman imaging) together with FRET target-activity biosensors, then link these values to which cells survive. This tests whether survivors are biologically primed cells or simply cells that receive less effective drug because of uneven uptake, efflux, or target occupancy.

title: Cell-by-cell ecDNA copy number and survival
description: Use ecDNA FISH or live-imaged ecDNA tagged with TetO/TetR to count, cell by cell, the copies of ecDNA carrying oncogenes or drug-target genes before treatment, and relate copy number to survival. Because ecDNA segregates randomly at cell division, genetically identical populations can differ widely in gene dosage, which is rarely measured in persister studies.

title: Tuning expression noise at fixed mean with synthetic circuits
description: Put a candidate resistance driver (e.g., a transcription factor or receptor) under a synthetic circuit that changes cell-to-cell variability without changing average expression, using negative-feedback or noise-tuner constructs. Then measure whether the surviving fraction tracks variance or mean. This directly tests whether expression fluctuations themselves, rather than a specific expression state, cause survival.

title: Testing cell-autonomy by density and microwell titration
description: Plate cells over a wide range of densities and as isolated single cells in microwell arrays, with or without shared medium, and measure the surviving fraction and its Poisson statistics. Departures from density-independent, per-cell survival would show that survival depends on local community effects (paracrine rescue, nutrient sharing, contact) rather than intrinsic cell states.

title: Tracking asymmetric inheritance of old or damaged cellular components
description: Use pulse-chase tags (SNAP/Halo-tag protein-age labeling, photoconvertible mito-Dendra2) to follow, over generations, how protein aggregates, aged proteome and mitochondria are split between daughter cells. Then test whether daughters that inherit younger or older material are more likely to persist, revealing a deterministic, division-linked source of survival differences.

title: Single-cell drug uptake and target engagement imaging
description: Use fluorescent or deuterium/alkyne-tagged drug analogs (imaged by stimulated Raman scattering or click chemistry), plus a FRET target-occupancy sensor, to measure how much drug and target inhibition each cell receives before its fate is known. This tests whether survivors received less drug or less target inhibition, as opposed to having a different downstream state.

title: Synthetic noise-tuning of candidate genes at a fixed mean
description: Place a candidate survival gene under a synthetic circuit (for example, a negative-feedback or bursty promoter series) that changes cell-to-cell variance while keeping mean expression the same. Then measure how the survivor fraction changes. This shows whether variability itself, rather than the average level, sets the rare surviving fraction.

title: Asymmetric organelle inheritance tracking
description: Use photoconvertible or timer reporters (MitoTimer, old vs. new centrosome markers, protein-aggregate markers) to follow how mitochondria, aggregates, and centrosomes are partitioned at division, and track daughter-cell fates under drug. This tests whether survival depends on inheriting particular organelle ages or amounts rather than on transcriptional state.

title: Label-free biophysical profiling before treatment
description: Image cells for several generations before treatment with quantitative phase imaging and Brillouin microscopy to record dry mass, growth rate, volume, and stiffness. Then add the drug and link fate back to each cell, to identify physical predictors of survival, such as density or growth-rate thresholds, that sequencing would miss.

title: Micropatterned control of neighbor number and geometry
description: Plate single cells or small groups on micropatterned islands with set area, shape and neighbor number, then treat with drug. This measures how much of the survivor fraction comes from local cell-intrinsic state versus contact, spreading or crowding. Spatial point-pattern analysis of survivor positions in standard dishes is used to cross-check the results.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug levels using a fluorescent drug analog, MALDI or nanoSIMS imaging of the compound, or a drug-displaceable target-binding biosensor. Correlate each cell's measured exposure with its later fate by tracked imaging. This tests whether survival reflects heterogeneity in drug uptake, efflux, lysosomal sequestration, or target abundance rather than a transcriptional program.

title: Memory timescale of the primed state by delayed-treatment sister assays
description: Isolate pairs of sister and cousin cells (micropatterns, microfluidic traps, or single-cell cloning), then treat them after systematically varied delays of 0 to many generations, scoring concordance of survival as a function of relatedness and elapsed divisions. The decay curve of fate concordance yields a quantitative half-life for the heritable determinant, distinguishing short-lived signaling fluctuations, multi-generation epigenetic memory, and permanent genetic differences without assuming what the determinant is.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming measured before treatment and linked to the same cell's fate
description: Apply BH3 peptides to individually tracked live cells with a mitochondrial membrane potential or cytochrome-c reporter to score each cell's proximity to the apoptotic threshold, then challenge the sister cell with drug. This asks whether survival is set by the apoptotic threshold (BCL-2 family stoichiometry) rather than by upstream oncogenic signaling, and whether persisters are cells that cannot execute apoptosis quickly enough.

title: Unequal partitioning of cytoplasmic contents at mitosis
description: Use live imaging with labeled mitochondria, lysosomes, aggresomes, and a dilutable protein marker to quantify how unequally cytoplasmic contents are divided at each mitosis, then follow both daughters through drug treatment. If survivors are systematically the daughters that inherited an excess of mitochondria, lysosomes (which can sequester drug), or damaged-protein aggregates, survival is caused by stochastic cell-division mechanics rather than regulated state switching.

title: Matched protein and mRNA measurements to locate the layer of heterogeneity
description: Combine single-cell proteomics or high-plex antibody imaging with transcriptomes from the same cells (e.g., antibody-plus-RNA co-detection) for the drug target and its pathway, and test which layer predicts survival in a subsequent fate-tracked round. If protein-level variability predicts fate while transcript level does not, this would point to translational and degradation control rather than transcriptional state as the source of persistence.

title: Tuning expression noise of a candidate gene at fixed mean
description: Use synthetic gene circuits (for example, negative-feedback versus open-loop designs, or promoter variants with different burst kinetics) to change cell-to-cell variability in a candidate survival gene without changing its average level, then measure the survivor fraction. If survival scales with variance rather than mean expression, this is causal evidence that rare high-expressing cells, not the bulk level, explain survival.

title: Measurement of drug uptake and target engagement in single cells
description: Pair fluorescent or clickable analogs of the inhibitor (or single-cell mass spectrometry) with a live readout of target pathway activity, such as an ERK kinase translocation reporter, in the same cells. This shows whether survivors are cells in which the drug never fully reached or inhibited its target (due to efflux, uptake, or target-level differences) or cells that were fully inhibited and survived anyway.

title: Unequal inheritance of organelles and proteins between sister cells
description: Use photoconvertible labels on mitochondria, lysosomes, or aggregated proteins to follow how these are split between sister cells at the divisions just before drug addition. Then test whether the sister that received more (or less) predicts which one survives. This separates a deterministic cell-division effect from heritable transcriptional priming.

title: Control of local neighborhood with micropatterning
description: Plate single cells or small groups on micropatterned islands with set neighbor number, spacing, and island geometry. Also mix barcoded cells with unlabeled carrier cells at different densities. This tests whether the chance of surviving depends on contact, local paracrine signaling, or mechanical context rather than on anything intrinsic to the cell.

title: Timed optogenetic or chemical induction of candidate states
description: Optogenetically or chemically switch on candidate drivers (for example, AP-1 factors or receptor tyrosine kinases) in random subsets of cells for short pulses at different times before and after drug is added, then measure the survivor fraction. This maps the time window during which a transient state is enough to confer survival, and shows how long that state's protective effect lasts.

title: Single-cell drug uptake and target occupancy imaging
description: Use a fluorescent or click-chemistry-tagged analog of the targeted drug, together with a target-engagement readout such as a phospho-substrate biosensor, to measure how much drug each cell takes up and how fully its target is inhibited during live imaging. Then check whether survivors simply received less drug or had less target inhibition, for example because of efflux pumps or lysosomal trapping, rather than having a different transcriptional state.

title: Micropatterned control of local geometry and density
description: Plate cells on micropatterned islands of defined size, shape, and neighbor number. Map survival against position (edge vs. center), local crowding, and YAP localization to test whether rare survival comes from microenvironment and mechanics within the dish rather than from an internal cell state.

title: Buoyant mass and growth-rate profiling before treatment
description: Use suspended microchannel resonators or quantitative phase imaging to measure each cell's mass and mass-accumulation rate before adding drug, then track which cells survive. This tests whether biophysical traits such as cell size, protein dilution, or growth rate predict survival independently of gene expression.

title: Tracking asymmetric partitioning at division
description: Pulse-label mitochondria, aggregated proteins, or the drug target using photoconvertible or SNAP-tag chemistry. Follow how these components are split between daughter cells in the divisions before treatment, and test whether daughters that inherit an unequal share are the ones that later survive the drug.

title: Mitochondrial apoptotic priming in sister clones
description: Expand barcoded clones, split each into two halves, and run single-cell dynamic BH3 profiling on one half while giving the drug to the other. This links each clone's distance from the apoptotic threshold (how close it is to triggering cell death) to its survival. It tests whether persisters are defined by how they handle death signals rather than by how they respond to the drug's signaling effect.

title: Sister cells given different challenges to test whether the surviving state is drug-specific
description: Image and micromanipulate individual mitotic pairs (or split barcoded clones across many wells) so that one daughter or sibling receives the targeted drug and the other receives an unrelated stressor (different-target inhibitor, chemotherapy, nutrient starvation, heat, immune attack). Concordance of survival across arms quantifies how much of the rare-survivor phenotype is a generic stress-tolerant state versus a drug-pathway-specific one, and defines the dimensionality of the predisposing state space.

title: Noise engineering with matched mean and varied variance of candidate determinants
description: Build isogenic lines in which a candidate resistance effector (e.g., an RTK, efflux pump, or anti-apoptotic protein) is expressed from synthetic promoter/UTR variants matched in mean abundance but differing several-fold in cell-to-cell CV and in state memory (autocorrelation time), using a knock-in at the endogenous locus plus degron tuning. Measuring survival fraction as a function of CV alone is a causal test of whether expression variability, rather than average expression, sets the size of the surviving subpopulation.

title: Allele-resolved nascent transcription to separate cis bursting from trans cell state
description: Use allele-specific single-molecule RNA FISH or MS2/PP7 live imaging at both alleles of candidate resistance genes, combined with fixation of the same cells after drug treatment. If the two alleles fluctuate independently in survivors, the rare state arises from stochastic transcriptional bursting at a single locus; if they covary, the cause is an upstream trans-acting cell state. The measured burst or state autocorrelation time predicts how long a cell remains in the survival-prone state.

title: Asymmetric organelle and damaged-protein inheritance at the last pre-treatment division
description: Pulse-label mitochondria, lysosomes, and long-lived or oxidatively damaged proteins with photoconvertible or SNAP/Halo pulse-chase tags. Time-lapse image the divisions immediately preceding drug addition and score which daughter survives. This quantifies whether survival is set by noisy partitioning at cytokinesis (mitochondrial mass/membrane potential, lysosomal drug sequestration capacity, proteostasis load) rather than by a transcriptional program.

title: Micropatterned arrays and neighbor ablation to test neighborhood effects on survival
description: Seed cells on micropatterned islands or in microwells with defined, imaged local density, neighbor identity, and ECM contact, then treat and map survival against each spatial variable. Follow up by optogenetic or laser ablation of specific neighbors, and by conditioned-medium and transwell swaps, to test causality. This distinguishes cell-intrinsic priming from non-cell-autonomous rescue via paracrine factors, local drug depletion, or contact-mediated signaling, which standard dissociated single-cell assays cannot separate.

title: Per-cell target engagement of the drug
description: Before and during treatment, measure in each cell how much drug is bound to its target, using a NanoBRET or FRET target-engagement reporter or a fluorescent drug analog. Then test whether survivors started with lower intracellular drug occupancy (from efflux, uptake, or target abundance) or were fully inhibited and survived through downstream rewiring.

title: Drug timing relative to the circadian clock
description: Synchronize cellular clocks with a dexamethasone or serum shock and add drug at different times across 48 hours. Measure whether survivor frequency varies with clock phase. Knocking out BMAL1 or CRY1/2 tests whether clock-controlled gene expression timing determines which cells survive.

title: Tuning expression variability of one gene at constant mean
description: Use synthetic gene circuits (for example, noise-tuning promoter or feedback designs) to express a candidate survival gene at the same average level but with different amounts of cell-to-cell variation. Then measure the survivor fraction. This tests whether the variation itself, rather than the average level, produces the rare surviving cells.

title: Drug pulse schedule variation to estimate state-switching rates
description: Treat parallel cultures with drug pulses across a wide range of on/off periods. Fit the survival curve against pulse frequency to a two-state switching model. This gives the rates at which cells enter and leave the drug-tolerant state, and how long they stay in it, without needing a marker for that state.

title: Sorting cells by physical and organelle traits, then treating each group
description: Before drug exposure, use FACS to sort live cells into bins by cell size, mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM), lysosome content, or ribosome/translation rate (OPP labeling). Treat each bin separately to determine which physical or organelle traits predict survival; these traits arise from unequal partitioning of cell contents at division and would not be detected in transcript or chromatin data.

title: Retrospective lineage tracing of the pre-treatment state
description: Barcode cells with an expressed, single-cell-readable lineage tag, let them divide a few times, then split the population so one half is profiled untreated and the other half is drug-treated. Barcode matching gives the pre-treatment transcriptome of the exact lineages that go on to survive, without relying on guessed marker genes.

title: Split-replicate barcode assay of heritability and memory duration of the primed state
description: Split an expanded barcoded population into two or more replicate flasks and treat each independently, then measure how strongly survivor barcode identity is shared across replicates; the concordance quantifies heritability. Repeating the split after increasing numbers of pre-treatment generations gives the memory half-life of the primed state. This single design distinguishes stable genetic causes, semi-heritable epigenetic priming, and purely stochastic late decisions.

title: Prospective sorting and amplitude-matched induction of the primed state
description: Use a live-cell reporter or surface marker for the candidate primed state to sort rare high-expressing cells before treatment, and compare their survival frequency to sorted low-expressing cells. Then test sufficiency by transiently driving the same gene at the amplitude and duration seen in natural fluctuations. Sorting plus amplitude-matched induction tests whether the state causes survival, which correlative profiling cannot do.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement imaging
description: Measure fluorescent drug analog accumulation and a phospho-specific target readout in the same cells during the first hours of treatment, so that each survivor can be classified as under-dosed, poorly target-engaged, or fully engaged but death-resistant. This rules in or out pharmacological explanations that are rarely measured and that would otherwise confound any transcriptional explanation.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming as a death-threshold determinant
description: Apply BH3 profiling or a comparable mitochondrial depolarization assay at single-cell resolution to untreated cells, then relate measured priming to survival after drug challenge in matched lineages. This tests whether survivors differ not in how the drug is sensed but in how close they already are to the apoptotic threshold, as an alternative to signaling-state explanations.

title: Split-clone fluctuation assay to partition heritable and instantaneous causes
description: Grow many small clonal populations from single cells, split each into a profiled half and a drug-challenged half, and compare the variance in survivor fraction across clones to the variance expected from chance alone. The shape of the variance distribution estimates how long before treatment the survival-determining state was set, and separates heritable priming from random events at the moment of drug exposure.

title: Lineage trees under drug to measure survival memory in divisions
description: Image barcoded or sparsely labeled cells continuously from several divisions before drug addition through the persister phase, reconstructing full lineage trees. Correlating fates between sisters, cousins, and second cousins yields a quantitative half-life for the tolerant state, which distinguishes transient signaling fluctuations from epigenetically heritable programs.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and cell-cycle phase at treatment
description: Before attributing survival to transcriptional states, measure intracellular drug concentration in each cell (fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging) and cell-cycle phase at the time of treatment (FUCCI reporter). This determines whether survivors are simply quiescent cells or cells with low drug accumulation; if they are not, state-based explanations are better supported.

title: Colony-splitting map from molecular state to survival
description: Index-sort single cells, let each grow into a small colony, then split every colony between transcriptional or chromatin profiling and drug challenge. Because sibling cells share the heritable state, this gives a prospective map from measured molecular state to measured survival probability, rather than a retrospective comparison of survivors to a bulk pre-treatment population.

title: Cross-drug and cross-host reproducibility of surviving lineages
description: Barcode one population and split it across several different targeted agents and across multiple xenograft hosts, then determine whether the same barcodes recur among survivors. Convergence implies a single general primed state, while drug-specific and host-specific survivor sets imply a repertoire of distinct, context-matched states. These two outcomes would call for different therapeutic strategies.

title: Sibling-split profiling to read the survivor's pre-drug state
description: Barcode a population, let each cell divide a few times, then split each clone so that one half is drug-challenged and the matched half is profiled untreated by single-cell RNA-seq. Because barcodes link the two halves, the transcriptome of cells that would have survived can be read without exposing them to drug, separating pre-existing priming from drug-induced adaptation.

title: Fluctuation analysis to estimate switching rates into and out of the tolerant state
description: Expand many independent parallel cultures from small inocula, treat each identically, and analyze the variance in survivor counts across cultures using a Luria-Delbrück-style framework extended to reversible states. The shape of the distribution distinguishes a rare heritable mutation from a transient, interconverting state, and fitting it yields quantitative switching rates rather than just a qualitative claim of plasticity.

title: Prospective reporter sorting to test priming
description: Knock fluorescent reporters into the endogenous loci of candidate priming genes, sort live untreated cells from the top and bottom of the expression distribution, and challenge each fraction with drug. The fold-enrichment of survival in the reporter-high fraction converts a correlational signature into a predictive, quantitative measurement, and re-sorting after varying culture times measures how long the state is retained.

title: Continuous live imaging through drug addition with in situ molecular endpoints
description: Time-lapse image a sparse cell population from before drug exposure through survivor outgrowth, recording cell-cycle phase, size, division history, and neighbor context for every cell. At the end, perform in situ sequencing or multiplexed RNA FISH on the same field, so each survivor and each non-surviving neighbor is assigned a complete behavioral and molecular history, which bulk or dissociated methods cannot provide.

title: Screening on survivor frequency rather than survival
description: Run a CRISPR or small-molecule screen whose readout is the fraction of cells that enter the primed state, measured by a priming reporter or by the number of independent surviving colonies per starting cell, rather than overall viability. Perturbations that change the frequency without changing the identity of the resistant state point to upstream machinery that generates rare-cell variability, a target class that conventional viability screens tend to miss.

title: Split-population barcoding to read out the pre-treatment state of future survivors
description: Barcode a clonal population and split it into two plates so that each barcode is represented in both. Treat one plate and deeply profile the untreated plate by scRNA-seq. Because survivors are identified retrospectively by barcode, this directly reveals the transcriptional state the surviving cells were in before drug exposure, rather than the state of cells already altered by treatment.

title: Measure the memory half-life of the primed state
description: Sort cells in the putative primed state (by a FISH-based or reporter-based readout), re-plate them, and assay drug survival and marker expression at a series of time points as the sorted population returns toward baseline. The decay curve gives a quantitative switching rate that distinguishes a transient transcriptional fluctuation from a stably heritable epigenetic state.

title: Fluctuation analysis of survivor counts to infer switching rates
description: Grow many small parallel cultures from few cells, treat each identically, and count survivor colonies per culture. The shape of the variance across cultures (Luria-Delbrück style) discriminates rare irreversible events arising early in the lineage from fast reversible state-switching, and yields switching and reversion rates without molecular profiling.

title: Single-cell multiome test of chromatin priming before transcription
description: Perform joint ATAC and RNA profiling on untreated cells to determine whether regulatory regions of resistance-associated genes are already accessible in cells that have not yet upregulated those transcripts. A population with open chromatin but no transcript would identify a pre-primed intermediate compartment much larger than the eventual survivor fraction.

title: Spatial and conditioned-media tests for non-cell-autonomous survival
description: Image whether survivor colonies are spatially clustered more than expected by chance, and complement this with conditioned-media transfer and mixed co-culture of labeled sensitive cells. Together these separate cell-intrinsic priming from local paracrine protection or density effects, a confound rarely excluded in single-cell priming studies.

title: Decay of survival correlation between related cells by generational distance
description: Separate pairs of related cells at defined numbers of generations apart (via dilution cloning or imaging-tracked micro-colonies), treat one relative, and score the other's descendants. Measure how the survival correlation between relatives decays with generational distance, which gives a quantitative heritability half-life of the non-genetic state and distinguishes a state reset every cell cycle from one that persists for many divisions.

title: Cross-drug identity test with shared lineage barcodes
description: Barcode one population, split it into arms challenged with mechanistically distinct targeted agents, and test whether the surviving barcode sets overlap more than expected by chance. Strong overlap implies a general drug-tolerant state (slow cycling, apoptotic unpriming), while disjoint sets imply drug-specific priming such as pathway-specific expression.

title: Decomposing survival into death, division, and arrest
description: Use week-long live imaging with an apoptosis/caspase reporter and automated tracking to measure, per surviving lineage, the death rate, the division rate, and the duration of arrest under drug. This distinguishes cells that never engage apoptosis from cells that die more slowly and from cells that keep proliferating, which are often conflated in endpoint colony counts.

title: Separating state frequency from state-conditional survival in a modifier screen
description: Run a CRISPR or small-molecule modifier screen with two independent readouts: the fraction of cells entering the primed state (scored by a reporter or marker before treatment) and the survival probability conditional on being primed. Hits that change entry rate point to regulators that generate the rare state, while hits that change conditional survival point to effectors that execute it; a conventional resistance screen cannot distinguish these.

title: Per-cell drug exposure measurement to rule out differences in drug access
description: Measure intracellular drug levels cell by cell using a fluorescent drug analog, a target-engagement reporter, or mass-spec imaging, and correlate exposure with fate. This tests whether survivors differ in uptake, efflux, or local drug access rather than in signaling state. Any residual variation in fate after conditioning on exposure is a cleaner estimate of state-driven survival.

title: Profiling future survivors via sibling-cell splitting
description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into two dishes, and treat one with drug. Use the barcodes of the survivors to identify their untreated siblings in the other dish and sequence or image them. This directly measures the pre-treatment state of cells destined to survive, rather than inferring it from survivors after the drug has altered them.

title: Fluctuation analysis of subclone survivor variance to estimate memory timescale
description: Expand single cells into many sibling subclones, treat each, and compare the variance in survivor number against a Poisson expectation (Luria-Delbrück style). Repeating this with different expansion times converts the variance into an estimate of how many generations the survival-conferring state is inherited, separating a heritable epigenetic state from a purely instantaneous stochastic one.

title: Prospective sorting to test sufficiency of a candidate state
description: Use a live marker of the candidate primed state (surface protein stain or a knock-in reporter) to sort the rare high-marker cells before any drug exposure, then measure their survival frequency against marker-low and unsorted cells. Enrichment that falls far short of the marker's purity would show the state is necessary but not sufficient, pointing to a second required factor.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming measurement
description: Apply BH3 profiling or a single-cell cytochrome c release assay before treatment to measure how close each cell is to the apoptotic threshold. This tests whether survivors are not signaling outliers but cells with more buffered mitochondria, an explanation that transcriptomics alone would miss.

title: Cross-drug barcode overlap of survivors
description: Split one barcoded population across several mechanistically distinct drugs and compare which barcodes appear among the survivors of each. Strong overlap would imply a general tolerant state such as slow cycling, while near-disjoint survivor sets would indicate many independent, pathway-specific primed states. The result bears on which combination therapies make sense.

title: Retrospective lineage barcoding with sister-cell profiling
description: Label cells with expressed barcodes, let them divide, then split the population. Treat one half with drug and profile the untreated sister cells by scRNA-seq/ATAC-seq to find the molecular state that existed before treatment in cells whose lineages went on to survive.

title: Measuring the duration of the primed state
description: Use FACS to isolate cells high or low for a priming marker such as EGFR or NGFR. Track their marker levels with smFISH and their drug survival over successive divisions to estimate how long the state persists and how often cells switch in and out of it. This shows whether survival depends on a short-lived fluctuation or on a stable memory across many generations.

title: Sister-cell fate concordance by live imaging
description: Track sister and cousin cells by time-lapse imaging during treatment, using signaling (ERK KTR) and cell-cycle (CDK2/p21) reporters. Measure how often related cells share the same fate and which pre-treatment reporter dynamics predict survival.

title: CRISPR screens for regulators of priming frequency
description: Run pooled CRISPR screens that read out how often cells enter the primed state or how many resistant colonies form, rather than overall viability. This identifies genes that control how often rare surviving states arise, separate from genes that affect general fitness.

title: Multi-dose and multi-drug clone tracking
description: Expand barcoded populations and split them across several doses and several targeted drugs. Then measure whether the same barcoded clones survive under each condition. This shows whether surviving cells share one general tolerant state or several distinct states, each specific to a drug or dose.

title: Split-sibling barcode design to test heritable memory
description: Tag a population with heritable DNA barcodes and let it expand so each barcode is represented by many sibling cells. Split the population into several arms and treat them independently. If the same barcodes dominate survivors across arms, the surviving state was present and heritable before treatment; if survivor barcodes differ across arms, survival is largely a chance event occurring during treatment.

title: Retrospective imaging of the same cells before and after treatment
description: Image a sparse, position-registered untreated population with live reporters for candidate pathway activity, then add drug and return to the identical fields over days to link each cell's pre-treatment state to its fate. This avoids the usual problem that profiling methods destroy the cell whose outcome is to be determined.

title: Reversibility and re-treatment kinetics after a drug holiday
description: Expand survivors in drug-free medium for varying lengths of time, then re-treat and measure how the survivor fraction changes. A return toward the original low frequency indicates a transient, reversible state with a measurable relaxation time, while persistent high resistance indicates genetic or stably epigenetic change.

title: Single-cell apoptotic threshold versus signaling output
description: In the same untreated cells, measure both proximity to the apoptotic threshold (for example by peptide-induced mitochondrial permeabilization) and drug-target pathway output. This distinguishes survivors that are genuinely drug-insensitive from those that receive full target inhibition but are harder to kill.

title: Tuning the state-switching rate to test causality
description: Use chromatin-modifying perturbations or controlled expression noise to raise or lower the rate at which cells enter the rare drug-tolerant state, then measure whether survivor frequency changes correspondingly. This turns a correlative observation about rare states into a causal test and suggests interventions that reduce the pool of survivors.

title: Sister-cell splitting across a delay series to time the fate decision
description: Split each cell's progeny into a treated arm and an untreated arm after delays of 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 divisions (using heritable barcodes plus imaging to track the splits), then measure how well one sister's fate predicts the other's as a function of delay. This directly measures whether fate is pre-encoded and for how long that information persists; a predictability curve that decays to chance within one division would indicate the decision is made during treatment, not before.

title: Neighbor ablation to test the role of the local niche
description: Image survival in situ without replating, and record each cell's local density and neighbor identity. Test causality by selectively killing or silencing defined neighbor subsets (inducible caspase or optogenetic ablation in a mixed co-culture) and by transferring conditioned medium from candidate protective neighborhoods. This tests whether survival is conferred by the local niche rather than by the cell's intrinsic state, going beyond correlational spatial description.

title: Single-cell DNA and mtDNA sequencing of survivors to test genetic identity
description: Run matched single-cell whole-genome sequencing (copy-number variation and aneuploidy) and mtDNA heteroplasmy sequencing on the parental population and on drug survivors from the same barcoded lineages, so that lineage identity distinguishes pre-existing variants from treatment-induced ones. If survivors are enriched for particular karyotypes or mtDNA variants already present at low frequency, the apparent non-genetic heterogeneity in that system is partly attributable to genetics.

title: Per-cell measurement of intracellular drug dose and target inhibition
description: Use a fluorescent or clickable drug analog (validated against the parent compound) plus live efflux-activity reporters and a fixed-cell target-engagement/phospho-signaling readout to quantify intracellular drug level and target inhibition in every cell, then relate these to cell fate. This tests whether identical treatment results in equal exposure at the single-cell level and whether apparent state heterogeneity is downstream of exposure heterogeneity.

title: Decomposing survival into sequential stages by continuous long-term imaging
description: Follow every founder cell by continuous imaging from drug addition through weeks of persistence and regrowth, scoring death, arrest, continued cycling, and re-entry into proliferation as separate events, and fit predictors to each transition independently. This replaces a single binary endpoint with a staged model and can show that early tolerance and late outgrowth are governed by different, even anticorrelated, cell properties, and that averaging across survivors conflates distinct routes.

title: Sister-cell splitting at increasing delays before treatment
description: Split pairs of sister cells at defined intervals before treatment (0, 1, 3, 7, 14 days of regrowth) and measure how concordance of survival between sisters decays with separation time. This gives the autocorrelation timescale of the resistant state and the residual fraction of fate that is random after drug exposure. It directly tests whether survival is predetermined and heritable. Clone-level (MemorySeq-style) profiling then identifies transcripts that fluctuate on the measured timescale.

title: Neighborhood-resolved survivor mapping with mixing and conditioned-medium controls
description: Live-image a labeled monolayer through treatment and test whether each survivor's local density, contact number, and spatial position at the time of dosing predict survival better than its own pre-drug reporter intensity. Follow with low- versus high-density plating, transwell or conditioned-medium transfer, and mixing of color-coded populations to separate paracrine or neighborhood-mediated protection from intrinsic cell state.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target engagement
description: Quantify how much drug each cell receives and what it does there, using a fluorescent drug analog or single-cell mass spectrometry/MALDI imaging for intracellular concentration, efflux-pump activity dyes, and a live pathway reporter such as an ERK kinase-translocation reporter. This tests whether survivors are simply cells with lower drug load or incomplete pathway shutoff rather than carriers of a distinct resistance program.

title: Single-cell genome, CNV, and mtDNA profiling of survivors versus pre-treatment cells
description: Perform single-cell WGS/low-pass CNV analysis plus mtDNA heteroplasmy calling on survivors and on a size-matched sample of the pre-treatment population, combined with high-complexity DNA barcoding to distinguish rare pre-existing genetic subclones from epigenetically fluctuating states. The key test is whether survivors are enriched for a variant already present, at the predicted frequency, before treatment.

title: Forcing the candidate state on and off, with retrospective lineage validation
description: Use inducible CRISPRa/CRISPRi or a degron to drive the candidate state in a tunable fraction of cells before dosing and measure whether survival probability tracks induced expression level quantitatively, establishing causality rather than correlation. Validate in the reverse direction with a Rewind barcode scheme that recovers the actual pre-treatment ancestors of eventual survivors and profiles them directly, instead of inferring their state from bulk survivor averages.

title: Sister-cell fate correlation decay over time
description: Separate sister cells (by imaging, or by barcoding followed by replicate splitting) and add drug at staggered intervals after division. Measure how the correlation in sister fates decays with elapsed time. Rapid decay implies a short-lived fluctuating state and bounds how much of the outcome is determined before treatment versus during it.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and target occupancy
description: Use a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spec imaging plus a live target-occupancy reporter (e.g., a pathway phospho-reporter or NanoBRET-style binding readout) to quantify intracellular drug concentration and inhibition depth in every cell before fate is known. Test whether survivors are simply the cells that received or retained the least drug, which would indicate that the apparent resistant state reflects efflux, uptake, or cell volume differences rather than a distinct cell state.

title: Controlled-neighborhood survival mapping
description: Use micropatterning or defined seeding densities, plus mixing of labeled cells at varying ratios, to measure survival probability as a function of local neighbor number and identity, with conditioned-media and transwell swaps to separate contact from secreted signals. This quantifies how much of the surviving fraction is explained by microenvironmental position rather than internal cell state.

title: Testing genetic heritability of rare survival with replicate-split barcode lineages
description: Barcode a population, split it into many independent replicate cultures, treat each, and ask whether the same barcodes survive reproducibly across splits. Pair this with single-cell DNA/CNV and mitochondrial heteroplasmy profiling of survivors. Perfect cross-replicate reproducibility implicates fixed genetic or stably heritable differences, while partial reproducibility quantifies a heritable-but-reversible component.

title: Sufficiency testing by imposing candidate states before treatment
description: Take states enriched in survivors and impose them prospectively using CRISPRa/CRISPRi or inducible expression of candidate drivers, or sort live cells on a reporter of the state and re-plate them. Then measure whether the surviving fraction shifts as predicted. A dose-response between imposed state level and survival probability would turn a descriptive signature into a causal, quantitative claim.

title: Split-clone assay with variable delay between profiling and treatment
description: Expand single cells into clones and split each clone into a profiled half and a drug-treated half. Measure how well the profiled half's state predicts the treated half's survival as a function of the delay between splitting and treatment. This tests whether survival is pre-determined, measures the memory timescale of the fate-determining state, and distinguishes heritable priming from a stochastic decision at the time of treatment.

title: Genome and mitochondrial genotyping of barcoded survivors
description: Barcode the population, then deep-sequence whole genomes, single-cell CNV/ecDNA copy number, and mtDNA heteroplasmy in survivor colonies versus matched pre-treatment sisters of the same barcode lineage. This drops the assumption of genetic identity and tests whether a 'non-genetic' persister phenotype co-segregates with cryptic structural, ecDNA, or mitochondrial variation.

title: Density- and neighbor-controlled survival mapping with causal perturbations
description: Seed cells on micropatterns or in microwells at defined local densities and neighbor genotypes, and image survival as a function of each cell's measured local neighborhood. Swap conditioned media or laser-ablate neighbors to test causality, quantifying how much of the rare-survivor probability is set by local context and paracrine signaling rather than by the cell itself.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and apoptotic-threshold measurement
description: Combine a fluorescent drug analog or MALDI mass-spectrometry imaging of intracellular drug with efflux-pump activity reporters, single-cell target-occupancy readouts (phospho-signaling by iterative immunofluorescence), and dynamic BH3 profiling of mitochondrial priming. This tests whether survivors differ in the dose they actually receive and in the death threshold they must cross, rather than in cellular identity.

title: Long-term fate classification by continuous imaging before retrospective profiling
description: Image thousands of cells continuously for weeks through treatment and regrowth to classify every outcome (immediate death, divide-then-die, arrest-then-resume, senescence escape, polyploidization), then retrieve and profile cells from each class separately. This avoids a binary survivor label and tests whether several mechanistically distinct routes to survival are being pooled together.

title: Separating genetic from non-genetic survival with barcoded replicate populations, single-cell DNA sequencing, and ecDNA analysis
description: Label a population with high-complexity heritable barcodes, split it into replicate flasks, and test whether the same barcodes survive drug in independent replicates (heritable/genetic) or different ones each time (transient state). In addition, perform deep whole-genome sequencing of pre-treatment single-cell-derived clones, single-cell DNA-seq, and ecDNA FISH on the untreated population to quantify how much of the rare-survivor fraction is explained by cryptic mutations or amplifications rather than by non-genetic state.

title: Retrospective profiling of pre-treatment cells destined to survive
description: Identify the barcodes enriched in survivors, then return to an archived, never-treated aliquot of the same barcoded population and physically recover those specific cells using barcode-targeted probes or barcode-driven reporters, so their transcriptome, protein, and chromatin state can be measured before any drug exposure. This separates the causal priming state from the reprogramming that drug treatment imposes on survivors.

title: Live per-cell drug exposure, target inhibition, and apoptotic priming linked to fate
description: Measure in each cell the intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging), degree of target inhibition (live kinase-activity or signaling biosensors such as ERK/AKT reporters), efflux-pump activity, and mitochondrial apoptotic priming by single-cell dynamic BH3 profiling. Then time-lapse track the same cells to death or survival. This tests whether rare survival reflects heterogeneous pharmacology and death-threshold setting rather than a transcriptional resistance program.

title: Neighborhood-controlled survival assay to isolate the cell-autonomous component
description: Compare survival frequency for cells seeded as isolated singletons in microwells or micropatterns versus matched cells in dense colonies, swap conditioned media, and use time-lapse imaging plus spatial transcriptomics to score each survivor's local density, contact history, and position within a colony. Cross-mixing differentially labeled populations then reveals whether a surviving cell confers or receives protection, distinguishing an intrinsic primed state from a locally created protective niche.

title: Timescale, heritability, and causal sufficiency of the pre-existing tolerant state
description: Build a live reporter of a candidate marker of the tolerant state and track lineages for weeks. Compute sister, cousin, and aunt correlation decay and state-switching rates to obtain the memory half-life and determine whether the state is discrete or continuous. Then sort marker-high cells, let them re-equilibrate for varying times before dosing to measure how quickly the survival advantage decays, and force the state on or off with inducible CRISPRa/CRISPRi to test whether it is causally sufficient rather than merely correlated.

title: Testing genetic explanations for survival
description: Perform matched single-cell whole-genome and mitochondrial sequencing on survivors versus naive cells, with attention to extrachromosomal DNA and focal copy-number gains at the drug target and its bypass pathways, using FISH or CUT&RUN on the same cells where possible. This tests the premise that the cells are genetically identical and quantifies how much survival is attributable to rare pre-existing genetic or ecDNA heterogeneity rather than cell state.

title: Sister-cell split design to separate pre-existing state from drug-induced change
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes or physical separation of daughter cells so that one sister is profiled molecularly while the other is exposed to drug and its fate recorded, testing whether the pre-drug state predicts the sister's outcome. Varying the delay between the split and treatment also measures how long the predisposing state persists, distinguishing a heritable primed state from transient fluctuation or drug-induced adaptation.

title: Neighborhood-resolved survival and causal density perturbation
description: Track survival by long-term live imaging with single-cell segmentation, then model each cell's outcome as a function of its local neighbor count, neighbor identity, and contact history, rather than only its own features. Follow with causal tests, such as micropatterned colonies of defined size, conditioned-media transfer, and co-culture with labeled sensitive cells, to see whether survival is conferred by neighbors instead of residing in the cell itself.

title: Clustering survivors into subsets and testing each subset's dependencies
description: Cluster survivors by multimodal single-cell profiling and treat the clusters as competing hypotheses, assigning each a candidate dependency and testing them in parallel with a pooled CRISPR screen performed under drug with a single-cell readout. If distinct survivor subsets have non-overlapping genetic dependencies, that falsifies a single-mechanism model and indicates several mechanisms sharing one phenotype.

title: Measuring the dose each cell actually received
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target engagement directly, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, mass spectrometry imaging, efflux-pump reporters, and live biosensors of the targeted signaling node. This tests whether survivors differ in pathway state at all, or only in pharmacology, and would explain apparent resistance as a difference in exposure rather than in cell identity.

title: Testing for genetic differences before invoking non-genetic plasticity
description: Run single-cell whole-genome sequencing plus ecDNA-sensitive assays (FISH, Circle-seq) on matched pre-treatment, survivor, and dying populations from the same isogenic culture. Test whether survivors are enriched for pre-existing CNVs, ecDNA copy number, or subclonal variants. This directly tests the premise that the cells are genetically identical and establishes what fraction of survival requires a non-genetic explanation.

title: Per-cell measurement of intracellular drug concentration and target engagement
description: Quantify intracellular drug concentration and target engagement per cell, using fluorescent or clickable drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, or a CETSA/NanoBRET-style occupancy reporter, jointly with survival outcome in the same cells. This tests whether pharmacokinetic factors (efflux-pump activity, lysosomal sequestration, or uptake variation producing sub-lethal exposure in a few cells) determine survival, rather than the RNA-level states usually measured.

title: Neighborhood-controlled survival mapping
description: Use micropatterned islands, defined co-culture ratios, and conditioned-medium swaps to vary each cell's local density and neighbor identity while holding genotype constant. Score survival as a function of neighborhood with live imaging, and test whether survival probability depends more on measured local context than on any cell-intrinsic marker.

title: Live imaging of a primed-state reporter linked to later sequencing
description: Continuously image cells carrying a reporter for the candidate primed state (e.g., a knock-in of a resistance-associated gene) from before drug addition through outcome, then retrieve individual cells for sequencing via in situ transcriptomics or Live-seq. This reveals whether the state pre-exists, how fast it fluctuates relative to the treatment window, and whether survivors were already in the state at t=0 or entered it stochastically afterward, which destructive snapshot measurements cannot distinguish.

title: Sufficiency test by synthetic state induction
description: Use inducible CRISPRa/CRISPRi or degron systems to impose the candidate survivor state in a tunable fraction of cells before treatment, and test whether the surviving fraction shifts quantitatively as predicted. This converts a correlative signature into a causal test; failure to shift survival would indicate the signature is a consequence or bystander rather than a driver.

title: Clone-splitting assay to partition survival variance
description: Using heritable expressed barcodes or physical splitting of small clones, treat one half of each clone and profile or re-challenge the other half. Quantify how much of survival probability is shared within a lineage versus private to each cell, and how fast the shared component decays over passages. This directly measures whether priming is a stable pre-existing property or a short-lived fluctuation.

title: Single-cell genome and ecDNA analysis of survivors
description: Run single-cell whole-genome sequencing plus DNA FISH for ecDNA and target-locus copy number on parental and surviving cells, with duplex sequencing of the drug target to detect mutations below 0.1% allele frequency. This tests whether the 'genetically identical' premise is false and whether rare copy-number or ecDNA high-copy cells, rather than transcriptional states, account for survival.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug dosimetry
description: Measure the actual drug concentration each cell receives using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, mass-spectrometry imaging, or a live target-engagement reporter, combined with per-cell efflux-pump activity, and correlate it with fate by live imaging. If survival tracks drug exposure rather than transcriptional state, expression-based explanations are confounded by pharmacology.

title: Neighborhood-controlled survival mapping
description: Micropattern or seed cells at defined local densities, image the full field during treatment, and model each cell's survival as a function of its own state versus the number, proximity, and death timing of its neighbors. Complement this with conditioned-medium and apoptotic-debris transfer experiments. This tests whether survival is cell-autonomous or depends on the local microenvironment and signals from dying neighbors.

title: Forced-state causal test with graded fate readout
description: Use CRISPRa/CRISPRi or an inducible/optogenetic construct to drive candidate primed-state genes in a titratable fraction of cells before treatment, and test whether the surviving fraction shifts proportionally. Score outcome not as live/dead but as a continuous live-imaging trajectory (death, arrest, dormancy, proliferation). This tests the state causally with a dose-response and resolves whether survivors are one population or several.

title: Cross-dataset meta-analysis of pre-resistant transcriptional states
description: Harmonize dozens of public pre-treatment scRNA-seq datasets across melanoma/BRAFi, lung/EGFR-TKI, breast/CDK4-6i and leukemia, and test whether the rare primed high-expressing subpopulations (AXL, NGFR, EGFR-high) reflect one shared program or lineage- and drug-specific ones. This distinguishes a universal priming axis from idiosyncratic per-model heterogeneity.

title: Reanalysis of public lineage-barcoding data for heritability and memory duration
description: Public Watermelon, ClonMapper, TraCe-seq, Rewind and CellTag datasets contain sister- and cousin-cell relationships that allow survival to be partitioned into heritable clonal and stochastic components. Fitting a state-switching model yields the number of generations a primed state persists, a quantity rarely extracted in the original papers.

title: Fluctuation analysis of published clonal outgrowth data
description: Apply fluctuation-test statistics to replicate-well colony counts reported after targeted-drug treatment to estimate the rate at which cells enter the drug-tolerant state. The shape of the across-well count distribution is used to distinguish heritable genetic mutation from reversible epigenetic switching.

title: DepMap/PRISM modeling of residual viability rather than IC50
description: Extract the dose-response plateau, i.e. the fraction surviving at saturating drug, across roughly a thousand cell lines in PRISM and GDSC, then regress it on baseline CCLE expression, methylation, chromatin and copy-number features. This identifies determinants of a large persister fraction that are independent of average drug sensitivity.

title: Benchmarking in vitro persister signatures against patient residual disease
description: Score published on-treatment and minimal-residual-disease patient biopsies (scRNA-seq cohorts in GEO, plus deconvolved TRACERx/TCGA bulk data) against cell-line-derived persister signatures. This shows which laboratory persister programs are present in patients after therapy and which are culture artifacts.

title: Fluctuation analysis with split sister clones
description: Grow many small clonal populations from single cells, split each into sister wells, and treat them with drug. Compare the variance in resistant-colony counts within sister pairs and between clones to distinguish a heritable pre-existing state (large colony-count differences between clones that sisters share, as in Luria–Delbrück fluctuation tests) from stochastic or drug-induced survival. Estimate how long the state lasts by varying the time before splitting (about $3–5k in plates, drug and imaging).

title: Barcoded sister-cell lineage tracing to capture survivors' pre-drug state
description: Label cells with a lentiviral barcode library, let them divide a few times, then split them so sister cells end up in both halves. Treat one half, sequence the barcodes of the survivors, and profile the untreated sisters with the same barcodes using targeted barcode capture plus one small single-cell RNA-seq run, to see which expression programs mark future survivors before any drug exposure (about $12–18k).

title: Multiplexed smFISH/HCR counts of rare primed cells before and during treatment
description: In thousands of untreated cells and along a fixed time course of drug treatment, image transcript counts of 10–20 candidate resistance genes (e.g., AXL, EGFR, NGFR, WNT5A, SOX10). This shows whether a rare subpopulation co-expressing several markers exists beforehand, how often it occurs, and whether its frequency matches the surviving fraction (about $4–8k in probes and reagents, using existing microscopes).

title: Live-cell imaging of signaling and cell-cycle history before drug addition
description: Express an ERK/AKT kinase-activity reporter and FUCCI cell-cycle markers and film cells for 1–2 days before and 3–5 days after drug addition. Track each cell's lineage to test whether survival is predicted by earlier signaling pulses, cell-cycle phase, quiescence, or inheritance from the mother cell (about $3–6k).

title: Sorting and perturbation tests of candidate survival states
description: Use FACS to sort the top and bottom ~1% of cells for candidate markers, and separately knock down or overexpress the candidate regulators with siRNA, CRISPRi or a small pooled guide library. Then count resistant colonies to test whether the marked state causes survival rather than merely correlating with it (about $5–10k).

title: Track lineages before treatment, then trace survivors back
description: Film cells for several generations before adding the drug, keep imaging through treatment, then trace every surviving cell back through its lineage tree. Compare how often sisters and cousins of survivors also survive, to show whether survival is a heritable pre-existing state, how many generations that memory lasts, and how this compares with a random or drug-induced event.

title: Testing whether pre-drug signaling or post-drug rebound predicts survival
description: Express multiplexed kinase translocation reporters (for example ERK, AKT and JNK KTRs) and quantify each cell's baseline pathway activity and pulse dynamics before the drug, plus how quickly signaling recovers after it. Then test whether a high baseline or a fast rebound of bypass signaling predicts which cells survive.

title: Live reporters of a primed state to measure switching
description: Knock fluorescent tags or MS2/PP7 tags into endogenous genes linked to rare resistant states (for example AXL, EGFR, NGFR, or loss of SOX10) and image their fluctuations over days. This gives the rate at which cells enter and leave the high-expressing state, and shows whether cells that are in or entering that state when the drug is added are the ones that survive.

title: Cell-cycle state at the time of drug addition
description: Use FUCCI and a CDK2/CDK4/6 activity sensor to record each cell's cycle phase and proliferation commitment when the drug is added. This tests whether survivors come from cells already in spontaneous quiescence (CDK2-low) rather than from drug-induced arrest, and tracks how and when they re-enter the cell cycle to form resistant colonies.

title: Predicting survivors from label-free imaging and neighborhood context
description: Train a model on pre-drug, label-free features (morphology, motility, nuclear texture), live dyes for mitochondrial membrane potential and ROS, and spatial neighborhood data (local density, distance to other future survivors). This shows how early survivors can be identified and whether survival depends on the cell's own state, its metabolism, or its surroundings.

title: Live imaging followed by in situ spatial transcriptomics of the same cells
description: Continuously image a dish of cells for days before and during drug exposure, recording each cell's growth rate, morphology, division history, and position. Then fix the same dish and run in situ spatial transcriptomics so each imaged cell has a molecular profile. Because cell identity is preserved, you can retrospectively determine which measurable features, hours or days earlier, predicted whether a cell died or persisted.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and target-engagement mapping
description: Measure how much drug each cell accumulates and how completely its target is inhibited, using a fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging together with single-cell phospho-signaling readouts by mass cytometry or quantitative immunofluorescence across doses and times. This separates survivors with less inhibited target (due to uptake, efflux, or sequestration) from survivors whose target is fully inhibited but whose downstream signaling and apoptotic machinery still keep them alive.

title: Persistence of the resistant state after drug withdrawal
description: Isolate survivors, let them expand without drug for a graded series of recovery times, and re-challenge equal numbers at each time point while profiling chromatin accessibility and transcription in parallel. The rate at which the enriched survival fraction and its associated chromatin state revert to baseline quantifies how long the non-genetic resistant state is retained and whether it is a stable alternative state or a transient one.

title: Time-resolved single-cell multiome for pre-existing versus induced survivor states
description: Profile joint RNA and chromatin accessibility in the same single cells at a dense series of time points spanning untreated, early killing, and established persistence, then search the untreated population for rare cells whose state already resembles the survivors. Finding such cells before treatment supports selection of a pre-existing state; their absence, with accessibility changes emerging only after drug, supports induction and adaptation.

title: Mapping the non-genetic context that sets survival odds
description: Systematically vary context without altering the genome: local cell density and neighbor contact, conditioned-medium transfer, nutrient and oxygen levels, matrix stiffness, and cell-cycle position scored by EdU incorporation and DNA content at the time of drug addition. Quantify how each factor shifts the survivor fraction and the spatial clustering of survivors. This shows how much rare survival is a property of a cell's environment and division state rather than of the cell alone.

title: Split-population barcode test in zebrafish melanoma transplants
description: Label ZMEL1 zebrafish melanoma cells with a high-complexity heritable barcode library, split the expanded population into replicate arms, and treat each with BRAF/MEK inhibition: shared survivor barcodes across arms indicate a pre-existing heritable state, while non-overlapping survivors indicate stochastic or transient origins. Varying the delay between splitting and treatment measures how many generations the survival-conferring state persists.

title: Retrospective isolation of primed cells before drug in a canine mast cell tumor line
description: In a KIT-driven canine mast cell tumor line treated with toceranib, use an RNA-detectable expressed barcode. Barcodes enriched among survivors can be found by hybridization in an untreated sister population. This allows the rare cells that would have survived to be sorted and profiled by scRNA-seq while still drug-naive. This measures the primed state itself rather than the post-treatment state, a common confound in persister profiling.

title: Live signaling-dynamics tracking with optogenetic testing of causality
description: Image ERK-KTR and AKT biosensors in rat or canine tumor cells for many hours before drug addition and follow each cell's fate, regressing pre-drug pulse frequency, amplitude, and duration against survival. Then use optogenetic ERK activation to impose the candidate dynamic pattern and test whether it is sufficient to generate survivors.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement to exclude pharmacokinetic differences
description: Quantify fluorescent drug-analog uptake, efflux-pump reporter activity, and a target-engagement readout in individual survivors versus dying neighbors in canine or rat lines. This distinguishes genuine cell-state heterogeneity from cells that simply received or retained less drug, a control rarely done at single-cell resolution.

title: Intravital imaging of survivor niches in Drosophila and zebrafish tumors
description: Image labeled tumor cells through treatment in living Drosophila Ras/scrib tumors or zebrafish transplants, scoring survivor position relative to vasculature, hemocytes/macrophages, and surrounding stroma. Genetic ablation of the implicated host cell type then tests whether the local niche causes survival rather than merely correlating with it.

title: Split-replicate clonal barcoding to test heritability of survival
description: Barcode a drug-sensitive cancer line lentivirally at low MOI, expand briefly, split the population into replicate arms treated identically with the targeted drug, and sequence barcodes in the survivors. The degree to which the same barcodes survive across replicates quantifies how much survival is driven by a heritable, pre-existing cell state versus chance at the time of treatment, and the time over which splits stop agreeing gives the memory half-life of that state.

title: Prospective sorting on candidate priming markers
