description: Use scRNA-seq of the untreated population to nominate markers of rare cells whose products are cell-surface or reporter-accessible. FACS-sort marker-high and marker-low fractions from drug-naive cells, treat both, and count colonies. If the marker defines the primed state, survival frequency should be strongly enriched in the marker-high fraction, giving a prospective causal test of the correlative signature.

title: Continuous live imaging across the treatment boundary
description: Image a sparsely plated, nuclear-labeled population for 2-3 days before drug addition and for a week after, so each survivor can be traced back to its own pre-drug history of division rate, cell-cycle phase at dosing, size, motility, and signaling-reporter level. This tests whether survivors are distinguished by quiescence, cell-cycle timing, or a transcriptional reporter state before the drug is added.

title: Washout and rechallenge kinetics to time resistance memory
description: Isolate drug survivors, culture them without drug for a graded series of durations (days to weeks), and re-challenge at each timepoint to measure how fast the surviving fraction decays to the naive baseline. Reversible, gradually decaying resistance implicates a non-genetic, epigenetically maintained state, whereas stable resistance points to a fixed genetic or permanently rewired cause.

title: Paired multiome and clonal genotyping of survivors versus naive cells
description: Run single-cell RNA plus ATAC on matched naive, early-persister, and late-resistant populations. In parallel, do low-coverage single-cell or bulk whole-genome copy-number analysis and targeted driver sequencing on the same samples. This separates chromatin and expression reprogramming from selection of a pre-existing genetic subclone, and identifies which transcription-factor motifs gain accessibility before expression changes appear.

title: Split-population barcoding with pre-treatment profiling of one half
description: Tag cells with heritable expressed barcodes, expand briefly, then divide the population into two matched halves; profile one half once by single-cell RNA+ATAC with no drug, and sequence barcodes once in the treated half at the endpoint. Barcodes shared between survivors and their untreated sister cells reveal which pre-existing expression and chromatin states confer survival, with each sample read out exactly once.

title: Fluctuation-test variance analysis for heritable priming
description: Seed many independent clonal cultures, grow them for varying numbers of doublings, treat each once, and count surviving colonies a single time per culture. The shape and variance of the survivor-count distribution across cultures distinguishes a heritable primed state from independent per-cell random survival, and bounds how many generations that state is retained.

title: Sort on a rare-state reporter, then score survival at one endpoint
description: Use multiplexed RNA imaging on fixed untreated cells to define the rare co-expression state (for example high AXL/NGFR/EGFR), build a live reporter or antibody panel for it, and sort high versus low cells. Treat each sorted fraction and count colonies at a single endpoint to directly quantify the fold enrichment in survival probability attributable to that state.

title: Genomic recorders of past signaling activity
description: Express CRISPR base- or prime-editing recorders driven by pathway-responsive promoters (MAPK, NF-kB, AP-1) so each cell writes its signaling history into its own DNA. A single-cell sequencing readout taken once after treatment recovers each survivor's cumulative upstream pathway activity, giving a retrospective time course from a single measurement.

title: Endpoint Perturb-seq on survivors versus the starting pool
description: Introduce a genome-wide or focused CRISPR library, treat the population, and perform single-cell CRISPR sequencing once on the surviving cells, comparing guide abundance and transcriptomes against a one-time profile of the untreated library. This identifies genes whose loss or gain changes survival odds and the transcriptional programs those perturbations act through.

title: Lineage-barcoded patient-derived organoids split into untreated and treated arms
description: Barcode a patient-derived organoid or PDX line at high complexity, split it into an untreated reference arm and a drug-treated arm, and test whether the surviving barcodes are reproducibly the same across replicate splits. Reproducible survivors indicate a heritable pre-existing state, while random survivors indicate stochastic induction, and the untreated arm allows direct profiling of survivor ancestors before drug exposure.

title: Serial pre-treatment, on-treatment, and progression biopsies at single-cell resolution
description: Collect matched biopsies from the same patients at baseline, at the residual-disease nadir 2-4 weeks into targeted therapy, and at relapse, and profile all three by single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. The residual-disease timepoint is the only direct view of persister cells in a human tumor and reveals whether the persister program pre-exists in a rare subpopulation or appears only under drug.

title: Spatial mapping of residual disease in on-treatment biopsies
description: Use imaging-based spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed protein imaging on on-treatment patient biopsies to determine whether surviving cells occupy non-random positions such as perivascular, hypoxic, invasive-front, or CAF- and immune-protected niches. This distinguishes cell-intrinsic tolerance programs from microenvironment-provided protection, which have different therapeutic consequences.

title: Whole-genome and clonal phylogeny analysis of survivor populations
description: Perform deep whole-genome sequencing and single-cell copy-number profiling on matched pre-treatment and residual or relapse patient samples to test whether survivors carry pre-existing resistance mutations, subclonal expansions, or no genetic distinction. Reconstructing the clonal phylogeny establishes whether relapse derives from a genetically distinct clone or from genetically identical cells in a permissive transcriptional state.

title: Live ex vivo drug exposure of fresh malignant effusions and circulating tumor cells
description: Expose freshly isolated pleural effusion, ascites, or CTC-derived tumor cells from patients to the targeted agent under live-cell imaging, then sort survivors for matched single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic analysis. Repeat sampling from the same patient across multiple taps to test whether the tolerant state is stable and heritable or transient and reversible.

title: Allele-resolved readout of the rare high-expressing state
description: In a cell line with heterozygous SNPs (or an engineered dual-reporter knock-in at both alleles of a resistance driver such as AXL or NGFR), use allele-specific single-molecule FISH or nascent-transcript imaging to determine whether rare high-expressing cells activate one allele or both. Biallelic activation implicates an upstream trans/signaling fluctuation shared by the nucleus, whereas monoallelic activation implicates a cis-chromatin switch, narrowing the mechanistic search before any screening.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement as an alternative explanation
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy in single cells before scoring survival, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, a target-engagement readout (e.g., single-cell CETSA/thermal shift or a proximity reporter for the inhibited kinase), and live efflux-pump activity dyes. This tests whether survivors are under-dosed rather than transcriptionally distinct, and quantifies how much of the survivor fraction that alone explains.

title: Sort-and-relax kinetics with a transition-rate model and quantitative sufficiency test
description: Isolate the extreme tails of a live reporter for the candidate primed state by FACS, return them to drug-free culture, and track how the expression distribution relaxes back to steady state over days. Fit entry and exit rates of a two- or three-state Markov model. Then test whether these independently measured rates numerically predict the observed survivor frequency and the frequency after a defined pre-treatment delay. A mismatch would indicate that another determinant is involved.

title: Manipulating the rate of state entry without altering resistance genes
description: Vary only the cells' drug-free history (confluence, nutrient or hypoxic pulses, transient inhibition of specific chromatin writers/erasers, or enforced slow versus fast growth) and measure the resulting survivor frequency together with the abundance of primed cells. Conditions that shift survivor frequency severalfold while leaving bulk drug sensitivity unchanged would identify the upstream process that generates the rare state, as opposed to a downstream marker.

title: Spatial neighborhood mapping of survivors in fixed coordinates
description: Image the monolayer at the moment of drug addition to record each cell's local density, neighbor identities, and contact geometry, then re-image the same field after the main killing phase to locate survivors. Testing whether survivors are spatially clustered, preferentially arise at colony edges, or sit beside specific secreting neighbors distinguishes a cell-intrinsic primed state from locally produced paracrine protection. Conditioned-medium and sparse-versus-dense plating controls can then confirm the result.

title: Single-cell imaging of intracellular drug concentration
description: Synthesize an alkyne- or deuterium-tagged analog of the targeted inhibitor (or use its intrinsic fluorescence) and quantify intracellular drug concentration cell by cell with stimulated Raman scattering microscopy or MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging, at early timepoints and in the eventual survivors. This tests the rarely excluded hypothesis that persisters are cells with lower drug accumulation (from efflux, lipid-droplet sequestration, or lysosomal trapping) rather than cells in a distinct signaling state.

title: Allele-resolved smFISH to distinguish transcriptional bursting from a stable state
description: Use intron/exon and SNP-discriminating single-molecule FISH on candidate priming genes (e.g. AXL, NGFR, EGFR) in drug-naive cells to measure nascent transcription at each allele, then fit burst frequency, size, and duration. Monoallelic, short-lived bursts with uncorrelated alleles imply priming is transient transcriptional noise; coordinated biallelic activation persisting across the cell cycle implies an upstream heritable chromatin or signaling state. Bulk or standard scRNA-seq snapshots cannot make this distinction.

title: CRISPR screen scored on survivor clone diversity rather than survivor number
description: Barcode the library-infected population so every cell carries both a guide and a lineage barcode, then score each gene knockout by the barcode diversity (effective number of surviving clones) among survivors rather than by total survival. Genes that change the number of independent surviving clones while leaving bulk killing kinetics unchanged are regulators of state-switching rate, distinguishable from genes that shift intrinsic drug sensitivity.

title: Optogenetic induction of the putative primed state to test sufficiency
description: Use an optogenetic actuator of the candidate upstream node (e.g., opto-SOS or opto-Raf for frequency-encoded ERK, or a light-inducible dCas9 activator at a candidate priming locus) to drive the whole population into the putative primed state with defined pulse amplitude and frequency before adding drug. If priming is causal and rate-limiting, the persister fraction should rise toward 100% in a dose- and frequency-dependent way; failure to do so limits how much of survival the state explains.

title: Micropatterned neighborhoods and apoptotic-body addition
description: Plate cells on micropatterns that fix colony size, spacing, and neighbor number, and separately add purified apoptotic bodies or conditioned medium from drug-killed cells to sparse cultures. This makes neighbor density a controlled variable rather than a correlate and tests whether dying cells promote survival of neighbors via released factors, apoptosis-induced proliferation signals, or metabolite transfer, rather than survivors being intrinsically special.

title: Single-cell drug accumulation and target engagement
description: Measure how much drug each cell accumulates and how much target it engages, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, lysosomotropic and efflux-pump reporters, cell volume and dry mass from quantitative phase imaging, and a single-cell target-engagement readout (e.g., NanoBRET or a phospho-substrate immunofluorescence dose curve). Then test whether survivors are simply the cells that received the lowest effective dose, i.e., whether tolerance reflects pharmacokinetic heterogeneity (sequestration, efflux, surface-to-volume ratio, cell cycle–linked volume changes) rather than a primed regulatory state. This also sets a baseline that any molecular model must outperform.

title: Copy-number heterogeneity from extrachromosomal DNA and mis-segregation
description: Perform single-cell DNA sequencing plus DNA-FISH for the target gene and known resistance loci on untreated cells, survivors, and regrown colonies, scoring extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) copies, focal amplifications, and whole-chromosome aneuploidy per cell. Because ecDNA segregates randomly at mitosis and generates heritable, rapidly reversible dosage variation that could resemble epigenetic priming, quantify its distribution before treatment and whether survivors come from the upper tail, to determine whether the phenomenon is genomic before invoking chromatin explanations.

title: Spatial statistics and engineered context to test survival as a neighborhood property
description: Map the spatial coordinates of every survivor relative to local pre-treatment cell density, colony edge, and the positions of neighbors that died, testing for clustering beyond what clonal relatedness predicts. Then control these variables directly with micropatterned islands of defined size, transwell separation, and medium conditioned by drug-killed cells. This tests whether the surviving fraction is partly set by paracrine signals released during apoptosis and by local crowding, which single-cell dissociation-based assays would destroy, and whether survivor frequency can be tuned by plating geometry alone.

title: Apoptotic threshold and mitochondrial inheritance
description: Profile the cell death machinery at single-cell resolution: BH3-peptide-induced cytochrome c release or MOMP timing imaged live, together with per-cell mitochondrial mass, membrane potential, and BCL-2-family protein levels. Track how unevenly mitochondria and these proteins are partitioned between daughters at each division. If survivors come disproportionately from the daughter that inherited the less-primed mitochondrial pool, survival is a downstream execution threshold with a short, division-generated memory, which predicts that lowering the threshold with a BH3 mimetic reduces the surviving fraction without affecting any upstream pathway.

title: Tuning expression noise at fixed mean as a causal test
description: For a candidate determinant, build isogenic lines expressing it from synthetic promoters or degron/feedback circuits that give matched mean levels but different cell-to-cell variability, and titrate global noise modifiers as an orthogonal arm; then measure survivor frequency across the panel. Most causal follow-ups shift the average level of a factor, which cannot distinguish whether more of the factor helps from whether variability in the factor creates the rare surviving cells. This design separates the two, and predicts that survivor frequency should scale with the variance, not the mean.

title: Single-cell drug exposure and target occupancy as the null model
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent analog, MALDI or nanoSIMS imaging), efflux activity, and target engagement (NanoBRET or an in-cell occupancy reporter), then test whether survivors fall in the low-occupancy tail. This tests whether fractional survival reflects pharmacological heterogeneity in uptake, efflux, and target abundance rather than a distinct regulatory cell state.

title: Sister-pair concordance decay to estimate memory of the survival state
description: Reconstruct lineage trees by imaging up to the time of dosing and score survival concordance between sisters, cousins, and more distant relatives as a function of generations since their common ancestor, giving a model-free estimate of how long the predisposing state is inherited. Combine this with quantification of what is asymmetrically partitioned at those divisions (mitochondria, lysosomes, efflux pumps, protein aggregates) to identify the physical carrier of that memory.

title: Fluctuation tests to estimate state-switching rates
description: Run Luria-Delbrück-style experiments with many parallel small cultures expanded for different numbers of generations before treatment, and fit the variance structure of survivor counts to estimate forward and backward switching rates between tolerant and sensitive states. Using only colony counts, this distinguishes rare stochastic switching, continuously fluctuating traits, and pre-existing stable subclones, and produces rate constants that any mechanistic model must reproduce.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming as a prospective predictor of survival
description: Apply BH3 profiling (single-cell or on sorted fractions) to the naive population to measure how close each cell is to the mitochondrial death threshold. Prospectively sort on mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial mass, or sensitizer-peptide response before any drug exposure to test enrichment for survivors. This tests whether survival is set by the apoptotic machinery's threshold rather than by target-pathway signaling or transcriptional identity.

title: Testing local cellular context as a determinant of survival
description: Image the local context of every cell at the time of dosing (local density, contact number, neighbor identity, distance to colony edge) and regress survival on these variables. Then manipulate context directly with micropatterned colonies of defined size, density-matched seeding, and conditioned-medium or transwell swaps. If local secreted factors or cell contact confer survival, cell-autonomous profiling would recover only correlates of position rather than causes.

title: Single-cell intracellular drug exposure measurement
description: Quantify per-cell drug concentration directly using mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI/nanoSIMS), a clickable or intrinsically fluorescent drug analog, and efflux-activity dyes in treated cultures, then correlate exposure with fate. This tests whether survivors are cells that simply accumulated less compound, ruling in or out a pharmacokinetic explanation that transcriptome-focused studies often skip.

title: Fluctuation analysis to measure the memory timescale of the primed state
description: Seed many replicate microcultures from small inocula, expand each for a different number of generations before identical treatment, and fit the across-well variance in survivor counts to a fluctuation model. The dependence of variance on expansion time yields a quantitative heritability timescale for the primed state using only colony counts, without sequencing.

title: Pulse labeling to separate active maintenance from passive carryover
description: Combine 4sU/SLAM-seq with pulsed SILAC on sorted persisters and bulk cells to decompose their distinctive profile into newly synthesized versus inherited, slowly degraded mRNA and protein. This distinguishes an actively transcribed regulatory program from passive inheritance of long-lived molecules, which imply different intervention points.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
description: Adapt dynamic BH3 profiling to imaging or flow cytometry at single-cell resolution to measure mitochondrial depolarization responses to BH3 peptides before and shortly after dosing, linking priming state to subsequent survival. Apoptotic threshold is the proximate determinant of cell death or survival and is largely not visible at the RNA level.

title: Asymmetric organelle partitioning at mitosis as the origin of fate divergence
description: In sister-pair live imaging, quantify unequal inheritance of mitochondria, lysosomes, and damaged-protein aggregates at each division, then follow both daughters through treatment. This tests whether survival originates in random physical partitioning at cytokinesis rather than in a stable transcriptional program.

title: Non-genetic Luria–Delbrück fluctuation analysis
description: Seed many parallel small cultures from few cells, expand them for varying numbers of generations, then treat each independently and count survivors, analyzing the across-culture variance-to-mean ratio rather than the mean. The shape of the distribution and its dependence on pre-treatment expansion time gives the state-switching rate and distinguishes pre-existing heritable priming from drug-induced conversion using only colony counts, without molecular profiling or assumptions about which genes matter.

title: Per-cell drug exposure and target engagement as the first explanatory variable
description: Measure intracellular drug concentration in single cells (fluorescent drug analog, efflux-substrate dye, or mass-spectrometry imaging) together with a direct target-occupancy readout such as NanoBRET or a proximal phospho-reporter, in the same cells whose fate is later scored. This tests whether survivors are simply cells that received or retained less drug, and quantifies how much fate variance remains after pharmacological heterogeneity is accounted for.

title: Promoter series varying expression noise at constant mean
description: Build a panel of synthetic or edited promoters driving a candidate tolerance gene that differ in transcriptional burst size and frequency while matching population-mean expression, then measure survivor frequency across the panel. If survival scales with variance at fixed mean, fluctuation-generated rare states are causally responsible, which correlative profiling of survivors cannot establish.

title: Dual-reporter decomposition of gene-specific versus global variability
description: Insert two spectrally distinct reporters under identical copies of the candidate priming promoter in the same cell and compare their correlated and uncorrelated fluctuations, alongside global physiology markers such as cell size, ribosome content, and mitochondrial mass. This separates whether the rare tolerant state reflects a gene-specific stochastic program or is a downstream readout of a broader cell-physiological axis, which changes what should be targeted.

title: Varying the microenvironment to test neighborhood-determined survival
description: Use micropatterned islands, controlled seeding densities, and co-culture with differentially labeled cells to systematically vary each cell's local neighborhood size and composition, plus conditioned-medium and transwell swaps to isolate secreted factors. Comparing survival statistics across these designs tests whether apparent cell-intrinsic rare states are actually stochastic local niches, a confound shared by essentially all dish-based survivor-profiling experiments.

title: Fluctuation analysis to measure state-switching rates
description: Adapt the Luria–Delbrück fluctuation test to a reversible, non-genetic state: expand many parallel sub-cultures from small inocula for varying numbers of generations, treat each in full, and fit the mean-versus-variance structure of survivor counts across cultures to competing kinetic models. The resulting statistics yield numerical entry and exit rates for the tolerant state, distinguishing a rare, stably inherited subpopulation from a rapidly switching one, without identifying the responsible molecules.

title: Sister- and cousin-cell fate concordance decay to estimate state memory
description: Physically separate related cells at defined lineage distances (sisters split immediately after mitosis, cousins after two divisions, with imaging to control elapsed time), treat all of them identically, and measure how fate concordance decays with the number of generations and hours since the common ancestor. The decay constant gives the memory half-life of the priming state, which can be compared with measured protein and chromatin-mark half-lives to suggest the class of molecule carrying the memory.

title: Single-cell drug exposure and target engagement measurement
description: Quantify, cell by cell, how much inhibitor each cell accumulates (fluorescent drug analog or efflux-activity dye) alongside live target-pathway reporters such as an ERK kinase-translocation reporter, then follow the same cells to their fate. This tests whether survivors are simply cells with incomplete target inhibition or rapid signaling rebound, rather than cells in a distinct transcriptional program.

title: Micropatterned neighborhoods and ratio-mixing tests of non-cell-autonomy
description: Seed cells on micropatterned islands that fix local density, neighbor number, and colony geometry, and separately mix differentially labeled isogenic cells at varying ratios and total densities before treatment. If per-cell survival probability depends on neighborhood configuration or on the abundance of dying neighboring cells rather than being constant, the rare survivor is determined by context, and conditioned-medium and transwell swaps can then separate secreted from contact-mediated signals.

title: Decoupling mean expression from cell-to-cell variability of candidate regulators
description: Using CRISPRa/dCas9 titration or a degron, shift the mean level of a suspected priming factor without changing distribution shape. Separately, install a negative-feedback or microRNA-based buffering circuit that reduces cell-to-cell variability while holding the mean fixed. Comparing survivor frequency across these two manipulations distinguishes a threshold acting on the rare tail of a noisy distribution from a mechanism that depends only on average expression.

title: Single-cell drug pharmacology: are survivors resistant or just under-dosed?
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug using a fluorescent drug analog (cross-validated by MALDI mass-spectrometry imaging of the parent compound), together with efflux activity (calcein-AM/rhodamine-123 extrusion), lysosomal sequestration (LysoTracker colocalization with and without bafilomycin), and a single-cell target-engagement readout such as NanoBRET or in-cell CETSA imaging. This separates low intracellular drug from target binding without change in pathway output, and is tested causally by blocking efflux or lysosomal trapping and asking whether the surviving fraction collapses.

title: Single-cell BH3 profiling of apoptotic priming
description: Measure each untreated cell's proximity to the mitochondrial apoptosis threshold by microscopy-based BH3 profiling (digitonin permeabilization, graded BIM/BAD/HRK peptides, per-cell cytochrome-c release or TMRE loss), and test whether the rare unprimed tail quantitatively matches the surviving fraction across doses. A BH3 mimetic should reduce the survivor fraction without changing targeted-pathway signaling, while graded BCL-2/MCL-1 overexpression should increase it predictably.

title: Mitotic partitioning asymmetry as the origin of the primed state
description: Time-lapse image the unequal inheritance of mitochondria, lysosomes, efflux transporters, damaged/aggregated protein, and the drug target itself at each division, then follow both daughters into drug to test whether partitioning asymmetry at a specific division predicts which sister survives. Perturb mitosis duration or mitochondrial fission (DRP1) to shift the asymmetry distribution and test whether survivor frequency changes as predicted, which would place the origin of priming in stochastic division rather than transcription.

title: Division-history and label retention of survivors
description: Install a division counter (doxycycline-pulsed stable H2B-fluorophore or photoconverted Dendra2) whose signal halves with each division. Determine, both retrospectively and by prospective sorting, whether survivors come from label-retaining, rarely dividing cells or from recently divided cells. This quantifies how many divisions ago the surviving state was set and separates protein age from transcriptional signature.

title: Niche-conferred survival: neighbor ablation, micropatterning, and medium transfer
description: Use micropatterns and defined local-density gradients to test whether survival probability depends on neighborhood geometry. Combine this with selective laser or optogenetic (KillerRed/miniSOG) ablation of a prospective survivor's immediate neighbors just before drug, and with transfer of conditioned medium from microwells that produced survivors. This tests whether survival is determined by cell-extrinsic location rather than a rare intrinsic cell state, which intrinsic-state assays cannot detect.

title: Retrospective profiling of future survivors using barcodes
description: Heritably barcode a clonal population, split it, treat one arm, and use the barcodes of surviving colonies to retrospectively isolate and sequence their untreated siblings from a frozen aliquot of the other arm. This directly measures the molecular state of cells destined to survive, before any drug exposure, instead of inferring it from post-treatment comparisons.

title: Live-cell histories linked to end-point molecular state
description: Image every cell in a well continuously from before dosing through colony outgrowth, then perform in-situ transcriptomics or protein imaging on the same fixed plate, registering each survivor to its full behavioral history. This separates survival driven by a pre-existing expression state from survival driven by transient events such as cell-cycle phase, division timing, or neighbor death at the moment of treatment.

title: Single-cell measurement of intracellular drug concentration
description: Quantify per-cell intracellular drug concentration using fluorescent drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, or efflux-transporter reporters, paired with a live readout of target-pathway inhibition in the same cells. This tests whether survivors are cells that received or retained less drug, rather than cells in a distinct signaling or transcriptional state.

title: Sharing of survival fate across clonal relatives of increasing distance
description: Physically separate sister cells, cousins, and progressively more distant clonal relatives, treat some while profiling or freezing the others, and measure how strongly survival fate is shared as a function of generations since common ancestor. This yields a measured memory half-life of the resistant state in units of cell divisions.

title: CRISPR and epigenetic-editing screens scored on variability and the distribution tail
description: Run CRISPR, CRISPRi, or epigenetic-editing screens scored on the fraction of cells surviving drug or on the shape and tail weight of a single-cell reporter distribution, rather than on bulk growth or mean expression. Identify hits that alter variability without altering the average. Follow with targeted epigenetic writing and erasing of the primed state to establish causal control over how many cells enter the surviving minority.

title: Isolating future survivors before treatment using clonal barcodes
description: Use clonal DNA barcodes plus barcode-specific RNA FISH (or a recorder that converts barcode identity into a sortable surface marker) to physically isolate, from an untreated population, the cells whose sister cells survive drug treatment in a parallel dish. Then profile them by single-cell multiome and proteomics. This measures the pre-existing state of future survivors directly, rather than inferring it backwards from resistant colonies that have been reshaped by weeks of drug.

title: Decay of survival concordance with time and divisions
description: Separate sister and cousin cells at defined numbers of divisions after a common ancestor, treat one branch while culturing the other drug-free for varying intervals, and measure how the concordance of survival decays with elapsed time and divisions. This gives a quantitative decay constant for heritability and distinguishes a stably inherited epigenetic state from a fluctuating state with a specific memory time that sets the size of the surviving fraction.

title: Per-cell intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy
description: Quantify intracellular free drug concentration and target occupancy in individual cells before and during treatment using fluorescent drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, and live target-engagement reporters, then correlate these with each cell's fate by imaging. This tests whether much of the variance in survival is explained by cell-to-cell differences in uptake, efflux, and drug–target stoichiometry rather than by a resistance program.

title: Making the rare state common
description: Use CRISPRa/CRISPRi, defined signaling pre-treatments, or forced cell-cycle and metabolic states to drive a large fraction of cells into the candidate pre-resistant state, then measure whether the surviving fraction shifts by orders of magnitude in the predicted direction. Pairing this with experiments that erase the state turns correlative single-cell profiling into a sufficiency-and-necessity test with an effect-size readout.

title: Fluctuation analysis for non-genetic states
description: Expand hundreds of small replicate subpopulations from single cells for varying numbers of generations before an identical drug challenge, and fit the distribution of survivor counts across replicates (a fluctuation analysis adapted to reversible states) to infer switching rates into and out of the primed state and its persistence time. Colony counts alone, without sequencing or imaging of cell state, can constrain the mechanism and rule out classes of models.

title: Sister-lineage retrospective profiling with multimodal readouts
description: Barcode cells, let them divide, and split sister lineages: treat one half, then sequence the untreated sister lineages of the survivors for RNA, chromatin accessibility and protein. This identifies the pre-existing state that predicts survival, and tests whether this primed state is a coordinated, transient program spread across many genes rather than a single marker or a stable subpopulation.

title: Live imaging of signaling history before drug exposure
description: Use long-term live-cell imaging of reporters for kinase activity (such as ERK and AKT) and the cell cycle, then add drug and link each cell's survival to its full pre-treatment history. This tests whether survival depends on how signals changed over time (pulse frequency, recent stress) rather than on a single-time-point measure of cell state.

title: Measuring inheritance of survival with fluctuation assays and sister-cell correlations
description: Run Luria–Delbrück fluctuation assays together with sister-cell and cousin-cell survival correlations at different times since the last division. This measures how strongly and for how long the tendency to survive is inherited. Comparing that timescale with gene-expression memory would show whether survival arises from transcriptional states, from inherited cell components (such as mitochondria or protein aggregates), or from chance.

title: Pooled CRISPR screens separating priming from conversion
description: Run barcoded single-cell CRISPR screens that separately score (a) how many cells enter the primed state and (b) how efficiently primed cells become stably resistant after drug addition. This would test whether the two steps are controlled by largely separate regulators that could be targeted at different times.

title: Spatial lineage tracing of survivors in tumors
description: Combine in vivo lineage barcodes with spatial transcriptomics, imaging tumors before and during treatment, to map where survivors start and which neighboring cells or local niches they sit in. This tests whether a cell's location and signals from nearby cells, rather than its own internal state, decide survival, and whether the in vitro finding of rare primed cells holds in tissue.

title: Retrospective capture of untreated clonal siblings of survivors
description: Give every cell a heritable barcode that is both transcribed and readable by hybridization capture, split the population into a treated arm and an untreated arm, then use the barcodes of the survivors to physically retrieve their untreated clonal siblings for single-cell RNA, ATAC, and imaging. This measures the pre-treatment state that caused survival rather than the post-treatment state that merely accompanies it.

title: Memory half-life by serial clone splitting
description: Isolate single survivors, expand them, and repeatedly split the progeny into drug-challenge and continued-growth arms at defined numbers of divisions. Fit the decay of enriched survival to extract a switching rate and memory half-life, which distinguishes a stably inherited epigenetic state from a transient fluctuation present at the time of drug addition.

title: Single-cell apoptotic priming and death timing
description: Combine single-cell BH3 profiling or live reporters of mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization with time-lapse tracking of death timing across the whole treated population. This tests whether survivors differ in their death execution threshold rather than in drug-pathway signaling, i.e., whether persistence reflects variability in the apoptotic machinery rather than rewiring of the target pathway.

title: CRISPR screens scored on the size and switching rate of the primed subpopulation
description: Run pooled CRISPR screens scored on the size and switching rate of the primed subpopulation, read out by barcode diversity and clone-size distributions of survivors, rather than on bulk viability. This identifies regulators that change the number of primed cells while leaving average drug sensitivity unchanged, which bulk viability screens would miss.

title: Cell cycle, neighbors, and intracellular drug dose at the time of exposure
description: Image cell cycle phase, local cell density, and intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent analog or mass spectrometry imaging) for every cell at the moment of treatment, then track each cell to its fate. This tests whether survival is explained by extrinsic position and actual delivered dose before invoking any intrinsic transcriptional state.

title: Clone-splitting to determine when survival is decided
description: Barcode a population, let each clone expand for a defined number of divisions, split sister cells across replicate plates, and treat all plates identically with the targeted drug. The degree to which the same barcodes survive across replicates distinguishes heritable pre-existing priming from stochastic survival at the moment of exposure, and varying the expansion interval measures how long the primed state persists.

title: Retrospective profiling of untreated sisters of future survivors
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes and sister-cell splitting to identify, after treatment, which barcodes survived, then deeply profile the matched untreated sister cells by single-cell RNA, ATAC, and surface protein measurement. This identifies the rare transient pre-treatment state that predicts survival, rather than the post-drug state of cells already altered by treatment.

title: Multigenerational live imaging of signaling and cycle history before drug
description: Track lineages for many generations with ERK/AKT activity reporters, cell-cycle reporters, and drug-target pathway sensors, then regress survival on each cell's full history, including pulse frequency, quiescence episodes, division timing, and asymmetric partitioning at mitosis. This tests whether temporal history predicts survival better than any single-timepoint snapshot of expression.

title: Perturbation screens scored on frequency of the primed state
description: Combine pooled CRISPR or small-molecule perturbations with a live reporter of the primed pre-resistant state and lineage barcodes. Score each perturbation by its effect on the frequency of primed cells and on the rates of switching into and out of that state. This identifies regulators of the variability itself, which are often distinct from genes that confer resistance once a cell is primed.

title: Same-barcode fate comparison across drugs, doses, and in vivo context
description: Split one barcoded population across different targeted agents, doses, and matched in vitro versus xenograft environments, then determine whether the same set of barcodes survives in each condition. Shared survivors would indicate a general primed state, while condition-specific survivors would show that the microenvironment and drug mechanism select different subsets, constraining which measurements could predict survival.

title: Memory decay curves from barcoded split populations
description: Barcode a population, let it grow, split it into replicate plates at different numbers of generations, and treat each plate with drug. Measuring how often the same barcodes survive across splits as a function of time since division gives a quantitative memory timescale for the pre-resistant state, as in a Luria-Delbrück fluctuation test. This would show whether survival is pre-encoded, heritable but transient, or decided only after the drug arrives.

title: Pre-treatment multiome profiling of cells whose descendants survive
description: Use lineage barcodes to identify, before treatment, the cells whose descendants later survived. Profile those cells with joint scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and protein measurements. Test whether rare survival arises from one coherent primed program or from many different low-probability states that each lead to survival, and identify the chromatin features that keep that state stable across divisions.

title: Continuous live imaging through drug exposure
description: Engineer cells with reporters for signaling dynamics (e.g., ERK/AKT pulses), cell-cycle phase and stress responses, then follow thousands of single-cell lineages from days before treatment through weeks on drug. Link each cell's fate to both its history and its earliest responses after the drug is added. This separates pre-existing state from events after drug exposure, such as cell-cycle phase at drug entry or how signaling recovers.

title: CRISPR screens for regulators of variability rather than resistance
description: Run pooled perturbation screens paired with barcoded fate readouts. Score each knockout by how much it changes the fraction of surviving cells, the diversity of survivor fates, and the stability of the primed state, not just average drug sensitivity. This could reveal genes that set how often cells enter rare states, which would be new targets for preventing resistance before it starts.

title: Same clones across many hosts or environments
description: Inject a single barcoded population into many mice, or into many in vitro microenvironments that differ in density, stroma, or nutrients. Treat each one and compare which barcodes survive. If the same clones survive everywhere, survival is cell-intrinsic; if the overlap depends on context, then microenvironmental factors such as neighbors, mechanics, or metabolism help determine which identical cells survive.

title: Clone splitting to test whether survival is a heritable pre-existing state
description: Barcode cells, let each clone expand for a few divisions, then split it. Profile one half (scRNA-seq, ATAC, imaging) and treat the other half with drug. Varying the time before the split measures how many generations the survivor state lasts, which shows whether fate is set by a heritable pre-treatment state or decided by chance after drug exposure.

title: Live-cell signaling dynamics linked to each cell's fate
description: Use multiplexed live reporters (for example ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters, cell-cycle sensors, and stress reporters) to track thousands of cells before and during treatment, then match each cell's signaling path to whether it survived. This tests whether survivors differ in how they adapt dynamically after drug exposure rather than in any static state measured before treatment.

title: Single-cell measurement of intracellular drug and target engagement
description: Measure how much drug each cell takes up and how much of the target it blocks, using fluorescent drug analogs, target-engagement biosensors, or single-cell mass spectrometry imaging. Then test whether survivors received or retained a lower effective dose because of efflux, cell size, or membrane differences, which would be a physical explanation not involving gene expression.

title: Perturbation screens that score how often survivors arise
description: Run pooled CRISPR or chromatin-modifier screens with single-cell readout. Score each perturbation by how much it changes the fraction of cells that survive and how fast cells switch into and out of the primed state, not only by whether resistance appears. This would map the regulatory network that sets the rate of rare survival, so the rare state could be expanded or eliminated on purpose.

title: Spatial and neighbor-context mapping of survivors
description: Follow drug-treated cultures and tumors with spatial transcriptomics and time-lapse imaging that records each cell's position, local density, and neighbors (including dying neighbors). Then test whether survival depends on the cell's surroundings, for example signals released by nearby dying cells or niche contacts, rather than on its own internal state.

title: Retrospective profiling of cells that will survive
description: Barcode a population, split it into two matched halves, treat one half with drug and profile the untreated half to recover the pre-treatment transcriptomes of the clones that went on to survive. This provides a direct measurement of the primed state that existed before any drug was applied, rather than a post-hoc description of resistant cells.

title: Measuring switching rates of the tolerant state
description: Adapt Luria–Delbrück fluctuation analysis to non-genetic variability: grow many small clonal expansions for varying durations before treatment, and use the variance in survivor number across replicates to infer rates of entry into and exit from the tolerant state. The output is a memory half-life and a switching rate.

title: Quantifying the drug itself in single cells
description: Use fluorescent drug analogs, mass spectrometry imaging, or target-engagement reporters to measure intracellular drug concentration and target occupancy cell by cell during treatment. This tests whether survivors differ mainly in how much drug reaches the target (through efflux, uptake, or lysosomal sequestration) rather than in downstream signaling or stem-like programs.

title: Continuous imaging from pre-treatment dynamics to final fate
description: Track thousands of individual cells by live imaging with reporters for pathway activity, cell-cycle position, and division history for days before and through drug exposure, then fix and profile the same cells in situ. This links time-varying features, such as signaling pulse frequency, time since last division, and inherited organelle content, to survival, capturing dynamic information that snapshot assays miss.

title: Testing whether survival is carried by the cell or set by its neighborhood
description: Map survivors against their local context (density, neighbor identity, position in a colony or spheroid). Then physically isolate candidate survivors and re-plate them in fresh contexts to see whether the survival phenotype is transferable. If survival is conferred by position and neighbors rather than carried by the cell, the view that persistence is a cell-intrinsic property would need revision.

title: Retrospective lineage barcoding of primed cells
description: Barcode a clonal population with heritable lineage tags, split it, profile one half by scRNA-seq before drug exposure and sequence barcodes in survivors after, so the pre-treatment transcriptional state of surviving lineages can be reconstructed. This distinguishes a rare pre-existing primed subpopulation from a state induced by the drug itself.

title: RNA-protein mismatch in survivors
description: Jointly measure single-cell transcript and protein levels for the drug target and bypass pathways using CITE-seq or smFISH combined with immunofluorescence. This tests whether survivors are defined by translational or post-translational buffering that is invisible to transcript-only resistance screens.

title: Continuous live-cell tracking of survival trajectories
description: Perform long-term time-lapse imaging with signaling and cell-cycle reporters spanning drug addition, tracking each cell's complete history. This reveals whether survival reflects a persistent fluctuating state, cell-cycle phase at the moment of exposure, or stochastic escape from apoptotic commitment.

title: Dense time sampling of transient states during treatment
description: Profile cells at many time points during the first 72 hours of treatment rather than only before and after, since the decisive state may be transient. Pair this with drug-on/drug-off pulse schedules to test whether the surviving state is reversible and whether the cells can be re-sensitized.

title: Single-cell metabolic activity of persisters
description: Quantify per-cell biosynthetic and metabolic demand in survivors using SCENITH or puromycin-incorporation translation-rate assays alongside dormancy markers and nutrient-limitation challenges. This tests whether persistence is an actively maintained low-consumption quiescent program rather than specific signaling rewiring.

title: Retrospective barcoding to read the pre-treatment state of survivors
description: Give every cell a heritable, transcribed DNA barcode (ClonMapper/Rewind-style) so that after treatment one can return to a pre-treatment aliquot of the same clone and examine its untreated sister cells by scRNA-seq. This separates rare pre-existing primed states from drug-induced states, and tests whether survival maps onto lineage.

title: Fixation-based single-cell time course profiling of dying cells and persisters
description: Run a fixation-based single-cell time course (fixed scRNA-seq or in-situ methods that retain dying cells) across the first 1-72 h of drug exposure, so apoptotic and arrested cells are sampled rather than lost to dissociation bias. Compare the trajectories of cells that die with those of persisters, which is more informative than an endpoint profile of survivors alone, since that profile reflects only selected cells and lacks context.

title: Live-imaging fate mapping followed by in situ molecular readout of the same cells
description: Image signaling and cell-cycle reporters (ERK-KTR, CDK2 sensor, ATF4/stress reporters) in thousands of individual cells through treatment, then fix the plate and perform MERFISH or multiplexed immunofluorescence on those same tracked cells. This directly maps each cell's measured pre-drug dynamic state to its individual survival outcome, rather than relying on correlations across separate populations.

title: Durability of the survivor state by drug withdrawal, serial re-challenge, and chromatin profiling
description: Take single survivor colonies, withdraw drug, and serially passage them, re-challenging sister sub-populations at intervals from days to months to quantify the half-life of the resistant phenotype. At each timepoint, perform single-cell ATAC-seq or CUT&RUN for H3K27me3/H3K4me1 to distinguish maintained chromatin memory, a genetically fixed mutation, and a reversible physiological state.

title: Survival as a property of local neighborhood
description: Systematically vary local context (seeding density, micropatterned colonies of defined size, conditioned-medium swaps, fibroblast co-culture) and record position-resolved survival by imaging. Combine this with spatial reporters of secreted factors to test whether survivors sit preferentially at colony edges or in regions of altered paracrine signaling, shifting the question from which cell survives to which location supports survival.

title: Pre-treatment expression-tail mapping by smFISH with re-imaging after treatment
description: Use single-molecule RNA FISH (or amplified clampFISH) against candidate resistance genes in millions of untreated cells. Then treat and re-image the same field to test whether survivors came from the rare high-expressing subpopulation. This quantifies how much survival is explained by the tail of each gene's expression distribution rather than its mean.

title: Kinetic origin of the rare high-expressing state via transcriptional bursting
description: Measure transcriptional bursting of the candidate driver gene using intronic FISH or live MS2/PP7 reporters to determine whether rare high-expressing cells arise from increased burst frequency, larger burst size, or slow mRNA/protein turnover. Then perturb each parameter via promoter swaps or degron tags and test whether survivor frequency shifts accordingly.

title: Live imaging linking division kinetics to survival fate
description: Track thousands of single cells through drug addition with FUCCI cell-cycle reporters plus death and division readouts, retrospectively linking each survivor's pre-treatment cycle length and signaling dynamics to its outcome. This distinguishes persistence through quiescence from persistence through active bypass signaling, which have opposite therapeutic implications.

title: Spatial neighborhood versus cell-intrinsic causes
description: Grow cells at controlled densities and in spatially resolved colonies, then use spatial transcriptomics or imaging mass cytometry to test whether survivors cluster in local patches (indicating paracrine or contact-mediated protection) rather than scattering at random. Follow up with targeted neighbor ablation and conditioned-media swaps to establish causality.

title: Cataloguing distinct survivor programs and their heritability
description: Profile survivors with single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) and phospho-CyCIF to test whether they occupy one state or several distinct bypass-pathway programs requiring different combination therapies. Pair this with heritable lineage barcoding and split-and-retreat experiments to measure how long each primed state persists and whether it is re-inducible, aiming to identify a common epigenetic mechanism underlying the variable states.

title: Clone-splitting with heritable barcodes to profile the pre-treatment state of future survivors
description: Transduce the population with expressed lineage barcodes, let each clone expand, then split it: treat one half with the targeted drug and immediately profile the untreated twin half by single-cell RNA-seq, so that barcodes shared with the eventual survivors reveal the pre-treatment state of those specific cells. This distinguishes a rare pre-existing transcriptional state from a state induced only after drug exposure, and can be extended with barcode-guided sorting to prospectively enrich and functionally test the primed subpopulation.

title: Continuous live-cell imaging of signaling dynamics through drug treatment
description: Image thousands of single cells for days to weeks using kinase-translocation reporters for the drug-targeted pathway (e.g., ERK or AKT activity), plus cell-cycle and stress reporters, tracking every lineage from before treatment through survival or death. Quantify whether survivors are distinguished by repeated transient signaling pulses, a longer quiescent pause, or a single sustained reactivation event.

title: Testing the microenvironment as a determinant of survivor location
description: Map where survivors are located and what they contact, using spatial transcriptomics or in situ imaging of treated 3D cultures and tumor sections to score survivor proximity to ECM-rich regions, fibroblasts, vasculature, or hypoxic cores. Pair this with micropatterned substrates of defined stiffness and ligand composition to test causality. If survival probability depends on anchorage and neighbor contact rather than intrinsic cell state, a cell-autonomous explanation would be incorrect.

title: Single-cell multiome time course to reconstruct and then perturb the regulators linking primed and resistant states
description: Collect joint RNA and ATAC profiles at closely spaced timepoints spanning the drug transition to infer which transcription factors and enhancers connect the rare primed state to the stable resistant state. Then test necessity by CRISPRi knockdown or degron depletion of the top candidate regulators at defined times, asking whether the surviving fraction drops when they are removed.

title: Serial challenge-and-withdrawal to measure persistence of the surviving state
description: Expand survivors, withdraw drug for varying intervals, re-barcode or re-sequence existing barcodes, and re-challenge, to determine whether the same clones survive again (heritable, stably altered resistance) or a new random subset survives (a transient, re-sampled state). The decay curve of clone re-use across withdrawal times gives a quantitative memory timescale that predicts whether drug holidays should resensitize the population.

title: Time-lapse measurement of the lifetime of the primed state
description: Knock a fluorescent reporter into an endogenous resistance-associated locus (AXL, NGFR, EGFR, WNT5A) and image untreated cells for days to extract per-cell dwell-time distributions in the high state. Add drug at a defined moment and retrospectively link survival to whether each cell was in the high state at treatment onset. This tests whether survival requires occupancy of a short-lived state rather than membership in a stable subpopulation.

title: Sister-cell splitting with varying delay to measure memory decay
description: Barcode cells, split each clone into two arms, and treat the second arm after delays ranging from hours to weeks. Twin-to-twin concordance in survivor frequency as a function of delay gives the decay constant of the heritable component, quantifying how long the primed state persists before returning to the population mean.

title: Retrospective capture of the pre-treatment state using expressed lineage barcodes
description: Use expressed lineage barcodes to identify, in an untreated replicate aliquot, the clones that survived in the treated arm, then barcode-sort those cells and profile transcriptome, chromatin accessibility, and histone marks. This captures the primed state in its original form, before survivors have transitioned to a different phenotype.

title: Reversion kinetics after drug withdrawal
description: Subject survivors to a drug holiday and track resensitization via single-cell profiling and clonal re-barcoding across timepoints, asking whether and how fast the resistant phenotype relaxes back to the naive distribution. Full reversion implicates a transient non-genetic mechanism, while a non-reverting subset separates genuinely mutated clones from epigenetically primed ones and quantifies the mixture.

title: Perturbing the duration of the tolerant state rather than its mean
description: Apply chromatin-regulator inhibitors (DOT1L, KDM5, EZH2, HDAC) or degron-controlled modifiers before drug, and use reporter time-lapse to measure whether each perturbation changes state amplitude, entry frequency, or dwell time; then test which parameter predicts survivor frequency. If interventions that shorten dwell time reduce survivors without changing how many cells ever enter the state, survival is causally set by how long the state persists.

title: Sister-cell split assay with fate concordance across generational distance
description: Separate sister cells immediately after each division by micromanipulation or microwell tracking, expose one to the targeted drug and profile the other by scRNA-seq, then quantify fate concordance as a function of generational distance (sisters, cousins, second cousins). The decay of concordance with lineage distance measures the heritability and memory half-life of the primed state, distinguishing a stably inherited epigenetic configuration from a transiently fluctuating one.

title: Live reporters of rare high-expressing states
description: Knock fluorescent reporters into endogenous candidate resistance loci (e.g., AXL, NGFR, EGFR, SOX10) and image untreated populations for days to identify rare, transiently high-expressing cells, then add drug and determine which imaged cells survive. This converts the retrospective question of what survivors were like beforehand into a prospective one, and also yields the on/off switching rates and state lifetimes that set the size of the surviving fraction.

title: Image-guided retrieval of tracked survivors for same-cell multiomics
description: Track rare survivors by live imaging through treatment, then photoconvert or laser-mark those cells and recover them for same-cell multiomic profiling (joint ATAC + RNA + surface protein), so the measured molecular state belongs to a cell whose behavioral history (division timing, motility, drug-response dynamics) is known. Pairing phenotype trajectory with molecular state in the same cell avoids the ambiguity of profiling bulk survivor pools in which several distinct escape routes are averaged together.

title: Barcode replicate-split studies of survival origin
description: Transduce a high-complexity expressed barcode library, split the population into replicate plates, and determine whether the same barcode lineages survive in independent plates and in independent rounds of drug exposure after a drug holiday. Reproducible barcode overlap implicates pre-existing heritable priming, non-overlap implicates stochastic induction, and partial overlap that decays over the holiday quantifies how long the primed state persists before it is re-created.

title: Timing of tolerant-state stabilization over drug on/off cycles
description: Run drug-on/drug-off cycles while sampling chromatin (CUT&RUN for enhancer remodeling, DNA methylation) and signaling (phosphoproteomics) at dense time points. At each time point, test reversibility by adding chromatin-modifier inhibitors or withdrawing drug. This identifies the window in which a reversible, fluctuating tolerant state becomes a stable resistant state, and which enzymes maintain it.

title: Barcode-based retrospective identification of pre-existing survivor states
description: Barcode a clonal cancer cell population and split it. Treat one half and profile the untreated half by single-cell RNA-seq, then trace survivor barcodes back to their untreated sister cells. This reveals whether the surviving state is a pre-existing transcriptional state present before drug exposure rather than a drug-induced change.

title: Timescale of transcriptional state fluctuation
description: Knock in live-cell fluorescent reporters at candidate priming loci (e.g., AXL, NGFR, EGFR) and use long-term timelapse imaging to measure dwell times and autocorrelation of the high-expressing state. Sorting cells by how long they have occupied that state and then challenging them tests whether survival probability depends on the duration, not just the level, of priming.

title: Spatial and paracrine determinants of survival
description: Treat cells at controlled densities and micropatterned spacings, then image survivors in situ with multiplexed single-molecule FISH or spatial transcriptomics to test whether they arise in non-random neighborhoods. Conditioned-medium and transwell co-culture experiments then determine whether tolerance is transferable between neighbors or strictly cell-intrinsic.

title: Quiescence and metabolic state of survivors
description: Combine FUCCI cell-cycle reporters or dye-dilution proliferation tracking with single-cell metabolic readouts such as NAD(P)H FLIM or SCENITH during the first days of treatment. This distinguishes survivors that are simply slow-cycling and metabolically low-activity from those running a distinct resistance gene program.

title: Reversibility across repeated drug-on/drug-off cycles
description: Barcode cells and run repeated cycles of treatment and drug holiday, sequencing barcode abundance plus matched single-cell DNA and RNA at each round. Recurrence of the same barcodes indicates heritable genetic or stably epigenetic resistance, whereas a new set of survivors each cycle indicates a transient state that cells enter stochastically.

title: Retrospective lineage tracing of survivors
description: Continuously image a whole well from before drug addition through survivor outgrowth, then trace each resistant colony back to its founder cell. This measures what the eventual survivor was doing hours to days before treatment (size, cell-cycle phase, reporter intensity, division history), rather than only what survivors look like at the end.

title: Fluctuation timescale of priming genes as a predictor of survival
description: Place live-cell reporters on candidate priming genes (AXL, NGFR, EGFR) and measure the autocorrelation time of their fluctuations in untreated cells. The prediction is that only cells whose high state persists longer than the drug's killing window survive, so fluctuation memory time, rather than peak expression level, would be the decisive measurement.

title: Sibling-split assays separating heritable from stochastic survival
description: Split single cells into daughter or granddaughter pairs, treating one branch with drug while profiling the untreated sibling by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. Concordance between siblings quantifies how many generations back the surviving state was established, distinguishing heritable priming from a random event at the moment of treatment.

title: Spatial niche mapping of survivors
description: Map each surviving cell's spatial context, including local density, neighbor identity, distance to colony edge, ECM stiffness and substrate contact, by combining live imaging with spatial transcriptomics on the fixed well. Comparing matched dying cells at equivalent positions tests whether microenvironment, drug access, or paracrine signaling explains survival independently of cell-intrinsic state.

title: Drug holiday and re-challenge to test epigenetic memory
description: Withdraw drug from survivors, expand them for defined numbers of generations, and re-challenge at intervals while profiling chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation. The decay rate of resistance distinguishes reversible transcriptional tolerance from stably encoded epigenetic or genetic resistance and identifies loci that remain in a primed state.

title: Retrospective capture of the pre-drug primed state with sister-cell split barcoding
description: Barcode an isogenic population and use a sister-cell split design (Rewind/ClonMapper-style) so that survivors' barcodes can be traced back to their untreated sister cells, which are profiled by scRNA-seq. This measures the cell state that existed before drug exposure, distinguishing pre-existing priming from drug-induced reprogramming.

title: Measuring the memory half-life of the resistant state
description: Isolate primed or persister cells, culture them drug-free for intervals from hours to weeks, and re-challenge at each time point to build a decay curve of resistance probability. The decay rate, compared to the division rate, reveals whether the state is a transient fluctuation or a heritable epigenetic memory.

title: Stochastic chromatin boundary loss at resistance driver loci
description: Combine single-cell ATAC/CUT&Tag with Micro-C or 4C at loci such as AXL, NGFR, or MET in primed versus naive cells, then apply CRISPRi to the implicated CTCF/cohesin boundary elements. This tests whether rare survival arises from sporadic loss of insulation that permits ectopic enhancer-promoter contact.

title: Signaling and cell-cycle phase at the moment of drug addition
description: Image cells carrying ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters plus a PIP-FUCCI cell-cycle sensor continuously through drug addition and for days afterward, linking each cell's pre-treatment dynamics to its fate. This tests whether survival is determined by the timing and phase of signaling pulses, a dynamic cause not visible in fixed-cell snapshots.

title: Survival as a property of the local cellular neighborhood
description: Use micropatterned islands, controlled seeding densities, and tunable-stiffness substrates, together with spatial transcriptomics of residual disease, to quantify how neighbor contacts, local density, and matrix mechanics predict persistence. Non-random spatial clustering of survivors would show that the rare state is partly environmental rather than cell-intrinsic.

title: Heritable barcodes plus a pre-treatment transcriptional reference
description: Transduce cells with expressed DNA barcodes and split the population into one arm profiled by scRNA-seq before treatment and one arm treated, so each surviving clone's barcode can be matched to the untreated transcriptional states. This directly tests whether survivors arise from pre-existing, heritable transcriptional states rather than random chance, and identifies the specific priming programs.

title: Optical tagging of rare primed cells before drug exposure
description: Live-image a fluorescent reporter for a candidate priming marker and use photoconversion or photo-crosslinking to permanently mark the rare brightest cells, then sort and sequence them while following matched wells through treatment. This provides a causal link between a pre-drug optical phenotype and eventual survival, rather than a post hoc correlation.

title: Sister-cell split assay to recover the survivor's pre-drug state
description: Physically separate sister cells right after mitosis, treat one sister with drug and molecularly profile the other, thereby inferring the pre-treatment state of the cell that lived or died. Varying the interval between separation and treatment measures how long the predictive non-genetic memory persists.

title: Fluctuation analysis plus reversibility kinetics
description: Perform Luria-Delbrück-style replicate expansions from small founder populations across a drug dose gradient to quantitatively partition survival into genetic, heritable-epigenetic, and transient non-genetic contributions. Then regrow survivor colonies without drug and re-challenge at increasing intervals to measure the timescale over which resistance is lost.

title: Spatial niche and paracrine factor analysis
description: Apply spatial transcriptomics to 3D cultures or co-cultures to test whether survivors occupy distinctive cellular neighborhoods. Pair this with conditioned-media transfer and ligand-trap or receptor-blockade perturbations to distinguish cell-intrinsic survival states from protection by secreted factors from neighboring cells.

title: Mark-then-profile retrieval of the pre-treatment state of future survivors
description: Use live imaging of a barcoded or photoconvertible cell population during treatment, then retrospectively identify which pre-treatment cells gave rise to survivors. This is done either by photoconverting or laser-marking their sisters in a split-population design, or by lineage barcodes shared with an untreated replicate. Then run scRNA-seq on those specific pre-treatment cells. This directly measures the priming state that preceded survival, rather than the post-treatment state of cells already altered by the drug.

title: Genetic versus non-genetic survival by single-cell DNA+RNA and fluctuation assay
description: Run matched single-cell DNA and RNA sequencing (e.g., G&T-seq or a scDNA panel plus scRNA-seq) and deep targeted sequencing on survivor colonies. This tests whether survivors carry pre-existing mutations, copy-number changes, or amplifications at the drug target, or are genetically identical but transcriptionally distinct. A Luria–Delbrück fluctuation assay of survivor frequency across sibling cultures quantifies what fraction of survival is genetic versus non-genetic.

title: Transcriptional burst kinetics of resistance genes
description: Use single-molecule RNA FISH plus MS2/PP7 live nascent-transcription imaging on candidate resistance drivers (e.g., RTKs, AXL, NGFR, efflux pumps) to test whether rare survivors differ by burst frequency/size rather than by expressing a unique gene set. Correlate each cell's measured burst history with its subsequent fate under drug.

title: Heritability half-life of the primed state across divisions
description: Sort or image-mark cells in the putative primed state, then re-assay their drug survival after defined numbers of divisions (1, 3, 5, 10) with and without a washout. This measures the heritability half-life of the resistant state and distinguishes transient fluctuation from stable epigenetic memory. Pair this with ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN at each time point to see which chromatin features persist.

title: Spatial neighborhoods of survival
description: Test whether survival is a property of cell neighborhoods rather than individual cells. Grow colonies at defined densities and track survivors by in situ spatial transcriptomics or sequential FISH on the fixed, intact monolayer. Ask whether survivors are spatially clustered and locally enriched for secreted-factor signaling. Conditioned-media transfer and microfluidic cell-separation controls then distinguish paracrine rescue from cell-intrinsic priming.

title: Barcoded sister-cell comparison to test whether survivors were already different
description: Label cells with heritable barcodes, let them divide, and split sister cells into two groups. Treat one group and profile the untreated sisters of the survivors with single-cell RNA-seq to determine whether survival comes from a state that existed before the drug (and what that state is) or from a response the drug induces.

title: Bimodally expressed genes: marker-high cells and state duration
description: Before treatment, use single-molecule RNA FISH to find genes that are high in a small fraction of cells and low in the rest. Sort the marker-high cells and track when they return to the population's normal mix and how their survival probability changes over time. Run a Luria-Delbrück fluctuation analysis alongside to separate short-lived fluctuations from stable, inherited variation.

title: Testing whether recent cell history predicts survival better than current state
description: Before and during treatment, film cells carrying live reporters, such as kinase-translocation reporters for ERK/AKT signaling and FUCCI for cell-cycle stage. Ask whether survivors share a pattern over time, such as slow cycling, signaling pulses, or a deep quiescent state, that a single snapshot would miss.

title: Single-cell drug exposure and target inhibition with efflux-pump inhibition
description: Measure intracellular drug levels in single cells (fluorescent drug analogs or mass cytometry) and the degree of target inhibition (phospho-flow or immunofluorescence). Combine this with efflux-pump inhibitors to test whether cell-to-cell differences in drug uptake or target inhibition explain part of the survival, separately from transcriptional state.

title: Spatial mapping of neighbor effects on survival
description: Perform spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed imaging on treated dishes or tumour sections, then vary seeding density and swap conditioned media. This shows whether survival depends on local crowding, signals released by nearby cells, or contact with neighbours, rather than only on cell-intrinsic traits.

title: Retrospective linkage of pre-drug expression fluctuations to survival
description: Knock fluorescent reporters into endogenous candidate resistance loci (e.g., AXL, NGFR, EGFR, MITF-low program genes) and continuously image a clonal population for several days before adding drug. Track each imaged cell's fate so that rare, transient, low-amplitude expression excursions can be scored as predictive of survival or not. Complement this with a transcriptome-wide version in which cells are split and one half is profiled by scRNA-seq while the sister half is treated, or with RNA-barcode capture, so the pre-treatment state of the eventual survivors is recovered rather than inferred.

title: Expressed lineage barcodes to separate heritable memory from short-lived fluctuations
description: Integrate expressed, scRNA-seq-capturable lineage barcodes (CellTag/Watermelon-style) into cells, expand, split the labeled population into replicate flasks, and treat each independently with the same targeted drug. If the same barcodes survive across flasks far more often than chance, survival is governed by a heritable (epigenetically memorized) state, whose half-life can be measured by varying the expansion time between splitting and treatment. If barcode overlap is at chance, survival is set by short-lived fluctuations or by the drug exposure itself.

title: Spatial neighborhood dependence of survival
description: Grow cells at defined local densities and in defined spatial patterns (micropatterned islands, mixed co-cultures with fluorescently marked drug-sensitive cells or fibroblast/stromal partners), then image which positions within a colony yield survivors. Test conditioned medium and Transwell separation to determine whether paracrine signals (HGF, NRG1, AXL ligands, extracellular vesicles) confer tolerance. Then perform spatial transcriptomics on treated colonies to correlate each survivor's transcriptional state with quantified neighborhood features, such as local density, distance to colony edge, and neighbor identity.

title: Kinetics of re-entry into the cell cycle: pre-existing quiescence vs. drug-induced dormancy
description: Use live-cell CDK2-activity and p21 sensors plus CFSE/H2B-photoconversion dilution to determine whether the cells that survive were already slow-cycling or arrested when the drug was added. Time-lapse the same fields through weeks of treatment to capture the exact division at which each persister resumes cycling. Pair this with drug-holiday experiments (remove drug, re-expand, re-treat) to quantify what fraction of tolerance is reversible dormancy versus fixed resistance, and with scRNA-seq at multiple time points to define the transcriptional trajectory from arrest to re-entry.

title: Single-cell measurement of drug uptake, efflux, and target engagement
description: Test whether survivors simply take up less drug by measuring intracellular drug concentration per cell, using an intrinsically fluorescent or click-labeled inhibitor analog, single-cell mass spectrometry, or MALDI imaging of the colony, together with efflux-pump reporters and dye-efflux (Hoechst side-population) assays. Pair each cell's drug level with a single-cell readout of target engagement (quantitative immunofluorescence for phospho-ERK/phospho-AKT or a FRET kinase biosensor), so that pharmacokinetic heterogeneity can be separated from downstream signaling-state heterogeneity as the cause of survival.

title: Clone-splitting to time the origin of the surviving state
