description: Expand single-cell-derived clones, then split each clone into a treated arm and an untreated arm that is profiled by scRNA-seq/protein staining, so that any pre-existing transcriptional program enriched in the untreated twin of a high-survival clone is identified as a primed state present before drug exposure. Varying the number of divisions between splitting and treatment (1, 5, 10, 20 generations) converts the correlation decay into a direct measurement of how many cell generations the survival-conferring state is inherited.

title: Absolute spike-in-normalized profiling of survivors
description: Quantify survivors with ERCC/UMI spike-ins plus measurements of cell volume, total RNA, total protein, and ribosome content, because standard scRNA-seq normalization hides changes in global level. This tests whether persisters differ by a uniform shift in transcriptome and biosynthetic scale (a slow-growing, low-output state) rather than by induction of specific resistance genes, which determines whether the therapeutic target is a pathway or the global growth/translation setpoint.

title: Barcoded re-challenge after drug holidays to test reversibility
description: Transduce cells with a high-complexity lineage barcode library, treat, expand survivors off drug for varying holiday lengths, then re-treat and sequence barcodes. If the same lineages survive again, the state is heritable (genetic or stably epigenetic); if a new random subset survives, the state is reversible and re-sampled. Whole-genome sequencing and ATAC-seq of the same expanded clones separate mutational resistance, chromatin-encoded memory, and stochastic re-sampling.

title: Spatial and neighborhood determinants of survival
description: Image cells at controlled densities and in micropatterned colonies, recording each cell's local density, contact number, and position (edge versus interior) before treatment. Follow survival by live imaging, and apply spatial transcriptomics or in situ sequencing at the fixed endpoint. This tests whether survivors are defined by a crowded or edge niche with local paracrine signaling and drug-gradient shielding rather than by a cell-intrinsic state, with conditioned-media and co-culture swaps as confirmation.

title: Continuous single-cell trajectories through treatment with retrospective in situ readout
description: Use long-term live-cell imaging with cell-cycle (FUCCI), signaling (ERK/AKT biosensors), and candidate-marker reporters to track every cell continuously from before drug addition through death or persistence, then fix the plate and perform single-molecule FISH or multiplexed immunofluorescence on the same imaged cells to link dynamic history to final molecular state. Comparing abrupt dosing with gradual dose escalation reveals whether survival depends on the cell's phase and signaling-pulse history at the moment of exposure or on an adaptive trajectory acquired during treatment.

title: Deep sampling of rare states in the pre-treatment population
description: Deeply sample 10^5-10^6 untreated cells by single-cell RNA-seq or multiome and explicitly model the rank-frequency tail of state abundances rather than cluster averages, asking whether drug-tolerant programs (receptor-tyrosine-kinase, neural-crest, quiescence modules) exist as discrete rare states at ~0.1-1% frequency. Validate by FACS-sorting the rare population on marker combinations and comparing colony survival to the bulk population.

title: Split-clone lineage barcoding with retrospective pre-treatment profiling
description: Label cells with heritable expressed barcodes, then split each clone into a treated arm and an untreated arm profiled immediately. Survivors in the treated arm identify barcodes whose siblings' pre-treatment transcriptomes and chromatin can be retrieved retrospectively. This directly tests whether survival is predictable from a prior molecular state or arises only after drug exposure.

title: Combinatorial perturbation screens to dissect priming programs
description: Treat each candidate priming program as composed of separable regulatory components (individual transcription factors, chromatin regulators, signaling nodes) and run CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens before drug addition, scoring changes in the frequency of surviving colonies rather than bulk viability. Pairwise perturbations then reveal which combinations are necessary versus merely co-occurring in the rare state.

title: Persistence and reversibility timescales of the rare state
description: Use long-term live imaging with endogenous fluorescent knock-ins of candidate priming genes plus sister-cell and drug-holiday experiments to measure how many generations a high-expressing state persists and whether resensitization occurs after withdrawal. Luria-Delbruck fluctuation tests on split subclones quantify whether the heritability is genetic, epigenetic with memory, or transient.

title: Microenvironment and drug exposure as confounders
description: Combine spatial/imaging-based transcriptomics with per-cell measurement of actual intracellular drug concentration (fluorescent drug analog or mass-spectrometry imaging) alongside local neighbor density, cell-cycle phase, and cell size. This distinguishes genuine intrinsic priming from positional explanations such as a cell simply receiving less drug, a key control before any rare-state model is accepted.

title: Clonal recurrence test with split-population barcoding
description: Transduce the cell line with a high-complexity heritable barcode library (e.g., ClonMapper/Watermelon), split the labeled population into replicate arms, treat each independently, and sequence barcodes in the survivors. The degree of barcode overlap between arms quantifies how much survival is driven by a heritable, pre-existing clonal state versus a stochastic, non-heritable process, and a barcode-plus-scRNA readout links each recurring clone to its expression program.

title: Retrospective identification of the pre-treatment survivor state
description: Image and single-cell-profile the untreated population, then apply drug, identify the rare survivors, and trace them back to their imaged or fixed ancestors (via live-cell tracking or barcode-guided recovery of the initial-state scRNA-seq profiles). This directly measures what surviving cells looked like before drug exposure, rather than inferring cause from the post-treatment state, which is confounded by drug-induced reprogramming.

title: Sister-cell divergence to measure the memory timescale
description: Live-image a reporter for a candidate priming factor (e.g., AXL, NGFR, or an ERK/EGFR activity biosensor) across tracked lineages, then treat and score which cells survive, comparing concordance of survival between sister cells, cousins, and unrelated cells as a function of time since division. The decay of concordance with lineage distance gives a quantitative half-life for the fluctuating state that confers tolerance, distinguishing short-lived signaling noise from multi-generation epigenetic memory.

title: Single-cell metabolic phenotyping of the quiescent/starved state
description: Apply label-free NAD(P)H/FAD fluorescence lifetime imaging plus SCENITH or puromycin-incorporation assays to measure per-cell translation rate, glycolytic/oxidative balance, and cell-cycle position at the moment of drug addition, then follow the same cells to survival outcome. This tests whether survivors are dormant, low-biosynthesis and sensitive to lipid peroxidation, and nominates metabolic co-treatments (e.g., GPX4 or OXPHOS inhibition) whose efficacy should track the measured state.

title: Spatial analysis of dying neighbors and local niche effects
description: Perform longitudinal imaging of the whole treated monolayer or 3D culture to record each survivor's local history: distance to dying cells, local density, and time-integrated exposure to factors derived from apoptotic cells and secreted factors. Compare against conditioned-media and spatially randomized controls. Pair this with spatial transcriptomics of survivor neighborhoods to distinguish cell-intrinsic priming from non-cell-autonomous rescue by dying or stressed neighbors, and test candidate ligands by blocking them.
